author: tomjn
body:
Closes #4598
Closes #394

A distribution can now ship its own wording for a language coilbox has, or add a language coilbox lacks, by putting a pack under `.coilbox/locales/<code>/`.

A pack is a `pack.json` (`code`, `name`, `direction`) plus the `messages.json` that `lingui compile --namespace json` writes. I picked the JSON output over Lingui's default `.js` module because the `.js` file is code. Reading the JSON with `JSON.parse` and checking every message against the shape Lingui compiles to means a pack is never run. It also means a malformed message is refused at startup rather than throwing on the first screen that shows it. A pack that fails is skipped and named in the profile health panel.

A pack for a bundled language is merged over that catalog key by key. A pack for any other code is merged over English, so a message it leaves out reads in English and not as a hash id. That code then appears in both the Settings picker and the first-run language page. `defaultLocale` in the profile is the default value of the Language setting, so it applies only while nothing is stored. An explicit pick of System still wins.

Size cap: each file is capped at 4 MiB in Rust, which checks the size before reading. I measured the compiled catalogs with `lingui compile --namespace json`. The largest real one is `uk` at 1,211,773 bytes, and `JSON.parse` of a 4,890,466-byte catalog took 13 ms in Bun on this Mac. 4 MiB is about 3.4 times the largest catalog. That headroom is my choice, not a measurement.

The unbundled code in the tests is `eo` (Esperanto). The issue named `pt-BR`, which is now bundled. `it` and `sv` have catalog issues open in this milestone, so a test built on either would break when its catalog lands. No issue plans `eo`.

`direction: "rtl"` is validated and stored on the pack, but nothing reads it yet. An `rtl` pack lays out left to right until milestone 91 does the right-to-left work. I did not set `<html dir>`, because flipping it before the layout supports it would make an RTL pack look broken.

The new health panel strings are extracted but not translated. The catalog work fills those in.

Portable instance with a `de` pack that renames "Play" to "Losspielen", in Deutsch. The sidebar's Play heading reads LOSSPIELEN, where the bundled catalog says "Spielen", and everything else keeps the bundled German:

![the sidebar in German with the Play heading reading Losspielen](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1435038d-5a5b-4a04-a0fc-73bb85265dd3)

With an `eo` pack added, the Language picker lists Esperanto:

![the Language picker listing Esperanto after the bundled languages](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3bf0d434-e0a7-4010-991a-97d10e74039e)

Picking it loads the pack over English, so the two messages it carries ("Ludi" and "Agordoj") show and the rest stays English:

![the app in Esperanto with Ludi and Agordoj in the sidebar and English elsewhere](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ed07d7d9-5d0b-4fa2-bd32-cf06da4355b8)

author: tossbaws
body:
**What:** one new step in the `linux` job of `dist.yml`, "Report bundled WebKitGTK version", placed after the AppImage smoke test (it reads the `squashfs-root/` that test leaves behind). It reports the build host's `libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0` package version, the `pkg-config` version, and the WebKit library files inside the extracted AppImage.

**Why:** the AppImage bundles the build host's WebKitGTK, and the WebKit crash on exit (#162, fixed in 2.54.1) is waiting on Ubuntu to ship the fix. We don't build our own WebKit, so this is how we notice when the fixed version arrives.

**Never fails the build:** the step has `continue-on-error: true`, starts with `set +e` (the default shell runs with `-e`), guards each lookup so a missing tool or file prints `unknown`, and ends with `exit 0`. If no libraries are bundled it says so; that's information, not an error.

**How to read it:** on any run, look for the **Bundled WebKitGTK** notice in the annotations, or the section of the same name in the job summary. The package and pkg-config versions are the WebKitGTK release to compare with 2.54.1. The library file name carries the soname version, which is a different number.

CI-only, so no CHANGELOG entry: the CHANGELOG doesn't log CI changes.

body:
## RT-A5 `minuend_final`: the held-status solve (S2 extraction + held solve) — DRAFT, not mergeable yet

> **Draft.** Merge order is I3a → P (+ §4 certificate) → this PR. This branch is stacked on RT-A3 P `78580da7e` merged with main `b32a17761` (`b8f3837e8`). It merges main after P and the certificate land, and its retained-pricing registration is its own D3 on that frozen predecessor. Every failure that remains until then is named below.

Owning design: DEL-05-02 `Work/operating-case.md` §7, "Held-status solve (`minuend_final`)". §6.9 now points there.

### What it does
- **One product function, two consumers.** It solves a named case with its nonlinear supports held at a named source case's final **status**. Only the status is frozen; displacements and forces come from the case being solved.
  - The first consumer is the declared subtraction `combinations[].subtrahend_support_state: "minuend_final"`.
  - Hanger sizing's `weight_support_state: design_operating_final` can later call the same function. Its contract is in §7.7; hanger integration is not in this PR.
- **NI, S2: a pure extraction** (`d02ec8789`). The loop's post-step tail becomes one crate-private function, `complete_iteration`, which the loop and the held wrapper both call.
  - RT-A3 approved the boundary as the loop's owner, and accepted the K-1 trace re-read (`db20978ca`).
  - Byte identity across 2,403 loop calls in both modes, with nothing excluded.
- **NI held wrapper** `solve_held_status_iteration`:
  - builds through `LoopSystem::assemble`;
  - runs one step, then `complete_iteration(…, Now)`, then a single `confirm_converged_state` attempt;
  - never confirms a gap state (R1);
  - starts the gap allotment at `GAP_RUN_WORK_LIMIT` and seeds iterations with the orienting iterate;
  - publishes a changed state as not converged, with its exit diagnostic.
  - The R2 pin is amended under option A, approved by RT-A3. The kd5 R2 one-line note is for RT-A3's review here.
  - `593b3fc24`: NI's `kd5_nonlinear_sources_name_no_formation_check_entry_point` pinned the wrapper's delegation without the new held-status `role` argument and failed. The pin now names `role`; the scan still checks one delegation after selection and pressure preparation, so R2's meaning is unchanged (RT-A3 confirmed). The same commit restates the stale `result_export` routing tree digest (stale since `fe419a44f`), the NI tree digest and the `s11k_tests.rs` read. NI lib 182 passed; hosted-CI routing tests 56 passed.
- **Frozen semantics per behaviour (§7.2).**
  - Held one-way, lift-off and sticking supports are prescribed at the target's ground. An active gap is at σ(c + σg).
  - Sliding uses the source's slip sense with the target's own normal; a differing sliding ground is refused.
  - The zero limit is fl(μ·N) = 0, in the classifier's order. Springs, constant-effort supports and rigid restraints are unheld.
- **Outcomes (§7.3).**
  - **E:** "Established within its stated numerical bound for the explicitly held system at this case's loads." It is followed by the caveat that it does not establish this case's own support state, an admissible sustained state, a load history or uniqueness.
  - **N:** kept but not established.
  - **R:** released, e.g. a tensile held reaction or a reversed derived normal. Inspection rows plus `HELD_STATUS_RELEASED`; never withheld.
  - **G:** gap-bearing, never confirmed.
  - No outcome publishes "confirmed" or qualifies the natural state.
- **Binding (§7.4).** `HeldStatusSource` carries an unpublished invocation token, the #97 evidence copy, the source's own loop input (both normal maps), springs, the receipt-bound result and the node-id map. It is checked in order, with refusals by `HELD_STATUS_*` name. The #97 seam lines are unchanged.
- **Admission (§7.5).** PF only, in both modes.
  - EX still refuses `difference_basis` first. Absent or `own` stays own, and `minuend_final` is never inferred.
  - The interim `…_SUBTRAHEND_SUPPORT_STATE_UNSUPPORTED` is removed at the solve and the applier for the admitted scope.
- **Publication.** Held-operand rows sit under the combination with the closed, typed `held_status_operand` basis, never as the sustained case's rows. Evidence is `contract_evidence.held_status_derivation`. Rule selection never selects a held-operand row (`a0142f49c`; DEL-06-01 §2.5).
- **Readers.** RE `preview_held_status.rs` plus the gates, operands, difference-basis, evidence and global-end readers, with a Python mirror.
  - Model-bound and model-free contracts, with ordinary and strict-gap contracts kept separate.
  - Provenance, normal source (support/node/DOF) and convergence are authenticated. Claims are limited to what is actually checked.
- **Contract texts.**
  - Policy v4: preview-physics-2 `f41b9d3e → 563db3c7`, timoshenko-1 `6f649490 → f64473f5`, retained-1 `b4377e73 → d0bab350`.
  - Both result schemas gain closed members. `LIMITATIONS[6]` is unchanged.
  - The registry gains main's `b32a17761` tables verbatim, and main's recorded PF runs are kept verbatim in `recorded_pre_rt_a5_mf_pf/`, with regressions. Nothing is resealed.
- **§4 certificate (RT-A3, unmerged).** Held-path `LoadCaseSolve` constructions carry the `certificate_operand: None` requirement. RT-A3's O-C2 marks non-default `subtrahend_support_state` combinations as not assessed. Policy (b) is unchanged.

### Decisions
- **Agent 0:** the S2 extraction only; the E wording; the smaller choices, with provisos.
- **RT-A3:** the S2 boundary; R2 option A with the gap condition; the PP lib.rs hunks cleared next to the certificate's.
- **Manager:** gap models admitted under G; `HELD_STATUS_*` prefix.
- **Deviations from §7, recorded in §7.3:** residual deltas measured from the orienting iterate; no `metadata.held_status_ref`; held rows closed under their references; the `held_solve` member; null `numerical_quality` for the held operand; reader order; no separate `solve_case_at_held_status` yet. The independent review found deviation 2 sufficient, 3, 5 and 6 acceptable, and 4 appropriate once repaired.

### References
`validation/references/op_mf_held_status/` holds H-1 to H-18 and their variants, plus H-7g, the product witness for G. They come from a standard-library generator that reads no product code; the reviewer independently recomputed a sample. PP `op_mf_held_status` runs them in both modes and covers:
- own versus held differing; release; friction (sticking, explicit and derived normal, μ = 0 and the zero limit, inactive);
- the coupled L-frame H-14/H-14r, with the uncoupled-normal and frozen-normal mutants killed;
- linear held twins (1e-9);
- forged, missing and cross-invocation bindings; repeat calls byte-identical; non-converged-not-promoted.

NI H-10 checks the wrapper against the loop on a widened corpus, including the unqualified mixed-gap witness compared as a value. Every binding, release and normal-source guard is mutation-checked.

### Checks (local, at the step-2 head and its repairs)
- NI 182+4, held 5. PP `op_mf_held_status` 9, held lib 3. RE held 4, all RE targets pass. Applier 423, runner 158.
- Python held 77. CI routing 116.
- Desktop: `tsc -b` clean; vitest full 3,650 + 3,731; src-tauri lib 1,028 (+ the fix).
- Carriers regenerated by their writers (`76846f78a`).
- `tools.deliverables check` 0 errors.

### Independent review (gpt-6-astra medium)
- **Design:** "revise", then repaired; focused confirmation; three small findings repaired.
- **Implementation (`6560b9e71`):** no P0/P1. Four P2s (normal-source identity, provenance, convergence consistency, coupled-frame/twin/H-10 coverage), repaired.
- **Focused confirmation (`92eb066f5`):** all four closed. One new P2 (separate support, DOF and node tamper cases) is repaired in `fe419a44f`, with mutation proof.

### Expected failures until this PR's D3 (named, with cause)

author: fatherlinux
body:
## What

Removes `[tool.sdlc.ci] skip = ["codeql"]`, so CodeQL runs in the required `sdlc ci` check.

## Why

Constitution XII: "CI runs push's checks except Gourmand and Gatehouse." CodeQL is one of push's verdicts, and the two exclusions are the image's decision, not a repo's. With the skip, the only place a CodeQL finding could block was the pre-push hook — a developer's machine, one `--no-verify` away — while the required `sdlc ci` reported green.

The skip's comment claimed the CodeQL Action covered it. The CodeQL Action does run on pull requests here, but its check is advisory: no ruleset requires it, so a finding annotated the PR and merged anyway.

I wrote that skip during the RT#1552 conversion, into 24 of the 33 repos. This is one of the 24. [python-sdlc#19](https://github.com/crunchtools/python-sdlc/pull/19) then makes `resolve()` refuse the config, so it cannot come back quietly.

## Verification

`sdlc ci` run locally with CodeQL in it: exit 0, `codeql: 0 new, 0 in the baseline`.

author: eriksaulnier
body:
This adds two ways to run unreleased loupe. Spec: `specs/053-prerelease-workflow/`.

**Try a release before merging its pull request.** The release pull request is opened with GITHUB_TOKEN, so `ci.yml` never runs on it. While one is open, `release.yml`'s new `snapshot` job builds main's head after each push with `goreleaser release --snapshot`, at the pull request's version. It uploads the result as the artifact `loupe-snapshot`. Nothing is tagged or published. `docs/releasing.md` has the download commands.

**Hand a branch to someone as a real install.** `prerelease.yml` is dispatched from `main` with `ref` and `version` (`X.Y.Z-rc.N`) and publishes a pre-release that is never marked latest.
- `validate` refuses bad input before anything is written. Only the repository's owner may dispatch or re-run it, and `release` checks this again because re-running failed jobs skips `validate`.
- `check` and `build` run the branch's code with a read-only token and no mise cache.
- `release` holds the write token and runs none of the branch's code. It verifies the archives, uploads them to a draft, checks that the draft holds exactly those files, and publishes with `gh`. goreleaser's free edition can't publish archives that another job built, so `gh` does it.
- `verify` checks the result, and then `install.sh` and `action.yml` install it on all four targets.

`.goreleaser.yaml` and the release jobs in `release.yml` are unchanged, so normal releases behave exactly as before. `docs/install.md` explains how to install an rc, and the plugin, from its tag, with the known limits.

## Checks

- `mise run check` passes after the last edit (pre-commit hook): 0 lint issues, actionlint and shellcheck clean, all packages `ok`. The test now includes rc pins in `TestInstallScriptPinnedVersion`.
- Trial on the public throwaway repo `eriksaulnier/loupe-prerelease-trial`:
  - `validate` refused, before any write: `v0.99.0-rc.1`, `0.21.0-rc.1`, a missing branch, a dispatch from a non-main branch, and a reused tag.
  - [`0.99.0-rc.2`](https://github.com/eriksaulnier/loupe-prerelease-trial/actions/runs/41954194362) passed every job, including the 8 install jobs.
  - `rc.1` found one bug. `releases/latest` returns 404 when every release is a pre-release, and `verify` treated that as a failure. Fixed in 144aec3.
  - Dispatching `release.yml` through a trial-only trigger opened a 0.22.0 release PR there. The snapshot job ran, and the documented commands downloaded a binary that prints `loupe version 0.22.0-SNAPSHOT-<main head>`.
- goreleaser 2.13.3 run locally covers snapshot naming, the local-tag build with the config kept outside the clone, and rc archive names.
- Two read-only Sonnet reviews ran, and all their findings are fixed. The 144aec3 fix was not reviewed, but the rc.2 run exercised it.
- Automated review: round 1 found 2 issues and round 2 found 1. All were fixed, and round 3 on `5fe6a30` had no findings. With the owner checks in place, [`0.99.0-rc.3`](https://github.com/eriksaulnier/loupe-prerelease-trial) passed all 13 jobs in the trial repo. The refusal of a non-owner is untested, because only the owner account was available.

## Not verified

- The `snapshot` job on a real push to `main`. The trial repo started no push-triggered runs at all, for reasons I didn't find, so the job only ran through a dispatch.
- That release-please ignores the rc tag. I read this in source at 17.6.0 but didn't run it.
- The Pi rc install command.

author: iamenahs
body:
Found by driving the Lead from the phone on a test desk: asking it to start small worker chats, then reading the phone's Sessions list and the Lead's replies.

## Problems → fixes

**A chat the Lead starts is titled "Lead message from …", and the phone says it is "by you".**
- The title is now the first line of the Lead's words. Markdown marks and fences are stripped, and the title is clipped at 200 characters.
- The Lead's instructions and its chat-start tool now say that a new chat's first line is its title: a short task name, then the brief.
- The phone marks a chat as the Lead's ("by <Lead name>") while the Lead directs it. That mark follows the holder, so a take-over makes the chat the person's again.

**The Lead shows chat ids to the person.** It is now told to name a chat, session, run, card or step by what it does, never by its id.

**The Lead can answer a person's message with silence, and Resume then starts the same work twice.**
- What happened: a desk change arrived during the person's turn, and its note ended "stay quiet if nothing needs the person". The Lead started the chat it was asked for, then replied with the quiet marker.
- The message then read as unanswered. Resume re-ran it, and a second identical worker chat started.
- The fix: when a person-owed turn ends quiet, the loop asks once more. The coalesced note and the instructions also say the person is still owed a reply.
- A quiet reply that carries a plan or card already counts as an answer. If the extra request does not complete, the first result stands.

## Tests
- protocol: titles come from the first line, with marks, fences and long lines handled.
- server: the phone says "by Lex" only while the Lead holds the chat.
- lead (681 pass): a quiet person turn gets asked once; an answered turn and a quiet plan proposal get no extra request.
- The plan-proposal test fails without its guard.
- `pnpm check:push --fast` is green.
- Live on a test desk with the phone: the new chat lists as "Add a snake case helper · by Lex", and the Lead names chats by task.

author: michaeldim
body:
## Problem

Log data and calldata are parameter sequences, but they were decoded as one tuple value, which expects a leading offset when any type is dynamic. Anything with a `string`, `bytes` or dynamic array failed to decode.

**`ethcli logs` silently returned no rows for those events, with exit code 0.** On the same range and contract, using ENS `TextChanged(bytes32 indexed node, string indexed indexedKey, string key, string value)`:

| Build | Exit code | Rows |
|---|---|---|
| 0.25.4 | 0 | 0 |
| This branch | 0 | 4 |

Function params in `tx` analysis, event params in `simulate`, and dynamic tuples in `rpc call --decode` had the same bug.

## Changes

- Use `abi_decode_params` at those four sites.
- Unnamed event params get distinct names (`param0`, `param1`) rather than overwriting each other.
- Indexed tuples and fixed arrays return the topic hash, which is all a topic holds, rather than garbage values.
- Struct function params resolve through `components`, so they decode.

## Testing

- New unit tests fail on the old decoding: dynamic event data, dynamic and struct function params. Others cover dynamic tuples in `rpc call`, unnamed params and indexed composites.
- `cargo test -p ethcli --lib --bins` and clippy pass.
- Live: the ENS event above, a static `Transfer` range (still 34 rows), and `rpc call --decode string` (still `"USD Coin"`).

`simulate` has no new test of its own: it's the same one-line change, and I didn't run it live. Dropped rows are logged at debug level only, and I didn't change that here.

body: Adds read-only bounded canonical graph neighbourhood queries using existing Phase 3.1 alignment and Living Health Knowledge Graph contracts. Enforces snapshot tenant boundary, authenticated research draft visibility, public-only approved nodes/edges, and prevents endpoint leakage through hidden nodes. Tests cover research access, draft exclusion, tenant isolation, bounds, and public graph. This is an in-process service; HTTP authentication, persisted Neon read adapter, live ISI ingestion and workbench wiring remain follow-on tasks. No clinical PHI or graph writes. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds a read-only governed graph query service that returns bounded neighbourhood reads from Living Health Knowledge Graph snapshots, enforcing tenant, visibility, and review-state rules before any data is returned. - Only approved public nodes are readable by anyone; governed research and clinician content require matching authenticated roles in the same tenant - Draft and in-review research content is hidden unless a researcher or reviewer explicitly requests it - Traversal is bounded by depth (0–3) and max edges (1–120); overruns are marked truncated instead of returned - Denies cross-tenant access, anonymous research reads, unbounded traversal, and reads from hidden seed nodes HTTP authentication, a persisted Neon read adapter, live ISI ingestion, and workbench wiring remain follow-on tasks. Written for commit 4e82d0614811bc8b398e5c35220e385444d73d29. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by Sourcery Establish a governed foundation for bounded tenant-scoped and public canonical graph reads. New Features: - Add a governed, read-only graph neighbourhood query service with tenant-scoped and public visibility controls. - Support bounded traversals with configurable depth and edge limits, including optional authenticated research draft access. Bug Fixes: - Prevent cross-tenant access, unauthorized draft visibility, and endpoint leakage through hidden graph nodes and relationships. author: myles-coleman
body:
First unit of the SigNoz budget (`26-spec-signoz-retention-budget`, task 1.0).

## What

`manifests/cluster/signoz/values.yaml` (rendered into `helm-chart.yaml`):

- ClickHouse claim **20Gi → 80Gi** (the committed chart still said 20Gi; the live object had been patched to 40Gi, which is the drift this removes).
- `clickhouse.nodeSelector` → `node4`.
- ClickHouse memory limit **3Gi → 6Gi**.

Diff is 6 rendered lines; the render is byte-identical to the committed file before the change, so the diff is exactly the intended edit.

## Why

- 40Gi filled at ~3 GB/day → read-only filesystem → 2.5-day crash loop.
- Merges died at the 2.7GiB ceiling (`Code: 241 MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`) on a 4GB node, so the pod never became Ready, `signoz-clickhouse` had no endpoints, and every `signoz-dashboards/*` plan failed — which is what blocks #33 in `homelab-terraform`.
- `node4` is the node with the RAM headroom (and the freshly added SSD).

## Known gap

The chart exposes no ClickHouse probe knobs (only zookeeper/signoz/otel collectors do), so the 300s startup budget cannot be declared here. If 6Gi + node4 still cannot start inside 300s, spec 26 task 1.3 records the fallbacks; that decision is deliberately not smuggled into a rendered-file edit.

## Verification after merge

ClickHouse schedules on `node4` with the 6Gi limit, reaches `Ready=True`, `signoz-clickhouse` gets an endpoint, and `https://signoz.cowlab.org` returns 200. Then the retention work (task 2.0) can run its TTL inventory.

author: maj0rpain
body:
Closes #2449

## Summary

When a comment object does not parse, `pr comments` and the issue's trusted read now say so: "could not read the comments of ...: its comments did not parse". `pr comments` no longer hand-rolls its read. It goes through the shared `comments_rendered`, and `comments_rendered` and `comments_trusted` now share one option parser, `comments_read`, which also takes a new `--exit 2`.

```
cmd_pr_comments
  comments_rendered --exit 2 adapter_pr_comments "read the comments of PR #n" n text   (was: gh_or_die + comments_render_trusted + bare die2)
comments_trusted  -> comments_read keep   [--exit 2] [--hint h] ...
comments_rendered -> comments_read render [--exit 2] [--hint h] ...
  comments_read: options -> gh_or_die (both) | parse die, render die -> die_hinted (--exit only, never --hint)
issue_json_trusted
  trust-filter die: "...: its comments did not parse"   (merge die unchanged: its input already parsed)
```

## Evidence

- given `adapter_pr_comments` prints `not json`, when `pr comments` runs, then it exits 2 with exactly "orch: could not read the comments of PR #57: its comments did not parse" and leaves the file unchanged.
- given `adapter_issue_json` prints `not json`, when `issue fetch 27 --json` runs, then it exits 1 with exactly "orch: could not read the comments of issue #27: its comments did not parse".
- given `adapter_issue_json` prints `not json`, when `issue comments 24 <file>` runs, then it exits 1 with exactly "orch: could not read the comments of issue #24: its comments did not parse" and the file stays byte-identical.
- given a bundle member whose comments do not parse, when `finding-triage bundle --into` runs, then the parse message carries no `--hint` suffix. The first full run caught this failure ("naming the issue and saying so - expected 'yes', got 'no'"), and it was fixed in 884bc7d2.
- No red run was recorded before the fix: the tests were written together with the code (see Deviations).
- scripts/test/all.sh - pass

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way
**Blast Radius:** `orch:` error wording for unparseable comments on `pr comments`, `issue fetch --json`, `issue comments` and the review pass's known items, plus every caller of `comments_trusted`/`comments_rendered` (finding-triage, ticket, review pass), whose behaviour without `--exit` is unchanged.

## Review

- `scripts/test/orch/issue.sh:1080` - the new `issue comments` parse-failure case repeats coverage the `issue fetch --json` case and the gh-failure untouched-file case already give - the spec's Testing Decisions name this case, so it stays.

## Spec review decisions

None.

## Issue rewrite

Rewrote #2449 from the plan (breakdown: none)

## Merge resolutions

None.

## Spec questions

None.

## Deviations

- #2449: Tests were written together with the code rather than seen failing first, so there is no red run to report; I wrote `changelog.d/2449.md` because the ticket is the spec issue itself.

## Host fallbacks

None (Claude Code).

author: zakisanbaiman
body: ## 概要 / Summary CI の `npm ci` を [Aikido Safe Chain](https://github.com/AikidoSec/safe-chain)（npm パッケージ `@aikidosec/safe-chain`）経由にします。Safe Chain は npm / npx などをラップし、インストール時にマルウェア情報を照合します。トークンは不要です。既定では公開から **48 時間未満のパッケージを入れません**（緊急 CVE 修正で Aikido がマルウェアなしと確認したものは年齢チェックの対象外）。 This routes CI `npm ci` through [Aikido Safe Chain](https://github.com/AikidoSec/safe-chain) (`@aikidosec/safe-chain`). Safe Chain wraps npm and checks installs against its malware feed. No token. By default it refuses packages published less than **48 hours** ago (confirmed malware-free urgent CVE fixes are exempt). このブランチは最新の `main`（`71399d9`、Dependabot #5–#13 を含む）の上にあります。ワークフロー差分は Safe Chain の 2 ステップだけです。 This branch is based on latest `main` (`71399d9`, including Dependabot #5–#13). The workflow diff is only the two Safe Chain steps. ## Dependabot #5–#13 の動作確認 / Did the major bumps break anything? 壊れていません。最新 `main`（`71399d9`）をそのまま checkout し、Node.js 22.23.4 / npm 10.9.9 で次を実行しました。いずれも成功です。この PR では依存関係の修正はしていません。 They did not break the install, tests, or typecheck. Checked out latest `main` (`71399d9`) as-is and ran the following with Node.js 22.23.4 / npm 10.9.9. All passed. This PR does not change dependencies. | コマンド / Command | 結果 / Result | | --- | --- | | `npm ci` | passed（51 packages added, 0 vulnerabilities） | | `npm test` | passed（8 files, 59 tests） | | `npm run typecheck` | passed（`tsc --noEmit`、出力なし） | 確認した major bump: - `typescript` 7.0.2 - `openai` 7.47.0 - `@types/node` 26.6.6 - `tsx` 4.23.15 - `actions/checkout` 7.0.1（`3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1`） - `actions/setup-node` 7.1.0（`949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1`） - `actions/upload-artifact` 7.0.2（`cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9`） - `actions/download-artifact` 8.0.2（`9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333`） - `actions/deploy-pages` 5.0.1（`368f82528645a54fb793d4d04e342629a3f51346`） これらの SHA は `main` のまま残しています。 Those SHAs are kept from `main`. ## 変更内容 / What changed `.github/workflows/daily.yml` の `build` ジョブだけです。`actions/setup-node` のあと、`npm ci` の前に次の 2 ステップを追加しました。 - `npm install -g @aikidosec/safe-chain@1.5.27` - `safe-chain setup-ci`（追加フラグなし） `setup-ci` は `~/.safe-chain/shims` と `~/.safe-chain/bin` を `GITHUB_PATH` に追記します。GitHub Actions はその PATH を**次のステップから**有効にするため、`setup-ci` と `npm ci` は別ステップです。以降の `npm ci` と `npm run generate` はシム経由の npm になります。 npm レジストリで確認した最新版は **1.5.27**（公開 `2026-10-30T08:24:46Z`）です。`package.json` には入れていません。`publish` / `deploy` は依存関係をインストールしないので変更していません。他のワークフローに `npm ci` / `npm install` はありません。ジョブ分割、最小権限、Actions のコミット SHA ピン、CSP、SSRF 制限はそのままです。 Only the `build` job in `.github/workflows/daily.yml` changes. After `actions/setup-node` and before `npm ci`: - `npm install -g @aikidosec/safe-chain@1.5.27` - `safe-chain setup-ci` (no extra flags) `setup-ci` appends `~/.safe-chain/shims` and `~/.safe-chain/bin` to `GITHUB_PATH`. That PATH applies on the **next** step, so setup and `npm ci` are separate steps. Later `npm ci` and `npm run generate` use the shim. Latest on npm is **1.5.27** (published `2026-10-30T08:24:46Z`). Not added to `package.json`. `publish` and `deploy` do not install npm dependencies. No other workflow runs `npm ci` / `npm install`. Job split, least-privilege permissions, SHA-pinned actions, CSP, and SSRF limits are unchanged. Safe Chain 自身のグローバルインストールは、シムができる前の素の npm で行います。バージョンを固定しているのはそのためです。 The global install of Safe Chain itself uses unwrapped npm, because the shim does not exist yet. The version is pinned for that reason. ## 48 時間ルール / 48-hour minimum age `2026-11-05T01:26:29Z` 時点で、現行 `package-lock.json`（Dependabot 取り込み後）の **118** バージョンはすべて公開から 48 時間以上経過しています。`npm ci` は年齢チェックでは落ちません。 一番新しいのは次の 3 つで、公開から約 **57.2 時間**（余裕は約 9 時間）です。 - `vitest@5.1.0`（`2026-11-02T16:12:37Z`） - `@vitest/mocker@5.1.0` - `@vitest/spy@5.1.0` このブランチでも Safe Chain 1.5.27 のシム経由 `npm ci` は成功し、`npm safe-chain-verify` は `OK: Safe-chain works!` でした。 今後、公開から 48 時間未満のバージョンを lockfile に入れると、そのバージョンが 48 時間経つまで CI の `npm ci` は失敗します。 As of `2026-11-05T01:26:29Z`, all **118** locked versions on the post-Dependabot lockfile are older than 48 hours, so the age check does not block `npm ci`. The newest are `vitest@5.1.0`, `@vitest/mocker@5.1.0`, and `@vitest/spy@5.1.0` (published `2026-11-02T16:12:37Z`, about **57.2 hours** old, ~9 hours of margin). On this branch, `npm ci` through the 1.5.27 shim also succeeded, and `npm safe-chain-verify` printed `OK: Safe-chain works!`. A future lockfile pin published less than 48 hours earlier will fail CI `npm ci` until that version ages out. ## 確認方法 / How to verify CI の build ログで次を確認します。 - `Enable Aikido Safe Chain` に `Added shims directory to GITHUB_PATH for GitHub Actions.` - 続く `npm ci` が成功する ローカル再現: ```bash npm install -g @aikidosec/safe-chain@1.5.27 safe-chain setup-ci export PATH="$HOME/.safe-chain/shims:$HOME/.safe-chain/bin:$PATH" command -v npm # ~/.safe-chain/shims/npm npm safe-chain-verify npm ci ``` In the build log, `Enable Aikido Safe Chain` should include `Added shims directory to GITHUB_PATH for GitHub Actions.`, and the following `npm ci` should succeed. ## 戻し方 / How to revert `.github/workflows/daily.yml` から Safe Chain の 2 ステップと直前のコメントを削除します。`package.json` や lockfile の変更はありません。 Remove the two Safe Chain steps and the comment above them from `.github/workflows/daily.yml`. There is no `package.json` or lockfile change.

**Hit tracking (`src/stats.ts`, new)**
- Introduces an in-memory per-code hit counter backed by a `Map`.
- `recordHit(code)` increments the count for a code.
- `statsFor(code)` returns the count for a code, defaulting to `0` when the code has never been hit.
- `topCodes(limit = 10)` returns codes sorted by hit count descending, capped at a default limit of 10.
- Counts live in memory alongside the URL store and reset on restart, which the module documents as acceptable for the demo.

**New endpoints (`src/server.ts`)**
- `GET /stats` — returns `{ top: [...] }` with the highest-traffic codes.
- `GET /stats/:code` — returns `{ code, hits }` for a specific code, reporting `0` for codes with no recorded hits.

**Redirect instrumentation (`src/server.ts`)**
- The existing `GET /:code` handler now calls `recordHit(req.params.code)` after a code resolves successfully, so hits are only counted for codes that exist.
- Unresolved codes still return `404` and are not counted.

## Behavior notes

- Stats are process-local and are not persisted, so all counts are lost on restart.
- The stats routes are registered before the catch-all `/:code` route, so `stats` is not treated as a short code.
- Unknown codes return `hits: 0` rather than an error, and no validation is performed on the requested code format.

## Review findings

The automated review raised one medium-severity item:

- **`src/server.ts:40`** — the hit is recorded before the `301` redirect is issued, so clients that cache the redirect will not re-request the URL and subsequent visits will not be counted, causing undercounting relative to actual usage.

Dá ao MCP autonomia para publicar imagens em contas cPanel, sem o modelo nunca carregar binários.

- Só PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF e AVIF, validados pelos bytes com Pillow (extensão precisa bater com o formato; 40 megapixels no máximo, decompression bomb vira erro).

- ACL `create-user-session` adicionada ao token operator (já feito no WHM e no `bootstrap_upstream_tokens.py`).
- Novas dependências: `pillow>=12,<13` e `python-multipart`.

Canário em `promocaosaborque/public_html/mcptest-images`: lote com os 5 formatos, `verified=true`, repetição recusada com `DESTINATION_EXISTS`, e remoção do diretório com `fileop trash`.

body:
## Summary
Row 4 of #18805 (`docs/specs/SPEC_PANE_MODALS_NOT_WINDOW_MODALS_2026_11_02.md`, decision D4 agreed by AgentX): an agent's request to control a native app was a window prompt shown in every window. It is now a card in that agent's own pane, docked above the composer.

- **`block/desktop-request-card.tsx`:** "<agent> wants to control <app>", the window, what it can do ("see this window, click and type in it; Stop in its pane; everything is logged"), and the same three answers (Don't allow / Allow for this session / Allow for N min). Condition 3 of D4: a warning-coloured frame all round and a tinted ground, so it does not read like a routine card.
- **Condition 1 (operator-only, AgentMux's own text):** the card is drawn only from srv's record (`app:desktop`), and the dock that hosts it is already `data-operator-only`, so an agent's UI query, click and keys never reach it.
- **Condition 2 (waiting for you):** srv raises its attention event for the asking pane while the request waits (the tone, tab badge, Swarm chip and notification), so the card adds no wait of its own (`waits: false`, as the Vault cards). It used to raise it for no pane (an empty `block_id`); this PR passes each request's own pane in `app_api/desktop.rs` and holds one attention per pending request (not only the first), so a second asking pane is signalled too.
- **`desktop-requests.tsx`:** each request with a `block_id` becomes a `paneRequests.push` card (shown in the window that has the pane); it goes when srv's list drops it (answered elsewhere); closing the pane with it open answers No. A request that names no pane is still the window prompt, so nothing is left unasked.
- Spec Progress gets the row 4 line, and records why row 5 (widget install) is not in this PR: `WidgetInstallRequest` has no pane field, though srv knows the asker's pane when it files it.

author: haowjy
body:
## Changelog

- Changed: the growth-plate trace checks (points off the tibia, gaps over the plate, jumps between sections, eroded marks, the width points, ROI-1 cutting through bone) now warn instead of stopping the IIOC and metaphysis steps. The worker either fixes the trace or raises a To check item.
- Removed: `tibia_frame.py --joint-end`. The joint end is the tibia's end that faces the femur.

## Why

#608 set the rule: a script refuses only when it cannot write a valid result. A check that judges the result warns, and the worker decides. This PR applies that rule to the growth-plate trace checks, whose limits were set on a few runs. One of them, the off-tibia check, stops 12 of the 45 lab hand traces (`workflows/mouse-oa/.context/TODO.md`). `--joint-end` had become redundant: after #608 the script used the end it detected over the flag.

## Design decisions

1. **The annotation checks return their sentence, or `None`, and the caller decides what to do with it.** `iioc.py` and `metaphysis_roi.py` warn (`warn_on`). `plate_snap.py` still refuses a snap that breaks a rule the worker's own curves met: the snap is an optional tool, and the worker keeps their curves. This replaces `plate_snap.py`'s `passes()`, which caught `SystemExit` to probe the old refusers.
2. **An empty femur label now refuses in `tibia_frame.py`.** Without the flag, the joint end comes only from where the femur lies.
3. **Still refusing:** `merge_labels.py`'s runaway-track check, since writing that merge would hand a big bone's voxels to a small structure's label. It already has `--max-big-share` as the way past it. It's noted in the TODO. Faces that cross, an empty ROI-3, and grid mismatches also still refuse.

## Walkthrough

### A trace problem no longer stops IIOC

1. Setup: this branch.
2. Run `iioc.py` with a `growth_plate_curves` point off the tibia.
3. Expect: the script writes ROI-1 and its values, and the printed line's `warnings` names the section.

## What changed

- **`annotations.py`:** `refuse_off_tibia`, `refuse_gaps` and `refuse_jumps` become `check_*` functions that return the problem sentence. Adds `warn_on`. `eroded_marks` warns.
- **`iioc.py`:** `refuse_width_points` and `refuse_cut_sides` become `check_*` functions that warn. The calls are wrapped in `warn_on`.
- **`metaphysis_roi.py`:** the calls are wrapped in `warn_on`.
- **`plate_snap.py`:** uses the returned sentences; `passes()` is deleted.
- **`tibia_frame.py`:** `--joint-end` is removed; `check_bone` returns the detected end.
- **Docs:** `oa-protocol.md`, the docstrings, `mouse-oa/.context/TODO.md`, `decisions.md`.

## Risk and where to look

- Breaks or changes: new runs only. A worker that passes `--joint-end` (from an old habit; no doc names it any more) gets an argparse error naming the flag. A live run uses its own workflow snapshot, so it isn't affected.
- Where to look: the `plate_snap.py` condition, `not check(ann…) and (problem := check(new…))`, and every caller of the renamed functions.

## Knowledge layers, docs and deletions

- **Docs:** as listed above.
- **Deleted:** `--joint-end`, `plate_snap.passes`, and the second-pass TODO item.

## Contract changes

None.

## Verification

- Ran: `sh workflows/test.sh` (ruff, then 212 passed); `ruff --fix` sorted the imports.
- Saw: the renamed functions have no callers left under their old names (checked with grep across `workflows/`).

## Left out

- [ ] `merge_labels.py`'s track check: `workflows/mouse-oa/.context/TODO.md`.

## Statement echo

| Source clause | Lean counterpart | Fidelity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Equation (3), rising factorials | `Q`, using `ascPochhammer ℂ` | Literal finite sum, binomial factor, two shifted products and their subtraction. |
| $n\geq3$ | `claim`: natural `n`, `3 ≤ n` | All such indices. |
| $\alpha,\beta>0$ | `claim`: real shifts, strict positivity hypotheses | Arbitrary positive shifts. |
| Nonnegative and nonzero sequence | `claim`: nonnegativity through `n`, one nonzero entry through `n` | The finite input is a function on the naturals. |
| Source zero convention | `claim`: $0<N\leq n$, zeros propagate through `n` | No condition is imposed at $N=0$. |
| Strict log-concavity | `claim`: every $1\leq k<n$ | Natural subtraction in indices. |
| Every root has negative real part | `claim`: complex root implies `z.re < 0` | Strict left half plane, including the zero-polynomial convention of literal universal evaluation. |
| Negation of the assertion | `result` | Exactly `¬ claim`. |

Real coefficients are embedded into the complex numbers. Values of `f`
beyond `n` are unrestricted because they do not enter the finite assertion.
The constructed positive sequence also extends to all natural indices.
These carrier choices add no hypothesis. The private exponent
$(\operatorname{Nat.dist}(k,10))^2$ equals $(k-10)^2+(10-k)^2$
with truncated natural subtraction. The scaled rising factorial uses
Mathlib's `Polynomial.scaleRoots` followed by composition.

## Result and limits

The sole public theorem refutes Conjecture 2 of D. Karp, *Positivity of Toeplitz determinants formed by rising factorial series and properties of related polynomials*, arXiv:1203.1482v1, equation (3) and Conjecture 2, p. 2. The public definitions are the source polynomial `Q` and its literal universal `claim`; all standing input conditions and strict negative-real-part root location are retained.

At n=20, equal shifts 1/t and strictly positive strictly log-concave inputs given by powers of t concentrate at the middle index. The scaled polynomial has a negative derivative-conjugate sign at a rational point in the right half plane when t=0. Continuity preserves the sign for some positive t<1. The logarithmic-derivative root-sum formula then forces a zero with strictly positive real part. The result asserts existence and supplies no explicit finite shift threshold.

Source note: `Library/Asymptotics/karp2012toeplitz.md`, DOI `10.48550/arXiv.1203.1482`; the DOI resolves to the arXiv source. No other Library note owns the source DOI on the searched dev revision. The registered Analytic/S3 module has 336 source lines, `generality: I`, certified-instance utility with `basis=refutes`, and no D5 imports.

The dossier `Problems/karp1203.md` distinguishes all six Triage items:

| Item | Status and evidence |
| --- | --- |
| General-shift assertion | Proved refuted by `result`; its consumed private construction uses n=20, positive strict log-concavity and a right-half-plane root. |
| Concentration mechanism | Kernel-checked private `scaledQ_zero`, `limit_negative`, continuity lemmas, `log_nonneg` and `positive_root_of_negative`. |
| Explicit finite examples | Computed exact Routh counts: n=20, A=1000 and A=10000 give positive coefficients and two right-half-plane zeros; A=100 gives zero. These are not Lean proofs. |
| Uniform family | Open in Lean: all m≥10, explicit shift thresholds and increasing unstable-root counts. |
| Sharpness and repair | Open: minimal degree, sharp shift threshold and hypotheses repairing arbitrary positive shifts. |

author: vroind-ausm-all
body:
Phase 6 nach `docs/MASTERPLAN_V2.md`, damit sind alle sechs Phasen umgesetzt.

Dokumentation:
- Bericht: `docs/BERICHT_PHASE6.md`
- Sicherheit: `docs/SICHERHEITSPRUEFUNG_V18.md`
- Betrieb: `docs/BETRIEB_UND_TEAM.md`

## Datenqualität (neuer Bereich „Datenqualität & System“)
- **Änderungserkennung:**
  - erneut ausgelesenes Impressum gegen die übernommenen Firmendaten (tolerant gegenüber Schreibweisen);
  - neue Website-Bewertung gegen die vorige (Gesamtwert, Rubrikwechsel);
  - Registerbekanntmachungen (Umbenennung, Sitzverlegung, Wechsel der Vertretung, Auflösung).

  Jede Änderung wird zum Prüfpunkt. Übernommen wird nur nach Bestätigung: der alte Beleg wird „veraltet“, der neue „bestätigt“.
- **Wiederkehrende Rechercheaufträge** für Impressen, Websites, Karriereseiten, gespeicherte Lead-Finder-Suchen und die Datenqualitätsprüfung.
  - Sie nutzen nur die bestehenden Module mit deren Schutzmechanismen (SSRF, robots.txt, Rate-Limits, Fair Use, Sperrliste) und kontaktieren niemanden.
  - Ein Hintergrund-Thread führt sie aus; mit `--no-scheduler` lässt er sich abschalten.
- **Veraltungs-Kennzeichen** je Datenart mit einstellbaren Fristen. Es ändert weder Werte noch Prüfstatus.
- **Löschfristen:** abgelaufene Datenschutz-Nachweise werden angezeigt, Löschung nur nach Bestätigung, Löschnachweis ohne Namen.
- **Konfigurierbare Gewichte** der Recherchepriorität (Summe 100, protokolliert).

## Sicherheitsprüfung – behobene Befunde
- **DNS-Rebinding:** Der Host-Header wird jetzt geprüft, unbekannte Hosts bekommen 421.
- **Clickjacking/Referrer:** `frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Frame-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, COOP, `Permissions-Policy`.
- **Robustheit:** Ein JSON-Array oder JSON-String als Anfragekörper führte bei `/api/tasks` und `/api/activities` zu 500 (gefunden vom neuen Fehlertest). Der Körper muss jetzt ein JSON-Objekt sein.
- **Audit-Log:** Ein Widerspruch schrieb den Personennamen ins unveränderbare Audit-Log. Das ist entfernt.
- **Ohne Befund:** keine GET-Seiteneffekte, keine SQL-Injection, kein Pfad-Traversal, keine Geheimnisse im Repository.

## Team-Vorbereitung
- **Login (optional, Standard: aus)** mit den Rollen admin, vertrieb, buchhaltung und lesen.
  - Passwörter mit scrypt; Sitzungs-Cookie `HttpOnly` und `SameSite=Strict`, gespeichert wird nur der Token-Hash.
  - Bremse gegen Fehlversuche; die letzte Administration ist geschützt; Notfallzugang `--reset-login`.
- **Netzwerkbetrieb:** `--host` mit einer anderen Adresse als 127.0.0.1 startet nur mit Login-Pflicht; dazu `--allowed-host` und der Hinweis auf einen TLS-Proxy.
- **Verschlüsselte Sicherung** (AES-256-GCM, optional `cryptography` über `requirements-team.txt`).

## Technik
- Neue Module `quality.py`, `auth.py`, `backup_crypto.py` und `public/quality.js`.
- Schema-Version 17 mit automatischer Sicherung vor der Migration.
- Neue Indizes; `prepare_database()` bündelt Sicherung, Migration und Wiederaufnahme.

## Tests
- **216 Tests grün** (29 neu). Mit Playwright, Chromium und `cryptography` laufen alle 216.
- **Migration** von echten Altdatenbanken, erzeugt mit dem Code von v0.9, v1.2 und v1.6 aus dem Git-Verlauf: Daten erhalten, GoBD-Schutz aktiv, Integritätsprüfung ok.
- **Last:** 1.000 Firmen; 8 parallele Schreiber plus 3 Leser ohne Fehler.
- **Fehlertest:** alle Routen × 4 Methoden × 7 fehlerhafte Anfragekörper ohne einen einzigen 500. Dazu Seiteneffekt-Test aller GET-Routen.
- **Klickdurchlauf in Chromium:** Änderung übernehmen, Personendaten löschen, Auftrag ausführen, Gewichte ändern, verschlüsselte Sicherung, Admin anlegen, Login-Pflicht, Anmeldedialog, Abmelden, Mobilansicht.
- **Nicht getestet:** wiederkehrende Aufträge gegen echte Websites (in den Tests ohne Netzwerk), Dauerbetrieb des Schedulers, Team-Betrieb hinter einem echten TLS-Proxy.

body: ## Summary `TC-TT-017.spec.ts` ("No access to a project") has intermittently failed in CI with `element(s) not found` on `getByRole('button', { name: 'Request sent' }).toBeDisabled()`. It is a documented recurring flake (issues #6107, with repeat occurrences on PRs #6364, #6709, and a 2026-11-02 follow-up from PR #8341), always correlated with the same CI shard position (12-14/15) shared by other independently-documented CI-load flakes in this repo (TC-WF-006, TC-DOCUMENTS-013/015/017). The component logic that retains the "Request sent" acknowledgement across a same-scope organization-bootstrap reload is already correct and extensively covered by `page.accessRequest.test.tsx` (20+ jsdom cases, including "retains the acknowledgement throughout a same-scope organization bootstrap"). That reload is a normal event on every real login, not just the spec's explicit `delayedScope`/`freshSession` scenarios — and its round-trip can occasionally exceed Playwright's **implicit default** assertion timeout under CI load, even though the eventual UI state is correct. Every other network-dependent assertion in this same spec file already carries an explicit `{ timeout: 30_000 }` (e.g. the "no access" state visibility check, the access-request POST wait). The two "Request sent" `toBeDisabled()` checks were the only ones left on the implicit default — this PR aligns them with the rest of the file's own convention. - Files to change: `packages/core/src/modules/staff/__integration__/TC-TT-017.spec.ts` — add `{ timeout: 30_000 }` to both `toBeDisabled()` assertions on the "Request sent" button. - No production code changes. ## Test plan - [x] Full validation gate run locally: `build:packages` → `generate` → `build:packages` → `i18n:check-sync` → `i18n:check-usage` → `typecheck` (42/42 packages) → `test` (50/51 workspaces; the sole failure, `create-mercato-app#test`, is the pre-existing local-only oracle-timeout flake that also fails on a clean checkout of the base branch — not caused by this change) → `build:app`, all green. - [ ] The Playwright integration spec itself could not be executed in this environment (no live app/DB/browser provisioned) — the next CI run against this branch is the real confirmation. If the underlying cause is CI-shard resource contention rather than this specific timing margin, the test may still occasionally fail; this change does not regress anything either way.    - Access: everyone
   - Roles: `reviewer` for the Ganymede Reviewer group, `admin` for the Ganymede Admin group
2. On this branch, run `cd secrets && agenix -e krater-env.age` and set `KRATER_WEAVE_CLIENT_SECRET`.
3. In `jaspermayone/infra` `tailscale/policy.hujson`, give `tag:patchwork-krater` access to `pw-skein:5432` again. The grant and test lines are in #32's body.
4. Merge this PR, then set `enable = true` in `hosts/weft/krater-production.nix`.
5. Deploy skein, which creates the `krater` role. Then deploy weft and run `systemctl start krater-prod-build` on it.
6. Merge the DNS PR for `krater` and `krater-storage` (patchworklabsorg/dns), then bump `patchwork-infra` in `jaspermayone/infra` and deploy alastor.
7. Check `https://krater.patchworklabs.org/healthz` and `/healthz/worker` return 200. Add outside uptime checks on both, every 5 minutes. The worker can't report its own death.

author: gdlinlin13
body:
## What this does
**Company users sign in with a username, and email becomes optional.**
- The login page asks for **company code + username + password**.
- Supabase Auth still needs an email for every login, so each username gets a hidden internal address: `<companycode>.<username>@users.quantivra.app`, built in `src/utils/loginEmail.ts`. It is never shown or emailed.
- Logins created earlier with an email can still type that email.
- The Create Company wizard and both Users pages now ask for a **Username** (required; 3–32 lowercase letters, numbers, `.`, `_` or `-`) and an **Email (optional)** for contact. User lists show the username.
- The server function builds the login from company code + username. Usernames are unique within a company, and a contact email is checked if one is given.
- Trade-off: people without a real email can't get a password-reset email. An admin resets their password instead.

**Timezone follows the country.**
- In the wizard, picking a country fills in its currency and timezone. Both stay editable.
- Timezone, in the wizard and in company Settings, is now a searchable dropdown of every timezone with its UTC offset.

## Database: migration `017_usernames.sql`
**It must be run before this is merged.** It:
- adds `company_users.username` (unique per company, with a format check),
- makes `email` nullable,
- makes the sign-in lookup also return the username.

Migration 011 can now be re-run safely after later migrations. The security test runner applies every migration from 011 onward twice, and stops loudly if any of them fails.

## Testing
- `npm test`: all 169 tests pass, including new tests for usernames, the server function and timezones (every country pack's default timezone is in the list).

author: yegamble
body:
## Failure mode closed

`importOneVideo` carried the web-video **original** only on a video's first import. After a `media-mode=none` run, or a run whose source store wasn't reachable, the video ledger says `done`, and no later copy or reference run ever revisited it. HLS, captions, posters, storyboards and avatars all have backfill passes; the original did not. On the SizeTube 8.3.1 snapshot that is 1,928 progressive files (~58 GB) that a metadata-first migration would strand for good.

## Change

- `carryOriginal` (new `entities_originals.go`): the existing copy/reference decision, moved verbatim out of `importOneVideo`, so the two callers can't disagree.
- New `original files` pass right after `videos`. For each imported video without a `kind='original'` row it carries the top web-video file and records a `video_file` ledger row (keyed by source UUID).
  - It only fills: a video that already has an original is recorded `done` and left alone, and that ledger row keeps a later deletion here from being undone.
  - An unplayable type is recorded `unsupported`. No source store means nothing is recorded, so a later run retries.
- No SQL, migration or API change. The pass reuses `GetVideoFileByKind` and `ImportInsertVideoFile`.

## Verification

TDD: `TestPeerTubeImportBackfillsOriginalAfterMetadataOnlyRun` (metadata-only run, then a copy run on the same destination, then a third run) was added first and failed (`originals backfilled = 0`). With the pass disabled it still fails, and with it enabled it passes. Existing tests already assert exactly one original after a single copy or reference run, so same-run duplication is covered.

```
go test -tags=integration -count=1 ./internal/peertubeimport/     (Postgres 18, local)
ok  	github.com/vidra/vidra-core/internal/peertubeimport	56.200s
make quality            → Staticcheck all four tag worlds: pass
go test -race -count=1 ./internal/peertubeimport/...  → ok 1.812s
```

Full local `make ci` could not complete: the Mac's disk is full (`no space left on device` during `test-race`). The required CI lanes run the full gate.

Not in scope: the dry-run plan still counts originals per video in the first-import loop, so it doesn't preview backfill counts.

Companion: #517 (holds MFA-enrolled source accounts).

author: tang3cko
body:
Cuts the crates a build compiles from 22 to 18 by dropping what caim does not need.

- **JSON output removed** (breaking): `caim --json`, `caim list --json` and the JSON concurrency holder records were the only uses of serde_json, which brought serde_json, itoa and zmij. The plain output already ends each task with one `[<task>] exit=N (reason)` line; no known caller reads the events. A holder record is now one tab-separated line (pid, task, mode, start time, checkout last).
- **toml without its writer**: caim only reads TOML, so `default-features = false` with `std`, `parse` and `serde` leaves toml_writer out.

toml and serde stay: every crate in the lockfile was checked before this change. Each `.crate` matches `Cargo.lock` and the crates.io index, its contents match the upstream commit its version tag points at, none is yanked, and the two RustSec advisories on record (hashbrown, regex) were fixed in versions older than the ones used.

Tests that read JSON now check the plain output and stderr instead. Verification: `./caim check` on macOS and `./caim linux --task check` pass.

author: lu9di
body:
## Objetivo

Reduzir a memória do servico `filtra-indice` (Render Free, 512 MB) sem tocar em dados, conteudo, SEO ou arquitetura.

## Mudanca

`indice/next.config.mjs`: `cacheMaxMemorySize: 8 * 1024 * 1024` (padrao do Next: 50 MB).

O cache ISR em disco continua sendo a fonte das paginas; o limite so define quanto HTML renderizado fica retido em RAM por instancia.

## Evidencia

Medicao local com `indice/scripts/diagnose-memory.mjs --br 700 --us 700`, `.next/cache` apagado nos dois ensaios (condicao identica, 1.400 paginas de detalhe renderizadas a frio):

| Metrica | 50 MB (padrao) | 8 MB | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pico BR (700) | 391,8 MiB | 324,1 MiB | -67,7 MiB (-17,3%) |
| Pico BR+EUA (1.400) | 460,9 MiB | 375,7 MiB | -85,2 MiB (-18,5%) |
| Plato final | 447,1 MiB | 374,3 MiB | -72,8 MiB (-16,3%) |
| p50 BR / EUA | 92 / 41 ms | 96 / 36 ms | +4 / -5 ms |
| p95 BR / EUA | 364 / 168 ms | 802 / 99 ms | cauda do BR piora |

Sem vazamento: o RSS estabiliza e cai no repouso nos dois ensaios.

Custo do modelo de dados, isolado com `scripts/diagnose-memory-data.mjs`: BR stats 34,5 MiB + ranking BR 5,9 MiB + EUA 3,7 MiB + lastmod 7,3 MiB (~51 MiB). O modelo nao explica os ~500 MB de producao; o runtime do Next e o cache ISR explicam.

## Bug corrigido no diagnostico

`diagnose-memory.mjs` usava a sigla do estado nas URLs dos EUA (`/indice/us/al/...`) em vez do slug (`/indice/us/alabama/...`): todas as requisicoes dos EUA respondiam 404 e nada era medido. Agora os caminhos vem das mesmas regras do sitemap, ha `--br N`/`--us N`, p50/p95 por fase e o script falha em qualquer status >= 400.

## Validacao

- `npm test`: 89/89
- `npm run typecheck`: ok
- `npm run build`: ok
- `npm run test:seo`: ok (43.920 URLs indexaveis, todas no sitemap)
- `npm run sitemaps:static:check`: artefato integro, 43.920 URLs em 5 shards
- `npm run audit:indexability`: ok

## Risco e rollback

Opcao de runtime do Next: nao altera build, sitemap, conteudo, status HTTP nem `revalidate`. Rollback = remover a linha e redeployar.

Efeito em producao precisa ser confirmado no painel (Render -> Indice -> Metrics -> Memory) nas primeiras 24 h; esperado cair de 487-507 MB para ~400-430 MB no pico.

## Fora deste PR

`docs/RENDER_DEPLOY_HEALTH_HORAS_2026-11-04.md` documenta o que depende de painel: health check `/api/live` na API, cache de build, horas gratuitas do workspace e conferencia de DDL/conexoes no Supabase. Nenhuma dessas acoes foi executada (sem acesso ao painel).

author: ashdamle
body:
## The defect

Delegate worktrees were destroyed the instant a job reached a terminal state, and **never destroyed at all** when a job failed. Net retention was **0 s on success, unbounded on failure.**

**Success path — reclaimed before `done` was observable.** `finalize_delegate_worktree` ran `git worktree remove --force` unconditionally from inside `_assemble_delegate_execution_result` (`delegate_router.py:572`), while `finish_delegate_job(state=terminal_state)` was written only afterwards (`:596`). The tree was gone before `state=done` ever existed, so **no consumer waiting for `done` could win the race** to read the patch back. That is the structural cause of the repeated honestreview hand-back losses — the surviving ones survived by luck.

**Failure path — no reaper existed.** `prune_delegate_jobs` deletes DB *rows* only; `reap_terminal_codex_sessions` reaps *codex sessions* only. Nothing reclaimed the directories. Measured leak at the time of diagnosis: **30 directories, 597 MB, oldest 2026-10-31.**

The defect demonstrated itself twice while this fix was being collected: both dispatches' own worktrees came back `retained: False` (`tmp98j23zpz`, `tmpbsotctxp`), because `spendguard delegate` is served from the installed build and so cannot yet be governed by this branch.

## The fix — a retention floor with a scheduled ceiling

`delegate_worktrees.py`:

- `DELEGATE_WORKTREE_RETENTION_S` (default 1500 s) and `DELEGATE_WORKTREE_ORPHAN_GRACE_S` (2×) read from config via `config._cfg_get`, with named defaults — no magic number at any call site.
- `schedule_delegate_worktree_reclaim` stamps `reclaim_not_before` into the worktree sidecar **instead of** removing the tree. The failure path in `run_isolated_delegate` stamps the same deadline, so every outcome — accepted, terminal-failed, or exception — gets the same inspectable window.
- `reclaim_expired_delegate_worktrees` is the new reaper. Sidecar deadlines are authoritative; journal-less directories fall back to mtime vs the longer orphan grace, because no authoritative deadline survived. It returns `{"reclaimed", "retained", "gaps"}`, removes **only** via `git worktree remove --force` (never `rm -rf`), and records anything it cannot resolve as a **named gap** rather than skipping it silently.

Wiring, deliberately with no new surface and no new scheduler:

- Opportunistic sweep in `create_delegate_job`.
- Scheduled ceiling in `execution_journal.reap_execution_codex_sessions`, which the already-installed `com.spendguard.codex-orphan-reap` launchd job drives — **no new plist.**
- `reclaim_not_before` surfaces on both `delegate --status` and `delegate --collect` for free, because `_delegate_job_workspace_details` (`delegate_jobs.py:239-242`) already projects the sidecar into `read_delegate_job` *and* `read_delegate_job_result` — **no capability-registry entry, SSOT conformance gate untouched.**

The TTL is a **floor**; the reap cadence sets the ceiling. Both are documented at the call sites.

## Review defects found and repaired before this was pushed

A four-axis audit of the first draft found four candidates; three were real.

- **A — the opportunistic sweep was `except Exception: pass`.** Containment is correct (a reaper failure must never break a dispatch), but the bare `pass` made a permanently broken reaper invisible forever, which is exactly what CLAUDE.md's *"never silently absent"* forbids. Now reports through `config.warn_once` carrying the exception text — the sink these modules **already** use for contained delegate failures (`cancel_delegate_job` calls it at `delegate_jobs.py:349`, `:358`, `:371`; the parallel reap precedent is `codex_daemon.py:136`). No new channel, no new file.
- **B — the scheduled path was uncontained,** so a worktree-reclaim failure would have broken codex *session* reaping, which worked before this change. Contained the same way, with the same message, and `return reap_terminal_codex_sessions(**dependencies)` still runs and still returns.
- **C — `_schedule_accepted_delegate_workspace_reclaim` had become a false name:** it is now called from the failure paths too. Renamed `_schedule_terminal_delegate_workspace_reclaim` (inner closure likewise `persist_terminal_delegate_envelope`). Verified: **1 definition repo-wide** at `delegate_router.py:454`, 7 reference sites, and **zero** remaining matches for the old name anywhere, comments and docstrings included.
- **D — the sidecar glob's depth was challenged and adjudicated NOT a defect.** `_persist_delegate_workspace_metadata` writes to `delegate_worktree_metadata_path(durable_execution_payload_paths(execution_id)["envelope"])`, whose parent is `_durable_execution_directory(execution_id)` = `root / execution_id` — exactly one level, so `glob("*/worktree.json")` is right and widening it would be wrong. A comment now records the one residual nuance: warm paths may set an alternate `current_durable_execution_root()`, so a warm sidecar can sit outside the globbed root; such a tree falls to the orphan branch and is reclaimed by mtime after the 2× grace — **a longer floor, never a silent never-reclaim.**

## Tests

`tests/test_delegate_worktree_retention.py` — seven tests, all wired into the `__main__` block (this suite runs each test file as a subprocess, so a file without that block is dead in CI, collected and passing vacuously):

1. Opportunistic sweep failure is **observable** and does not break job creation — asserts the job is created *and* that the exception text reached the sink. Asserting only "it did not raise" would have been satisfied by the bare `pass`.
2. Scheduled sweep failure is observable **and** session reaping still runs and returns its value.
3. A failed isolated delegate stamps the reclaim deadline.
4. A tree inside its floor is retained; the same tree past the deadline is reclaimed.
5. Orphan age and unresolved trees are visible as named gaps.
6. The retention window is config-driven.
7. Both job channels project `reclaim_not_before`.

Every clock is injected — **no `time.sleep` anywhere**; deadlines are passed in, never waited for. Every value with a real-world meaning is a named constant.

The three existing tests that asserted the old behaviour were **inverted, not weakened**: `retained is False` → `retained is True` **plus** a new assertion that `reclaim_not_before` is set, with explicit `git worktree remove --force` cleanup added so the fixtures no longer rely on the production path destroying their trees. Every pre-existing assertion (patch contents, primary-checkout cleanliness, persisted-equals-returned) is kept.

## Verification

Whole chunked suite (the default, not `--sequential`) under the gated interpreter, with `PYTHONPATH` pinned to this worktree so the import is proven to be this code:

- Resolved `spendguard.__file__` → `/Users/ashdamle/Documents/claude/sg-worktree-retention-ttl/src/spendguard/__init__.py`
- `spendguard doctor` → `ENFORCING HERE: 🟢 YES`
- **Pre-repair baseline: 824 passed, 0 failed, exit 0.**
- **Post-repair: 824 passed, 0 failed, exit 0** — identical, so the A/B/C repair is attributable rather than guessed at. Both historically-flaky isolated-pip-build tests (`test_catalog_ssot_enforcement`, `test_install_hook_end_to_end`) passed in both runs.
- honestreview precommit judges ran over the commit and passed.

## Note

This branch cannot fix hand-back for the *currently installed* `spendguard delegate`, which is served from a stale build (`v0.16.28-45-gfbb39b50`). The retention floor governs dispatches only once this lands and is reinstalled.

Cost: `real $0.00 = $0.13 API + $0.00 Remote :: est sub value $0.03` — the code was written by codex on its own subscription; the API line is honestreview's precommit judging, not this feature.

body:
Spec 109 Part B, PR 3 of 3. Crash recovery keeps copies and discarded sessions on disk; without this they would be hidden data.

**Settings → Crash recovery** (encrypted vaults only) lists what's kept, with date and size.
- **Restore** a copy: confirmed. The copy is authenticated first, this session is sealed, that seal is kept as a copy, and only then does the chosen copy go in place. It can be undone the same way. The dialog says it can bring back deleted data and shorten the audit trail. The vault locks and returns to the unlock screen.
- **Delete** a copy or a discarded session: confirmed and permanent, by an id that can only name a recovery item. A recovered session can't delete the copy that is its own way back.
- Discarded sessions can be listed and deleted, not opened.

**Fixed before this push, from independent code review**
- A failed restore could leave the session bound to the wrong seal, and a restore followed by a crash could silently undo itself.
- The three-copy limit could delete the chosen copy before it was in place.
- Restore left the user on Settings with no way to unlock.

**Limits**
- Only the three newest copies and stale sessions are kept. Unverifiable sessions stay until deleted.
- Restore has no anti-rollback protection. It is a deliberate user action, stated in the dialog.

**Verification:** `tsc` and `npm test` pass locally. Rust and the new native journey `encrypted-vault-restore-a-kept-copy` first run in this PR's CI.

author: huanglininn
body:
Closes #1408

## What and why

On Windows, OpenIDE sent `setBreakpoints` with forward-slash source paths (`D:/work/xxxController.cs`). netcoredbg accepts the request but keeps the breakpoint at `verified: false`, so the session never stops on it — even though the module event already reports `Symbols loaded.`. The same path written with backslashes binds immediately.

`adapter_path` normalized Windows separators for `java-debug` only. This sends Windows `netcoredbg` sessions through the same helper (renamed `java_source_path` → `windows_source_path`), records the adapter → editor path mapping, and maps `stackTrace` paths back in `client_path` so frames still open the editor path.

The reported difference, same DLL and same adapter, only the separator changes:

```
{"source": {"name": "xxxController.cs", "path": "D:/work/xxxController.cs"}, ...}
  -> {"verified": false}

{"source": {"name": "xxxController.cs", "path": "D:\\work\\xxxController.cs"}, ...}
  -> {"verified": true}   and stops on line 26 when the action is hit
```

## How it was verified

- `cargo test -p ide-dap --lib` — 45 passed, 1 ignored (`kotlin_official_release_ten_no_delay_runs`, needs the official Kotlin adapter).
- New test `netcoredbg_windows_source_paths_round_trip` fails before the fix (`left: "D:/work/xxxController.cs"`, `right: "D:\\work\\xxxController.cs"`) and passes after it. It also checks that `stackTrace` returns the editor path again.
- `cargo clippy -p ide-dap --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean. `cargo fmt -p ide-dap -- --check` — clean.
- `cargo build --release -p openidea --features tauri/custom-protocol` — builds.
- Reproduced the reported flow on Windows in the built app: a breakpoint on `xxxController.cs:26` verifies and stops on the HTTP request; the module event still shows `Symbols loaded.`.

Sibling sweep: `adapter_path`/`client_path` are the only places that translate source paths. The java-debug case keeps its behaviour, the Godot and Kotlin mirror branches are untouched, and the new branch is gated by `cfg!(windows) && adapter == "netcoredbg"`, so macOS/Linux and every other adapter are unchanged. UNC paths (`\\server\share`) are covered by the existing `is_windows_source_path` check.

What could break: `stackTrace` paths for .NET now go through the adapter → editor map first. When the adapter returns a path OpenIDE never sent, the lookup returns `None` and the path is used as returned — the same fallback as before.

Not verified: non-Windows platforms; no .NET session was available there. Upgrading netcoredbg does not help, which is why the fix belongs here: 3.2.0 shows the same behaviour with a forward-slash path and binds with a backslash path, so the separator is what the adapter is missing.

## Review focus

`client_path` keeps the java-only fallback, and the mapping is keyed by the separator-normalized path that was actually sent, so a later `stackTrace` for the same file round-trips instead of loading a duplicate.

author: kentbull
body:
Locksmith disabled derived registry issuance for group issuers, leaving those issuers unable to establish shared state-opening keys with a holder through the wallet.

Enable group issuer → individual holder issuance using KERIpy's existing group thresholds, DH owner and encrypted Keeper. Members review and approve the exact Grant and public DH query separately. Only the elected custodian retains the issuer root; signing does not copy it to other members. The accepted BUP reaches the holder, whose credential admission remains a separate decision.

## Background

The adapter preserves the original Grant, coordinator and deadline. Cancellation and vault closure abandon unfinished authority; reopening does not resume the agreement. Group-holder coordination follows separately.

This cohesive change exceeds 500 changed lines because it includes the protocol adapter, its existing worker/UI integration and one real two-member regression. Read `group_dh.py` first, then `auxiliary.py`, Registry setup and the focused test. The test follows explicit RIP, Grant, query and BUP approvals through holder Admit without mocks.

author: dexhunter
body:
## TL;DR

- Speeds up the SM3 message expansion `_expand` in `src/dtk/signing/native/sm3.py`, used by every A-Bogus signature.
- It reads the 16 words with one `struct.unpack` call and writes the fixed rotations as plain shifts.
- Benchmark (A-Bogus signing test workload, timed in alternating runs on one isolated core): 477.96 ms -> 432.51 ms, 9.5% faster.
- The signing, worker, MCP and download tests pass unchanged: 469 passed, 72 skipped.

Refs #820

## What & Why

Before, `_expand` called `_rotl` four times for each of the 52 new words.
Each call did a modulo, two shifts and a mask.
It also decoded the 16 input words with 16 separate `int.from_bytes` calls.

Now the 16 words come from one `struct.unpack(">16I", block)` call.
The 15, 23 and 7 bit rotations are written as shift pairs, with one 32-bit mask per new word.
W' uses `map(operator.xor, ...)` because both inputs are already 32-bit words.
The recurrence follows GB/T 32905 line by line, so the digests stay byte for byte the same.

## Results

Median of 5 runs on one isolated CPU core, CPython 3.12.

| Situation | Before | After | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_expand` on one 64-byte block | 45.12 us | 28.78 us | 36.2% faster |
| `sm3_hash` of a 64-byte message | 320.04 us | 288.07 us | 10.0% faster |
| `sm3_hash` of a 4 KB message | 10.97 ms | 9.73 ms | 11.3% faster |
| `ABogus.get_value` for one detail query | 1.81 ms | 1.65 ms | 8.7% faster |
| `XBogus.sign` (does not use SM3) | 93.94 us | 93.17 us | no change |

## Why this is safe and easy to maintain

The change touches only the body of `_expand` and adds two standard-library imports.
The code still reads as the published recurrence, with one comment for P1.
`tests/unit/test_signing.py` checks the SM3 test vectors and pinned A-Bogus signatures, and it passes unchanged.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/unit/test_signing.py tests/unit/test_worker.py tests/unit/test_mcp.py tests/integration/test_api_downloads.py`: 469 passed, 72 skipped (no PostgreSQL or Redis here).
- `pytest tests/unit`: 7 failed and 2 errors in `test_public_endpoints.py` and `test_demo.py`. The base commit gives the same result on this machine.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `mypy` pass on `sm3.py`.
- The whole-workload timing above was repeated three times; the after/before time ratios were 0.876, 0.905 and 0.909.
- Short reproduction: `python -m timeit -s "from dtk.signing.native.sm3 import _expand; b = bytes(range(64))" "_expand(b)"`.

## Checklist / 自查

- [x] `make fmt` — `ruff format --check` passes on the changed file
- [ ] `make lint && make type` — ruff and mypy ran on `sm3.py` only, not the full targets
- [ ] `make test` — not run in full; see the test results above
- [ ] `(cd web && npm run verify)` — not needed, `web/` is untouched
- [ ] documentation in `documents/en/` and `documents/zh/` — not needed, no user-visible change
- [x] none of: CJK in source, a hex colour outside the tokens file, literal prose in JSX, a `TODO`, a `.env`, a fixture with a real cookie
- [x] no key, password, cookie or API key in the diff or in this description

## AI assistance

Candidate versions of `_expand` were generated by Codex (gpt-6.1-sol) and tracked with Weco Observe.
An automated benchmark and the test suite picked this version.
The patch and this description were prepared with Claude Code.

Weco share link: https://dashboard.weco.ai/share/oWDDyyuZD5m5xWKltHRlzPjHwgTllBzW

author: yotamleo
body:
## What

Only the worker merges (merge-on-green.sh), and the chief only writes the GO file. So a worker that goes silent after READY leaves a GO'd PR unmerged. That happened to PR 4689 on 2026-11-04, and the operator merged it by hand.

The new chief-kit helper `scripts/handover/chief-kit/silent-go-merge.sh` runs on each chief-wait sample. It merges a worker's PR only when all of the following hold:

- the worker's newest marker bullet is `READY <pr> <head> GREEN`, or all of these hold:
  - its last bullet is a hand-off, not a negated mention such as "no handoff possible";
  - no HALTED, BLOCKED, PARKED-*, WRAPPED or MERGED marker is newer than its newest READY;
  - that READY names the PR;
- the GO file `<GO root>/.locks/go/<pr>.<head>` exists and carries `head=<head>`;
- neither the worker doc nor the GO file has been written for `CHIEF_WAIT_WORKER_SILENT_MIN` minutes (default 45, the same bound as the waiter's worker-silent check);
- no process carries the doc's stem in its argv. A hand-off waives this check. An unreadable process table counts as alive. If the worker is alive and only quiet, it sends one alert and does not merge;
- `ready-check.sh <pr> <head>` passes when re-run at the GO head;
- `TRUST-PATH: no`, or `TRUST-PATH: yes` with a `trust-reviewed=` line in the GO file;
- the waiter runs from a himmel checkout root.

Then it runs the bare relative `bash scripts/handover/merge-on-green.sh <pr> [--jira-transition] --worker-doc <doc> --go <GO file>`, bounded by `CHIEF_SILENT_GO_TIMEOUT`, so merge-on-green and its GO verification stay the authority. The worker doc's `completes-ticket:` line decides `--jira-transition`.

Every merge, failed merge or refusal sends one operator page and writes one chief-doc bullet: `SILENT-WORKER-MERGE`, `SILENT-WORKER-MERGE-FAILED` or `SILENT-WORKER-HELD reason=...`. Each fires once per (worker, PR, head, outcome), keyed in `<inbox>.wait.silentgo`. chief-wait.sh wakes as `WAKE silent-go`. The waiter doc section explains it, and the dev graph's chief-wait coverage lists the new wake.

This follows the chief's ruling on the design:

author: stdmaru
body:
Step 5 of ServerManager (roadmap, Phase 3): servers on other machines over SSH (T30).

## What changed
- **Profile `hosts`**: `name`, `destination` (host, user@host, or a `~/.ssh/config` Host), remote `x2ctl` path, optional `ssh` command. A server with `host` is remote.
- **Default ssh command** (`DefaultSshCommand`): `ssh -T -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=10`, plus on Linux `ControlMaster=auto`, `ControlPath=<control dir>/ssh-%C`, `ControlPersist=60`. Windows OpenSSH has no ControlMaster.
- **Remote servers are attached, never started**: they are the host's services, so they do not depend on the ssh link. If one is not running, it fails with `could not attach on <host>`, and the ssh/x2ctl message is in its log.
- **Discovery**: `Discover()` lists local sockets now and runs `x2ctl list` per host in the background, collected by `Update()`. Results are in `Listed(i)` and `HostAt(h)`.
- **Stop of a listed but unattached server**: attaches, then sends the protocol stop, so the shutdown is logged. This covers `x2ctl stop` without a separate path.
- `TransportEvent::error` marks stderr lines.
- The probe prints discovery results and no longer waits for "all ready" once a server has failed.

## Checklist
- [x] Profile parsing/validation and the x2ctl/ssh command line (tests)
- [x] Orchestrator through `x2_fake_ssh`: discovery, attach, detach, stop of a listed server, unreachable host, server not running
- [x] Real ssh to localhost with the default command (ControlMaster): discovery, ordered attach, failure message, reverse stop, exit 0
- [x] Docs: ServerManager (remote servers), roadmap
- [x] Linux Clang debug: no warnings, ctest 9/9
- [x] GCC: affected targets, no warnings, servermanager tests
- [x] Windows test machine (clang-cl): 9/9, no warnings
