author: delano
body:
Custyard could not read Bunny Database aliases or use its documented v2 SQL protocol. Add explicit provider selection, required/conflicting credential checks, interactive-session preflight, guarded transactions and primary-routed standalone statements. Existing Turso keeps v3 behavior; Bunny callers use Ecto transaction APIs rather than raw transaction-control SQL.

Complete runtime portability with mounted file-volume identity checks before Repo access, deliberate initialization, provider-specific client IP/scheme handling and Bunny origin authentication before Phoenix sockets/static/routes. Add maintenance-only, checksum-verified file backup/restore and interrupted-restore protection. Backup and restore share a 16 MiB manifest limit, and configured roots are expanded before overlap checks.

Add separate Fly staging configuration, explicit secrets-file targeting and manual digest-based promotion. The workflow verifies OCI metadata/source and requires the candidate digest to match an immutable publication record from the exact successful main CI run attempt with both database lanes, serializes environments, requires production protection/acceptance and checks the previous Bunny digest. Private GHCR content is mirrored to Fly with digest preservation. The narrow Bunny updater sends only image fields and suppresses provider response/error contents. Setup instructions and a validation/finding record accompany the implementation.

Upgrade Ecto 3.14.2 to 3.14.3 and require the patched minimum for CVE-2026-118391, which otherwise blocks the security gate. Follows #61.

## Validation

- Final-head follow-up: 11 file-volume tests and 22 Python promotion tests passed, with exact-cap/over-cap manifests, equivalent/nested paths, publication digest matching, run attempts, later rebuilds, corrupt archives and credential-free redirects covered.
- Warnings-as-errors compilation, repository formatting, strict Credo, actionlint and whitespace checks passed. The CI record writer produced the expected JSON with isolated dummy inputs. All 13 local links/fences in the two changed guides passed; the new GitHub rerun reference was verified separately.
- Earlier full local baselines: SQLite 3,088 tests (0 failures, 48 skipped); Bunny v2 against native local libSQL 3,088 tests (0 failures, 49 skipped). Production assets/release, SQLite/Turso release smoke tests, Sobelow, Hex/dependency audits, ShellCheck, shell/TOML/JSON and original documentation checks passed.
- Final-head CI passed on `b3ad4d53e2ff3533b81bb433bde7ae5809d5f030`: 3,090 tests in each SQLite, Turso v3 and local Bunny v2 lane, zero failures (2 SQLite skips; 49 in each remote-driver lane). Container runtime smoke, release, security, CodeQL and both Claude/Greptile review gates passed. All three actionable review threads are resolved. CI and review evidence: https://github.com/custyard/custyard/actions/runs/41968862277 and https://github.com/custyard/custyard/actions/runs/41968862196.

- Post-merge main CI passed on `e9130c4ce0d9d09b20bf9edcbb7e6c61ac38f96d` and published `ghcr.io/custyard/custyard@sha256:5588c4721bcba512da7c4973057f49305349b91f6af694ea13b334da346276c1`. Read-only validation accepted the real CI publication record and GHCR OCI metadata and rejected a different digest. Main CI/publication: https://github.com/custyard/custyard/actions/runs/41969401038/attempts/1. This check made no Bunny API or database requests.

## Acceptance boundary

The local Docker daemon is unavailable; Linux container CI successfully built and loaded the image and checked real volume ownership/identity/recovery, entrypoint startup, origin protection, HTTPS and graceful shutdown. Image publication is intentionally skipped on PRs and occurs after successful main CI.

Live managed-Bunny acceptance checks are disabled at the user's request. No credentials are required for this review; keep managed checks disabled until explicitly re-enabled. Local libSQL v2 and isolated container CI remain enabled. Production setup, live CDN/LiveView/mail acceptance and a recovery rehearsal are separate future deployment work. See docs/ops/bunny-setup.md and docs/ops/bunny-portability-validation.md.

author: big-cookie
body:
Fixes the setup sheet's lie — "Could not reach your agent" — and the request that never left the phone (#430).

## What was wrong

The sheet reported a network failure while the gateway logged **no inbound request at all**. The request never left the device: the setup turn was being sent on a client that was not the active profile's, and every failure on the way down — an unconfigured profile, a missing key, a client that could not be built — was collapsed into one sentence about the network.

## The four commits

1. **The setup turn goes on the active profile's client.** This is the cause. The turn was built from the default client rather than the profile the user had just configured, so the connection that had been verified was not the connection the turn used.
2. **The failure's cause is kept and shown.** The setup path stops discarding the exception's reason; the sheet says which failure it hit.
3. **The reason is scrubbed before display.** A failure message can carry a URL, a token or a hostname. What is shown is the *kind* of failure, never the raw text.
4. **An unconfigured send is a stated cause, not "not set up yet".** The empty-configuration case is named as itself rather than being folded into a vaguer message.

## What the user sees now

A setup that fails says what failed. "Could not reach your agent" only appears when the request was actually sent and nothing answered — which is the only case where that sentence is true.

## Verification

- A test that a request which is never sent cannot produce the network message.
- A test that the shown reason carries no URL, host, key or path.
- The device case from #430: a verified connection that fails setup now reports the real cause instead of blaming the network.

`gate.sh` green; skill claims re-anchored.

author: tomitoivio
body:
Phase 1 of #1152: a **writing worksheet**, not a rules engine and not a decoder.

There was no canonical home for dream scenes — only legacy material from the earlier game — so `docs/campaign/DREAMS.md` is now the single one, indexed beside campaign 01 and linked from its memory/revelation section.

## The rules that matter

- **Provenance is never labelled.** A dream can be private, shared, astral, Time/Space, telepathic, precognitive or nothing at all. The moment a scene is stamped *"astral projection"*, the player stops interpreting and starts reading a map.
- **No PSI prerequisite.** A character with no psychic ability at all can have an involuntary astral dream — and that dream grants nothing: no daytime telepathy, no voluntary travel, no evidence, no solved case.
- **Dream Helsinki is dream geography**, never a claim about real tunnels under the University.
- **Dream actions are scene-bound**, and **precognition is a lead, never a proof**.
- **Spoiler discipline per act**, so Act I cannot confirm anything.

Prose-led throughout, a place to write in every section, two worked examples marked .

## The guard

It counts dream documents and fails on a second one, refuses code fences and field names in the author's file, and checks the ambiguity rule, the no-PSI-prerequisite rule and the investigation boundary are still there.

One existing guard needed a **fix** rather than a workaround: the campaign test counted every file in  as an outline, so it now names the companion worksheet instead of miscounting it.

**76 tests.** Phase 2 is Tomi's, nothing here is implemented, and **#1152 stays open**.

body:
Plan 207: cash handling safety record (two-person count and safe/till note)

Scope: One cash-handling record per count (date, amount, counted by, witnessed by, safe or till location). It records the count and custody only: it counts no denominations itself and it moves no money. Checked first: the denomination count (Plan 4), the cash-in-hand limit (Plan 90), and the collector settlement statement (Plan 129) — none of them records who counted the cash, who witnessed it, and where it was kept, so this module adds only that missing piece and never reads or rewrites any of their records.

Acceptance:
- Each record names two people (counter and witness) and a location; a count with only one person is flagged, not refused, so the gap stays visible until a witness is named. A witness who is the counter is flagged too, and a missing location is flagged separately.
- A record's amount is compared against the day sheet figure the caller supplies for that date; the comparison reports matched or a signed mismatch and never rewrites either figure. A missing day sheet figure leaves the record unchecked, never matched.
- Recording a count never changes any payment, handover, cash-in-hand, denomination, or settlement figure by itself. There is no edit function — a record is recorded or removed — and duplicate ids are never rewritten.

What was built:
- New pure, import-free module cash-handling.js (store shahdara_cash_handling_v1 in app.js wiring): strict YYYY-MM-DD dates via a days-in-month table (no clock object, so the purity fence holds), unknown fields dropped, inputs never mutated.
- Minimal wiring only (app.js + import, store, render function and render call; index.html +1 SHOP & OWNER panel after the payment-reminder panel): record form (date, amount, counted by, witnessed by, safe/till location, note), remove, filter by counter and location, flagged-counts list, day-sheet comparison, Export CSV.

Verification:
- node --check passed on cash-handling.js and app.js.
- New tests: 20 — half-formed refusal, strict dates (leap years, 31-day months), unknown-field drop, duplicate-id rules, find/remove, sorting, date/counter/location filters, single-person flagging (missing and same-person witness), no-location flag, day-sheet match/mismatch/unchecked, summary text, record text, HTML escaping, CSV + filename, non-mutation, list normalization, purity fence, panel-id presence, app.js wiring, deployment guard. Focused run: 20 pass.
- Full unit gate after npm ci: 9,887 pass / 0 fail / 9,887 tests (572 files) — Plan 206 baseline 9,867 + 20, an exact match.
- Build gate: passed.
- Playwright e2e: not run locally (no browsers in a bare VM); CI e2e will run on the PR.
- No test waived, no golden test changed, no build budget loosened.
- Remote-branch verification: all four remote blob SHAs verified matching local files by reading back each blob from the branch (cash-handling.js, test file, app.js, index.html).

Limitations: the panel wiring is verified by pure-module tests plus code review, not by a DOM test of the panel view itself (same precedent as Plans 6-206). Counters, witnesses, locations, and amounts are only as true as what the operator types; the module verifies format and ordering, not truth.

author: regibyte
body:
## Problem

`npm run test:page-boot` failed on CI's Linux runners in about 5 of the last 32 runs of main with "the unfolded floor counts no drafts, not the one kept", and passed on a rerun.

## Cause: a lost click, not the drafts count

- **Every failing run took the page's ~1.3 s draw plus exactly the check's 15 s deadline.** So the tray never appeared at all. It did not appear empty and then fill late. The tray draws nothing for an empty collection, but the board carried the draft in every run I read (diagnostic below).
- **The page rewrote the sidebar's floors (`floors.innerHTML = …`) on every render**, even when the HTML was the same.
- **About 100 ms after the first draw it always renders that same sidebar again**, from the first board's `tower.store` write echoing back and from the next board.
- **A repaint between the mouse press and its release replaces the button under the pointer**, so Chrome fires no `click`. The floor stays folded and the tray never draws.
- **The check clicks within 50 ms of the first draw**, right in that window. On a slower runner its press and release straddle the repaint.

The bug is real for users too: any click held across a board that changed nothing in the sidebar was lost.

Evidence (headless Chrome, a tower alone):
- Without a click, `#floors` is written at about 280 ms, 280 ms and 380 ms after load, and the last write is identical to the one before it.
- A forced repaint between press and release: no `click` event, the floor stays folded, the tray never draws. That is the CI failure exactly.
- A 100 ms press right after the first draw, before the fix: **1/10** unfolded. After: **10/10** (also 10/10 at 300 ms). The driver's instant press: 10/10 both ways.
- On GitHub's ubuntu runners, through a throwaway diagnostic branch (since deleted): 248 runs of the boot passed, including 8 jobs that replayed CI's whole sequence first. At ~15 % per CI run, that the flake didn't show isn't surprising: an instant press seldom straddles the repaint. Every run's board carried the draft (`drafts: 1`), which rules out the collections watch and the fold.

Ruled out:
- **The check reading too early.** It already waits for the tray to exist, and the tray never existed.
- **The tray drawn before its data.** It mounts with the count it has, and it updates.
- **A late collections scan or fold.** Items are scanned before the first board, and the board carried the draft.
- **Chrome CPU throttling** (6×, 20×) and 8-way concurrency locally: 0 failures in 68 runs.

## Fix

1. `fix: a board that changes nothing in the sidebar keeps its controls`
   - The floors are painted through `paintOnce`, which now returns whether it wrote. No caller used its return value before.
   - A render that writes nothing calls the new `rows.refresh(root)`, which updates the tray rows where they stand. A row whose pick changed is mounted afresh in its place.
   - kb `ui-model` says so.
2. `fix: the page-boot check says when a click on the floor's sign left it folded`. A lost click now reads as itself, not as a drafts count.

No fixed sleep anywhere.

**Scope: no-op renders only.** A render that does change the sidebar's HTML still replaces the whole list, so a press held across it is still lost. That covers a status word, a lamp, a new card, or a fading subagent's `animation-delay`, which changes on every render while one fades. With busy workers that is common. For the same reason, this check could flake again if a board after boot ever changes something the sidebar draws. The real cure is patching each floor, or each row, by key, so a press survives a render that changes other rows; kept as a follow-up draft (`mossy-dahlia`, which also covers the board strip).

## The `processes: Error: linux …` traces

They don't matter for this failure. `scanProcesses` throws on plain Linux, and `loggedRead` logs the error and keeps the last (empty) read. They appear in passing runs just the same, and they touch neither collections nor the sidebar. Follow-up proposed: say an unsupported platform once rather than every 5 s, or have `tower-alone` not observe the machine. Not done here.

## What was run

- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm test` (663/663)
- `npm run tower3d`, `npm run test:tower3d-boot`, `npm run test:page-boot`
- `kb.mjs verify` (0 errors; `--since origin/main`: no suspects)
- `git status` clean afterwards

On a sandbox, in WebKit (`tool:webkit`):
- Clicks on the floor's sign fold and unfold it.
- With the floor open, a draft added on disk moved the tray from 2 to 3 with **zero** writes to `#floors` (the refresh path).
- Not run: Tower.app itself, and the board strip (`board.strip` repaints the same way, so it could lose a click too; worth the same change in a follow-up).

![The lab floor open, its tray at 3 in drafts after a refresh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RegiByte/the-tower/pr-assets/pr-413/webkit-tray-refreshed.png)

author: wiatrek-kevin-s
body:
Step 2 of the registry plan (design set, section 10). **Stacked on #1**: it targets `registry-operations`. Merge #1 first; GitHub then retargets this one to `main`.

## What's added

**Harvested implementations, 1,040 of them.** Each engine describes its own tools and `harvest/` turns that into `implementations/<software>/<id>.yaml`:

| Engine | Version | From | Tools |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GDAL | 3.13.3 | `gdal --json-usage` | 117 |
| PDAL | 2.10.2 | `pdal --drivers/--options --showjson` | 136 |
| PostGIS | 3.7.0 | the database catalogue (`pg_proc`), every overload | 335 + 146 raster |
| Shapely | 2.2.0 | introspection | 143 |
| GeoPandas | 1.2.0 | introspection (own methods only) | 163 |

Facts only (names, types, defaults, choices, ranges, overloads); no engine help text. Re-running a harvester on the same version reproduces the files byte for byte.

**Mappings, 39 files.** `mappings/<software>/<id>.yaml` holds what a person knows: which operation a tool implements, a crosswalk for each parameter (including `fixed` when the engine always behaves one way, `#N` for unnamed SQL arguments, `pass: values`), `presets`, differences and effects. 38 implementations are mapped to 16 of the 17 operations; `gdal vector dissolve` gets a warning instead, because despite its name it is not Dissolve. All `draft` until a person reviews them.

**Validation** checks each crosswalk against both sides (the operation's parameters, the engine's harvested ones) and reports a mapping whose tool disappeared or whose parameter was renamed after a re-harvest.

**Equivalence tests** (`checks/equivalence.py`) run every mapped GDAL, Shapely, GeoPandas and PostGIS tool on the same small inputs, translated through its crosswalk, and compare the results. Locally: **29 runs pass, 0 fail, 9 skipped** for documented differences (no engine's buffer dissolves in the same call; `ST_MakePoint` sets no CRS; `ST_Union`/`union_all` need grouping first). A deliberately wrong crosswalk fails.

**Engines workflow**: runs the equivalence tests on PRs touching mappings, harvesters or operations, and every Monday re-harvests the newest conda-forge releases and opens a PR with what changed.

## Compatibility

`checks/index_compat.py` passes against `main` and against #1. The tables Columbus reads are untouched; implementations live in their own tables (whose final layout is now in #1, so this PR only adds rows).

## Not in this PR

- DuckDB spatial: its extension downloads from extensions.duckdb.org at run time, which the build machine could not reach; it will be added and tested in CI.
- Raster equivalence cases (slope, aspect, hillshade, zonal statistics, clip/reproject raster) need raster fixtures; next.
- ArcGIS Pro, QGIS, GRASS, WhiteboxTools harvesters (step 3).

## Needs a repository setting

The weekly re-harvest opens pull requests with the built-in token. GitHub allows that only when **Settings → Actions → General → "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests"** is on. If it is off, the job fails at that step and nothing else is affected.

author: fizzbeom
body:
The DKIM signer encodes `domainName` for the `d=` tag with the bundled RFC 3492 codec (`punycode.toASCII`), while address headers go through `normalizeDomain()`, which applies UTS-46 mapping through `url.domainToASCII` first. For a domain with an upper case or mapped non-ASCII code point the two disagree, so the signature names a different domain than the one in `From:`:

| domainName | d= before | From: domain / d= after |
|---|---|---|
| `JÕGEVA.EE` | `xn--JGEVA-voa.EE` | `xn--jgeva-dua.ee` |
| `compa\u00ADny.com` | `xn--company-pka.com` | `company.com` |
| `ﬁnance.example` | `xn--nance-td82a.example` | `finance.example` |

`xn--JGEVA-voa` encodes an upper case U+00D5, which is a different label from `xn--jgeva-dua` (U+00F5) even after DNS case folding, so a verifier looks up the selector under a domain that does not exist and DMARC alignment with `From:` fails. Lower case input such as `jõgeva.ee` is not affected.

The change moves `normalizeDomain()` (and the two helpers it needs) from `mime-node` to `shared` without modifying it, since `mime-node` only has a default export, and uses it on the lower cased value for `d=`. The control char and delimiter stripping in `generateDKIMHeader()` is unchanged and still runs first.

Tests: a new case in `test/dkim/sign-test.ts` covers the rows above plus `NODE.EE`; it fails on master and passes with the change. The existing DKIM and mime-node tests pass, `npm run lint` and `test/package/cjs-smoke.cjs` pass. On my Windows machine 8 tests in `mail-composer-test.ts`, `permission-model-test.ts` and `types-consumer-test.ts` fail with and without this change, so they look environment related.

body:
Medal art for the quest system, plus the scripts that build it. This PR only adds art and tools; the web app does not use the medals yet.

## What's in it

- `frontend/public/badges/`: 44 medals, 512px WebP with transparent backgrounds, named `<quest>_<level>.webp` (for example `fire_10.webp`, `podium_vodka_2000.webp`).
- `tools/badges/frames/`: 15 empty frames made with an AI image model (5 shapes × bronze/silver/gold). The centre is generated black and tinted per quest in code, so every quest reuses these 15.
- `tools/badges/poses/`: 11 new mascot poses. Each one was made by giving the model the real art from `frontend/public/tiers/*.webp` as a reference, so the faces match the originals.
- `tools/badges/build_all.py`: rebuilds every medal without calling any API. It tints the centre, turns the mascot into embossed metal, adds the number plate, and engraves the Thai quest name on gold banners. The quest table, thresholds and colours are in this file.

## Look

- Themed after the club logo: black and hot pink, the queen-cat crown, shuttlecock feathers and rackets.
- Shape shows the category: circle = streak or cumulative, shield = skill, rounded square = friends, star = monthly, diamond = secret (shows "?" until unlocked).
- Higher tiers add more parts: silver adds a feather wreath; gold adds a sunburst, a pink/black bow, the crown and a banner.
- The centre colour follows the tier colour of the mascot (`TIER_CARD`).

## Choices made without a spec

These are easy to change in `build_all.py`:

- บ่มมานาน (aged) 300 uses the gold frame with a brand-pink centre.
- ล้างแค้น (revenge) has two levels: 1 is silver, 3 is gold.
- ขึ้นแท่น (podium) has one medal per ELO tier. The plate shows that tier's starting ELO, and the metal is bronze for Milk–Highball, silver for Wine–Whisky and gold for Vodka–Absinthe.
- The star (cat) and diamond (secret) medals have no number for now.

## How to rebuild

```bash
python3 -I tools/badges/build_all.py
```

No API key is needed to rebuild. Regenerating a frame or a pose calls a paid model (`OPENAI_API_KEY` / `GEMINI_API_KEY`) and costs about ฿1.8 per frame and ฿4.5 per pose. `tools/badges/README.md` has the details.

[VXG RealForever]

## Purpose

Preserve one future VexBoard horizon discovered while the Screen Lens/source-projector foundation is still stabilizing, without widening that active acceptance boundary or granting implementation authority.

This capture keeps the idea in two rightful VexWork surfaces:

- `projects/vexboard/SEMANTIC-BLUEPRINT-IDE-FOUNDATION.md` — architecture/design expression;
- `work.vexboard.source-projectors.temporal-reversible-projection` — durable parked Work identity.

## Preserved expression

The horizon is:

```text
exact historical/current/candidate source revision
-> source facts
-> accepted architecture relationship semantics
-> normalized source-derived relationship graph
-> VexBoard projections

desired Origin / UX
-> intended semantic relationships + explicit UNBOUND edges
-> compare with current relationship graph
-> identify missing / incompatible connective tissue
-> candidate source under rightful source authority
-> regenerate relationship graph
-> compare ACTUAL candidate projection with DESIRED projection
```

It preserves these distinctions:

- HISTORICAL / CURRENT / DESIRED / CANDIDATE are different projection states around stable identities.
- Family / State / Control / Act / Effect / Projection and typed Port / Connection coordinates may provide machine-readable joins where current source actually establishes them.
- construction/lifetime, provider/store, observation/reconciliation, convergence/Relay, history and proof remain separate ownership questions.

- semantic reversibility is not source-authority reversibility.

author: benvanik
body:
The AMD GPU completion worker held the retirement mutex while polling native completion words. A caller waiting for one queue could therefore be prevented from retiring its already-completed work while the worker polled another queue. Release that ownership during observation so independent completion helpers can make progress, while preserving the lifetime of every observed word.

## Completion ownership

Source callbacks still run under the existing mutex and remain authoritative for completion, resource retirement, and public semaphore signaling. Polling observes cached coherent words outside that mutex; a changed word only requests another authoritative drain.

The cached hints belong to the worker. Helpers obtain and discard their own hints, so a helper cannot change the snapshot the worker is reading. The backing lifetime follows the source:

- **AQL:** retain the existing native signal before unlocking. A helper may retire the submission, but its signal cannot be recycled or trimmed until the observer releases its reference.
- **PM4 and SDMA:** completion words belong to the queue. Source removal joins observation before the queue can release that backing.
- **Source replacement:** request replacement through the existing state word, wait for the last observer outside the drain mutex, then acquire the mutex to join callbacks and swap the table. Stop retains its synchronous worker join.

Atomic admission into observation closes the race between retaining a hint and a concurrent replacement request. The observation bit protects borrowed memory; it does not exclude completion helpers.

## Cost and measured behavior

The source entry grows from 32 to 40 bytes on 64-bit builds: 16 additional bytes per reserved source across the two existing membership tables. Each armed AQL hint acquires and releases one existing reference per observation interval. Poll iterations perform coherent loads without reference updates or native calls. There is no new per-submission storage, allocation site, worker, or GPU command.

The comparison uses the same public HIP workloads on an MI300X, interleaving baseline and changed builds with fixed iteration counts and five repetitions per process. Both retain the existing 100 µs worker observation budget. Enqueue timings exclude final completion; end-to-end timings include it. Values are medians of process medians.

| Operation | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Foreground dispatch during registered 64 MiB downloads | 95.184 µs | **47.409 µs** |
| Process CPU per foreground operation in that workload | 115.187 µs | **62.030 µs** |
| Foreground dispatch during pageable 64 MiB downloads | 30.427 µs | 29.598 µs |
| Registered background download throughput | 53.478 GB/s | 52.760 GB/s |
| Pageable background download throughput | 15.437 GB/s | 15.869 GB/s |
| Direct dispatch enqueue | 1.357 µs | 1.351 µs |
| 4,096-dispatch graph enqueue | 4.246 µs | 4.307 µs |
| 4,096-dispatch graph end to end | 6.439 ms | 6.480 ms |

The large-graph completion ranges overlap: 6.427–6.482 ms before and 6.479–6.481 ms after. Warm host-allocation counters remain zero for direct submissions and recorded command buffers with up to 5,000 dispatches.

The concurrent-copy rows above use HIP's Auto wait policy. With the existing Spin policy held constant across a separate comparison, registered-copy foreground latency falls from 91.858 to 17.057 µs; background throughput is 53.824 versus 51.071 GB/s. This demonstrates that an active waiter can now help retirement while the worker observes other work. It does not establish an inference-serving gain: asynchronous request completion uses a different waiting path. Wait-policy defaults are unchanged.

## Lifetime coverage

Tests use the real signal pool to exercise helper progress during observation, replacement followed by immediate trim, stop and failure, and repeated reuse of a single signal cell without growing capacity. Existing queue-owned-word and native-event cases cover the other backing contracts.

## Reviewer Notes

The key boundary is `completion_begin_observation` through `completion_end_observation`: signal references and the source table must remain live until the final read, while the retirement mutex stays available to helpers. Review `completion_set_sources` alongside that boundary; its replacement request must prevent a new observer from entering between the reader join and the table swap.

author: sunkenintime
body:
![Hermitcraft's shopping district on the map at dusk: the day picture eases into a moonlit night while lamp-lit streets keep a warm glow](https://codex-file-host.shawnadedeji.workers.dev/files/diorama-204-night/9cbdc25da941-hermit-dusk.gif)

![The same view by day (top) and at night (bottom)](https://codex-file-host.shawnadedeji.workers.dev/files/diorama-204-night/b8c13fe7174a-hermit-day-night.png)

*Hermitcraft's shopping district on the RTX 4070, 26.3, as the world's clock runs from 11,500 to 14,000 ticks. World: Hermitcraft Season 10 by the Hermits.*

Night on the map, for [#204](https://github.com/SunkenInTime/diorama/issues/204): the map and minimap get dark at night like the world does, and torches, lamps and lava light them up. Before this, the sky view was always a daytime picture.

## What a player sees

- **Look → Day and night: World time** (the default) follows the world's clock: the map eases into night at dusk and back at dawn, darker in storms, as vanilla's sky does. **Always day** and **Always night** pin it.
- Night is the day picture tinted toward moonlight, with a warm glow wherever block light falls (Dara's pick "E" of five looks, chosen on a comparison page of real Hermitcraft tiles). The fog and the clouds over unexplored land ([#265](https://github.com/SunkenInTime/diorama/pull/265)) dim with it, and so do Create contraptions.
- Caves, the Nether and the End don't change: caves and the Nether are lit by the game's own light already, and the End's sky never moves. Another dimension's saved map, browsed from the map screen, shows by day.
- **Image export** has a **Night** checkbox, off by default; the preview shows what it will save.
- Maps made before this update have no light stored, so their lamps stay dark at night until drawn again. In singleplayer the save fill draws everything the map had once more, in the background, on the main map and sub-maps alike. On servers they light up as the player revisits.

Xaero's World Map is the precedent: its Lighting option (on by default) follows the world's clock, it stores block light per pixel in its region files, and its export has a Nighttime checkbox, off by default. It dims to plain grey; Dara picked a moonlit look with brighter lamps. JourneyMap stores a whole second night picture per region and switches between them; this stores only the light.

## How it works

The day picture already holds the sun's light, so night only needs the block light. Each sky view tile keeps one value per block, 128 x 128 a tile: the block light where the tile's pixels landed. At night a shader multiplies the day colour by moonlight plus a warm glow from that light. Nothing is baked twice and no second picture is stored.

- **Baking.** The tracer records the block light in front of the face each sample hits (a lamp's own light where that's brighter), and each block's pixels are averaged into one value. The GPU baker does the same: the mesher passes the light per face, the bake shader writes it, the composite averages it into the overlay texture's green channel (now RG8), and both backends read it back. The save fill now reads block light from region files for the sky view too.
- **Storage.** An `LIT1` block after the spots (or an overview's chunks) in the `.omt` file, 16 KB before compression, mostly zeros. Overview tiles shrink their children's light as they do their pixels. Older Diorama versions stop reading before it. No new folder: the picture is unchanged, so old tiles keep their place and pick up light when baked again.
- **Drawing.** By day nothing changes: same pipelines, same draws. At night a tile with no light anywhere (most of the wilderness) draws with the usual pipeline and a moonlight tint in its vertex colour. A tile with light draws through a new `tile_night` shader with its light texture as a second sampler, on every version path (the fog's way of taking two textures). Crisp and averaged sampling both carry over.
- **Keeping it current.** A block light change re-bakes and re-saves the sky view where it can show: a section change, or a server light packet's block light sections, reaching the chunk's lowest visible surface. Torches deep in a mine don't.
- **Old maps.** `saved-chunks.bin` moves to `DSC2`. Reading a `DSC1` file in a sky view with a night marks every chunk it had drawn (from the save or live) to be drawn once more. The fill draws those even where it otherwise doesn't fill in (sub-maps, filling turned off), and only those.

## Cost

Frame time, median frame in ms (fps), median of two runs each, measured before master gained the clouds (#265; by day this branch draws exactly what master draws, and at night the clouds only take a tint in their last line, in a layer that already redraws every tick), Hermitcraft's shopping district, the world frozen and nothing baking, every run starting from the same saved map. Master → this branch by day → this branch at night:

| Machine, setting | Master | Branch, day | Branch, night |
|---|---|---|---|
| **RTX 4070**, map open, close (4 px a block) | 10.5 ms (95) | 10.2 ms (98): same | 10.6 ms (94): same |
| RTX 4070, map open, 1 px a block | 10.6 ms (95) | 10.2 ms (98): same | 10.3 ms (97): same |
| RTX 4070, map open, far (0.25 px a block) | 10.1 ms (99) | 9.8 ms (102): same | 9.8 ms (102): same |
| RTX 4070, minimap only | 9.0 ms (111) | 8.8 ms (114): same | 8.7 ms (114): same |
| **No GPU** (boat VM, Mesa llvmpipe), map open, close | 646 ms | 341 ms: same | 602 ms: same |
| No GPU, map open, 1 px a block | 672 ms | 345 ms: same | 573 ms: same |
| No GPU, map open, far | 622 ms | 459 ms: same | 481 ms: same |
| No GPU, minimap only | 534 ms | 601 ms: same | 345 ms: same |

"Same" on the RTX: inside the runs' own spread (worst frames 26.8 ms master, 37.0 ms one branch-by-day run, 28.2 ms night). On the software renderer most of each frame is vanilla drawing the world behind the map, and the same build varies by up to 2x from one run to the next (branch by day ran 229 to 454 ms on one setting); by day the branch issues exactly master's draw calls, so those gaps are noise, not cost, in either direction.

- **Disk:** +0.70% on the map filled around the shopping district, Hermitcraft's most lit area (72 tile files: the 40 with light add about 2.7 KB each, the 32 without about 70 bytes).
- **Baking:** the tracer's tile time is the same (680 ms master, 562-696 ms branch on this PC; 443-500 vs 480-578 ms on the boat VM, within its noise).
- **Old maps:** the one-time redraw costs what a fresh fill from the save does; not measured separately here.

## Ground truth

- New `day-night` game test, passing on boat on 26.3, 1.21.1, 1.20.1, 26.3-neoforge and 1.20.1-forge, beside `saved-chunks`, `image-export` and `tile-filter`. It builds a floating platform with glowstone and a torch and checks light beside the glowstone and none in a far corner, on the tile and in the saved file, that the tile gets a light texture, screenshots by day, at night and at midnight on World time, then takes the platform out of the world, rewrites the fill's progress as from before this update, drops the tile's light, and checks the fill draws it again with its light and writes the new progress.
- The same test with GPU baking forced on, on the RTX 4070: 26.3 (Blaze backend) and 1.21.1 (GL backend), both with "GPU baking matches the tracer", so the GPU's light readback holds on both backends. That run caught a real bug here: the composite pipeline still declared its second target as R8, so GPU baking would have switched itself off on 26.2+; fixed in this PR.
- All 23 nodes compile (main and game tests), after merging master with #265, #276, #277 and #279 in.
- Astra reviewed: underground light packets re-baked the sky view (fixed), old maps on sub-maps or with filling off would never relight (fixed), and the old-tile test didn't go through the migration (rewritten as above). Greptile: the RG8 mismatch (fixed) and night

author: justin17553-boop
body:
Audit de sécurité de la nuit du 5 novembre 2026, fait avec le skill d'audit de Cloudflare, recopié dans le dépôt cette nuit. Les correctifs ont été relus par l'agent `gardien`, et son constat bloquant est corrigé.

⚠️ **Cette demande touche `server/` : la fusionner déploie le VPS.**

## Ce qui change
- **`/api/sendmail`, mode avancé (C1, fuite par requête vers des adresses internes).** Avant ce correctif, n'importe quelle entreprise cliente pouvait faire joindre au serveur une adresse interne (127.0.0.1, réseau privé, métadonnées de l'hébergeur). L'erreur renvoyait alors la bannière du service joint, et un port fermé se trahissait par `ECONNREFUSED`. Le nouveau `server/hote-public.js` :
  - résout tout hôte par `dns.lookup`, littéral compris ;
  - déplie l'IPv6 et la juge sur liste blanche : seulement `2000::/3`, sans `2001:db8::/32`, Teredo ni 6to4 ;
  - refuse les adresses de la machine elle-même ;
  - se connecte à l'adresse normalisée, avec le nom en `tls.servername`, pour que le certificat soit toujours vérifié.

  Les ports sont limités à 25, 465, 587 et 2525. L'erreur renvoyée est un message à nous et le code nodemailer, jamais le texte du serveur joint.
- **`/api/devis/generer` (C2).** Un anonyme vidait le quota commun de 100 devis par jour avec le nom de l'espace bêta, qui est écrit en clair dans `beta.html`. Trois bornes sont ajoutées :
  - 60 devis par heure et par adresse (`req.ip`) ;
  - 50 par jour et par entreprise (`anthropic.quotaEquipeJour`) ;
  - une réserve de la bêta hors du quota commun (`anthropic.quotaBeta`, 40 par défaut).

  La place réservée est toujours rendue, même si le modèle ou la consigne échoue.
- **Skill `security-audit`** (Cloudflare, MIT) recopié dans `.claude/skills/`, avec `LICENSE-cloudflare`, `PROVENANCE-cloudflare.md` et un bloc « Adaptation TeamOP ». Le scan SkillSpector donne « DO_NOT_INSTALL ». Ses 14 constats ont été relus en contexte : ce sont tous des faux positifs de mots-clés (de la méthode d'audit, et les fixtures de test non recopiées). Les deux validateurs `.cjs` n'utilisent que `fs`, `path` et `util`.

## Preuves
- `test-3281` : 76 ✓. Il joue le vrai serveur isolé, et résout par le vrai `dns.lookup` 18 littéraux piégés (`012.0.0.1`, `0:0:0:0:0:ffff:7f00:1`, `::7f00:1`, `fec0::1`, `0x7f.0.0.1`…). Contre-épreuves :

  | Mutation | Résultat |
  |---|---|
  | liste blanche IPv6 retirée | 57 ✓ 19 ✗ |
  | connexion sur le nom au lieu de l'adresse | 75 ✓ 1 ✗ |
  | port libre | 75 ✓ 1 ✗ |
  | réserve bêta retirée (passe de l'auteur) | 46 ✓ 5 ✗ |
- Autres bancs, tous verts : 2692 (91), 2980 (77), 2981 (26), 2982 (64), 2983 (31), 726 (144), 3140 (91), 3239 (11), 3255 (48), 3258 (9).
- Fournisseurs de messagerie vérifiés avec `hotePublic` : OVH (`ssl0`, `smtp.mail`, `pro1`), Gmail, Office 365, Outlook, Orange, Free, SFR, Yahoo, IONOS, Gandi. Tous sont acceptés sur leur adresse publique.
- TLS (relecture de `gardien`, faux serveur avec certificat) : 465 et 587 passent avec le bon nom ; un mauvais nom ou l'absence de `servername` est refusé.

## Reste à décider (Justin)
- **D1 — `/api/espaces/lien`** : un anonyme qui connaît `t` peut poser `clePerimee`. Il faut choisir une politique.
- **D2 — `/api/compte/identifiants`** : la route envoie un courriel sur la seule foi du `teamId`. La fermer demande que `app.html` envoie `x-teamop-kh`.

author: jieunsse
body:
## 배경

대시보드 아래 「마감 목록」은 다섯 묶음을 세로로 쌓고, 머리줄을 눌러 접고 펼쳤어요. 접힌 묶음이 세로로 길게 늘어서서 한눈에 보기 불편했어요.

## 의도

전체 보기에서 다섯 묶음을 가로로 나란히 놓아, 화면을 내리지 않고도 묶음마다 급한 티켓을 볼 수 있게 해요. 묶음 전체는 지금 쓰는 표로 그대로 볼 수 있게 남겨요.

## 구현

- 묶음마다 카드 하나를 둬요. 넓은 화면에서는 「기한 지남」과 「오늘」 카드가 위 줄을 반씩 차지하고, 「이번 주」, 「그 뒤」, 「기한 없음」 카드가 아래 줄을 3분의 1씩 차지해요. 태블릿은 두 줄, 휴대폰은 한 줄로 놓여요.
- 카드 한 줄에는 번호, 제목, 담당자 프로필, 기한 칩이 들어가요. 제목이 길면 말줄임으로 잘라요. 담당자 이름은 프로필에 마우스를 올리면 보여요.
- 카드에는 5건까지 보여요. 5건이 넘으면 「n건 더 보기」, 5건 이하면 「전체 보기」 버튼을 둬요.
- 0건인 카드는 「없어요」만 보여 주고, 다른 카드보다 낮게 놓여요. 누를 곳은 없어요.
- 카드 머리줄이나 아래 버튼을 누르면 그 묶음이 선택돼요. 그러면 카드 대신 그 묶음의 티켓 전부가 표로 보여요. 위쪽 탭이나 숫자 칸으로 골랐을 때와 같은 화면이에요.
- 묶음을 고른 상태에서는 도구 줄에 「묶음 선택 풀기」가 생겨요. 누르면 카드 화면으로 돌아가요.
- 표는 더 이상 접히지 않고 줄 수도 자르지 않아요. 5건까지 보여 주는 일은 카드가 맡아요.
- `docs/spec.md`의 마감 목록 설명도 이 배치에 맞게 고쳤어요.

## 확인 방법

- `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test`를 돌렸고 모두 통과했어요(테스트 282개).
- `pnpm dev --port 3100`으로 넓은 화면(1440px)과 휴대폰 폭(375px)을 직접 확인했어요. 휴대폰에서도 가로 스크롤이 생기지 않아요.
- 카드의 「전체 보기」를 누르면 위쪽 탭이 그 묶음으로 바뀌고 표가 보이는지 확인했어요.

## 중점 리뷰 사항

- 묶음 표는 아래로 펼치는 방식이나 팝업 창 대신 「묶음을 선택하는 방식」으로 보여 줘요. 위쪽 탭, 숫자 칸과 같은 값을 바꾸기 때문에 동작이 하나로 맞아요. 이 방식이 괜찮은지 봐 주세요.
- 카드나 풀기 버튼을 누르면 그 버튼이 화면에서 사라져요. 그래서 키보드 포커스를 「마감 목록」 영역으로 옮겼어요. 위치는 `Dashboard.tsx`의 `selectFromList`예요.

## 기타

- 구현을 모르는 새 리뷰어에게 diff를 보여 줬고, 나온 지적을 이 PR에 반영했어요.
- 최신 main(페이지 도구 줄 PR #22)을 합쳤어요. 「묶음 선택 풀기」 버튼은 도구 줄 오른쪽에 들어가요.

author: redjester14
body:
TODO HM6. Discord sign-in sits beside Google on `/login` and `/signup`. Google already ships, so this PR adds only Discord, through the same OAuth path.

## What changed

- **One button, one list, one callback.** `components/auth/google-sign-in-button.tsx` → `oauth-sign-in-button.tsx` (`OAuthSignInButton` / `OAuthSignInButtons`). The providers come from one list, `lib/auth/oauth-providers.ts`. Every provider uses `signInWithOAuth` → `/auth/callback?redirectTo=…` (PKCE) → `safeRedirectPath`. There is no second callback or redirect rule. Google keeps `prompt: "select_account"`. Discord passes **no** `scopes` option: Supabase Auth's Discord provider already asks for exactly `identify email`, and a `scopes` option is added on top of that list, so it would only duplicate them.
- **Discord shows only where `NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_DISCORD=1`.** Why a flag: supabase-js navigates straight to Supabase Auth's `/authorize`. Where the provider is off, the visitor lands on a raw JSON error page, and the app never sees an error it could word. Checking first would cost a network call per render. The flag is inlined at build time, so changing it needs a redeploy. Side finding: the old Google button's "isn't enabled yet" toast could never fire, for the same reason.
- **A provider's refusal reads calmly.** `/auth/callback` now handles `?error=` before any code exchange (`lib/auth/oauth-callback-error.ts`):
  - Cancel on Discord's screen (`access_denied`) → `/login?error=oauth-cancelled`, shown as a quiet status: "Sign-in was cancelled, so nothing changed…".
  - A provider email that isn't verified → `oauth-verify-email`.
  - Anything else → `oauth-failed`, logged on the server.

  The redirect is kept, so a retry lands where the visitor was going. No message says whether an account exists. Before this PR, a cancel showed "That sign-in link didn't work — it may have expired…".

  Supabase's default email links (reset, signup confirmation, email change) also land on `/auth/callback`. An expired or used one (`error=access_denied&error_code=otp_expired`) is **not** read as an OAuth refusal: it keeps the old "That sign-in link didn't work" message, is never exchanged, and carries no redirect. Only a refusal relayed from the provider (an `error` with no `error_code`), `provider_email_needs_verification` and Supabase's OAuth-only codes count as OAuth refusals.
- **New accounts:** the 0094 / 0127 signup trigger is unchanged.
  - The handle is **generated**. Supabase sends Discord's name as `full_name` / `name`, never as `username`, the only key the trigger reads for a handle.
  - The display name is the Discord username, cut to 64 characters.
  - The avatar is a built-in one; only Google pictures are kept.
  - Then onboarding, as today.
- **Same email as an existing account:** Supabase's automatic identity linking applies. A Discord account with a **verified** email signs in to the existing account, and no second profile is made. An unverified one is refused, and the login page asks the visitor to verify it with Discord. No account linking of our own.
- **`supabase/config.toml`:** an `[auth.external.discord]` block, **off**, with `client_id` / `secret` read from `env(…)`. `enabled` is a literal `false` on purpose: `enabled = "env(…)"` fails the CLI's config parse whenever the variable is unset (checked with CLI 2.84.2), which would break CI's stack and the preview branches. Locally, the CLI's own `SUPABASE_AUTH_EXTERNAL_DISCORD_ENABLED=true` override turns it on. This PR touches `supabase/`, so it gets its own preview branch, with Discord off.
- **Docs:** a new `docs/AUTH.md` with the owner setup (Discord app, production dashboard, the dev branch as code, local). There are pointers from `docs/EMAIL.md`, `docs/ENVIRONMENTS.md`, `.env.example` and `CLAUDE.md`'s Auth bullet. No credentials and no project refs.
- **CI:** `.env.e2e` gets `NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_DISCORD=1` so the e2e checks that both buttons render. The provider stays off; nothing leaves the app.

## Tests

- `tests/unit/auth/oauth-sign-in-button.test.tsx` covers the button:
  - the provider sent, and Google's query params;
  - Discord: no scopes and no query params;
  - unsafe redirects → `/dashboard`;
  - the busy state while leaving for the provider;
  - the error and throw toasts;
  - accessible names, with decorative marks.
- `tests/unit/auth/oauth-callback.test.ts` covers the callback: cancel, unverified email, other refusals (never exchanged), an unsafe redirect never carried, a good code, a failed exchange.
- `tests/unit/auth/oauth-auth-pages.test.tsx` covers the pages:
  - the flag on and off on both pages;
  - each refusal's message;
  - a cancel is a status, not an alert;
  - no message names an account.
- e2e `tests/e2e/oauth-buttons.spec.ts` checks:
  - both buttons by accessible name on `/login` and `/signup`, the same size;
  - the cancel path end to end.
- `/signup` joins the axe scan.
- Local: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` and `npm run test:unit` pass (1082 files, 19072 tests).

Screenshots, desktop and 390 px, of `/login`, `/signup` and the cancelled message: taken against the local stack with the flag on, and sent alongside this PR. Both buttons measure the same: 382×48 on desktop, 292×48 at 390 px.

## Manual testing (preview)

**Discord can't be tested on this PR's preview.** The PR touches `supabase/`, so its preview runs on its own short-lived Supabase branch, where Discord is off. It has no Discord secrets and no registered redirect, and the Vercel flag isn't set. What can be checked on this preview (any `dev_*` account, signed out):

1. Open `/login` and `/signup` signed out. Expected: "Continue with Google" above the "or … with email" divider, exactly as before, and **no** Discord button (the flag is unset on Preview).
2. Open `/auth/callback?redirectTo=%2Fdecks&error=access_denied`. Expected: you land on `/login?error=oauth-cancelled&redirectTo=%2Fdecks` with the calm "Sign-in was cancelled, so nothing changed…" note. Previously: "That sign-in link didn't work — it may have expired or already been used."
3. Sign in with `dev_free` by email. Expected: unchanged.

**Once the owner has done the setup in `docs/AUTH.md`** (Discord app → production dashboard → `NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_DISCORD=1` on Production, redeploy), on production:

1. `/signup` → **Continue with Discord** → Discord's consent screen asks only for "Access your username, avatar, and banner" and "Access your email address" → **Authorize**. Expected: onboarding with a generated handle (e.g. `ember_sphinx_4821`), never your Discord name or email. Your Discord username is the display name, and the avatar is a built-in one.
2. Sign out → `/login?redirectTo=/decks` → **Continue with Discord** → **Cancel** on Discord's screen. Expected: back on `/login` with the calm cancelled note, and the redirect still there.
3. With a Discord account whose verified email matches an existing PipGlyph email account → **Continue with Discord**. Expected: signed in to THAT account. No onboarding, no second profile.
4. `/login` at 390 px: both buttons full width, the same height.

For previews later: configure the dev branch as `docs/AUTH.md` §3 says, then set the flag on Preview. Discord then works on every preview that uses the dev branch, never on a per-PR branch.

TD-1389, design §6 rule 6.

A member that closed a board line (`done board:<key>`) or a red PR's order and declared `none` was told that same order as lane news on every declaration, because the board reading lags origin by up to `REPOS_EVERY` and work orders are never in the first `lane_seen`.

- `_lane_news` holds out of the news, and out of `lane_seen`, a work order the member itself reported `done` while the reading that holds it was taken no later than that `done`: `work_orders.at` for `board:<key>`, `prs.at` for `pr:<n>` (matched by the ref or by a `done`'s `pr`). A reading taken after the `done` that still holds it — the close did not land — tells it once.
- §6 rule 6 now states that work orders are never in the first write, and this exception; a §6 history line.
- Test: `test_a_work_order_the_member_closed_is_no_news_until_a_reading_after_the_close_still_holds_it` (fails without the fix).

body:
Fixes #119. Fixes #110. Fixes #111.

Problems the scenario step could have caught kept reaching the maker or the guardian. A test that only checked a one-time wording change went on the wall. An old test or a may-not file the red forced to change surfaced as a stop on the maker, with no warning. A value check had no red case for a wrong input. Amendments the watch drafted left out the test name or the may-not line they loosened. And a `covers` item that named a point by number did not count, so the scenario step stalled.

Now the scenario brief marks one-time wording tests slice-only, and asks for a red case for each way a value can be wrong, including a read-only agent claiming what only a person may give. Its report names `old_tests_forced` and `may_not_files`. The record keeps both, a report that leaves one out clears it, and the maker's prompt shows them. The maker may change a named old test and records the move. From the may-not list it may change only `.xv/picture.md`, and only when the report names it; any other named file still stops as `protected_changed`. The watch brief has each amendment name four things. A `covers` item may name a scenario point by number, but never an amendment's point.

This changes briefs and a may-not list, so `CHANGELOG.md` has a line. The repo is solo, and Sean decided it.

The slice took five scenario runs and four guardian passes, and $7.31 of a budget Sean raised twice, from $4.30 to $8.50. Three of the stops were `red_misses_point` stalls from the number naming this slice fixes. Two guardian passes sent it back: once because 2a and 2b were in the briefs only, once because the words still let the maker change any named file after Sean narrowed point 7. The scenario brief does not yet say that a number never covers an amendment's point; that is #125. The record and packet are in `.xv/slices/2026-11-04-scenario-catches.*`.

Where: `skills/scenario/SKILL.md`, `skills/maker/SKILL.md`, `skills/guardian/SKILL.md`, `skills/watch/SKILL.md`, `scripts/record.py`, `scripts/prompt.py`, `scripts/run.py`, `.xv/picture.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and tests in `tests/test_run.py` and `tests/test_briefs_picture.py`.

author: milo37
body:
Refs #504

## 변경

P7 PR4b-2: SSO 계정 erasure 요청(`phase7_request_sso_account_erasure`)을 API(`apps/api/src/auth/accountErasureAuthority.ts` `requestSsoAccountErasure`)의 Prisma transaction으로 옮깁니다(god 승인 계획, bca29a 조건). 옛 SQL과 같은 순서·조건이고 응답 코드는 바꾸지 않습니다.

순서: runtime 확인 → 계정 Session 확인 → User FOR UPDATE → 재확인(없으면 `AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED`) → ACCOUNT_FRESH proof 확인(`SSO_FRESH_REQUIRED`) → 열린 작성 후보(`SSO_ACCOUNT_DELETION_BLOCKED`) → receipt 형식(22023 `Invalid private erasure receipt.`) → Account FOR UPDATE → request INSERT → User `DELETION_PENDING` → SsoAccountFresh proof·transaction 삭제.

- `accountErasureAuthority.ts`: `requestSsoAccountErasure`, 내부 `accountSession`(옛 `phase7_sso_account_session`), `accountFreshProofIsValid`(옛 `phase7_sso_account_proof_valid` + ACCOUNT_FRESH 경로의 `phase7_sso_account_context_valid`).
- `ssoAccountRepository.requestErasure`가 TS를 호출(repository client에 `$transaction` 추가).
- migration `20261118090000_erasure_request_to_api`: 열 단위 GRANT, 신설 트리거 3개(함수 2), `validate_phase7_user_change` 교체, `phase7_request_sso_account_erasure` DROP. 모두 search_path 고정. forward-only.
- `runtimeRoleAttestation`(`User.accountStatus` UPDATE), ops pin(72개).

SQL로 남는 것: `phase7_sso_account_session`·`phase7_sso_account_proof_valid`·`phase7_sso_account_context_valid`(계정 fresh·link·unlink SQL이 계속 사용 → PR5).

### 열 단위 권한 (nihongo_app, 이 PR에서 추가)

| 테이블 | 권한 |
|---|---|
| `User` | UPDATE(`accountStatus`) — 아래 트리거가 ACTIVE→DELETION_PENDING만 허용 |
| `SsoAccountErasureRequest` | INSERT(`userId`, `receiptDigest`, `providerCleanup`, `receiptExpiresAt`) — 아래 트리거가 `userId`·`receiptDigest` 외 값을 서버 값으로 덮어씀 |
| `SsoAccountFreshProof` | SELECT(`proofDigest`, `context`, `verifiedAt`, `expiresAt`, `userId`), DELETE(테이블) |
| `SsoAccountFreshTransaction` | SELECT(`userId`), DELETE(테이블) |

### 트리거

| 트리거(함수) | 내용 |
|---|---|
| `SsoAccountErasureRequest_prepare_api_insert`(`prepare_sso_account_erasure_request`, 신설, INVOKER) | nihongo_app 직접 INSERT일 때: User가 ACTIVE가 아니면 42501. `providerCleanup`은 그 User의 apple·google Account로 다시 계산(모두 `PENDING`), `receiptExpiresAt` = 지금 + 1일, `appStatus` = DELETION_PENDING, `createdAt`·lease·`completedAt`은 서버 값. **API가 provider 정리를 완료로 적을 수 없어** PR4a의 erasure 확정 조건(provider 정리 모두 COMPLETED)이 SQL provider cleanup 함수만으로 채워집니다. |
| `validate_phase7_user_change`(교체, DEFINER) | 신뢰 실행 없이 상태를 바꾸는 nihongo_app 쓰기는 **ACTIVE→DELETION_PENDING만**, 다른 열 변경 없이, 같은 User의 이 transaction에서 만든 DELETION_PENDING 요청(`createdAt >= now()`, `completedAt IS NULL`)이 있을 때만. 그 뒤는 지금과 같이 열린 후보 검사, revocation 기록, 세대 +1, Session 삭제. `updatedAt`은 트리거가 설정. |
| `SsoAccountFreshProof`/`SsoAccountFreshTransaction_limit_api_delete`(`limit_sso_account_fresh_delete`, 신설, INVOKER) | nihongo_app 직접 DELETE는 그 User의 DELETION_PENDING 요청이 있을 때만. SQL 함수(소유자)와 User 삭제 cascade는 그대로. |

INVOKER 트리거는 `current_user`로 API 직접 쓰기와 SQL 함수 경로를 나눕니다(PR4a와 같은 방식).

## 검증

body:
## 변경 목적

최초 예산 설계 A·B 결과를 기존 추천 API·사용자 승인·추천 화면에 연결합니다. 미분류로 낮게 잡힌 B 예산은 후보를 가정한 복사본에서 다시 계산해 보완하며, 보정 때문에 다른 항목의 최종 금액이 줄지 않도록 합니다.

**Draft 유지 / 새 서비스 연결은 기본 OFF입니다.** 아직 정책 설정과 이력 검증 콜백이 없으며, 실제 사용자에게 새 기능을 활성화하지 않았습니다.

## 최종 구현

- **A/B 자동 선택:** 이번 달을 제외한 완료된 3개월 이력과 수집·정합성 검증을 사용합니다. 미분류 제외 카테고리별 3개월 거래 건수 최댓값이 11건 이상이면 B, 10건 이하·이력 불충분이면 A입니다. 후보 가정으로 B 자격을 만들지 않습니다.
- **A 개인화:** 서버가 1~3순위별 작은·중간·큰 증액 미리보기를 계산하고, 합성 비교 창의 LLM이 유지·부분 이동을 선택합니다. 생활비 20% 전체 한도는 목표액이 아니며, 감액이 있는 제안은 재검토합니다. 실패하면 기본안으로 복귀합니다.
- **B 기준:** 실제 거래가 있으면 거래별 이상치 제외 후 3개월 평균, 월 합계만 있으면 기존 중앙값 대체입니다. 쇼핑·미용은 MAD만 사용하고, 다른 활성 항목의 지배 규칙은 3건 이상에서만 적용합니다. 사용자 재포함·반복 가맹점 보호를 유지합니다.
- **B 미분류 보정:** 유효한 최상위 후보 하나를 복사본에 가정해 같은 계산을 다시 수행합니다. 양의 차액만 기존 배분 잔액 안에서 보완하고, 원본 분류·사용자 최소액·정확한 잠금을 바꾸지 않습니다. 후보 없음·모호한 점수·잔액 없음은 기존 B를 유지합니다.
- **최종 단위 및 보정 기록:** 만 원 우선/필요 시 5천 원, 잠금은 원액입니다. 보정 없는 B의 최종 단위를 먼저 정산해 다른 항목의 금액과 기존 여윳돈 충당액을 보존합니다. 실제 증가액만 기록하고, 최종 증가가 0이면 보정 원인을 제거합니다. 출발액 사전도 별도로 복사합니다.
- **잠금 오류 수정:** 최초 B 설계에서 잠금 후 실제 출발액이 target보다 작으면 차액을 unallocated로 반환합니다. 과거 합계만 보고 중단하던 문제를 고쳤고, 기존 예산 조정 도구가 사용하는 비례 기본안은 유지합니다.
- **합계·보호 검수:** 카테고리 합계+unallocated=target, 최소액·잠금·하한·원장 causes 합=diff를 서버가 검사합니다. 명시적으로 공급한 상위 여윳돈으로 실제 부족액을 충당하는 기존 경로는 유지하며, 미분류 보정에 추가 상위 여윳돈을 사용하지 않습니다.

## API·승인·화면 연결

- 기존 추천/작업 조회/승인 URL과 DB 모델을 재사용합니다. 마이그레이션 및 공용 recommend.py·check_result 변경은 없습니다.
- 새 초안의 선택 결과·정책/이력 fingerprint·여윳돈 이동액·설명을 기존 validation_summary에 저장합니다.
- 계산·초안 생성 때 프로필 생활비를 바꾸지 않습니다. 사용자 승인 후 검수된 여윳돈 이동액만 반영하고, 반복 승인 시 중복 이동하지 않습니다.
- 설정·정책·이력이 달라지면 초안을 만료시킵니다. 새 추천 실패 때 예전 초안을 잘못 승인하지 않도록 추천 화면을 정리했습니다.
- 주거·통신/여행은 월 예산·잠금 화면에서 제외하며, 서버 금액·설명·여윳돈 충당 정보를 화면에서 재계산하지 않습니다.
- 상위 1~3순위의 평소 기준 대비 30% 초과 감액 안내를 서버 문장으로 표시합니다.
- **실사용 API에서는 외부 LLM을 호출하지 않습니다.** 합성 입력 비교 창의 A 도구·B 예측 실험은 유지합니다. 외부 전송 동의와 LangSmith 실사용 설정은 별도입니다.

## 검증

현재 작업 브랜치에서 **849개 테스트 통과**했습니다.

| 범위 | 결과 |
| --- | ---: |
| PostgreSQL 예산 앱 전체: python manage.py test budgets --noinput | 506개 통과 |
| B·A/B 비교·계산 창: tests/budget_design | 291개 통과 |
| 프론트 Node 유틸 테스트 | 9개 통과 |
| 프론트 Vitest | 43개 통과 |

- 로컬 전용 ML 환경/모델의 실제 추론과 계산 창 smoke test도 실행했으며, 위 291개에 건너뜀은 없습니다. 10개 비율 합 1, 금액 합 및 모델 체크섬/버전을 확인했습니다.
- 미분류 보정은 정상 예산이 생성되는 합성 400건의 최종 전후 금액 비교와 기존 합성 150건을 포함합니다. 실제 분류 후보 정확도나 추천 수용성을 입증하는 실험은 아닙니다.
- 프론트 npm run build 통과. npm run lint는 오류 없고, 변경하지 않은 MoneyInput.jsx의 기존 Fast Refresh 경고 1건이 있습니다.
- 이번 공유 검증에서는 외부 LLM을 실제 호출하지 않았습니다. 운영 서버 모델 배포와 실제 사용자 금융정보 전송은 검증하지 않았습니다.

## 병합·활성화 전 확인

1. 거래 수집·정합성 담당 나은님과 BUDGET_HISTORY_VERIFIER(user, month_ids)를 연결해야 합니다. coverage는 이미 사용하지만 수집 완료가 거래 정합성 보장을 뜻하지는 않습니다. 미검증을 임의 verified로 채우지 않습니다.
2. 이미 정한 정책을 BUDGET_DESIGN_POLICY에 설정해야 합니다. 설정이 없으면 needs_policy로 추천을 중단합니다.
3. ML 모델과 BUDGET_MODEL_PATH / BUDGET_INFERENCE_PYTHON을 배포 서버에 준비해야 합니다. 모델·원자료·.env·개인 local_workspace는 PR에 포함하지 않습니다.
4. PM의 fix/manual-loan-consent-copy도 backend/budgets/api.py를 수정하므로 상호 통합 검토가 필요합니다. 이 PR에서는 고정지출 목록 구간을 수정하지 않았습니다.
5. origin/main 786b2b3과 새 커밋의 git merge-tree 검사는 충돌 없이 통과했습니다. main의 22개 후속 커밋을 작업 브랜치에 실제 병합한 실행 결과는 아닙니다.
6. 가정 후 계산이 불가능할 때 감액 전 출발액으로 보정하는 제안과 후보 확신도 임계치는 보류했습니다. 현재 승인된 후보 재계산·실패 대체를 유지합니다. 의료·식비의 최신 물가 자동 검토는 아직 구현하지 않았습니다.

author: nathan-muir
body:
## 🎯 Changes

Since #2312 (in `1.0.0-rc.1.2`), `finalizeRow` strips internal route metadata from every output row of every query with `transformPublicContainers`, and builds a callback view of the row the same way. That walk calls `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptors` on every nested object and array before it can tell nothing changed. So a row with deep nesting is copied up to three times, even when there's nothing to strip. On `0.15.2` this only happened in includes mode.

- **`transformPublicContainers` scans first.** The new `needsTransform` returns early when no container under the value holds an omitted key and no leaf transforms. In that case the full walk would return the value unchanged anyway. Otherwise the full walk runs exactly as before.
- **`finalizeRow` skips the callback-view walk when `sourceViews` is empty.** Its transform is then the identity, so the walk can't change anything.

Two differences in the scan, neither of which changes results for plain row data:
- It reads enumerable values directly, so it would call an own getter, where the full walk skips accessors. If the getter's result changes under the transform, the full walk still decides.
- It walks arrays by index, so it ignores extra string-keyed properties on arrays.

## 📊 Measured

A Vue app with 73k items in a project, eager sync, 4× CPU throttle, max-size cold load of two pages, one profiled run each:

| | 0.15.2 | 1.0.0-rc.1.2 | rc.1.2 + this change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Page A ready | 17.2 s | 32.0 s | 18.9 s |
| Page B ready | 20.7 s | 35.9 s | 22.8 s |
| Self time in `route-metadata` | — | 13.2 s | 0.6 s |

Almost all of the rc.1.2 time comes from `finalizeRow`; `.fn.*` callbacks add about 0.1 s.

## ✅ Checklist

- [ ] Oracle suites from #2312 run locally
- [ ] Benchmark workflow

author: onoya
body:
## Description

Two changes to how the spend monitor raises its platform alerts (`platform_spike` and `platform_cost_spike`). Both build on the trusted-account tier from #6541.

1. **The platform ratio and floors leave out trusted spend.** Before this, one trusted account spending 5k-15k credits per 15-minute window against a low overnight baseline paged "Platform spend spike" at critical. Now the floors and the ratio are judged on standard-tier spend only, in both the current window and the baseline history. The alert still reports the full platform total, and Slack shows the trusted share separately, so a platform-wide anomaly stays visible.
2. **A platform alert needs both floors.** It fires only when standard-tier credits reach `spendMonitorPlatformSpikeFloorCredits` AND standard-tier provider cost reaches `spendMonitorPlatformCostFloorUsd`. Before this, each metric was checked on its own, so either could alert alone. The two rules stay separate, so a cost spike with a normal credit ratio is still reported as a cost spike. All defaults are unchanged.

## Customer note
none

## Changes
- `evaluate.ts`: account candidates and their trust are now resolved before the platform check.
  - Credits of trusted owner scopes (User, Organization, Agent) are subtracted from the platform's current window and from its history. Their rollup series are read once per owner type. API key scopes are skipped because their spend is already inside the owner's.
  - Owner rollups carry no provider cost, so the trusted cost is estimated at the platform's own cost per credit in each window.
- `rules.ts`: `evaluatePlatform` takes standard-tier observations plus the full `total`. It returns nothing unless both floors are met. A breach reports `value: total` and, when trusted spend was left out, `trustedExcluded`.
- `incidents.ts`: `trustedExcluded` is stored in the incident context.
- `slackMessage.ts`: when trusted spend was left out, "Normal" reads "Normal excl. trusted" and a "Trusted accounts, not in ratio" field shows the excluded amount. The cost figure is marked "(est.)".

## Guide for Testers
Backend only (a scheduled worker). The unit tests cover:
1. About 15k credits per window from a trusted account against a 300-credit baseline: no platform alert.
2. The same spend from an untrusted account: a critical platform spike reporting 15,000 credits.
3. A standard spike alongside trusted use: the alert reports the full total, a ratio computed without trusted spend, and the trusted share, and the Slack post shows that share.
4. Trusted use in the baseline history is subtracted too: a 2,000-credits-per-bucket history that is mostly trusted gives a 300 standard baseline, and a standard spike against it pages critical.
5. Both floors: a credit spike with cost under the cost floor stays quiet, a cost spike with credits under the credit floor stays quiet, and the alert fires once both are met.

### What NOT to test
No UI changes. Account-level alerts are unchanged.

## Additional Information
A trusted account counts toward this only while it is an account candidate in the current window (at or above the lowest account floor). A trusted account that was busy earlier but is quiet now stays in the baseline history, and the median baseline absorbs it.

author: dandenney
body:
Closes #5

Locked SHA: d0908c434c42360adf1ad10352df4dcab0760331

`git diff d0908c4..HEAD -- packages/simulation/test/inventory/fin-001.locked.test.ts` is empty. The branch merges `origin/main` (merge commit, no rebase).

## What changed

- `src/inventory/pools.ts`: input validation in `addProduct`/`addMaterial` (positive safe-integer quantity, non-negative cost) and `addReservation` (`0 < quantity ≤ available`, new ID). `removeProduct`/`removeMaterial` now refuse to over-remove or to empty a pool without taking all of its cost. New pure helpers: `checkReservation`, `takeProduct`/`takeMaterial` (unreserved stock only, cargo "take"), `consumeReservations` (rules 3 and 4, returns the `writtenOff`/material cost), `takeForContract` (rule 5), `releaseContractReservations` (rule 7), `storageUsed`. None of them writes the ledger, the journal, or the counters.
- `src/inventory/release.ts`: `registerInventory` handles `RELEASE_RESERVATION` (rule 2) as a `RESERVATION` transaction with no entries, keyed `idempotencyKey("RESERVATION", id, "RELEASE")`, emitting `RESERVATION_RELEASED { reason: "PLAYER" }`. The reservation is judged before `coordinator.begin`, because immediate dispatch doesn't run `validate` and a second release would otherwise hit the duplicate-key path and report success.
- `src/game/systems.ts`: the appended `{ name: "inventory (T02a)", register: registerInventory }` line, plus the import it needs.
- `docs/decisions/0013-reservation-release-rules.md`: the eight rules, the alternatives, and the consequences.
- `test/inventory/pools.test.ts`: tests for the extra guards (residue on emptying, duplicate reservation ID, product consumption, `releaseRejection`).

## Outside owned files (please review)

- `test/sprint-zero/id-order.test.ts`: a 3-line fixture change. The test reserved corn on a fresh game with no corn pool. The locked tests require `addReservation` to throw when quantity > available, so the fixture now buys the 4 corn first (`buyCorn`, already imported). What the test checks is unchanged. There was no way to satisfy both tests without this edit.

## Tests

`pnpm --filter @eov/simulation test test/inventory && pnpm check`:

```
$ vitest run test/inventory
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  24 passed (24)

pnpm check (typecheck → lint → test), exit 0
@eov/simulation   Test Files  20 passed (20)   Tests  157 passed (157)
@eov/persistence  Test Files  1 passed (1)     Tests  7 passed (7)
@eov/economy-lab  Test Files  1 passed (1)     Tests  3 passed (3)
```

Lint ran from this worktree's root and passed.

## Replay hashes

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Reference scenario (`test/kernel/reference-scenario.test.ts`, pinned) | `fnv1a64:0f3c258a09c81be8` | `fnv1a64:0f3c258a09c81be8` |
| Sprint Zero path (buy corn + sugar, produce 1, sell 1, truck returns; the `path.test.ts` determinism run) | `fnv1a64:356d462e35305432` | `fnv1a64:356d462e35305432` |

Both unchanged. Registering the inventory system adds a command handler only (no phase hooks), and the Sprint Zero path never removes more than a pool holds or reserves more than is available.

author: metamergebot
body:
Stacked on #48512 (rust-server startup guards): this PR targets that branch, so its diff is the one commit on top; it rebases onto main once #48512 lands.

## Motivation

In Python-frontend mode the launcher posts `/freeze_gc` once the startup warmup finishes (or at once when `--skip-server-warmup` is set): the tokenizer manager turns it into a `FreezeGCReq` carrying `--gc-threshold`, and every scheduler rank applies the thresholds and calls `gc.freeze()`, so the objects allocated during startup stay out of every later full collection.

The Rust frontend never ran that step. `--gc-threshold` reaches the scheduler only through `FreezeGCReq`, so in Rust mode the flag was silently ignored and every full collection in the scheduler walked the whole startup heap.

## Modifications

- `ServerArgs` (Rust) gains `gc_threshold`, filled from `--gc-threshold` by `_build_server_args`.
- Each listener's `startup_warmup` sends `FreezeGCReq` once its warmup generation succeeds, immediately when the warmup is skipped, and after the disaggregation exception that keeps the server up on a failed warmup. A failed or timed-out warmup sends nothing, as in Python.
- The scheduler sends no reply to `FreezeGCReq`, so it leaves through a new one-way intake event (`TmEvent::OneWay`) instead of the awaited control path, which would hang. The intake pushes it on the reserved lane that aborts already use, so a full request ring cannot drop it, and reports back whether it was queued; a failure is logged as an error.
- `Scheduler.handle_freeze_gc` forwards the request to the detokenizer socket only when no Rust server is embedded: in Rust mode the detokenizer runs inside the scheduler process, which the freeze already covers, and nothing reads that socket.
- Propagation follows Python: without local control broadcast, the DP0 listener's message is broadcast to the TP group and the other listeners' copies are dropped; with `--enable-dp-attention-local-control-broadcast` each DP group freezes its own ranks; PP stages receive it through the normal forwarding.

No `/freeze_gc` HTTP route is added to the Rust server: in Python mode its only production caller is the launcher's own post-warmup request, which the Rust server now makes internally.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable (no change to model execution).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable here; the effect is the one `/freeze_gc` already has in Python mode (startup objects excluded from later full collections, `--gc-threshold` applied in the scheduler).

## Checklist

- `app.rs::startup_warmup_freezes_gc_once_warm`: skipped warmup, successful warmup (nothing frozen until the warmup reply arrives), failed warmup (nothing frozen, failure reported), failed warmup in disaggregation mode (server stays up and freezes); checks the exact `FreezeGCReq` wire array.
- `to_scheduler_tests.rs::one_way_control_bypasses_request_ring_capacity`: a full one-slot request ring still takes the message.
- `test_rust_server_extension.py::test_freeze_gc_skips_the_detokenizer_socket_in_rust_mode`.
- The `runtime.rs` tests that boot a real runtime with the warmup skipped, and `test_rust_server_crash_dump.py`, now take the startup `FreezeGCReq` off the ring before their own requests.
- `cargo test --locked -p sglang-server --all-features` and the registered unit tests above pass locally on this branch.
- Beyond the change itself: one `assertEqual` in `test_rust_server_crash_dump.py` is joined onto a single line, the ruff-format form that upstream `lint` requires; no other line differs from the behaviour change.

author: linfeng-z
body:
Replay currently emits one recorded output per tick regardless of its timestamp. Add explicit `timestamped=True` options to the replay helpers and pipeline methods. Default sequential replay still ignores recorded times and publishes at the current tick.

Timestamped in-process replay waits until an output is due and preserves its publication timestamp. Times use seconds and the caller's time origin. MCAP replay reads exact step times from metadata in file order, so nanosecond conversion cannot move an output past its original tick. Repeated timestamps and distinct float times that share a nanosecond retain their order. Legacy MCAP reads keep their existing nanosecond-derived timestamps.

The option rejects nonfinite or decreasing times, backward ticks, RRD input, and MCAP outputs without matching step metadata. It emits at most one due output per tick. Set an explicit `step(now=...)` anchor before advancing with `step(dt=...)`; an unanchored first delta tick raises before Flow initialization. Coarse ticks can still delay downstream sampling. The option does not reconstruct transport arrival order or an asynchronous wake schedule.

`replay_from` forwards the new keyword only when enabled, so existing replay overrides continue to work. Documentation and the notebook source now state that recordings contain node output snapshots, rather than each consumer's complete sampled input history.

Validation in an isolated Python 3.11 environment:
- Initial test-first baseline: 6 failed, 1 passed because the option was absent.
- Precision and compatibility regression baseline: 4 failed, 10 passed before the fixes.
- `python -m pytest tests/core/test_timestamped_replay_rt.py tests/core/test_pipeline_step_rt.py -q`: 35 passed. Coverage includes an MCAP write/read/replay round trip at the original fractional ticks, repeated and subnanosecond times, exact publication times, real future buffer times, missing metadata, RRD rejection, delta stepping, reset, empty input, and default override compatibility.
- `python -m pytest tests -q`: 451 passed, 2 skipped.
- `python scripts/docs/sync_notebooks.py --check`: all 5 notebooks synchronized. Generated changes preserve existing cell IDs and affect only the corrected notebook.
- `npm run build` in `docs-site`: 23 pages built. Dependency setup used `npm install --no-package-lock --no-audit --no-fund` because the existing lockfile is missing two optional dependency entries; no lockfile changes are included.
- `python scripts/release/check_public_history.py --base b0d766329c045b33eacf5e978e0279f277f7d558`: passed, with an additional scan of the complete introduced commit range and final diff.

body:
Builds the QS-19 ruling.

- `ulo_rpc::Capabilities`, `ulo_http::BackendLimits` and `ulo_http::embed::EmbedLimits` share one shape: private per-capability fields, every boolean held by default, a `false` declared only through `without_<capability>(reason)`, read through `<capability>()` and `why_not_<capability>()`. `Backend::limits` takes `&self`.
- RPC defaults flip to held (`binary`, `native_backpressure`, `miss_signal`, `holds_unserved`, `durable_replies`, `ordered_control`). Each first-party link declares the values it had before, with reasons. A link declaring nothing speaks CBOR and runs every scenario.
- `Embed::STRIPS_PREFIX` becomes `EmbedLimits::strips_prefix`. `fans_out_requests` becomes `without_delivers_requests_once`.
- Refusals and warnings print the declared reason, including the client's binary-payload refusal.
- The RPC suite skips `cancel_follows_its_request` from `ordered_control`; the WebSocket suite skips every scenario but the declaration scenario for a host declared without `upgrades`. libtest counts a skip as a pass; tests cover both directions.
- `MigrationLock` carries `#[diagnostic::on_unimplemented]` naming the stores that support migrations; `migrate` and `migrate_within` move to a method bound so the message prints. A compile_fail snapshot pins it.

author: juanp-ing
body:
## Por qué

Una auditoría UX/UI (con capturas móviles reales) encontró que la app confundía: había elementos que aparecían sin motivo, el registro de series quedaba muy abajo, el "hoy" salía en UTC, la navegación y los textos eran confusos, y la interfaz era una pila de tarjetas iguales. Este PR corrige eso en cuatro pasos.

## Qué cambia

### 1. Arreglos rápidos
- **`[hidden]` no ocultaba nada** en varios componentes: se veían siempre un cronómetro «01:30», un «¡Nuevo récord!» y un aviso de rutina falsos, y las pestañas de Rutinas mostraban los dos paneles a la vez. Ahora hay una regla global.
- **Día local:** el navegador guarda su zona horaria en la cookie `ft_tz` y el servidor calcula «hoy» con ella. Antes, a partir de las 7 pm en Colombia, la app ya marcaba el día siguiente.
- Un récord por ejercicio en el resumen, gráfica del mapa con el ejercicio más entrenado, zoom permitido (WCAG 1.4.4), sin códigos hex en textos y confirmación al borrar una rutina.

### 2. «Hoy» en dos estados
- **Antes de entrenar:** tarjeta «Hoy toca · 5 ejercicios · 17 series · ~46 min» con un único botón.
- **Modo foco:** el ejercicio actual con sus series en puntos y un panel fijo al pulgar con el descanso, **Deshacer** y el botón principal. Al terminar aparece un resumen.
- La sesión activa la entrega el servidor y se retoma al recargar. Nuevo endpoint `DELETE /api/sesiones/<id>/series/<serie_id>`.

### 3. Navegación
- Barra inferior **Hoy · Rutinas · Progreso · Perfil**. «Salir» pasa del encabezado a Perfil.
- Nueva vista **Perfil**, editable mediante el onboarding con redirección segura y botón Cancelar.
- **Rutinas:** «Entrenar» abre Hoy con esa rutina, y crear una rutina va en una hoja con días, series, descanso y orden.

### 4. Capa visual
- **Racha de semanas** y meta semanal en Hoy.
- «Tu mes» con **comparación real contra el mes anterior** y estado vacío ilustrado.
- **Celebración de récord** a pantalla completa. La primera serie de un ejercicio cuenta como «primera marca», no como récord.
- Escala tipográfica en tokens, nombres escapados en `innerHTML` y pesos con 2 decimales (discos de 1,25 kg).

## Notas para revisar
- No hay cambios en los modelos ni migraciones; funciona con la base de datos actual.
- La regla «primera marca» cambia lo que cuenta `nuevos_prs` en `/api/resumen-mensual`: ahora es un récord solo si hubo series anteriores de ese ejercicio. Se añadieron `primeras_marcas` y `comparativa`.
- Se mantienen los textos «Rutinas Famosas (12)» e «IDEAL PARA TU PERFIL» porque los exige una prueba existente.

## Pendiente (fuera de este PR)
- Rediseñar «Músculos y récords»: la gráfica mezcla peso y volumen en un mismo eje.
- Que «Usar esta rutina» no marque la copia como principal si ya tienes una.
- `/api/auth/register` devuelve el código de verificación en la respuesta.

## Pruebas
- `pytest`: **95 pasan** (54 existentes y 41 nuevas, unitarias, de integración y funcionales).
- Verificado en Chromium sin interfaz a 390×844 recorriendo todos los flujos (Hoy, modo foco, deshacer, récord, Rutinas, Progreso y Perfil).

The Guild release workflow copied from the template in [blip-box/guild#11](https://github.com/blip-box/guild/pull/11), the `[release]` table in `guild.toml` (the library paths, four weeks of staleness, the two version files, the alpha series, so the first proposal will be `0.1.0a1`), the workflow in CI's `scheduled` job, and the handbook rows that name it.

The publishing workflow and the PyPI trusted publisher are not part of this; the proposal's checklist assumes them, and they are the first-alpha item on the roadmap.

v0.4 del roadmap, CEO Orchestrator: el director entrega un **objetivo** y la oficina devuelve un **informe consolidado**. author: pl0n3r
body:
Closes #1570

<!-- brvtal-reservation-id: 695880c9-1f13-4dfc-990d-0f59e7a7a919 -->

## Qué y por qué
El propietario reportó que «ACTIVAR SONIDO» a veces no suena en algunos dispositivos. Causas en `js/public-cromo-sound.js`: el botón pasaba a «Apagar el pulso» sin esperar a `ctx.resume()` ni comprobar `ctx.state`; el primer nodo de audio nacía en un `setInterval`, fuera del gesto del clic; iOS mutea Web Audio con el interruptor de silencio salvo que se declare reproducción de medios; y una suspensión del audio (llamada, segundo plano) dejaba el botón diciendo que sonaba.

- Declara `navigator.audioSession.type = 'playback'` cuando existe; en iOS anteriores usa un `<audio>` silencioso dentro del gesto.
- Reproduce un buffer silencioso dentro del clic para desbloquear el contexto.
- Espera `resume()` y solo activa el pulso si `ctx.state === 'running'`; si falla o queda suspendido, vuelve a «Activar sonido» y permite reintentar.
- Escucha `statechange`: si el audio se suspende con el sonido activo, el botón lo refleja.
- Sigue sin autoplay y apagado por defecto; el sonido procedural no cambia.

## Criterios de aceptación
- [x] AC-01 Un nodo silencioso arranca dentro del clic y se configura la sesión de audio de iOS.
- [x] AC-02 El botón solo muestra «Apagar el pulso» con `ctx.state === 'running'`; resume fallido o suspendido vuelve a apagado.
- [x] AC-03 Cambio a `suspended`/`interrupted` con sonido activo se refleja en el botón.
- [x] AC-04 E2E con `AudioContext` simulado (running, suspended, rejected); versión patch 0.1.213.
- [ ] CI exact-HEAD y revisión final única antes del merge.

## Pruebas
- `python3 -m unittest tests.test_public_cromo`: PASS.
- Simulación en Node con `AudioContext` falso: running → activo; suspended/rechazado → apagado; `audioSession.type = 'playback'`.
- Nueva prueba Playwright (3 casos) en `tests/e2e/public-cromo-home.spec.mjs`; no ejecutada en local (sin `node_modules`), la corre el CI.
- **No verificado en dispositivo real**: lo cubre #1507.

## Riesgo y reversión
Solo JavaScript de cliente y una prueba; sin datos ni medios. Reversible con revert de squash.

## Fuera de alcance
Diseño del botón, sonido procedural, autoplay e interruptor de `/contact` (#1514).
