Validate queue selection before downloading an agent or creating a token, so onboarding failures explain which self-hosted queues are available.

author: patrickcmd
body:
## Summary

After [PatrickCmd/digital-twin#3](https://github.com/PatrickCmd/digital-twin/pull/3) deployed to dev, every route (including `GET /health`) returned API Gateway's generic `{"message":"Internal Server Error"}`, meaning the Lambda fails before handling a request. The fresh build resolved the newest `pymupdf4llm`, which now depends on `pymupdf-layout`, `onnxruntime` and `numpy` (~190 MB) and runs a layout model when the PDF is converted at import time; far too heavy for the 512 MB Lambda.

- `build_knowledge.py` converts `data/me/linkedin.pdf` to `linkedin.md` once; `deploy.py` runs it before packaging and excludes the PDF. The markdown is committed.
- `resources.py` reads the markdown (falls back to the PDF only in local dev when `pymupdf4llm` is installed).

author: andrewx192
body:
The carousel destroyed its swiper instance on beforeremove. CanJS only
dispatches that event when a live binding removes the component. The test
helpers clean up with a jQuery remove(), which never triggers it, so the
swiper instance and its resize watcher stayed alive. When a resize had been
debounced before the removal, it later called onResize on the swiper, which
throws in updateClasses.

In the unit tests this threw during context-bar's hooks ("Cannot read
property 'classList' of undefined" at swiper.js:4658). Mocha then moved on
while the hook was still running, and the stale callback failed or aborted
whatever ran next. It happens in about 1 run in 4 on master. Most recently
it caused 7 failures in #63's test job:
https://github.com/arcus-smart-home/arcusweb/actions/runs/41978534919

Tear down on removed instead, and cancel any pending debounced resize.

author: hona
body:
After an update, a process still running the old binary (a relay `mesh exec self --serve`, a CLI, an old sync) that finds no daemon of its build registers the autostart with **its own, outdated template** and restarts the daemon with it.

- **Seen on air (dev.28 → dev.29):** the plist was rewritten twice without #2's `ProcessType Interactive`, so the daemon stayed `spawn type = daemon (3)` and timers ran 14 ms late. Fixed by hand on air.
- **Fix:** `daemon::ensure()` first checks whether this process's binary was swapped: it runs from the install dir, and the installed file doesn't contain its build id (`exec::BUILD`, one file read, no spawn). If so, it runs `<installed mesh> daemon --start`, so only the installed build writes the autostart.
- `daemon --start` calls the new `ensure_here()`, so the installed build never delegates to itself.
- **Checked:** every release binary contains its build id as plain bytes (air, vps, and Windows `mesh.exe` and `meshw.exe`).
- **Spec:** §6.6 "Taking over after a new binary".

body:
💡 What: Introduced a dedicated `keywordRegexCache` to `internal/worker/alert_worker.go` to store compiled regexes using the raw keyword string as the cache key.
🎯 Why: Previously, `getKeywordRegex` constructed a full regex pattern string (e.g., `(?i)\b` + `regexp.QuoteMeta(keyword)` + `\b`) *before* checking the cache. This string concatenation caused memory allocations on every function call, even for cache hits. This function is called repeatedly inside a tight loop for every asset keyword against every CVE description.
📊 Impact: Eliminates memory allocations and reduces CPU overhead (string concatenation + `QuoteMeta`) on cache hits, making the alert evaluation loop measurably faster and generating less garbage.
🔬 Measurement: Run a CPU and heap allocation profile over `processAlerts`. The allocations in `getKeywordRegex` will drop to zero for repeated keywords.

author: palbibek
body:
## What broke

In Chrome 156, `element.scrollIntoView()` returns a Promise. Two effects returned it from an arrow body:

- `components/session/SessionChat.tsx` (the chat)
- `app/sessions/[id]/subagents/[subagentId]/page.tsx` (a subagent's page)

React treats whatever an effect returns as its cleanup, and calls it before the effect runs again. Here it called a Promise: `TypeError: destroy is not a function`, and the page crashed. When you open an older session, its history loads and the message count changes. The cleanup runs right away, so the page crashes just after it opens.

## The fix

React's rule (react.dev, `useEffect`: setup "can optionally return a cleanup function"; react-dom warns "An effect function must not return anything besides a function, which is used for clean-up"). There is one hook, `lib/session/useScrollToEnd.ts`. Its effect body is a statement, so it returns nothing. Both pages now use it.

## Tests

`useScrollToEnd.test.ts` has three tests:
- The hook scrolls on each change. When `scrollIntoView` returns a Promise, React reports no error.
- The same check catches the crash when it is given the old arrow form. An error boundary keeps the reproduction inside the test.
- Nothing happens before the end element exists.

I changed the hook back to return the Promise to check the first test. The test then fails. tsc, eslint and vitest (48 files, 247 tests) pass.

author: alexdima
body:
Fixes #210371

## Problem
In languages that only have block comments (HTML, Markdown, CSS…), `<!-- MARK: Label -->` shows up in the minimap as **"Label -->"**. The default `editor.minimap.markSectionHeaderRegex` captures everything to the end of the line, so the closing token ends up in the label.

## Change
- `FindSectionHeaderOptions` gets optional `blockCommentStartToken` and `blockCommentEndToken`. It stays a plain object, so it can still go to the worker.
- `SectionHeaderDetector.createOptions` fills both from the language's `commentsConfiguration`.
- `collectMarkHeaders` removes a trailing end token **only when the captured header is inside a block comment**: scanning the line in order up to the start of the `separator`/`label` captures leaves the language's block comment open. Measuring from the captures (not the match start) also covers custom regexes that consume the opener, such as `^<!--\s*MARK:\s*(?<label>.*)$`, and the in-order scan handles identical start/end tokens such as Python's `"""`. So `<!-- MARK: Label -->` and `/* MARK: Label */` are cleaned up, while `// MARK: Regex /foo.*/` in JavaScript keeps its full label.
- When a custom separator group swallows part of the token (`<!-- MARK: - -->` with `(?<separator>[- ]*)`), only the token is removed and the separator line is kept. Separator and label are only joined this way when the captures are contiguous in the source. The default regex's `<!-- MARK: -->` (separator `-`, label `->`) still produces no header.

### Why not change the marker regex?
The regex defines *what a marker is*. It is a user setting (`editor.minimap.markSectionHeaderRegex`) shared by every language, so it can't know each language's comment syntax. Hardcoding `-->|*/` into the default would miss other languages and every custom regex, and could eat legitimate label text. The comment tokens come from the language configuration, and they are used only to remove the syntax of the enclosing block comment.

## Tests
`./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/editor/test/common/services/findSectionHeaders.test.ts` → 20 passing. Against the previous revision of this PR, the 2 newest regression tests fail.
- HTML `-->` and CSS/JS `*/` are stripped inside block comments.
- `// MARK: Regex /foo.*/`, `// MARK: … */ trailing`, and `/* closed */ // MARK: … */` keep their labels.
- A custom separator regex with `<!-- MARK: - -->` keeps the separator line.
- A custom regex that consumes `<!--` still strips `-->`; non-contiguous captures (`<!-- MARK: - -> -->`) keep their label.
- Python `""" MARK: Doc Section """` → `Doc Section`; `"""closed""" # MARK: Quote """` keeps `Quote """`.
- No tokens, and a custom regex whose label excludes the token, are left unchanged.

## Visual verification
`mark.md` with `<!-- MARK: Label -->`: the header ink width went from 81px (`Label -->`) before to 45px (`Label`) after (first revision; the HTML case behaves the same in this revision).

**Validation (macOS arm64):**
- The changed files are identical between this PR's base and `d1a91b3af88`. Unit tests were run there after `pnpm run build-fast --client-only` (the PR base's `node_modules` were stale), with the results above.
- `pnpm run eslint <changed files>` → clean
- `pnpm run typecheck-client` → passed

## Notes for reviewer
`MinimapModel.getSectionHeaderText` caches the fitted text in an LRU keyed by the raw text. That is unaffected here, because the stripped text is a new key. Detection is still per-line text, not tokenization (the worker has no tokens). A block comment opened on an *earlier* line isn't detected, so the token is kept there, which is the conservative choice.

🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @alexdima.

## Change

The rule documents contradicted themselves between "absolute" and "contextual" wording (verified in #98). An agent that read §14 last would card every view; one that read line 6 or §18 last would not. This PR scopes the four absolute passages to the recipe they came from and adds a lint so the wording cannot return.

- `DESIGN-LANGUAGE.md` §10 → "Selection UI inside consumer-service cards" + `Scope:` line (native selects, radio groups, checkbox filters valid elsewhere, §18).
- §14 → "Consumer-service default: content lives inside cards" + `Scope:` line (flat reading flow, selectable rows, uncarded sections valid under other contracts, §18 / METHODOLOGY §2).

body:

right people know. There are language-specific teams for reviewing recipes.

| Language        | Name of review team           |

Then, a bot will label the PR as 'review-requested'.

Due to GitHub limitations, first time contributors to conda-forge are unable
to ping conda-forge teams directly, but you can [ask a bot to ping the team][1]
using a special command in a comment on the PR to get the attention of the
`staged-recipes` team. You can also consider asking on our [Zulip chat][2]
if your recipe isn't reviewed promptly.

[1]: https://conda-forge.org/docs/maintainer/infrastructure.html#conda-forge-admin-please-ping-team
[2]: https://conda-forge.zulipchat.com

All apologies in advance if your recipe PR does not receive prompt attention.
This is a high volume repository and the reviewers are volunteers. Review times
vary depending on the number of reviewers on a given language team and may be days
or weeks. We are always looking for more staged-recipe reviewers. If you are
interested in volunteering, please contact a member of @conda-forge/core.
We'd love to have the help!
-->

Checklist

- [x] Title of this PR is meaningful: e.g. "Adding my_nifty_package", not "updated recipe".
- [x] Recipe uses the v1 `recipe.yaml` format, or this PR explains the exceptional requirement for deprecated v0.
- [x] License file is packaged (see the [v1 example recipe](https://github.com/conda-forge/staged-recipes/blob/main/recipes/example-v1/recipe.yaml) for an example).
- [x] Source is from official source.
- [x] Package does not vendor other packages. (If a package uses the source of another package, they should be separate packages or the licenses of all packages need to be packaged).
- [x] If static libraries are linked in, the license of the static library is packaged.
- [x] Package does not ship static libraries. If static libraries are needed, [follow CFEP-18](https://github.com/conda-forge/cfep/blob/main/cfep-18.md).
- [x] Build number is 0.
- [x] A tarball (`url`) rather than a repo (e.g. `git_url`) is used in your recipe (see [here](https://conda-forge.org/docs/maintainer/adding_pkgs.html#build-from-tarballs-not-repos) for more details).
- [x] GitHub users listed in the maintainer section have posted a comment confirming they are willing to be listed there.
- [x] When in trouble, please check our [knowledge base documentation](https://conda-forge.org/docs/maintainer/knowledge_base.html) before pinging a team.

## Summary

Adds EnergyPlus 26.2.0, the U.S. Department of Energy's whole-building energy
simulation program, using a v1 recipe adapted from
[EnergyPlus-conda](https://github.com/luzechao/EnergyPlus-conda).

- Builds from the official tagged source tarball, verified with SHA-256
  `0f77c71449e2f03fe33c8db2ab1f16aa210322ea978d62bdc38bc47317be408b`.
- Includes the simulation executable, `pyenergyplus` API, required data files,
  and command-line preprocessing/postprocessing tools.
- Uses the environment's Python runtime and standard library instead of
  bundling Python; omits bundled examples and optional graphical applications.
- Declares conda-forge C/C++/Fortran compilers and the C standard library.
  Windows uses MSVC with MinGW gfortran for CMake's Fortran subprojects,
  and GNU Make from conda-forge, without provisioning the runner's MSYS2.
- Requires Python 3.12 or newer and macOS 13.3 or newer.
- Lists `luzechao` as the recipe maintainer.

## Validation

### Exact staged-recipes submission: Windows

[Windows CI run](https://github.com/luzechao/EnergyPlus-conda/actions/runs/41976095125)
**passed** for both Python 3.12 and 3.13 on Windows 2022.
The workflow checked out staged-recipes commit
`542c82e9cf9876354b64775478d1d027a2ac5b1f`.

Both jobs passed the helper tests, built the tarball-based package, ran its
package tests, and uploaded the resulting `.conda` artifact. No packages were
published.

Commands run by the workflow:

```text
python recipes/energyplus/test_prepare.py

rattler-build build --recipe recipes/energyplus/recipe.yaml --target-platform win-64 --variant python=3.12 --variant c_stdlib=vs --variant c_compiler=vs2022 --variant cxx_compiler=vs2022 -c conda-forge --package-format conda:19

rattler-build build --recipe recipes/energyplus/recipe.yaml --target-platform win-64 --variant python=3.13 --variant c_stdlib=vs --variant c_compiler=vs2022 --variant cxx_compiler=vs2022 -c conda-forge --package-format conda:19
```

All three commands **passed**; rattler-build was pinned to version 0.80.0.
Package tests cover the CLI, Python API, and an upstream Python-plugin
simulation. The plugin test verifies that embedded Python loads the standard
library and extension modules from the installed conda environment, even with
invalid `PYTHONHOME` and `PYTHONPATH` values.

### Local validation

- `pixi run -e conda-smithy conda-smithy recipe-lint --conda-forge recipes/energyplus` -- **passed**.
- `pixi run -e conda-smithy shellcheck recipes/energyplus/build.sh` -- **passed**.
- `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/python3 recipes/energyplus/test_prepare.py` -- **passed**, five tests.
- `git diff --check` -- **passed**.
- Source patches were successfully applied to files extracted from the
  checksummed tarball; required vendored source paths and plugin fixtures
  were verified.
- Dependency rendering/solving passed for Linux x86-64, Windows x86-64,
  and macOS ARM64 with Python 3.12 and 3.13.

## Licensing

EnergyPlus uses `LicenseRef-EnergyPlus`. The recipe packages its upstream
license and available third-party `LICENSE*`, `COPYING*`, copyright notices,
and ObjexxFCL license files.

The build retains upstream bundled libraries and statically links internal and
third-party targets into the shared API. The audit of the Windows Python 3.12
artifact found no shipped static implementation archives: the sole `.lib` is
the import library for `energyplusapi.dll`.

The recipe now packages Windows-CalcEngine's `Legal.txt`, supplemental
valijson 1.0.5/nlohmann JSON 3.12.0/MIT milo license texts, and notices extracted
from the pinned bundled BCVTB, DElight, fast_float, milo, nlohmann, valijson,
SQLite, zlib/MiniZip, and active SSC subtrees. Source paths and source
availability are retained in the notice files.

A license-only verification build using the exact `license_file` list passed.
Archive inspection confirmed all 61 selected license/notice files are
packaged byte-for-byte under `info/licenses/`.

body:
## What this does

Feature #73, "Two Features, one engine". Two stories, built one after the other on this branch.

- **#82 Two sessions build two Features at the same time, safely.** Each `/implement <fid>` session claims its Feature (a second session on the same Feature is refused, naming who holds it; a take-over after 30 idle minutes is announced). Under `verify-lock: global` every suite in every session queues on one test lock (`test-lock.js`). The disk check counts the other Features being built; git lock files held by another session are retried; numbered files never take a number another Feature reserved. ADR-0006 records one session per Feature.
- **#83 One story loop for every run.** A standalone story or bug runs the same loop as a Feature story: tests first, red recorded, code, test runner, two story reviewers, the fix re-reviewed over its own diff, one commit. Retired: `story-executor-agent`, waves and `must_fail`, the plan-lint hook, `scripts/tdd-rig.js`, `/troubleshoot` and its investigator (a failed e2e gate goes to `/debug` and the prover's diagnose job). The installer removes them, but only when the harness installed them.

## Commits

- 6101470 feat: two sessions build two Features at the same time, safely (Story #82)
- be3de2f feat: one story loop for every run; retire the executor, waves, plan-lint and /troubleshoot (Story #83)
- 0722de6, c9e21df, 7b24ceb, a843fa4: the Feature panel's findings, fixed in five rounds (rounds 4 and 5 approved by the person after round 3 still found new findings)

## Review

The seven-check Feature panel (security, architecture, acceptance, made-false on opus; complexity, dead code, loosened on sonnet) ran on the whole branch, then on each fix round. Triage: `tasks/features/73/review/findings.md`.

What the rounds fixed, in short: a story's Goal has one home; the test lock reaches every suite; the session-start cleanup leaves a live Feature's worktree alone (`feature-state.js live`); git writes go through `worktree.js git`, which runs only the run's own fixed shapes (named files, the checked-out branch, never main) and which the safety hook judges as the git command it runs, so this branch's hook asks and denies everything main's does; test-lock escaping and stale-lock edge cases; the updater no longer deletes a person's own file with a retired name.

Not fixed here, with reasons in the triage: the complexity of `claim` and `test-lock` (each layer fixes a #82 review blocker).

## Deferred (registered)

- #85 Test that the hook registries agree (and the `todo-render-trigger.js` example mismatch)
- #86 Hold the shared test lock across a whole start, test and stop sequence
- #87 Updater can delete a person's own files through an old backfilled manifest (older than this Feature)
- #88 worktree.js push can be steered onto main by a deliberate git config

Accepted and logged: a test lock left by a crashed session on the other platform of the same host (WSL vs Windows) waits out the 60-minute timeout; a hand-made `owner` folder inside a lock is treated as ownerless.

## Needs a person

Two demos, on a throwaway project with the harness installed:

1. Two sessions build two Features at once; a third session on one of them is refused. This also shows that Claude Code substitutes `${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID}` in the skill text.
2. A standalone bug follows the loop: test, red, fix, green, no executor wave.

`npm test`: 1129 pass, 0 fail; lint clean (at a843fa4).

Closes #82
Closes #83

From `tasks/features/73/decisions-log.md`. The first #82 and #83 lines were lost when a fix job overwrote the file; #82's decisions are in its commit and ADR-0006, and the #83 lines below were rebuilt from the builders' reports.

Closes #418

Adds the two small-signal silicon NPNs that the classic pedals use, and the 1N914 part row.

### What changed

- `models/bjts.lib` (new): `Q2N3904` and `Q2N5088`, each with the provenance header (datasheet title, manufacturer, URL, fit points, author, license).
  - `Q2N3904`: `IS=1e-14 BF=200`. IS fits VBE = 0.655 V at IC = 1 mA, VCE = 5 V; BF 200 sits between the sheet's 70 min at 1 mA and 300 max at 10 mA.
  - `Q2N5088`: `IS=8e-14 BF=500`. IS fits VBE = 0.601 V at IC = 1 mA, VCE = 5 V; BF 500 sits between the sheet's 350 min at 1 mA and 900 max at 0.1 mA.
  - Only IS and BF are in the models: the sheets tabulate nothing else in the small-signal region.
- `models/parts.toml`: rows `2N3904` (npn, `Q2N3904`, TO-92), `2N5088` (npn, `Q2N5088`, TO-92) and `1N914` (diode, `1N4148`, DO-35), each with a provenance.
- `models/README.md`: the model-file table, the parts table, the palette note, and the "What is not bundled" list.
- `tests/Ssp.Core.Tests/BjtModelTests.cs` (new): a common-emitter fixture (Vce source at 5 V, Vbe source, one NPN) built from `models/bjts.lib`; the test bisects Vbe until IC = 1 mA, then asserts hFE and VBE(on) inside the datasheet band for each part. Also asserts the three parts rows, their kinds and models, and the four provenance header tags.

### Proof

### Out of scope

Germanium transistors; the editor palette default NPN model; the changelog (written in the release PR).

body:
This pull request introduces three new composable screens for the games feature: `GameDetailScreen`, `GamePlayScreen`, and `GameResultScreen`. These screens together provide a complete flow for viewing game details, playing a mini-game, and displaying the results after completion. The implementation uses Jetpack Compose and leverages the app's design system components for a consistent look and feel.

The most important changes are:

**New Game Screens Implementation:**

* Added `GameDetailScreen` to display mini-game details, statistics, instructions, and a button to start the game. This screen uses several custom composables for artwork, statistics, and layout.
* Added `GamePlayScreen` to handle the quiz gameplay, including question navigation, answer selection, feedback, progress indication, and transition to the result screen. State management is handled with Compose's `rememberSaveable`.
* Added `GameResultScreen` to show the final score, XP earned, and options to replay or return to the games list, with a prominent trophy visual and styled summary card.

**Design System Integration:**

* All screens make extensive use of the app’s design system components such as `EcoAppHeader`, `EcoButton`, and `EcoCard` for consistent UI and theming. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4c529607d48a9aa87f25b02ccd1ecd305e40e8c091ed6365bcf597a9c2171aa8R1-R275) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-12e17058511bb8a507bc3cabb717905ac78bc73765fee11bb63f638f3c279fd3R1-R345) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-c5d5c7aee23810d0041f4125bcf333f27dfbef78a905dd8d9c335aeac399a5e4R1-R208)

**Game Flow and State Management:**

* The game play logic, including answer validation, XP calculation, and result aggregation, is encapsulated within the composables using Compose state primitives, ensuring smooth transitions and user feedback throughout the flow.

These changes lay the groundwork for a polished and interactive mini-games experience in the app.

author: jakeomega
body:
## Summary

**Autonomous Logistics gets a flat crew.** The Trade Center's last trade-quantity method (`pm_trade_center_trade_quantity_advanced_4`, Smart Grids) now cancels International Trading's per-level staff and hires a fixed crew, as the flat-crew AI-managed methods do (#993):

- `level_scaled`: −800 clerks, −200 shopkeepers. That is the whole per-level staff on either base method (`pm_trade_center` and `pm_trade_center_principle_external_trade_2` both employ exactly that), and no other group of the building employs anyone, so the cancel is exact and nets to 0 a level.
- `unscaled`: 1,000 clerks (International Trading's own trade; owner, 2026-11-05) and `building_job_attractiveness_mult = 5`. That is the same crew size and +500% attractiveness as the other flat-crew methods, which hire engineers.
- The Merchant Marine input and the weekly trades stay `workforce_scaled`, so with the crew hired every level still counts (the `ai_managed_flat_output` self-check reads this).

**A marker for robotic or AI-managed methods.** A new script-only boolean building modifier, `building_robotic_or_ai_managed_bool` (`common/modifier_type_definitions/te_automation_policy_modifier_types.txt`, loc "Robotic or AI-Managed"), sits in the `building_modifiers` `unscaled` block of the 39 methods the Automation Policy already counted, and of Autonomous Logistics: 40 in all. Because it's in `unscaled`, it holds at any staffing level. It shows in each method's tooltip, so players can see which methods the laws act on. The Human Labor Quotas preview now points to it and names Autonomous Logistics.

**Automation Policy reads the marker.** `te_ap_runs_automated_method` used to be 160 lines of `is_building_type` / `has_active_production_method` blocks. It is now just `modifier:building_robotic_or_ai_managed_bool = yes`. To count a new method, give it the marker plus the quotas' `disallowing_laws`, and add its building to `te_ap_automatable_building`. The Trade Center is now on that list, and Autonomous Logistics carries the quotas' gate. Only production methods may carry the marker, because a building's `modifier:` read also picks up its country's lines.

## Self-check (an unverified engine fact)

The design depends on a method's `unscaled` script-only building line reaching that building's own `modifier:` read. Nobody has confirmed this in game yet: the grid's `grid_cable_range` check, which tests the same thing, is still open. If the read fails, the automated share reads 0 everywhere, and Robot Tax, the Dividend and Displaced Workers do nothing, with nothing in any log.

So `te_ap_marker_selfcheck` logs `TE_SELF_CHECK OK|BROKEN automation_marker` once a game. It compares the levels on three sample methods, named directly (`te_ap_marker_sample`: Robotic Assembly Lines in a Tooling Workshop, Robotic Service Providers in an Urban Center, Autonomous Logistics in a Trade Center), with the levels among them that read the marker. A partial count waits a month, so a building that changed method just before the count can't trigger a BROKEN. The fallback (restore the per-method list, keep the marker for the tooltip) is in the Self-checks table in `docs/testing/era-13-playtest.md` § Phase 3: Automation Policy, with play-test items 10 and 11.

## Tuning calls for the owner

- Crew profession: settled on clerks (owner, 2026-11-05). Crew size: 1,000, matching the other flat crews.
- Autonomous Logistics is now withdrawn by Human Labor Quotas, like every other marked method. Its levels count toward the automated share (Trade Centers are in the share's base).

## Tests

- `test_automation_policy.py`: the counted methods now come from the marker in the merged PMs, not from the trigger text. New checks: the trigger reads the marker and nothing else; the type is a script-only building boolean declared once, with loc; every marker is `yes` in `building_modifiers` `unscaled`; nothing but production methods carries it; the trigger header's count matches; the self-check's samples are marked methods on the buildings that run them; Autonomous Logistics cancels both base methods' staff exactly and hires a crew of clerks. The existing checks still apply: quotas gate equals the marked set, every group keeps a fallback, the ladder rule, and the share's building list. A mutation run (taking the marker off Robotic Service Providers) fails four of them.
- `test_ai_managed_flat_staff.py`: the attractiveness rule now covers any marked method with a flat crew, so Autonomous Logistics is held to it.
- `pm_costs.py` regenerated Autonomous Logistics' cost comment (`# Employment: -1000`). It touched nothing else.

Local results for the first commit (CI's commands, dummy `VIC3_*` env vars): the full suite (`pytest -n auto --dist loadfile`) gives 11,265 passed and 90 skipped. `ruff check .`, the tab check, `check_localization_files`, `check_loc_spelling --check` and `organize_loc --check` all pass, as do the 37 offline audits in their CI modes (including `pm_employment_audit --strict`, where the Trade Center's level bucket nets to 0 and its unscaled bucket to +1,000, plus `loc_coverage_audit --strict` and `effect_trigger_validity_audit --strict`), `check_post_load_rosters`, `check_gui_lint`, the player guide lint and `build_player_guide.py --check`. The clerk follow-up only swaps the crew's profession, so it was left to CI at the owner's request.

## Player guide

06-politics, "Automation policy": the list of counted methods adds Autonomous Logistics in Trade Centers and notes that each one says Robotic or AI-Managed in its tooltip. PDF rebuilt. The flat crew itself is below the guide's level of detail, since the guide doesn't cover the other flat crews either.

## Docs

`docs/systems/mod_systems/automation_policy.md` (the marker, Autonomous Logistics, counts 40 methods / 26 groups / 47 buildings), `docs/testing/era-13-playtest.md` (items 10–11 and a Self-checks table), `docs/testing/ai-managed-flat-staff-playtest.md` (item 7), and one paragraph in `docs/guides/scripting_best_practices.md` on marking methods with a building boolean instead of a hand-kept `has_active_production_method` list.

<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:

  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #213027

## Problem
Each section header (for example `#pragma region`, `//#region` or `// MARK:`) is drawn as a label `sectionHeaderFontSize * 1.5` tall, but a minimap line is only 2–4px tall. When headers are on adjacent or nearby lines, such as nested regions or a long region title followed by another region a few lines later, the labels overlap. The later label paints over the earlier one, and neither can be read.

## Change
In `InnerMinimap._renderSectionHeaders`, the decorations are already sorted by line. A colliding label is now **pushed down to start just below the previous label** instead of being drawn on top of it, so the labels stack:

- Every header stays visible and readable, so a user looking for a section still finds it in the minimap.
- The first label of a group stays exactly at its line, and each stacked label sits directly beneath it, still next to the code it belongs to.
- Headers that don't collide are drawn exactly as before.
- Separator-only decorations keep their position.

An earlier revision of this PR hid the colliding labels instead. That made the sections invisible in the minimap, which is worse for people scanning for them.

## Visual verification
Columns, left to right: Insiders 1.145.0 (overlap), the previous revision of this PR (the "Beta" label is dropped), and this revision (stacked).

Rows, top to bottom:
1. Adjacent `#pragma region Alpha` / `Beta`.
2. Three nested `//#region Outer / Middle / Inner`.
3. A long region title with another region two lines later (the case in the issue comments).

![213027-stack-compare.png](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/91cf1db8-7bde-4ca4-88d7-53fdf624d24c)

Measured on the decorations canvas: rows of header ink grouped into bands, one band per readable label.

| File | Insiders | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| adjacent.cpp | `[5,7],[13,25]` (garbled) | `[5,20],[32,44]` (two labels) |
| nested.ts | `[5,7],[12,15],[21,33]` (garbled) | `[5,17],[31,44],[59,71]` (three labels) |
| longtitle.ts | `[4,15],[21,33]` (overlapping) | `[4,20],[32,44]` (two labels) |
| spaced.ts | `[4,17],[141,153]` | `[4,17],[141,153]` (unchanged) |

**Validation (macOS arm64):**
- `node test/scenario/out/runScenario.js .build/vscode-playwright-mcp/213027-stack.cjs --dev` after `pnpm run build-fast --client-only`: Dev build, all four steps passed. The previous revision of this PR fails step S2, because "Beta" is not drawn.
- `pnpm run eslint src/vs/editor/browser/viewParts/minimap/minimap.ts`: clean.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed.

## Notes for reviewer
- A tall stack covers a few more minimap lines under the labels. This is the same trade-off a single long label already makes, and the labels keep their translucent background.
- #346191 (the #244902 fix) touches the same function and has already merged. This branch merges cleanly with current `main`.

_Requested by **あまぎ れい** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01YMpxkYjtLC2kxDmnDR6tGW?thread=cmsg_01YMpxkYjtLC2kxDmnDR6tGW6gdzP6JWCHMi8hfakJHZxv)_

Follow-up to the review of #153 (the upload route).

## What changes

- **P1, retry after a failed write.** When an upload of new bytes failed after its record was written (the store transaction failed), the item stayed on the older bytes. A retry with the same new bytes then found the record unchanged and answered `changed: false` with the old version. `SourceSync.upload` now compares the item's stored `content_hash` with the bytes, so the retry stores them, answers the new version and publishes its `document.fetched`. Regression test: `engine/source-sync/test/sync.test.ts`, "an upload that failed after its record was written stores the file when retried", on memory and Postgres (it fails without the fix).
- **x-inspiration-modified is tighter.** It must carry its offset (`Z` or `±hh:mm`) and name a day the calendar has; `2026-02-30T09:00:00Z` and `2026-11-04T09:12:00` are now 400. The web app sends `toISOString()` and the business layer passes the header through, so neither changes.
- **One writing process.** `upload()`'s doc comment says uploads take turns within a process and that the engine runs one writing process for now, as the review noted.

## Checks

`biome check`, `tsc` and the source-sync and upload tests with the stack up pass locally.

author: dnplus
body:
## Why
A full company directory sync takes ~12 minutes, past the 300-second limit on an agent's commands. New data dirs therefore fell back to `--online` hydration, which took minutes per lookup. Company directory content is the same for every employee, so one account syncs it and everyone else imports a file.

## What
- `m2k directory export --output <file> [--addressbook <sel>]`: writes the cached company branch (default: the site profile's `company_directory_root`; personal address books are never included) as `m2k-directory/1` JSON, atomically.
- `M2K_DIRECTORY_CACHE=<file>`: `directory search/resolve/self/chart` import the file once per `generated_at`, under the sync lock, applying its collections as authoritative snapshots (departed people disappear). A missing or bad file warns on stderr and the lookup continues on the local cache. Nothing is written next to the file (works on a read-only mount).
- Fix: `directory sync --scope company` failed with `項目識別碼已被快照範圍外的資料使用`. Caches written before collection ids were canonicalised keep lowercase `%3d%3d` ids; a resync emits `%3D%3D`, `parse_contact` reuses the old id, and `replace_items` rejected it. `apply_collection_snapshot` now treats stored collections with the same DAV identity as aliases and replaces them in place.

## Verification
- `cargo test`: all suites pass (2 new tests in `tests/directory.rs`: legacy-encoding company sync against a mock CardDAV server, and export/import round trip incl. personal-book exclusion, authoritative removal, no re-import).
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean, `cargo fmt --check` clean.
- Against a real site: exporting the company branch took well under a second; a fresh data dir with no password resolved a person in about half a second including the import, and in tens of milliseconds afterwards.

## Not verified
- A full real company sync with this build (~12 min) has not been re-run; the regression test reproduces the exact real error.
- After such a resync, re-export so the shared file carries canonical ids.

## 概要 開発ツールを最新のメジャーに寄せる作業の 2 本目。18 個の package.json で tsup を ^9.0.0 に上げる。tsup 9 の破壊的変更は Node 22.18 未満の切り捨てだけで、`.node-version` の 24.22.1 は満たす。 当初は vite 8 を 2 本目にする予定だった。しかし Storybook 8.6 の `@storybook/builder-vite` の peer が `vite ^4 || ^5 || ^6` なので、vite 8 は Storybook 10 の後に回す。 ## build 出力の変化 同梱の esbuild が 0.28 に上がり、tsconfig の `target: ES2022` に従って `useDefineForClassFields` を true として扱うようになった。tsup 8 と tsup 9 で同じソースを build し、全 18 パッケージの出力を比べた。差分は 81 ファイル、+205 / -74 行。 - **クラスフィールドの宣言（101 件）:** パラメータプロパティなどが、クラス本体に宣言として現れるようになった。どれもコンストラクタで代入しているので、値は変わらない。基底クラスでは `Object.keys` の並び順だけが変わる - **`HTTPException` の `message`（nakadachi-interactor）:** `public message` のパラメータプロパティが、Error の列挙されない `message` を列挙されるプロパティに定義し直していた。そのため `JSON.stringify`・スプレッド・`Object.keys` に message が現れていた。パラメータプロパティにするのをやめて、tsup 8 と同じ出力に戻した（f8b4bcb） - **d.ts:** `export { type X }` が `export type { X }` の形に変わった。公開している型は変わらない。TS 5.9 の NodeNext で、.mts / .cts の両方から読めることを確認した - **その他:** `__esm` ヘルパーに例外処理が入った。chunk のファイル名（ハッシュ）が変わった ## 確認したこと - `turbo run build lint test --force` は 56/56 成功。警告の数は変わらない - npm audit は 0 件 公開パッケージの実行時の挙動は tsup 8 と同じにそろえたので、changeset は付けない。 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Confidence Score: 4/5

マージを妨げる不具合は見つかりませんでしたが、例外の非列挙性を守るテストの追加を推奨します。

Findings

1.  **列挙可否の変更を検出できない** ▶
Fix with agent prompt `````markdown ### Issue 1 packages/nakadachi-interactor/src/exceptions.ts:6 `HTTPException.message` の非列挙性を維持する修正に、回帰テストがありません。既存テストは新しく作った例外との比較だけなので、両方の `message` が列挙可能になっても検出できません。 ビルド後の ESM・CommonJS から `MethodNotAllowedException` を作り、`message` の値と非列挙性を確認するテストの追加を推奨します。 Note: If this suggestion doesn't match your team's coding style, reply to this and let me know. I'll remember it for next time! --- For each issue above, determine whether it is valid and should be fixed. If so, fix it directly. `````

Summary

18 パッケージの `tsup` を `^9.0.0` に更新しています。 - All 18 package builds now use tsup 9. - HTTP exception messages keep their usual Error behavior. Reviews (1) · Last reviewed commit: ["fix(nakadachi-interactor): HTTPException..."](https://github.com/rymizuki/rym-lib/commit/f8b4bcbd752293e86b839c8b1f22f4d7aa658c5b) · [Reviewed by Greptile](https://www.greptile.com/?utm_source=greptile_review&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=review_public&utm_content=rymizuki/rym-lib)

body:
## Windows install errors

- A refusal in any of 38 Windows languages is classified as a permission problem, accents or not; a payload step that fails for an unknown reason counts as one too.
- Windows error text that arrived as the wrong code page is read back in its own language (new `desktop/src/windowsText.js`), so the log and the error details stay readable.
- A blocked folder is retried after 5 s and 20 s before the install gives up, and the screen says "Folder is blocked, retrying (n/m)".

## Send feedback in the open-source edition

- Send feedback opens the same inquiry form as Customer support when the build carries the support address, and the GitHub issues page when it does not.
- The open-source form is titled Feedback and has no Payment or refund kind.
- Both editions carry `PERSODUB_INQUIRY_URL`; the Windows workflows pass it from the repository secret.

author: janmikes
body:
## What changed

S-23.9b (research/19 § 5.2 "Task", TD-033): the 1 986-line `task-detail.tsx` with thirteen equally weighted sections is now a pull-request page, split by part:

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `task-header.tsx` | `PageHeader`: ticket title (untrusted) + key muted, `StateLabel`, one meta line (template · stage · cost so far · age), `PhaseTrack`; **one primary action by state** (`taskPrimaryAction`: *Hand back…* / *Answer* / *Approve…* / *Resume* / none) and a `···` menu (Pause, Resume, Take over…, Retry stage…, Return to stage…, Rework…, Raise this task's cap…, Download JSON, Cancel task…) |
| `task-dialogs.tsx` | one dialog per multi-field/destructive command, carrying the inline forms' fields under the same labels; the stage-command form state lives in the page so the picked stage and a gate-feedback untick outlive a dialog |
| `task-callout.tsx` | beacon `Flash` for open questions (answered inline), pending approvals (decided inline), an escalation (the row's recorded word + its ways out) and a breakdown waiting for a maintainer |
| `task-tab.ts` | `?tab=` (zod, `.catch`: an unknown tab opens Overview); `?artifact=` selects Artifacts |
| `task-overview.tsx` · `task-artifacts.tsx` · `task-runs.tsx` · `task-activity.tsx` | the four tabs (timeline now with duration + cost + return glyph; artifacts list + body with raw JSON behind Details; runs `ListBox` with `StatusIcon`; who-did-what as a `Timeline`) |
| `task-checks.tsx` · `task-checks-text.ts` · `stage-outcome.ts` | the merge box (summary line, rows of icon + label + value, definition tooltip, basis in an expandable row), the cost `<meter>`, the links; the sentences moved, the statuses are new |

`ui/`: `Flash` tone `beacon`; `ActionMenuLinkItem`; `DownloadLink` accepts a host's props (spread first, so never its `href`/`download`/label); `TimelineItem` takes a test id. The Ask, Feedback and Breakdown submit buttons and the callout's buttons are no longer primary, so a view has one beacon.

## Acceptance → tests

1. Header + one primary + menu/dialogs → `task-page.test.tsx` › "the header", "one primary action per state" (census of beacon buttons in `main` per state), "the ··· menu"; `stage-commands.test.tsx`, `take-over.test.tsx`, `raise-task-cap.test.tsx`, `task-record.test.tsx` (each gained the open-menu/dialog step; same labels).
2. Callout → `task-page.test.tsx` › "the needs-you callout" (inline answer + header *Answer* focus, inline approve + *Approve…* dialog with reason, escalation word, absent when nothing waits); `stage-commands.test.tsx` (HINT + callout buttons); `breakdown-panel.test.tsx`.
3. Tabs → `task-page.test.tsx` › "the tabs" (`?tab=`, `?artifact=` selects Artifacts, raw JSON behind Details, unknown tab, schema/search helpers); `run-cost.test.tsx`, `take-over.test.tsx` (`?tab=runs`), `task-record.test.tsx` (`?tab=activity`); `task-timeline.test.tsx`, `live-stage.test.tsx` unchanged.
4. Merge box → `checks-panel.test.tsx` **unchanged** (eleven labels, both directions); `task-page.test.tsx` › "the merge box" (summary never passes an undecided/unrecorded row, statuses, `<meter>` without `style`).
5. Split → files above; `no-html.test.ts` now finds `<ExternalLink` in `task-checks.tsx`; `untrusted.test.tsx` › "takes a host's props, and never its href, download or label".
6. e2e → `screens.spec.ts`, `xss.spec.ts` updated (open ···, open a tab, expand a row); `verify:web-e2e` PASS. User guide § 4 rewritten; technical/09's Task detail row updated. Bundle: the task route stays a lazy chunk (`bundle:check` 269 279 B of 300 000).

## Decisions I made

- Commands the server refuses for **everybody** are not offered: Resume only on `paused`/`needs_human`; Pause not on a paused/finished task; Cancel not on a finished one; no stage command on a task with no stage (was an empty state — the e2e now asserts the menu has none); `···` is not drawn when it would be empty.
- Header *Answer* focuses the callout's answer box rather than duplicating the form; *Approve…* opens a dialog with an optional reason.
- Merge-box statuses are derived only from the value's own record (documented in `task-checks-text.ts`); *required* = CI, tamper, rebase, review threads, verdict, criteria, dependencies, questions, approvals.
- Feedback's submit is default tone on the run page too (shared component).

## Not done (BACKLOG)

- 850 escalation brief is not on the task DTO (callout shows the row's recorded word instead).
- 851 no chat thread URL on the task DTO (links: ticket, MR).
- 852 `TASK_STATE_STATUS` may duplicate S-23.9a's board-card map.
- 853 returns drawn as glyph + *try N*, no `returned_to` on the DTO.

author: alexdima
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #244902

## Problem
With `editor.minimap.size: "fill"`, `MinimapOptions` makes the canvas backing store wider than its CSS box (`canvasInnerWidth` is multiplied by up to `min(2, minimapScale / configuredScale)`, while `canvasOuterWidth` is not). The browser then shrinks the canvas horizontally to fit, which distorts the section header labels: they look narrow and squeezed. With `fit`/`proportional` the ratio is exactly `pixelRatio` and labels look fine.

## Change
In `InnerMinimap._renderSectionHeaders`:
- Compute `horizontalScale = max(1, canvasInnerWidth / (canvasOuterWidth * pixelRatio))`. It is `1` for every non-fill configuration, so nothing changes there.
- Draw the labels inside `ctx.save(); ctx.scale(horizontalScale, 1) … ctx.restore()`, so the CSS downscale cancels out.
- Fit the text and the background to `labelAreaWidth = canvasInnerWidth / horizontalScale`.

## Visual verification
`page.html` with `<!-- MARK: Section Header -->`, measured by the fraction of the canvas width the header ink covers. Before: fill 48% vs fit 72% (squeezed). After: fill 57% vs fit 57% (identical). The fit value changed only because the combined build also includes the #210371 fix, which drops the ` -->`. Before/after (fill):

![Before and after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a8cba56d-2769-4d96-8cb7-cf4a74503d43)

**Validation** (macOS arm64, with all four minimap fixes in one build):
- An automated UI scenario measured the minimap canvas in Insiders 1.145.0 (before) and in a dev build with the fixes (after).
- ESLint on the changed files and the client type check pass.

## Notes for reviewer
This touches the same function as the #213027 PR; they merge cleanly.

author: riyaagrahari
body:
## Summary
Harness owner week-2 task : add the Gate 2 suites that were missing from `run_harness.py`.

- `--suites in22`: IN22-Gen fertility (tokens / word), same method as FLORES and as `BrahmicTokenizer-131K/evaluate_fertility_in22.py`. Pass `--in22-parquet`, or it reads the HF cache (dataset is gated).
- `--suites heldout`: tokens / char and tokens / word on the tokenizer sample's held-out parquet packs. Pass `--heldout-dir`.
- `--suites roundtrip`: `decode(encode(text))` must equal the tokenizer's own normalisation of the text, on up to 1,000 docs per pack (`--roundtrip-docs`, default 1000). Docs are chosen by sha256(`doc_id`) so every run uses the same set. Local `tokenizer.json` only (baseline and `--candidate`). Failures print `doc_id` + offset only, never the text.

Also: `--candidate` without the FLORES suite no longer crashes; the pass bar is skipped with a message. HumanEval/MBPP were already in `--suites code`, so no change there.

## Test plan
- [x] Stand-in heldout (code-java pack + synthetic Indic): round trip PASS on baseline and on an NFC-normalizer candidate (normalizer changed 4 docs on purpose).
- [x] Broken-decoder candidate: round trip FAIL, exit code 1.
- [x] Guard rails: missing `--heldout-dir`, unknown suite, missing IN22 cache → clear errors.
- [x] Real sample `heldout/` + C1–C3: not run yet (waiting on CAP sample download). Will post the Gate 2 table after that.

## Example
```bash
python teams/03-tokenizer/harness/run_harness.py \
  --tokenizers BrahmicTokenizer-131K \
  --brahmic-dir /path/to/BrahmicTokenizer-131K \
  --candidate c3=/path/to/c3/tokenizer.json \
  --suites heldout,roundtrip \
  --heldout-dir /path/to/sample_v0/heldout \
  --roundtrip-docs 1000
```

author: apal-rp
body:
## Summary

Implements live order tracking (FR-044 through FR-049) for Brew ni Cat Connect, featuring Supabase Realtime broadcast channels (`order:*`), 30-second polling/reconnection fallback, cryptographic URL-hash token validation for guests (FR-045), server-side ownership checks for authenticated customers (FR-044), 5-stage visual progress tracking (`pending`, `accepted`, `preparing`, `ready`, `completed`), and customer-safe rejected order handling with shop rejection reasons and actionable next steps (FR-049). Includes PR #93 review fixes: restoring the original Section 6 and 5 rules in `execution-paths.md` with the live order tracking flows as a dated update, hiding the Next Steps card for final order statuses (`rejected`, `cancelled`, `completed`), and renumbering test case IDs to `TC-P5-040` through `TC-P5-063`.

## Requirement IDs Addressed

- FR-044: Authenticated order tracking and server-side customer ownership verification
- FR-045: Guest order tracking via cryptographically secure URL-hash possession tokens (`#token=...`)
- FR-046: 5-stage live order progress tracking and history timeline
- FR-047: Supabase Realtime broadcast event listeners on order topics (`status-changed`)
- FR-048: Connection drop fallback, offline state indicator, manual refresh, and 30s background polling
- FR-049: Exceptional and rejected order presentation with rejection reason and customer-safe next steps

## Changes

- **Live Order Tracking Component & Hook (`OrderStatusTracker`, `useOrderStatus`):** Implemented real-time subscription, event broadcast handling, re-fetching canonical state via `fetchOrder()`, 30s background polling, visibilitychange refresh, deduplication, and automatic cleanup on terminal statuses.
- **Access Control & Security:** Added SHA-256 token hashing for guest possession links stored in hash fragments (never transmitted in HTTP request headers, access logs, or Referer headers) and server-side `customer_id` ownership checks via Supabase RPC `get_online_order`.
- **Review Fixes (PR #93):**
  - Restored original Section 6 diagram and 5 rules in `docs/execution-paths.md`, retaining the implementation flows as a dated update (`### Update (2026-11-04, PR #93)`).
  - Hidden the Next Steps card on `/orders/[reference]` when order status is final (`rejected`, `cancelled`, `completed`) using `isFinalOrderStatus(order.status)`.
  - Added focused unit test (`TC-P5-063`) proving that the Next Steps card is hidden for a rejected order and displayed for non-final statuses.
  - Preserved test ID numbering (`TC-P5-040` through `TC-P5-063`).
- **Review fixes I made in `18e821a` (Rodnee):**
  - `docs/execution-paths.md` section 6: restored the original diagram and moved the detailed diagram under "Update (2026-11-04, PR #93)".
  - `docs/test-cases.md`: PR #94's cases stay section 31, as on `main`; live order tracking is section 32, with rows for TC-P5-063 and TC-P5-064.
  - `tests/unit/order-confirmation-page.test.tsx`: renamed the realtime test from TC-P4-263 (used by PR #94) to TC-P5-064.
  - `tests/e2e/order-tracking.spec.ts`: TC-P5-061 and TC-P5-062 save the five screenshots when `CAPTURE_EVIDENCE=1`; I retook them from a fresh build.
  - FR status note range now ends at TC-P5-064; added the 2026-11-06 development log entry.

## Testing

- **Unit & Integration Tests:** Ran focused Vitest suite for order confirmation (`order-confirmation-page.test.tsx`), `use-order-status.test.ts`, `fetch-order.test.ts`, and `order-status-tracker.test.tsx`. All tests passed successfully (including new unit test `TC-P5-063`).
- **QA & E2E Validation:** Verified via Phase 5 order-tracking evidence suite (`TC-P5-040` to `TC-P5-064`). Full QA suite and screenshots handled by Rodnee per review instructions.
- **Full checks by Rodnee on `18e821a`:**
  - `python3 scripts/validate_phase0_docs.py`: `PHASE0_DOC_VALIDATION=PASS`
  - `NODE_OPTIONS=--no-experimental-webstorage npx vitest run`: Test Files 66 passed (66), Tests 538 passed (538)
  - `npx tsc --noEmit -p .`: passed, no errors
  - `npx eslint . --max-warnings=0`: passed, 0 warnings
  - `npx prettier --check .`: All matched files use Prettier code style!
  - `npm run build`: ✓ Compiled successfully
  - `CI=1 npx playwright test --project=chromium`: 32 passed, 3 skipped
  - `CAPTURE_EVIDENCE=1 npx playwright test tests/e2e/order-tracking.spec.ts --project=chromium`: 2 passed (the five screenshots below)

## Screenshots

![Pending Order](https://github.com/eendor/Brew-ni-Cat-Connect/blob/18e821ab5dc4c5e113dee513f0c2456e1cd88d73/docs/evidence/phase-5/order-tracking/order-tracking-pending.png?raw=true)

![Preparing Order](https://github.com/eendor/Brew-ni-Cat-Connect/blob/18e821ab5dc4c5e113dee513f0c2456e1cd88d73/docs/evidence/phase-5/order-tracking/order-tracking-preparing.png?raw=true)

![Ready Order](https://github.com/eendor/Brew-ni-Cat-Connect/blob/18e821ab5dc4c5e113dee513f0c2456e1cd88d73/docs/evidence/phase-5/order-tracking/order-tracking-ready.png?raw=true)

![Completed Order](https://github.com/eendor/Brew-ni-Cat-Connect/blob/18e821ab5dc4c5e113dee513f0c2456e1cd88d73/docs/evidence/phase-5/order-tracking/order-tracking-completed.png?raw=true)

![Rejected Order](https://github.com/eendor/Brew-ni-Cat-Connect/blob/18e821ab5dc4c5e113dee513f0c2456e1cd88d73/docs/evidence/phase-5/order-tracking/order-tracking-rejected.png?raw=true)

## Security/Privacy Impact

- Guest tracking tokens are passed strictly in the URL hash fragment (`window.location.hash`), ensuring zero exposure in HTTP request headers, server access logs, or Referer headers.
- Server-side RLS and RPC function `get_online_order` enforce strict customer ownership verification (`o.customer_id = auth.uid()`), preventing cross-account data disclosure.
- Zero internal error or database schema leakage on missing or unauthorized orders (returns generic "Order Not Found").

## Known Limitations

- Realtime broadcast delivery relies on Supabase Realtime channel WebSocket connectivity; fallback mechanisms (30s polling, manual refresh, visibilitychange) ensure robust operation when Realtime is unavailable.

## Documentation Updated

- `docs/execution-paths.md`: Restored original Section 6 diagram and 5 rules, with implemented live order-tracking flows documented as a dated PR #93 update.
- `docs/test-cases.md`: Updated test case IDs to `TC-P5-040` through `TC-P5-062`.

## Checklist

- [x] Branch synchronized with `main` and conflicts resolved by Rodnee.
- [x] Original Section 6 restored in `docs/execution-paths.md` with implementation as dated update.
- [x] Next Steps card hidden for final order statuses (`rejected`, `cancelled`, `completed`).
- [x] Focused unit tests added and passing (`TC-P5-063`).
- [x] Test IDs `TC-P5-040` through `TC-P5-063` preserved.
- [x] Focused validation executed successfully.

author: thekalamwala
body:
## ASH-35 Phase 1: reliability + consent + payout fixes from the YANTRA audit

Founder approved Phase 1 (a–i) on 2026-11-05 (ASH-37, "go with all recommendations from agents"). One commit per item so each can be reviewed or reverted on its own. No migration, no flag change, no prod write.

| Item | Commit | What changed |
|---|---|---|
| **b. Contacts opt-outs** | `fix(contacts)` | `contactsService` read contacts/profiles/bookings/purchases/leads unpaged, so PostgREST returned at most 1,000 rows. Contacts past that cap were re-upserted opted-in / not suppressed with a new id, re-subscribing people who had opted out. All reads now page, a read error aborts instead of resetting consent, and the upsert is chunked (500). |
| **c. Route double-transfer** | `fix(payouts)` | `createHeldTransferForBooking` (capture hook + reconciler + admin button) now does an atomic DB claim (`transfer_status='creating'` on a row with no transfer id) before touching Razorpay. It adopts a transfer already on the payment tagged with this booking id (`payments.fetchTransfer`) instead of creating a second one. A transfer that succeeded but failed to save is never marked `failed`, and only the claim holder writes status. `settlementService` treats `creating` as in transit (not manually withdrawable). Admin reconcile runs under the cron's lease (409 if busy). The reconciler gives back the attempt when the claim is held elsewhere. |
| **d. Job stall after deploy** | `fix(jobs): release…` | `runIfDue` leases (2x interval, never released) locked a new pod out for up to 48h. `runLocked` gains `release: true` (only runIfDue + admin reconcile use it; setInterval jobs keep the sticky leader lease). The runIfDue lease is capped at 30 min. A faster retry after an error is opt-in (`retryOnError`), set only on idempotent hourly jobs (otp/rate-limit/ip cleanups, ledger reconcile). Sender jobs keep once per interval. |
| **e. Job errors visible** | `fix(jobs): report…` | Every thrown cron error now reaches Sentry via `runLocked`. Per-row errors in the ledger + payout reconcilers are reported. `otp cleanup` checks its delete error. |
| **f. CRM messages lost** | `fix(crm)` | A thrown dispatch left the row `processing` forever. It now goes through retry/backoff, guarded on `status='processing'` so a row already `sent` is never re-queued. Rows stuck >30 min are marked failed (not resent). A failed sequence enqueue no longer skips the step; it retries in 1h. |
| **g. Queue double-send on >1 instance** | `fix(queues)` | 4 workers leased 2 min against a 300s interval, now 2x their interval. `email_logs` and `campaign_recipients` are claimed (`sending`) before the send. Stale email claims go back to queued (a booking/OTP email is never lost). Stale campaign claims are marked failed (no duplicate marketing). A campaign stays `sending` while any recipient is claimed. No migration: neither status column has a CHECK. |
| **i. Engineering report** | `feat(agents)` | `GET /api/agents/reports/engineering`, same `x-agent-token` gate as the other SUTRA reports. Covers cron health, queue/stuck counts, Route transfer states, and contacts size + consent counts. Counts only, missing table → null. |

**Not in this PR:**
- **a. Backup fail-loud.** The push was refused because the bot token lacks the GitHub `workflow` scope needed to edit `.github/workflows/backup.yml`. The 3-line patch is attached to ASH-35 for the founder to apply. The daily backup still passes green while taking no backup until the secrets are set.
- **h. multer 2.x.** `npm install` is outside my allowlist, so this needs a one-line `npm install multer@^2.0.2` in `server/` by someone with install rights.

### Review summary
- **`code-review` (high):** 9 findings. Fixed 5: reconciler burning attempts on a held claim, error-retry re-sending partial batches, unbounded contacts upsert, campaign marked sent mid-send, untested email claim. Skipped 4 as cosmetic/minor: raw `creating` label in admin UI, duplicated `fetchAll` helper, double contacts scan per admin sync, sweep UPDATE frequency.
- **`cso` (diff, daily 8/10 gate):** 0 findings. The new endpoint is behind the fail-closed agent token and returns counts only. The `.or()` filter value is server-generated. Adoption reads only our own payment's transfers. The double-pay surface is reduced.
- **Tests:** `npm test -- tests/unit`: 375 suites, **3,441 passed**, 0 failed. New tests cover >1,000-row opt-out preservation, read-error abort, upsert chunking, claim lost / adopted / save-failed / cannot-check payout paths, `creating` not withdrawable, lease release + sticky mode, retryOnError on and off, Sentry capture, CRM requeue guard + stuck sweep + sequence retry, queue claim races, and the engineering report (counts, null fallback, no PII, auth).
- Client untouched, so no client build needed.

### Deploy notes
- No migration. `creating` / `sending` are new transient status values on text columns with no CHECK constraint.
- After merge, set `AGENT_REPORT_TOKEN` access for YANTRA to read `/engineering`. Watch `contacts.email_opted_out` / `email_suppressed` for unexpected drops on the first sync.

body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

`MaxQuerySeriesCutoff` must only make a failing query fail sooner. This PR runs the `logqltest` corpus with the cutoff enabled and verifies this.

- Adds a `maxQuerySeriesCutoff` stack option, `withMaxQuerySeriesCutoff`, which sets `EngineOpts.MaxQuerySeriesCutoff` in every engine a stack runs: the querier and the query-frontend. Engine options are now built once per stack by `newEngineOpts` and passed down, rather than rebuilt from defaults at each call site.
- Adds a query-frontend stack with `MaxQuerySeriesCutoff` on, so every script in the corpus runs against it.
- Adds `TestLogQLScripts_ShouldNotChangeAnyOutcomeWithTheMaxQuerySeriesCutoff`, which runs every script under a low `max_query_series` with the cutoff off and on (direct, and query-frontend with and without sharding), and checks each eval ends the same way.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

N/A

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

- A tie is allowed in the comparison: with the cutoff enabled. A query may fail on the series limit where the same query without it fails on a pipeline error in the same step.
- The test lives in `runner_test.go`, not in the corpus, because the extra stack runs with a non-default series limit, which eval expectations can't describe (as per the README)

Último punto del backlog del Estudio: exportar el lienzo a PNG.

Ya se podía bajar el PNG de UNA pantalla o un ZIP con todas. Faltaba **una sola imagen con todo el lienzo**, para pegarla en un chat, una presentación o un ticket.

- Botón **Lienzo PNG** junto a «ZIP + imágenes».

- vitest: 2851 pasan (+5 de la disposición: columnas, filas, alturas distintas, sin huecos a la derecha, reducción).

body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:

* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.

Fixes #202389

## Problem
With `editor.minimap.side: "left"` and side-by-side editor groups, the `editorGroup.border` separator is hidden behind the minimap of the right-hand group. The separator is `.split-view-view:not(:first-child)::before` at `z-index: 5`. The minimap has had `z-index: 5` since #188499 (to paint above sticky scroll, which is `z-index: 4`), and because it comes later in the DOM it wins over the separator.

## Change
`.monaco-editor .minimap` goes from `z-index: 5` to `z-index: 4`, with a comment explaining the constraint.
- Sticky scroll: `.sticky-widget` is also `z-index: 4` in the same stacking context (`.overflow-guard`). The minimap is appended after it, so it still paints on top and #188499 stays fixed. A scenario step checks this (see below).
- Other editor elements at z-index 5 are only gutter glyph margins, which never overlap the minimap.
- Alternatives considered: raising the separator to z-index 20 was tried in #172020 and reverted in #175862 because it covered `tab.activeBorderTop` (#174134). Lowering the minimap avoids touching workbench layering.

## Visual verification
Two groups, left minimap, `editorGroup.border` set to bright green. Rows of the group edge that show green: before 106/1604 (hidden behind the minimap), after 1608/1610. Before/after (top = Insiders, bottom = this change):

![Before and after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2311f651-1f1b-405f-95bd-d421dff2d0bd)

Regression check: with `editor.minimap.side: right` and sticky scroll active in a long JS file, `document.elementsFromPoint` at the overlap returns the minimap (`minimap-decorations-layer`) both before and after.

**Validation** (macOS arm64, with all four minimap fixes in one build):
- An automated UI scenario measured the minimap canvas in Insiders 1.145.0 (before) and in a dev build with the fixes (after).
- ESLint on the changed files and the client type check pass.

body:
## Why

People search for these conflicts as questions. The tracker pages are titled as trackers. US monthly volumes (DataForSEO, 2026-11-05):

| Query | Volume |
| --- | --- |
| what is happening in sudan | 8,100 |
| what is happening in gaza | 4,400 |
| what is happening in nigeria | 2,900 |
| what is happening in congo | 1,600 |
| what is happening in haiti / lebanon | 880 each |
| what is happening in myanmar / afghanistan | 590 each |
| ukraine war tracker | 210 |
| gaza war tracker | 10 |

In Search Console, the tracker pages' current impressions come from "tracker", "monitor" and "live map" queries ("war monitor ua" 63, "red sea tracker" 47, "myanmar civil war map live" 31). The new title therefore keeps "tracker", and the tracker name stays on the page as the eyebrow above the H1.

## What changed

- **Question per crisis.** `scripts/data/crisis-editorial.json` gains a `question` per crisis, for example "What is happening in Sudan?".
- **Title.** `<title>` (and og/twitter title) is `<question> <year> tracker | World Monitor`. The year comes from the editorial `lastReviewed` date, so the title never claims a year the copy was not reviewed in. Titles run 55–71 characters.
- **H1.** The H1 is the question. The eyebrow above it, which used to say "Bounded crisis tracker", now shows the tracker name ("Sudan war tracker").
- **FAQ section.** "Questions about the <conflict>" has matching `FAQPage` JSON-LD. Each answer reuses copy already on the page, so nothing new is unsourced:
  - The question is answered by the latest sourced background paragraph plus "Last reviewed <date> against the linked sources."
  - "What did the last published monthly figures show?" gives the HAPI/HDX totals from the dated weekly snapshot. It names the countries actually summed, names any country missing that period as excluded, and is rendered only when combined totals exist (040a68b053, from review).
  - "Which countries does the tracker cover?" lists the registry coverage.
- **Build validation.** The build fails on a question without a question mark, or on a title over 72 characters.
- **Hormuz.** The Hormuz tracker asks "What is happening in the Strait of Hormuz?". "Is the Strait of Hormuz open?" stays with `/chokepoints/strait-of-hormuz/`, which already uses it as its title.

## Verification

- `node --import tsx --test tests/crawlable-corpus.test.mjs`: 170/170 pass. Three new tests, including a partial-coverage test for the figures answer:
  - Validation rejects a question with no question mark, a missing question, and a title over 72 characters.
  - On each of the 14 built pages:
    - The title equals `crisisPageTitle(question, lastReviewed)`, and titles are unique.
    - The og:title matches the title.
    - The H1 is the question and the eyebrow is the tracker name.
    - The first FAQ answer starts with the latest background paragraph.
    - The `FAQPage` JSON-LD matches the visible questions and answers exactly.
- The existing crisis-family limits still hold: 700+ words per page and mean pairwise overlap under 0.30.
- `tests/schema-graph-contract.test.mts`, crawlable live-tools, pulse refresh and freeze, SEO residue and landing-metadata, canonical-host and country-risk suites: 243 pass, 2 skipped, 0 fail.
- `build-llms-full.mjs --check` and `build-ai-search.mjs --check`: unchanged.
- Built the corpus locally and rendered `/crises/sudan-conflict/` at 1280 and 390 px. There is no horizontal page scroll at 390 px.

Not verified: ranking or CTR change. That shows up in Search Console 2–4 weeks after deploy. The broken logo and the "Live refresh unavailable" badge in the screenshots happen only because the static build was served locally without the API.

author: jun-engineer
body:
## Issue #82 — safe Staging slice, no schema or operational writes

Builds a **pure display-only** `assessB2BReturnProgress` which derives physical return progress from immutable event totals and the requested/approved quantities, avoiding premature status transitions:
- Recognizes pending review, rejected/withdrawn, awaiting dispatch, in-transit, partial inspection, partial physical return and inspected/awaiting credit review.
- Rejects impossible per-line invariants (negative, fractional or over-approved/dispatched/inspected/credit-draft allocation), duplicate IDs, invalid terminal states and early CLOSED.
- Computes outstanding dispatch, in-transit units, inspected but not allocated units and **a review hint** for credit drafts. Draft allocation is never represented as a settled credit/refund.
- Pure financial next-step planner separately identifies missing invoice, reconciliation and possible *manual* settlement-method review; neither PAID nor ISSUED status triggers a payment or automatic offset.

author: tyler-y-liu
body:
## 问题

窗口放大缩小时画面错乱，原因有三：

1. 只靠 50ms 定时器重画，不处理 `WindowEvent::Resized`；新尺寸的帧出来之前，macOS 把旧帧贴在左上角（softbuffer 的 `kCAGravityTopLeft`），露出空白条、面板错位。
2. 办公室的逻辑尺寸随窗口逐像素变化，每变一点就是一套新布局，`store_caps` 跟着改每层工位数（实测宽 1100→1288 之间 8→10→12→14→16），拖动时房间不停重排、小人在楼层间瞬移。
3. 比例只能取美术密度 4 的倍数（4、8、12），跨档时办公室面积直接减半或翻倍；宽 1800 时高度在约 1040 物理像素处 4↔8 跳变，窗口停在附近轻轻一拖就在两套布局间来回切。

## 改动（只改 `src/floating/mod.rs`）

- 收到 `Resized` 立即重画一帧。
- `ResizeHold`：最近 300ms（`RESIZE_SETTLE`）内窗口还在变，就沿用当前显示的比例和逻辑尺寸（放大时多出的区域是背景色，缩小时被面板和底栏盖住），停下后才按新尺寸布局，一次拖动只重排一次工位。
- `fit_for` 加滞回：当前比例下办公室高度仍在 110–300 个单位内（`KEEP_SCALE_UNITS`）且放得下最小布局时保持比例，超出才换档。宽 1800 时 4→8 在约 1200、8→4 在约 880，中间有约 320 物理像素的缓冲。

## 测试

- `a_resize_holds_the_office_until_the_window_settles`：拖动中比例不变，未满 300ms 不变，满了才换；停下后直接改尺寸立即生效。
- `a_height_near_a_scale_step_keeps_the_scale_shown`：分界上下 40px 内长高保持小比例、缩矮保持大比例；远离分界会换档。
- 两个测试都确认过：把对应逻辑去掉后会失败。
- `cargo test --release` 全部通过（73 + 4），编译无警告。

**画面未验证**：改动在云端（Linux，无显示器）完成，跑不了窗口。请在 macOS 上运行 `cargo run --release` 拖动窗口确认：拖动是否流畅；比例 4 时办公室最高 300 个单位，美术是否太小（太小可调低 `KEEP_SCALE_UNITS` 上限）。

author: sachaservan
body: Since v1.1.0, every update of a streaming reply re-rendered the whole chat page and re-parsed the whole reply as markdown, which froze the page on slow phones (including browsers without a JavaScript JIT). With #724 an update renders at most once per frame; this makes each of those renders cheap. - Message, sidebar, project sidebar and composer handlers keep their identity across renders (a small `useStableHandlers` hook following the existing question-actions pattern), and the sidebars, composer and drag context are memoized, so while a reply streams only that reply re-renders. - A streaming reply renders as top-level markdown blocks, each memoized, so an update parses only the block still being written. A block is closed only where later text cannot change it (after the next block's first line, or a blank line that cannot continue a list, with no raw HTML element open); a text with link or footnote definitions renders whole. Tests compare every step of nine streamed replies (code fences, math, lists, tables, setext headings, blockquotes, HTML) against a whole render. - Expanded reasoning streams through the same block rendering, and its resize observer is created once per expansion instead of once per update. On a 7.3k-character reply with Node's JIT disabled, the markdown parse per update went from 14-30 ms to about 1.3 ms. --- ## Summary by cubic Since v1.1.0, every update of a streaming reply re-rendered the whole chat page and re-parsed the entire reply as markdown, which froze the page on slow phones. author: jeewoo-lee
body: An end-to-end launch on a fake Modal SDK, so the first real run isn't also the first time the whole path runs. **It passes with no changes to `sky/`.** This PR only adds tests. No real launches, no Modal credentials, no spend. The driver runs under a scrubbed environment with fake token values, and the sandbox only sees a clean environment. ## How it works `tests/unit_tests/test_modal_launch_e2e.py` runs `execution.launch` in its own process, in a temporary HOME, through the real `CloudVmRayBackend`. The real exec helper and `ModalCommandRunner` carry every command. The fake `modal` gains `App`, `Image`, `Sandbox.create/list/poll/terminate`. A sandbox is `sleep infinity` as PID 1 of new PID, mount, UTS and IPC namespaces, chrooted into an overlay on a debootstrapped Ubuntu 22.04. Exec enters with `nsenter`. So daemons outlive the exec that started them, and runtime setup (`pkill -9 dpkg`, `rm -rf /etc/security/limits.d`) acts on the sandbox and not the host. The image's real `IMAGE_SETUP_COMMANDS` run when the image is built. It's skipped by default because it needs root, the network (the cluster installs uv, Python and Ray) and about 4 minutes: ``` sudo debootstrap --variant=minbase jammy /tmp/jammy http://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/ sudo SKY_MODAL_E2E_ROOTFS=/tmp/jammy pytest tests/unit_tests/test_modal_launch_e2e.py ``` ## What ran | Step | Result | |---|---| | Provision, reuse of the running sandbox on relaunch | Works | | `internal_file_mounts`, workdir and file mounts over rsync | Works | | Runtime setup (uv, Python, Ray, wheel) | Works, about 15 s | | `start_ray_on_head_node` | Works, about 13 s | | `start_skylet_on_head_node` | Works, about 2 s. Skylet, GCS and raylet are alive in later execs | | Job submit, including a 100 KiB script over the 64 KiB exec limit | Works | | `job_lib` status: SUCCEEDED, FAILED, CANCELLED, FAILED_SETUP | Works | | `tail_logs`: stdout and stderr, env vars, 2.7 MB of output, invalid UTF-8 | Works. Exit code 100 for a failed job | | Cancel | Works, and the job's process is gone | | `download_logs` over rsync | Works | | `down` | Works, about 25 s, of which `ray stop --force` is about 24 s | | Sandbox ends on its own | `status` refresh removes the cluster | The test sets `SKYPILOT_ENABLE_GRPC=1` to prove Modal stays on the legacy path. Removing `clouds.Modal` from the gate in `is_grpc_enabled_with_flag` makes the test fail, because the backend enters the gRPC path. In that check it failed on a missing `google` module in my venv, not on a gRPC connection. ## What this can't tell us These depend on Modal's runtime and are still open for the first real run: - Whether daemons outlive their exec on Modal - Ray under gVisor - Whether `exec(timeout=...)` kills the process - Modal's PID 1: here orphans become zombies under `sleep`, which caused no problem The fake also shares the host's network and runs a minimal Ubuntu rather than `nvidia/cuda`, with no GPU. ## Found along the way These aren't fixed here, and none blocks a run. 1. **If daemons don't outlive exec on Modal, the launch still succeeds.** I ran the driver once with every process an exec started killed when it exits (a temporary mode, not committed). `launch` returned job 1 after 47 s, the job stayed PENDING for the full 2 minutes I waited, `status` went to INIT ("Failed getting cluster status despite all nodes being up"), and `tail_logs` returned 100. On the first real run, a job stuck in PENDING with the cluster in INIT points to this, so run `ray status` in a separate exec right after launch. 2. **A sandbox that ends during runtime setup takes about 6.5 minutes to fail.** The helper's exit code 255 reads as a lost connection, so `_setup_node` retries with "likely due to the reboot of the instance". SSH clouds behave the same, so I left it. A separate exit code for "sandbox gone" would make this fail fast. 3. **`|| true` in `IMAGE_SETUP_COMMANDS` hides a failed install.** In my first version of the fake, apt failed because `/dev/null` wasn't usable, and the image built anyway without curl. The first symptom would come later, in runtime setup. ## Decisions - **Autodown is not tested.** `core.autostop(down=True)` raises `NotSupportedError` on the current base, as designed. The Modal cloud rebuild in #2 (start probe, idempotent create, autodown) hasn't landed, so this runs against the base's cloud. It should be re-run once that lands. - **The fake's sandbox is started outside the client's process tree**, because `kill_children_processes` in SkyPilot would otherwise kill it. A real sandbox isn't a descendant of the client. ## Testing - `test_modal_launch_e2e.py`: 12 passed in 235 s with the root filesystem, 12 skipped without it - `test_modal_command_runner.py` still passes with the extended fake - yapf and isort are clean. Pinned pylint 2.14.5 crashes on Python 3.12 here, so it wasn't run 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

_Requested by **Ruby** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_011FzBMxj5mDVrksN6HUkhtE?thread=cmsg_011FzBMxj5mDVrksN6HUkhtEWcWxksYFbCBqRXQaSQYB7d)_

## Why
`cluster/detect_tasks.sbatch` read its task list once. A task that ended with failed tiles (`!`) or died without cleaning up (`S`) was listed by `status.py --todo`, but nothing ran it until someone made a new list and resubmitted.

## What
- When the list is done, the job asks `status.py --todo` what is still missing. It keeps only the lines that were in its own list (so a 2026 list stays 2026), waits 16 min, and runs those. It does this for up to `ROUNDS=4` rounds in all (`sbatch --export=ALL,ROUNDS=6 ...` to change).
- 16 min: a dead task's lock goes stale after 15 min, and Earth Engine's busy spell has passed. It checks again after the wait, because other jobs may have finished them meanwhile.
- Stops early when nothing is left. A stop signal (scancel, the time limit) ends the wait at once and starts no further round.
- Each round's list is kept in `<run>/logs/leftovers_<job>_round<n>.txt`.
- README sections on restarting updated.

What stays manual: a task that still fails after 4 rounds, and the `S` tasks of a job that ended completely (node lost), when no other job of that list runs later.

## Checks
- `bash -n cluster/detect_tasks.sbatch`
- Ran the script with fake `detect.py`/`status.py` (tasks needing 1, 2, 3 and 9 attempts): each finished in its round, the 9-attempt one stopped after round 4, a list of 2 tasks ignored the run's other leftovers, and a `TERM` during the wait ended the job at once.
- Not run on Goethe.
