body: ## What this adds ### `` markup For every responsive set: ```html ``` - The preferred format goes in ``, and the fallback goes in ``. - `width`/`height` are the real dimensions, so the page layout doesn't jump while images load. - `sizes` is a starting point for each role. - **Lazy images** use `sizes="auto, …"`. Chrome and Firefox then pick the width from the actual layout; Safari uses the fallback list. - **Hero images** load immediately with `fetchpriority="high"`. - Each expanded row shows the markup with a **Copy** button, and **Copy HTML** in the toolbar copies the markup for every image. - The **image path** (default `/images/`) is set right next to the markup. Changing it doesn't re-process anything. ### `manifest.json` in the ZIP It lists every output's file name, format, dimensions and size. For responsive sets it also includes `sizes` and the markup. ### Per-image roles, with automatic graphic detection - **Logos, illustrations and UI screenshots** are detected and get the **Graphic** role: lossless WebP with a PNG fallback. - Previously they got the batch role, usually AVIF + JPEG. - Detection uses a 256 px nearest-neighbour sample. In testing, graphics had **<2% unique colours and >90% identical neighbouring pixels**; photos had 40–72% and <10%, so the margin is wide. - JPEGs skip the check. - **Each row shows its role and lets you change it.** That re-processes only that image. - The image dimensions moved under the file name, which frees a column. ### Fixes found while checking at phone width - **Phantom columns on phones:** the expanded row spanned 6 columns while only 4 are visible, so the browser added phantom columns that squeezed file names. It now spans only the visible columns. - **Toolbar wrapping on desktop:** the path field moved out of the toolbar and in next to the HTML, so the toolbar fits on one row again. ## Testing - `pnpm test`: 40 tests. New ones cover the markup (lazy, hero, graphic, path handling, escaping), the manifest, and graphic detection (flat PNG, noise-like photo, JPEG skip). - `pnpm test:e2e`: 2 tests. - The markup contains the right `srcset`. - **Copy HTML** fills the real clipboard. - A flat PNG is detected as Graphic and gets `-800w/-1600w.webp` + `.png`. - Switching that row to Content re-processes it into AVIF. - **Manual run** with five images (photos, a transparent graphic, a UI screenshot): - All done in about 50 s, at desktop and phone width. - Both PNG graphics were detected as Graphic. - The screenshot now comes out at 190 KB as lossless WebP, instead of 33 KB as lossy AVIF that would blur text. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01STHRjFYWhkJBxSKG3tJdap

body:
Card: tsk-j9ktmj7e4fxq

## What

The Team page's Organisation tab gets a second face, **Paths**, beside the tree (Tree | Paths, kept per browser). It follows the designer's approved draft:

- The team drawn top-down from `reports_to`, humans first, each lead centred over its members. More than six members of one role under one lead fold into one box with tiles ("Coder · 13 members"). A click opens it in place, and a Fold button closes it again.
- A **Reporting lines** chip, on by default, plus four event chips: Review result, Not listening, Request to a human, Card assigned. A chip draws where that event goes (dashed orange, with arrows) and lists it in the panel under the drawing. The panel has three parts: at a glance (`Lead > Coder × 13 · ops`), the route, and the legend.
- Clicking a member keeps only its lines: its reporting lines blue, everything else dimmed.
- At phone width (≤ 700 px) the drawing gives way to a list in the tree's order. Each card shows whom the member reports to, who is under it (a large group said once) and, with a chip on, what reaches it.

## Which edges are computed and which are "usual"

As the lead decided (req-x3hgj0b7xzy3, 1A + 2A), every edge comes from `GET /members` and the routing of docs/api.md §8.2/§8.4:

- **Review result:** reviewer → its `reports_to`. Computed.
- **Not listening:** agent → its `reports_to`, → the project's admins (never a meat proxy), → the owner. Computed.
- **Request to a human:** agent → its owner (`owner_id`). Computed.
- **Card assigned:** lead → member and lead → the member's owner. **All usual.** Who assigns is set on each card, which the members list does not carry. These edges are drawn dotted and marked "usual route, not read from the members" in the legend.
- The review result's author and lead are named only in the chip's note. The members list does not say who wrote the reviewed PR.

## Files

- `web/js/paths.js` (new): routes, layout, drawing, panel and list. Sizes go through the style object (CSP).
- `web/js/org.js`: the face toggle, plus a redraw on member events.
- `web/css/app.css`: `--route` (5.43:1 on `--surface` light, `#f79009` dark) and the Paths styles.
- `web/i18n/en.json` / `js/i18n/en.js`: `org.face.*` and `paths.*`.
- `web/context/views.md` + index: a new entry on edges from the members API, usual edges marked. `web/README.md` gets the file-tree line. Changelog fragment `changelog.d/agent-d-kg22-paths.md`.

## Tests

- `make smoke`: the routes per chip; folded and opened layout, lead centred; group click and Fold; the glance; no style attribute; the face toggle and the five chips; lines on/off; a chip's route in the panel; selection keeping one member's lines; the phone's list in tree order, a large group said once; a project's own role named `constructor` lays out like any other (role buckets are Maps). Each check was counter-checked against a mutation of the code (proxy in the admins, no dimming, no centring, list sorted by name, object buckets).
- `web/tools/e2e.py`, scenario: Paths on the real hub. Not listening gives "E2E Agent ⇢ Owner" with a drawn route, axe at 1280/390 light and 1280 dark, then back to Tree.
- `web/tools/e2e.py`, new `paths_views` (fixture mode), the layout state matrix:
  - widths 2560, 1280 and 390;
  - the sign-in banner on and off;
  - the fixture team and a 26-member team shaped like Maity's (13 coders under one lead, one role of the team's own), folded and opened;
  - reporting lines on and off, with the Card assigned chip on.

  Each state measures that the page has no horizontal overflow, that no chip leaves the window, that no two boxes overlap, that every box stays inside the canvas, that every part of a box (shape, session badge, name, sub line, group label, tiles) lies inside it on all four sides and no text is wider than it, that the panel stands under the drawing and the scroll frame inside the window, and that the box counts are 14 folded and 26 opened. At 390 px it checks that the list shows instead of the drawing and that every card stays inside the window. Counter-checked: `GAP = -60` fails on overlap; moving the 700 px breakpoint to 300 px fails on "the list is not the face shown"; the first version of the pressed Reporting lines chip fails axe color-contrast; the sub line moved 100 px down fails, and so does the old 4 px top padding (the badge cut off).

**Known:** `make check` on main currently reports `js/errors.js: error code 'restricted_quota' … has no words` (from #1374), so the web job is red here until #1387 merges. It is not from this diff.

body:
## What changed

### 3D models per project
- Upload GLB / glTF / DAE / OBJ / FBX / IFC on the project page and open them in a 3D viewer (`/model3d/[projectId]`): system toggles from SketchUp tag/group names, asset codes (e.g. `AC-201`) linked to repairs and warranty, X-Ray, height cut, unit and orientation fixes saved per file. IFC is read with `web-ifc` (WASM copied to `public/wasm` by `postinstall`).
- **Direct `.skp` upload.** `POST /api/skp` converts SketchUp files to GLB on the server with [OpenSKP](https://github.com/iamahsanmehmood/openskp) 1.5.0 (MIT). Instancing is kept, 2D CAD linework and far-away stray groups are dropped so the building fills the view. Demo mode posts the bytes; live mode uploads the `.skp` to Supabase Storage first and the server converts it there (keeps large files out of the request body).
- OpenSKP 1.5.0 is patched (`patches/openskp+1.5.0.patch`, applied by `patch-package` in `postinstall`) to read SketchUp 2019 files: `CCustomLineStyle` layer line styles, null line-style refs, and colour (0x08) attribute values. A test fails if the patch isn't applied.

### Quantity takeoff (`/takeoff`)
- 7 categories (masonry, plaster, paint, ties, corner bead, floor tiles, wall tiles) from the project's house model or an uploaded IFC; every line coded (อ1, ซ12 …), filter by floor/room, 3D highlight, CSV/JSON export.
- Wall editing (height, block type, add/remove openings, exclude a wall), saved per project + source.
- Material prices from the company price book with labour split out, printable report with signature boxes, save totals as a BOQ estimate, rule-based checks plus an optional AI review.

### AI
- Claude Opus 5.5 (effort `medium`, structured outputs, prompt caching, server-side refusal fallback) added next to Gemini; `AI_PROVIDER` chooses the default, a request may name a provider.
- Every call returns tokens and cost (USD/THB) and is logged per task; `/settings/ai` compares providers side by side with a package-cost calculator; `npm run ai:bench` benchmarks real app prompts.

## Why
Customers send SketchUp/IFC files and the team needs accurate 3D and quantities without asking designers to re-export, plus real per-call AI cost numbers to price packages.

## Reviewer notes
- **Proxy:** `/api/skp` is excluded from `src/proxy.ts` because the proxy buffers request bodies only up to 10 MB (`proxyClientMaxBodySize`), which truncated SketchUp uploads. The route checks the signed-in user itself.
- `serverExternalPackages: ["openskp"]` in `next.config.ts`; `/api/skp` sets `maxDuration = 300`. Converting a 109 MB file took ~7 s and ~1 GB RSS.
- New env vars (see `.env.example`): `AI_PROVIDER`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_WORKSPACE_ID` (only for org-scoped keys), `CLAUDE_MODEL`, `CLAUDE_EFFORT`, `AI_USD_THB`, `AI_PRICES`.
- `.gitattributes` keeps `*.patch` on LF so the patch applies on Windows checkouts.
- **Not tested:** live mode with Supabase Storage (a 109 MB `.skp` exceeds the free plan's 50 MB per-file limit), and GLB/FBX/DAE exports from real SketchUp. Gemini Flash prices double from 2027-01-01 and Gemini 4 Argon from 2026-12-01; the price table switches on those dates.

## Testing
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, ESLint on changed files, `npm test` (262 passing, including new takeoff, IFC, pricing, schema and SketchUp tests that write and read a real `.skp`).
- Browser: uploaded a real 109 MB SketchUp 2019 file through the form (converted in 7 s, 72.4 × 39.3 × 15.4 m, 4.9 M triangles); takeoff, wall edits, IFC source, report and BOQ export exercised in demo mode.

author: elie222
body:
## What

When a bot from an organization that is not currently selected calls you, answering from the lock screen (the native call screen on iOS or the notification's Answer action on Android) failed: the call kept ringing and the answer ended in an error. The app now finds the caller in the account's call stream, which covers every organization, and only falls back to the active organization's list.

## Why

One account can belong to several organizations and switch between them in the mobile app, so a call can arrive from a bot outside the active organization. The native answer path resolved the caller from the active organization's bot list only, so the answer never reached the server and the call rang until it expired. The in-app screen worked, which made the lock-screen failure look random.

## Changes

- A native answer action and a notification answer now resolve the caller from the account call stream snapshot first; that snapshot carries the caller's Space, which the answer request pins.
- On a cold start the answer can arrive before the stream's first snapshot: it waits up to 5 seconds for that snapshot instead of failing at once.
- The roster (spaces/list, active organization only) is checked before that wait so same-organization answers are not delayed when the stream is slow; it stays the fallback only for callers the stream has not reported after the wait.
- A wait is bound to the session it started in: stopping the incoming-calls feed cancels pending waits, and a stale continuation neither answers nor completes the native action. Stream callbacks from an aborted feed are ignored so they cannot resolve a newer wait.
- The ringing restore path is unchanged (display only): the stream itself fills cross-organization calls.

## Tested

Unit tests in `apps/mobile/lib/incoming-calls.test.ts`: a native answer action and a notification answer for a bot in another organization (stream knows the bot, spaces/list returns only the active organization's) send `threads/answerCall` pinned to the caller's Space header; the notification path waits for the stream's first snapshot; a same-organization native answer uses the roster without waiting on the stream; a stopped session's wait does not re-answer. Not tested on a real device with CallKit.

Fixes #3497

Supersedes #3498 by @zicochaos (fork tip plus the same-org roster-before-wait and aborted-feed snapshot guards).

author: cf3901646
body:
## Summary of Changes
Fixed a bug where draft forwards were appending empty records to the target model's expert statistics window. The issue occurred because the `_on_forward_pass_start()` and `_on_forward_pass_end()` methods in `_ExpertDistributionRecorderReal` didn't check the `_disable_all` flag before performing reset and append operations.

## Motivation & Context
Closes #48603

The draft model already has a `disable_this_region()` context that suppresses expert-counting hooks, but the outer recorder lifecycle still resets counters and appends records when the draft forward finishes. This causes the target statistics window to lose history to forwards that don't contribute target observations.

## Verification
The fix ensures that when a draft forward is inside the `disable_this_region()` context (i.e., when `self._disable_all` is True), the recorder skips the reset and append operations. This prevents empty draft records from being added to the target statistics window, preserving the target history for the placement planner.

author: atm-lucasmantegari
body:
## Problem

With the **cornas** supplier order PDF model, when a line description is too long and continues on the next page, the price columns end on the wrong page. The document gets extra pages that contain only numbers (price, quantity, total of a line). For example, a supplier order with 8 lines, each with a description of 5 to 12 lines, was generated on 7 pages instead of 2.

## Cause

After printing the description (which ends on page N+1), the model goes back to page N to print the VAT, quantity and price columns, then computes the start of the next line with:

```php
$nexY = max($pdf->GetY(), $nexY);
```

This mixes a Y position on page N with a Y position on page N+1.

## Fix

Use the column position tracker of `CommonDocGenerator` (`resetAfterColsLinePositionsData()`, `setAfterColsLinePositionsData()`, `getMaxAfterColsLinePositionsData()`). It stores the end position of each column together with its page. This is the same fix as #42362 for zenith, and the same mechanism already used in cyan, sponge and eratosthene.

## Tests

I regenerated a real supplier order that had the problem, with and without the patch. It went from 6 pages (7 on the customer's server) to 2, and every line has its price, quantity and total on the page of its description.

Note: `expedition/doc/pdf_espadon` still uses the old pattern and is probably affected too. It is left out of this PR. `supplier_order/doc/pdf_muscadet` does not use the pattern: its price columns do not update the next line position.

Refs #7817, #12529.

With `use Cro::HTTP2::RequestParser` loaded, a `.map`/`.grep` callback's captured env held 13 names the inline loop installed in the consuming frame and removed again for every chunk: three lexical-type keys (`\u{1}GENERAL_NAME`, `\u{1}DH_1_0`, `\u{1}Stream`), six `__mutsu_state_key::__ANON_STATE#N__` keys, and `?FILE`, `=pod`, `!`, `__mutsu_callable_type` (listed with a temporary `eprintln!` in the plan builder, not committed).

`droppable_subject` now also covers the two key shapes whose only readers name something the body would have to mention:

- a lexical type's own key (`\u{1}Foo`, `term_names::LEXICAL_TYPE_PREFIX`) is consulted only by a reader that names the type `Foo`;
- a `state` variable's metadata key (`__mutsu_state_key::<name>`) is read only for a free variable `<name>` of the running body (`vm_closure_dispatch.rs`, the `cc.free_var_syms` loop).

A body that mentions the type or the variable keeps them (`droppable_subject` is only consulted for a body without a nested closure/routine or by-name lookup, and `mentions_name` covers free variables and string constants). `t/routines/closure/map-grep-closure-state-and-lexical-type-captures.t` pins both directions (a state variable the body assigns, one it ignores, a lexical class, an enum, a routine-local class) and agrees with `raku`. Left with Cro loaded: `?FILE`, `=pod`, `!`, `__mutsu_callable_type` (machinery reads them, not named) and the chunk-at-a-time pull of a chained `.map.grep` (each pull runs `enter_inline_loop_env`/`leave_inline_loop_env` for one element).

_Requested by **Kunal** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01QmYq1vKhpJFn23Mc5bG7iA?thread=cmsg_01QmYq1vKhpJFn23Mc5bG7iA4LppMQt1S4nxHzcbWxxGqe)_

## What and why

This fixes the three medium findings from the handbook's security review (#35). It also brings the older docs up to date past Milestone 13.

**S1: vendor shared secret.** `presentVendor(v, role)` now returns `secret` only to ADMIN (`SEES_VENDOR_SECRET`), as Kunal decided. ZAPX has no separate super admin role; ADMIN is the highest. Programmers and viewers no longer receive it. Programmers can still edit vendors and rotate the secret, but an admin passes the new one on. The secret signs entry links, redirects and callbacks, and it authenticates the vendor API.

**S2: AWS secret list.** `SENDGRID_API_KEY` is added to `app_secret_keys`. The Terraform README's example secret JSON now lists every key (`TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN` was missing, which would have stopped the first release). A test fails if the two drift apart again.

**S3: passwords.**
- `POST /api/auth/change-password` requires the current password. It signs out the member's other sessions and keeps this one.
  - Sessions now carry `iatMs`, so a new session can be told apart from older ones issued in the same second.
  - Older tokens fall back to `iat`.
- `POST /api/users/:id/password-reset` (admins) creates a one-time link. It is shown to the admin once and also emailed when `EMAIL_PROVIDER` is set.
- `POST /api/auth/forgot-password` emails a link. It always answers 204, sends at most one email per member per 2 minutes, and is skipped for SSO-only roles.
- `POST /api/auth/reset-password` sets the new password from a link.
- Reset tokens:
  - stored only as SHA-256 hashes in the new `PasswordReset` table (migration `20261117000000_password_reset`)
  - work once and expire after `PASSWORD_RESET_HOURS` (default 24)
  - are voided by a newer link
  - clear an account lockout and sign out every session.
- Every change is audited.
- Studio:
  - "Forgot your password?" on sign-in
  - `/forgot-password` and `/reset-password` pages
  - My account (`/account`) with a change-password form, linked in the sidebar
  - a "Reset password" button in Settings → Team.

**Docs.**
- The root `README.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/operations/go-live.md` and `docs/security.md` now cover M14–M20 and the open PRs.
- Stale "known limits" are fixed.
- The handbook is updated: findings marked fixed, the new routes, table, setting and pages, and the changelog.

Not done here: sealing `Vendor.secret` at rest with `SecretBox`, which needs a data migration. It is noted in the handbook.

## How it was tested

- [x] `pnpm check --no-docker` on this branch:
  - install, secret scan, format, lint, build and typecheck pass
  - migrations apply
  - all unit and API tests pass (api 288)
  - audit passes
  - e2e: 24 of 25 passed on the first run
- [x] The one e2e failure, `blueprint5.spec.ts` at the area-theme preference poll, passed alone and on a full re-run of all 25.
  - It looks like a race in `ThemeProvider`: a change made before the first preferences load finishes is kept only locally.
  - That code is from #27/#34 and was not touched here.
- Docker was not built, and Terraform is not installed here, so its checks were skipped.
- New tests:
  - `apps/api/test/security-fixes.test.ts`: viewer vs editor vendor answers, change password, admin link (one use, voided by a newer one, expired, disabled member, lockout cleared, only the hash stored), forgot password via a local SendGrid stand-in, Terraform/README secret keys.
  - `e2e/tests/security-fixes.spec.ts`: reset link → new password → change password, through the UI.

## Checklist

- [x] Database changes come with a migration, and tenant isolation is kept (`tenantId` on every query)
- [x] New endpoints validate input and check roles
- [x] Secrets and model ids come from configuration, not code
- [x] Docs or an ADR updated if a module boundary or contract changed

author: sahusanket
body:
# Enforce handler-level RBAC in Pipeline Studio and `deleteDatasets`

## Summary
Some Pipeline Studio service endpoints, and `DefaultNamespaceAdmin.deleteDatasets`, ran with only an incidental namespace existence/`GET` check. Callers with read-only access could therefore reach operations that need write or admin permissions. This PR adds explicit authorization checks to those paths, consistent with the existing checks in `ConnectionHandler` and `DefaultNamespaceAdmin.delete`. No IAM or role changes are required.

## Endpoints Changed

Studio paths are relative to `/v3/namespaces/system/apps/pipeline/services/studio/methods/`.

| Handler | Endpoint | Check added | Source |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ValidationHandler` | `POST v1/contexts/{ctx}/validations/stage` | `CREATE` on applications in `{ctx}` | Reported |
| `ValidationHandler` | `POST v1/contexts/{ctx}/validations/pipeline` | `CREATE` on applications in `{ctx}` | Proactive (sibling) |
| `DraftHandler` | `GET/PUT/DELETE v1/contexts/{ctx}/drafts[/{draft}]` (4 endpoints) | Reject `system` context (any case) with `400` | Proactive |
| `ConnectionHandler` | `POST v1/contexts/{ctx}/connections/test` | `CREATE` on `ConnectionEntityId(ctx, "*")` | Proactive (sibling) |
| `OAuthHandler` | `GET v1/oauth/provider/{p}/authurl` | `GET` on system secure key (client creds) | Reported |
| `OAuthHandler` | `PUT v1/oauth/provider/{p}` | `UPDATE` on system secure key (client creds) | Reported |
| `OAuthHandler` | `DELETE v1/oauth/provider/{p}` | `DELETE` on system secure key (client creds) | Reported |
| `OAuthHandler` | `PUT v1/oauth/provider/{p}/credential/{c}` | `UPDATE` on system secure key (refresh token) | Reported |
| `OAuthHandler` | `GET v1/oauth/provider/{p}/credential/{c}` | `GET` on system secure key (refresh token) | Reported |
| `OAuthHandler` | `GET v1/oauth/provider/{p}/credential/{c}/valid` | `GET` on system secure key (refresh token) | Reported |
| `DefaultNamespaceAdmin` | `DELETE /v3/unrecoverable/namespaces/{ns}/datasets` | `DELETE` on namespace `{ns}` | Reported |

## Justification per Handler

**`ValidationHandler`**: Validation creates plugins and evaluates macros (secure keys, connections, OAuth), so it can run in TaskWorker. Previously it only checked that the namespace exists. Validation is part of authoring a pipeline, so it now requires the same permission as creating one. The check runs *after* the existence check, so a missing namespace still returns `404` before `403`.

**`DraftHandler`**: List/get were already protected by the namespace `GET` check in `AbstractDataPipelineHandler.respond`, and put/delete by `UPDATE`. The gap was the `system` context: `respond()` skips the namespace lookup for it (and lowercases `SYSTEM`), and system-namespace reads are allowed for everyone. Drafts are never stored in `system` (the UI always uses the current namespace), so a single `respond()` override rejects it, matching `ConnectionHandler`. No other draft behavior changes.

**`ConnectionHandler`**: Added in the same change as the RBAC for the other 7 connection endpoints, but `testConnection` was missed. It evaluates `${secure()}`/`${oauth()}` macros and calls the connector, so it now requires connection `CREATE`, the same permission as creating a connection.

**`OAuthHandler`**: None of its endpoints checked permissions. Provider config and tokens live with secure keys in the system namespace, so each endpoint is now authorized against the exact secure key it touches (`GET`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE`). The check runs before any store write or outbound call. `respond()` now passes through `HttpErrorStatusProvider` codes, so a denial returns `403` instead of `500`. The runtime `${oauth()}` macro is unaffected: it runs as system principals and already needed secret access through the secure store. `OAuthStore` key helpers are made `public` so the handler uses the exact key names.

**`DefaultNamespaceAdmin.deleteDatasets`**: Its sibling `delete()` requires `DELETE` on the namespace, but `deleteDatasets` (which wipes every dataset) only had the incidental `GET` from `exists()`. It now requires `DELETE` too. The check sits after `exists()`, like `updateProperties`, so a missing namespace still returns `404`.

## Testing
- **Unit tests:** `DraftServiceTest`, `OAuthServiceTest`, `DataPipelineConnectionTest`, `DefaultNamespaceAdminTest`. Each covers `403` for unprivileged callers and success once the permission is granted. Also covered: `system`/`SYSTEM` drafts → `400`, `404` before `403` for missing namespaces, and the OAuth provider not being modified or deleted by denied calls.
- **Live E2E:** on an RBAC-enabled Cloud Data Fusion instance, before/after the image change. VIEWER and NOROLE now get `403` on all changed endpoints, while ADMIN behavior is unchanged.

author: daneelvt
body:
Stacks on #144 (the Lookout and the Cavalier); base `looks-lookout-cavalier`. **Awaits the owner's review of the looks**: the line-up front and behind, the faces, every look in every colour and two skin tones, and the dressing room on the phone. Nothing in play changes. The looks are built, shown in the dressing room and loadable by the fleet, but no boat chooses them yet. No catalog or protocol change.

**Pictures:** https://claude.ai/artifact/XPkWkDNEMWhM5sGor6cJ8D (private). The page has:
- both looks front and behind, beside the earlier looks from behind at the deck level, and in black;
- the faces and the backs of the heads, in four main colours and Tones 1, 3, 4 and 6;
- each woman from the side;
- the habits standing and at the helm;
- the four review sheets, and the strips of the habits and of the long waistcoat in the cross and the climb.

## What it does

### The Quartermaster (`art/sailors/looks/quartermaster.yaml`)
- **The wrap:** indigo cloth wound high over the head and swelling as it rises. Its turns are striped in gold, rising toward the back. Hers is the taller (about 11 cm above the crown, his about 9.5 cm), and it leans back.
- **The waistcoat:** a long waistcoat in the main colour (madder orange by default) to mid-thigh, buttoned to the waist. Its skirts are open at the front, vented at the sides, and open at the back below the seat.
- **Under it:** a linen shirt with full sleeves, dark breeches, pale stockings, buckled shoes.
- **Belt and book:** a leather belt with a brass buckle, and a small tally book tucked in it at the right of the front.
- **Earrings:** gold hoops for her, small rings for him.
- **Hair:** coily hair close under the wrap; hers shows in small coils at the nape. His beard is trimmed close.
- **Habit, tallying in the book:** the sheet hand goes to the book, comes up before the chest with the head bowed over it, then a look across the boat and a nod as each thing is counted, and back. At the helm on either side, and standing.

### The Old Salt (`looks/oldsalt.yaml`)
- **Age:** older and weathered (0.72 and 0.75), the eyes narrowed by years of squinting at the sea.
- **The cap:** a red knitted Monmouth cap, thick. Its brim is turned up in a roll, and its top droops over and hangs out behind: to the left and back for him, further back for her.
- **The jacket:** a short sea jacket of heavy wool to the hip, in the main colour (black by default). No collar or lapels. It is open at the throat over a linen shirt and buttoned below, its sleeves turned back at the wrist in a narrow band.
- **Neck and legs:** a wool neckerchief wrapped at the throat, its ends in the jacket's opening; wide canvas slops to below the knee, grey stockings, shoes.
- **Hair:** her white hair in a plait down the back from under the cap; his short under it, with a full white beard.
- **Habit, squinting at the sky:** the hands stay on tiller and sheet; the head lifts to the sky to windward, turns slowly ahead along the clouds, and nods. At the helm on either side, and standing.

Each habit is written under the names the game asks for (`names: {quartermaster-habit: habit, ...}`). Every look keeps the 85-bone skeleton and the deck atlas's 512² size.

### The build learns (`art/sailors/build/`)
- **`scarf.py`, more than a headscarf:**
  - a **wrap** wound high (`tall`: the rows rise above the crown and swell, leaning back, the top rounded), with `folds` where it is wound;
  - a **knitted cap**, its brim turned up in a `roll` and its top drooping over it (`droop`: a tube laid over the cap toward an azimuth, its base sunk in the crown, its end hanging out beyond);
  - the knot may sit at any azimuth or be left off (`knot: null`);
  - the hem's stand-off (`hem`) and its smoothing (`smooth`) can be set;
  - the cloth can take a `pattern`;
  - under a roll, a stray column of the lowest rows (a ray led astray at the brow) is brought back to its neighbours.
- **`patterns.py`:** `wound` stripes that wind round the cloth as a wrap's turns lie.
- **`gear.py`:**
  - **a belt**: a sash with no knot or ends, and a `buckle`;
  - **a tally book** tucked in the belt, rigid on the belt's weights;
  - **earrings** hung through the ears' lobes. There are no ear landmarks in MPFB, so the lobe is found as the lowest point of what stands out from the side of the head behind the eye.
- **`hair.py`:** a hair cap made without strands (under a scarf) is mended to be manifold before its UVs are laid.

The build's changes leave every committed look's files as they are, and nothing is added to the garments' key, so no committed garment goes stale. If the Bosun is built again, her knot and tails come out exactly as before; only her hair cap is mended earlier.

`sailors.spec.ts`'s habit test runs over the new pair.

## Measurements

| | Quartermaster ♀ | Quartermaster ♂ | Old Salt ♀ | Old Salt ♂ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gates | **408, all pass** | **417, all pass** | **398, all pass** | **407, all pass** |
| triangles close / deck / far | 10,584 / 2,910 / 291 | 10,990 / 2,994 / 296 | 9,980 / 2,764 / 297 | 10,542 / 2,830 / 298 |
| close, gzipped (limit 300 KiB) | 220.2 KB | 226.0 KB | 231.2 KB | 223.0 KB |
| deck + far, gzipped (limit 150 KiB) | 91.2 + 13.4 KB | 95.8 + 14.0 KB | 100.8 + 14.9 KB | 98.3 + 15.0 KB |
| clips, gzipped (limit 150 KiB) | 126.3 KB | 127.2 KB | 121.5 KB | 121.9 KB |
| build (one version, garments made afresh) | 278 s | 285 s | 264 s | 269 s |
| build (one version, garments kept) | about 120 s | about 115 s | about 140 s | about 160 s |

KB = 1,024 bytes, gzip -9. The last full build of all four ran on this branch after merging #144's machine fix, so its new gates are in the counts: the skirts are kept over the thighs and knees in every frame of every clip.

- **Close level by mesh, the men:**
  - Quartermaster ♂: body 3,856, waistcoat 1,098, wrap 868, hair 864, shirt 800, waistcoat skirt 688, breeches 660, stockings 532, shoes 378, beard 376, belt 352, earrings 224, trims 142, eyes 140, tally book 12.
  - Old Salt ♂: body 3,866, jacket 1,364, cap 976, slops 958, hair 876, jacket skirt 552, stockings 530, beard 476, shoes 380, neckerchief 280, eyes 140, trims 90, shirt 54.
- **Clips:** 18 a version: every sailor's 16, plus the habit seated on both sides and standing. Every one passes the motion gate, and nothing goes through the boat in any frame at any level.
- **The habits:**
  - Quartermaster: head peak-to-median 3.8–4.5, hand jerk ≤ 22 m/s³, reach ≤ 0.85, range ≤ 0.71, elbow ≤ 0.20 m/s.
  - Old Salt: head peak-to-median 2.7–3.9, hand jerk ≤ 2.1 m/s³ (its hands stay put), reach ≤ 0.85, range ≤ 0.69.
- **Silhouettes** (`silhouettes.test.ts`, every pair of a version; the test's threshold is 0.2). Most new pairs clear it comfortably; the closest are thin:
  - from above: Bosun–Old Salt 0.203 (♀), Bosun–Quartermaster 0.205 (♂) and 0.222 (♀), Old Salt–machine 0.232 (♂);
  - from behind: Old Salt–Quartermaster 0.233 (♂), Bosun–Old Salt 0.242 (♀).

## Checked by hand

- **In the dressing room:** both looks on WebGPU at noon: front and back, the faces close, four main colours and four skin tones, the habits at the helm and standing.
- **The bust:** both women keep a defined bust under the waistcoat and under the jacket (the sheets' side views).

author: hazelmayank
body:
## Summary

The `/oidc` handler and the logout provider had no timeout on OIDC discovery or the token exchange, so an identity provider that accepts the connection but never answers kept the request open forever. The timeout is now set on the HTTP client and not on the context, because the context is stored in the oauth config and reused later by `/oidc-callback`.

## Related Issue

Fixes #8270

## Changes

- `pkg/auth`: add `WithClientTimeout`, which copies the HTTP client in the context (or `http.DefaultClient`), keeps its transport and sets a timeout. The original client is not modified.
- `cmd`: add `oidcRequestTimeout` (30s, a var like `externalProxyTimeout` so tests can lower it) and apply the helper before `oidc.NewProvider` in the `/oidc` handler and in `getOIDCLogoutProvider`, after the TLS client is configured.
- Tests: a stalled discovery endpoint and a stalled token endpoint both return an error status instead of hanging, and unit tests for the helper.

## Steps to Test

1. `cd backend && go test ./cmd -run 'TestOIDCStart_TimesOutWhenIdPNeverResponds|TestOIDCCallback_TimesOutWhenTokenEndpointNeverResponds' -count=1 -v`
2. `go test ./pkg/auth -run TestWithClientTimeout -count=1 -v`
3. Without the fix (keeping only the `oidcRequestTimeout` variable) both handler tests fail after their 5s deadline.

## Screenshots

N/A, backend change.

## Notes for the Reviewer

The refresh-token path (`RefreshAndCacheNewToken`) has the same problem: it also calls `oidc.NewProvider` and the token source with a context that has no deadline. I kept it out of this PR and will send it separately using the same helper.

author: rodohasarrived
body:
<!-- phase:PR7 -->

## What changed and why

Fixes the two High paper-trading findings from the 2026-11-04 assessment. The two code commits can each be reverted on their own. The follow-up commits fix an architecture-ratchet violation, address the Codex review, keep generated docs and the reviewed source-hash baseline in step, and merge `main`.

**H3: margin interest was charged twice** (`beac46bd`)
- **Bug:** `AccrueMarginInterest` grew `MarginBorrowed` *and* debited `Cash`. Equity (`Cash + MV − MarginBalance`) therefore fell by 2× the interest, and the sale paid it again when it repaid the inflated loan.
- **Fix:** interest is now paid from cash once and the loan principal is unchanged. Each accrual posts a balanced `Margin Interest Expense / Cash` ledger entry, as `SimulatedPortfolio` already does. An optional `asOf` parameter sets the timestamp of that entry.

**H4: the option contract multiplier was ignored for cash and P&L** (`a8a77793`, `81a3e3d2`, `32dea95e`)
- **Bug:** paper cash, ledger, lot basis, market value and P&L were all `qty × price`. One $2.50 option moved $2.50, while `OrderNotionalResolver` sized the same order at ×100 and `DrawdownCircuitBreaker` read the understated `PortfolioValue`.
- **Which fills are scaled:** each fill resolves a money multiplier.
  - Listed premium contracts use the contract multiplier. These are options and warrants, whose catalog descriptor declares `UsesOccOptionSymbols`, plus unclassified reports that carry an option identity or an OMS multiplier above 1.
  - Face-value instruments and every other asset class use 1.
  - **Futures intentionally stay at 1×** until the book has a variation-margin cash model.
- **What stays the same:** `CostBasis`, lot entry prices and `MarketPrice` stay per-unit quotes, because every downstream reader applies the multiplier itself. Only money amounts are scaled.
- **New rejection:** a fill whose multiplier differs from the open position's multiplier throws.
- **Supporting changes:**
  - The aggregate `Positions` view carries the multiplier its P&L was computed with.
  - `PortfolioStatePositionTracker` divides P&L by `qty × multiplier` to recover the mark. This also corrects brokerage option positions.
  - `OrderFillProcessor` stamps `LotMultiplier` onto the fill increment. It is not part of the canonical fill id.

**Codex review fixes** (`32dea95e`)
- **Replay:** sessions recorded before this PR already carried the Security Master multiplier, so they replayed at 100×.
  - Paper fills whose scale is not 1 are now stamped with `ExecutionReport.BookedMoneyMultiplier` before persistence.
  - Replay uses `ApplyRecordedFill`: a stamped record replays at its stamp, and an unstamped record replays at the 1× it was booked at.
  - The field is omitted when null, so existing records serialize and hash unchanged.
- **Accounting:** `TradeExecutedEvent` gains `MoneyMultiplier`, and `GrossValue` applies it. A profitable option close no longer gives `LedgerPostingConsumer` a negative cost basis (which made it throw), and a losing close no longer books a wrong journal. The posting digest includes the multiplier only when it isn't 1.
- **Margin:** `CheckMarginStatus` gives the margin models money-scaled quotes, so a Reg T option loan and its holding are measured on the same scale and there's no false margin call.
- **`PositionState`:** gains `ContractMultiplier` (default 1), applied to `UnrealizedPnl` and `MarketValue`. Both trackers set it.

**Docs, generated output and merges**
- **Module READMEs:** Execution, Execution.Sdk and Ui.Shared describe the behaviour above. After that review, only their `source-hash-manifest.json` entries are refreshed (`validate-doc-hashes.py --write-module`).
- **Merges:** `d6ff9402` and `aed37026` merge `main`.
  - The generated doc-health files were regenerated.
  - For the reviewed hash manifest, `main`'s entries are kept and only this PR's three modules are refreshed.
  - `SRC-UI-SHARED` combines `main`'s reviewed Direct Lending and workbench changes with this PR's `BrokeragePortfolioState` change.
- **Phase:** `PR7` is the narrowest phase that covers `src/**`, `tests/**` and `docs/**`. No workflow files changed.

## Risk and verification

Risk tier: [ ] Level 1 routine  [x] Level 2 financial/architectural  [ ] Level 3 sensitive/destructive

- **Checks actually run and results:**
  - `dotnet build` of `Meridian.Execution` and `Meridian.Tests` (Release) succeeds.
  - Paper portfolio, fill processor and tracker tests after the review fixes: **125 passed, 0 failed**.
  - Wider `dotnet test` before the review fixes (Execution, Risk, Backtesting, paper-related UI, endpoint and acceptance tests): **2,215 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped**.
  - CI's `core-platform-domain-root` shard, after the ratchet fix: **4,700 passed, 0 failed**.
  - Mutation check: against the original `src`, 16 of the 22 original new or changed tests fail.
  - `validate-doc-hashes.py --summary`: 0 errors. `check-generated-output.py`: no drift. `enforce_phase_scope.py` with `phase:PR7`: passed.
- **Existing tests whose expectations changed:**
  - `AccrueMarginInterest_OneDay_…` (renamed `…_DeductsInterestFromCashOnly`) and `AccrueMarginInterest_MultiDay_ScalesWithDays` previously asserted that the loan grows. They now assert it does not.
  - `OptionFills_CarryTheContractMultiplierIntoThePortfolio` gained a cash assertion.
- **Checks not run or blocked:**
  - A wide local regression run on the review fixes is still in progress. I'll post its result.
  - Full `bash scripts/ci.sh` was not run locally. `Meridian CI / quality-gate` is authoritative.
- **Remaining risks and follow-ups:**
  - Futures need a variation-margin cash model; `FuturePosition.SettleDaily` is the model to reuse.
  - `PaperTradingCostModel` computes basis-point fees and slippage on options without the multiplier.
  - Live-broker `TradeExecutedEvent`s still carry `MoneyMultiplier = 1`. Only paper fills are stamped, so live option gross values keep their existing scale.
  - Reg T margin models allow margin on long options.
  - The OMS multiplier resolution (`OrderManagementSystem.cs:276`) has no face-value guard. Paper is unaffected because face-value fills always use 1.
- Evidence scope: [x] Synthetic  [ ] Live verified  [ ] Live untested  [ ] Not applicable

## Safety and governance

- [x] No credentials, private account data, or unrelated changes included
- [x] Financial/security invariants remain protected where applicable
- [x] Existing required GitHub checks and branch rules remain in force
- [x] Governance files changed: none

body: Refs #1179 ADR 0048 H3 PR-2: every single-Actor turn goes through the harness Mailbox. ## What changed - **Host Mailbox (D3).** `HostMailbox` (`packages/im/agent/src/collaboration/host-mailbox.ts`) owns one long-lived harness per IM route generation and per `ZhinAgent`. Every IM ingress turn, every `ZhinAgent.processTurn` / `processStream` turn and every scene-event wake is a Mail turn of that harness. Workroom turns and turns whose product resolves its own intent each get a lane of their own (`turn:`). Human and scene-event Mail use the sessionKey lane (D1); webhooks will use `event:`. - **InboxPolicy wired (D2).** `createInboxPolicy` (#725 queue / same-sender supersede / FIFO between members / explicit stop / ADR 0038 merge window, stale reply and danmaku window) now decides admission. The ingress `#gate` scheduling is gone. - **Q2.** The first Engagement carries a merged turn. Its Authority is the intersection (`mergedAuthority`), and its principal is the first human. - **Q3.** A scene-event wake (already coalesced and rate-limited by `SceneEventWake`) posts one `kind: 'event'` Mail on the scene lane. It queues behind the scene's human turns and is never merged into them. - **Q4 (breaking rename).** `ai.agent.inboundQueue` is now `ai.agent.mailbox`. A config that still sets the old key fails startup validation with `MAILBOX_MIGRATION_HINT`. - **Q5.** `SessionMessageQueue` is kept. - **Q6.** `harness.attach` / `detach` are deleted. Collaboration binds to the turn's Mail through an ALS mail-turn context, and actor turns keep the root turn's async context. - With no peers, the turn gets no collaboration tools or prompts (D3). ### Deleted - `turn/turn-admission-gate.ts` (its tests are ported to `tests/turn/host-mailbox-admission.test.ts`, 46 cases). - `turn/inbound-turn-queue.ts` and its test. - `turn/inbound-queue-runtime.ts`. - The `runWithInboundQueue` wrapping in `process-stream.ts` / `ZhinAgent`. - The `inboundTurnQueue` dispose branch. - The `InboundTurn*Error` names in `turn-terminal.ts`, replaced by `MailboxTurnRejectedError`. - `harness.attach`. ### Renamed - `inbound-queue-config.ts` → `mailbox-config.ts` (`normalizeMailboxConfig`, `ResolvedMailboxConfig`, …). - The `inboundQueue` config key → `mailbox` (schema, generated docs, zh/en docs, READMEs). ## Mid-turn deliver API: `harness.deliver` `harness.deliver(input)` is the mid-turn delivery API, and `harness.open` is the same call (IM uses `open`). - It posts a root Mail on `input.lane` (the sessionKey). The result carries `disposition` (`queued | merged | superseded | stopped`) and `position`. - `onPosting(root)` is called synchronously before the post, so a host can correlate the turn before the pump starts it. - `cancelSender(actor, lane, senderId)` drops a sender's queued Mail. Interrupt and stale handling: - A same-sender correction that arrives before anything was delivered aborts the running turn with reason `superseded`. The replacement batch answers both Mails. - The ingress / scene / eval reply ports refuse to send once the admission signal is aborted, and they drop replies when `staleCheck()` says `discard`. A superseded answer is never sent. ## Timer (PR-3, not in this PR) No timer Mail is delivered here. The intended shape is a `kind: 'timer'` Mail with `timerId`, `content` and `owner` (principal and Venue reply target), delivered to the target Actor's Mailbox on lane `timer:`. `harness-timer-*` stay skipped. The merged `deliverTimerMailInbound` hook from #1182 still throws. ## Evals These six cases are unskipped and pass: - `harness-mailbox-admission-gate`: new fixture `addressed: false` gives `not_addressed` and `termination: 'none'`. - `harness-mailbox-inbound-queue-serial` - `harness-mailbox-merge-window-coalesce` - `harness-mailbox-merge-skip-noise-sender` - `harness-mailbox-danmaku-pick-one` - `harness-mailbox-interrupt-stale`: new fixture `deliver: { duringStep: 1 }` posts the correction while step 1 is served. The Mailbox supersedes the turn, the stale answer is suppressed, and the batch [old, new] is answered by step 2, giving one outbound. The eval driver posts every inbound to a per-case `HostMailbox`. The multi-message ingress eval framework now drives `HostMailbox` instead of `TurnAdmissionGate`. No scene-event eval stubs were added. ## Tests (local) - harness: 183/183 - agent unit + harness + eval framework: 3737 passed / 8 skipped - agent evals: 216 passed / 4 skipped (`harness-timer-*`) - ingress evals: 8/8 - `basic/cli/tests/plugin-runtime/agent`: all pass - Remaining `basic/cli/tests` failures in a local unbuilt WT are only the "`@zhin.js/cli` is not built yet" tests. - `tsc` is clean for agent and harness; eslint reports 0 errors. ## Deviations - New `MailBody.human.unaddressed` marker and InboxPolicy reject code `not_addressed`, plus the eval fixture fields `addressed` and `deliver` (needed for the admission-gate and interrupt-stale cases). - `collaborationIdle()` / the registry now track host Mailboxes by their collaboration engagements only, so it can be awaited from inside another turn. - The gate test "ignores `live` when no danmaku window is configured" was dropped. The host Mailbox always has the live policy, as production always did. --- ## Summary by cubic Every IM and `ZhinAgent` turn now runs through a long-lived host Mailbox (`HostMailbox`) instead of `TurnAdmissionGate` and the inbound turn queue. Admission, merge / danmaku windows, stale-reply checks and supersede are now the harness inbox policy; scene-event wakes post one event Mail on the scene lane, so it queues behind that scene's human turns. Six `harness-mailbox-*` eval cases are unskipped. **Breaking config rename** - `ai.agent.inboundQueue` is now `ai.agent.mailbox`; fields are unchanged except `coalesceWindowMs`, which is dropped. - A config that still sets `ai.agent.inboundQueue` fails startup validation with a migration hint. **Removals and the new delivery API** - `TurnAdmissionGate`, `InboundTurnQueue`, the inbound-queue runtime wrapping, and `harness.attach` / `detach` are removed. - `harness.deliver` (`harness.open` is the same call) is the mid-turn delivery API and reports the Mail disposition (`queued | merged | superseded | stopped`) or rejection code. - A same-sender correction arriving before anything was delivered supersedes the running turn; the stale reply is never sent. Written for commit c563f3b920285a1fd2c5ff70a3e269e21f2c9abf. Summary will update on new commits.

author: boenkkk
body:
Part of #475 — this covers Oracle only. DB2 is not included, so the issue is not closed automatically.

## What and why

Adds Oracle as the sixth database driver, so Oracle users no longer have to leave the app for SQL Developer to browse tables, run queries, see DDL or read plans.

SQLx has no Oracle backend, so the adapter uses `rust-oracle` (ODPI-C) behind a `bb8` pool, with every blocking call on `spawn_blocking` — the same shape as the SQL Server adapter. The Oracle Instant Client is **not bundled**: the data source stores its directory (or `ORACLE_HOME` is used), and a missing client, wrong password or unknown service is reported as an `IdeError` instead of a panic.

- Backend: `DbDriver::Oracle` (default port 1521); `oracle://user:pass@host:1521/service` and `jdbc:oracle:thin:@//host:port/service` URLs; pooled connections with validity checks; PL/SQL-aware statement splitting (`BEGIN … END;` blocks stay one statement, a lone `/` terminates); `EXPLAIN PLAN` + `PLAN_TABLE`; introspection from the `ALL_*` views, with system schemas hidden unless "Show system objects" is on.
- Frontend: Oracle in the vendor list with its own icon, the Instant Client field in Options (required before Test Connection), Oracle/PLSQL keywords and completion, Oracle DDL/DML generation, English and Chinese strings.
- The second commit fixes a connection bug found while testing against a live server: the pool's check-out ping used `execute` on `SELECT 1 FROM DUAL`, which rust-oracle rejects. bb8 therefore discarded every connection and retried until its 30 s timeout, which surfaced as "timed out connecting to the database" (and Test Connection hid it). The ping now reads a row, `connect` validates eagerly so a wrong password shows ORA-01017 instead of a timeout, and a failed client load is no longer cached, so a corrected Instant Client path works without restarting the app.

Instant Client setup for macOS, Windows and Linux is in `docs/databases.md`.

## How it was verified

Against a live Oracle Database 12.2 Enterprise server: Test Connection, opening the data source, table browsing, column/index introspection and the console all work. A schema with 174 tables lists in about 260 ms, a query round-trips in about 25 ms, and result pagination returns the expected page. Column metadata was cross-checked with SQL*Plus.

Commands run:

- `cargo fmt --all --check`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo nextest run -p ide-db -p ide-host` — 306 + 286 passed. `close_project::detached_close_returns_while_runtime_workers_wait_for_the_closing_thread` flaked once under parallel load and passes alone.
- `pnpm gen:bindings` (no diff), `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm knip`
- `pnpm vitest run src/features/database src/platform/locales` — 151 passed
- `pnpm build`; `pnpm e2e e2e/oracle-source.spec.ts` — 1 passed (selects Oracle, checks port 1521 and the default URL, requires the Instant Client field before Test Connection, then checks the Test Connection payload)
- Live Oracle test, skipped unless the environment names a server: `OPENIDEA_ORACLE_TEST=user/password@host:port/service OPENIDEA_ORACLE_CLIENT=/path/to/instantclient cargo test -p ide-db --lib oracle::` — connect, query and result pagination through the pool.

Unit tests cover URL parsing, identifier quoting and paging SQL, PL/SQL splitting, plan mapping, Oracle object DDL/DML, vendors, dialect and completion. The UI change is covered by the e2e spec above; no screenshots are attached.

## Review focus

- `crates/ide-db/src/oracle.rs`: connection lifetime (a cancelled statement closes its session), LOB caps, error mapping.
- `crates/ide-db/src/split.rs`: the PL/SQL depth rules — `END LOOP` / `END CASE` must not pop twice, `END IF` must not close a block.
- Whether requiring the Instant Client directory in the Options tab is the right answer to the packaging question in #475.

author: langyo
body:
## Summary

Seven defects in the reactive runtime, the patch-apply path and the DOM platform layer, all reachable from ordinary app code. Found while porting a Dioxus app onto tairitsu, where they combined into one very confusing symptom: clicks fire the handler a growing number of times, updates land in bursts or never, and none of it reports an error.

### 1. Fragments broke child indexing

`rsx!` expands `for` and `if` bodies into a `VNode::Fragment` stored as a **single** entry in `VElement::children`, but every renderer treats a fragment as transparent and appends its members directly to the parent. The vnode child list was therefore shorter than the DOM child list, and every patch the diff produced carried a **vnode** index that `apply_patch` resolved against the **DOM**. With a fragment present, every index after it shifted; patches landed on the wrong node or on `None` and were silently dropped. The visible symptom was a `for` list that never grew.

`VElement::child` / `children` now flatten fragments recursively.

### 2. A lost frame froze every later update

`scheduled` is cleared only inside `flush_render`. When the host never ran the callback it booked (background-tab rAF throttling, a swallowed animation callback id), every subsequent `mark_dirty` short-circuited at `AlreadyScheduled` and the queued work was dropped with no error. Bookings now carry a request time; a booking older than `FRAME_DEADLINE` (32 ms) is treated as lost and flushed directly.

### 3. Rendering re-subscribed components to every signal they read

`track_signal` and `subscribe_component` pushed the component id on every call, but a render re-reads its dependencies each time, so the list grew per render and `notify_signal` fanned one write out to as many `mark_dirty` calls as the component had ever rendered.

### 4. `flush_render` left mid-render marks unqueued

Components dirtied *during* a render stayed queued with `scheduled` already cleared and nothing booked them a flush. It now drains until the queue is empty.

### 5. A re-entrant flush double-borrowed the apply callback

Guest code inside render/apply callbacks reaches `flush_render` again through `mark_dirty`'s fallbacks. The nested drain re-entered `render_component` while the outer apply callback was still borrowed — "RefCell already borrowed" — and the unwind left the stored vnode already replaced, so every later diff saw no change and the UI froze with no error and no recovery. A flush already draining defers to it now; the flag is RAII-guarded so a panicking render still releases it.

### 6. Event listeners stacked one per render

Re-renders replace handler closures, so the diff emits UpdateEvent (remove + add) per handler per render. With the host-side removal missing (see 7), only the add half landed and the DOM gained a listener per render — a ported button carried seven click listeners and its handler ran 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 times across five clicks. `add_event_listener` now drops any entry it still tracks for the same (element, event) before attaching.

### 7. Debug tracing left in the patch apply path

The `eprintln!` probes from #116's investigation still shipped on master's `InsertChild`/`UpdateChild` arms. In a component-model host, stderr is an OutputStream **resource bound to the thread that first resolved it**: from any other entry point (an animation-frame callback, a timer) the write throws "Not a valid OutputStream resource", which aborts the apply mid-patch and — via 5 — wedges the runtime permanently. This PR removes them (same change as #120, included here so the branch is self-contained).

Also exposes `ReactiveSignal::component_id` and `runtime::debug_state` for embedder diagnostics.

## Tests

- `vnode::tests::test_child_flattens_fragment` / `test_children_flattens_nested_fragments` / `test_empty_fragment_child_adds_nothing`
- `runtime::tests::test_schedule_callback_can_flush_synchronously`
- `runtime::tests::test_mark_dirty_does_not_stall_after_a_lost_frame`
- `runtime::tests::test_track_signal_deduplicates_components`
- `runtime::tests::test_reentrant_flush_defers_to_active_drain`

`cargo test -p tairitsu-vdom -p tairitsu-hooks --lib` — 253 passed. Clippy and fmt clean.

## Verification in a consumer

End to end in a real browser through the published glue (langyo/tsdm-x5-pokemon-plugin, a Dioxus → tairitsu port): five consecutive clicks append exactly one row each (2→3→4→5→6→7, incremental patches, no remount), one click issues exactly one request, an async fetch round-trip updates the UI ("OK (163 bytes)"), and the animation-frame scheduler delivers every frame (7/7). Before this PR the same page needed a full-tree remount per update and its fetch bridge never delivered.

body:
## KatoSync 4.0 – Trust Gate 7: Serverseitige One-Time-Challenge und getrennte Admin-Freigabe

**Draft, kein Beta-Release.** Stacked auf PR #237 → #236 → #235 → #234 → #233 → #232 → #231 → #230. Projekt-Tracking #229.

### Live-Änderungen in KATOOS Supabase (05.11.2026)
- Additive Migration **`20261105084427_katosync_feature_owner_one_time_challenge_gate7.sql`**, nach erfolgreichem transaktionalem SQL-Dry-Run in der **echten** KATOOS-Datenbank `xbnnlyyxiilklsygxcof` angewandt. Dateiversion entspricht exakt der Live-Migrationshistorie.
- Drei neue server-only RLS-Tabellen unter Schema `katosync`: `feature_approval_reviewers` (independent reviewer allowlist), `feature_owner_challenges` (32-Byte-Nonce und atomarer einmaliger Verbrauch) und `feature_owner_review_decisions` (append-only Review-Entscheidung). **Alle Tabellen RLS an, kein SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE für anon/authenticated.**
- Beide SQL-RPCs `feature_owner_challenge_issue` und `feature_owner_challenge_consume` sind `SECURITY INVOKER`, **kein EXECUTE für anon/authenticated**, ausschließlich Server-`service_role`. Das externe Login allein reicht nicht: Projekt muss admin-registriert und aktiv sein, Konto KatoSync-Mitglied, konkreter Grant vorher von Admin als `pending` vorgegeben.
- Nonce entsteht mit `extensions.gen_random_bytes(32)` **im Postgres**, unter `FOR UPDATE OF g`-Lock, mit 2-minütigem TTL, nur einer offenen Challenge je Grant und 30-Sekunden-Ratenbegrenzung.
- Server-side Challenge-Verbrauch nur einmal, atomisch, mit grant-/Projekt-/UID-/Key-Fingerprint-Bindung. Vorher prüft das QA-Edge-Backend die echte Ed25519-PoP-Signatur; PostgreSQL selbst verifiziert Ed25519 nicht.
- Aktivierung aus `pending` zu `active` durch Gate-7-Erweiterung des bestehenden `feature_approver_audit_guard()` **nur nach verbrauchter Challenge UND einer späteren `approved`-Entscheidung einer anderen, aktiven, unabhängig administrativ registrierten Reviewer-UID**. Revocation-/Unveränderbarkeits- und Audit-Trigger bleiben fail-closed. Kein Self-Approval und keine Revision ohne administratives Verfahren.
- **Live-SQL-Prüfung:** 0 Projekte, 0 Grants, 0 Reviewer, 0 Challenges, 0 Decisions. RPC-Issuance ohne bestehenden administrativen Pending-Grant liefert **0 Zeilen**; Consume eines nicht registrierten Proofs ergibt **`false`**. Es wurden **keine Accounts oder Projekte freigegeben**.
- Security Advisor: neue Tabellen nur als `rls_enabled_no_policy` **INFO** (gewollter vollständiger Default-Deny), keine neuen Gate-7-Funktionswarnungen.

### Deployte QA-Edge-Funktion
- `feature-owner-challenge-qa` **Version 1**, `verify_jwt=true`, reale URL `https://xbnnlyyxiilklsygxcof.supabase.co/functions/v1/feature-owner-challenge-qa`.
- Nur `POST {action:"issue"|"verify", projectId, ...}`, streng limitierte JSON-Eingaben; keine Approve-/Activate-Route, kein CORS und keine service-role-Credentials in Browsern.
- Validiert aktuellen `/auth/v1/user`-Issuer-Nachweis und aktive KatoSync-Mitgliedschaft. `issue` ruft nur die serverseitige atomare Nonce-Funktion auf. `verify` nutzt den **gemeinsamen** `src/lib/featureOwnerKeyProof40.ts`-Ed25519-Verifikator gegen den exakt servergespeicherten Admin-Key und verbraucht die Nonce einmalig über DB-RPC.
- Antwort bei korrektem Besitz lautet **`proof_consumed_pending_independent_review` mit `grantsRights:false`**; keine stille Aktivierung. Realer unautorisierter HTTP-Aufruf → **401**.

### QA
- **716/716 Node-Tests grün** mit `--test-concurrency=4`, darunter sechs zusätzliche Gate-7-Tests: Erfolgskette, Signaturmanipulation, Zeitablauf, Missing-Admin-Provision, Rollenabweichung, Replay- und DB-RPC-Race-Resultate.
- Direkter TypeScript-DOM-Check des Edge-Handlings und vollständiger TypeScript/Vite-Build (1.909 Module) grün. Bestehende Bundle-Chunk-Größenwarnung ohne Build-Abbruch.
- Keine Rust-Code-Änderungen in diesem PR; Rust Gate 6 hatte **290/290 Tests grün** (8 planmäßig ignoriert). Kein installierter App-Build.
- Dokumentation `docs/KATOSYNC_4_0_OWNER_CHALLENGE_GATE7_2026-11-05.md`.

### Weiterhin P0 vor KatoSync-4.0-Beta
1. Zwei-Personen-Onboarding / unabhängige Reviewer-Identitätsprüfung und dokumentierte Admin-Zuordnung der **echten** Projekt- und Eigentümer-UID; derzeit **0 aktive Freigaben**. Ein service-role-Datenbankreview ist noch **keine kryptografisch vom Menschen signierte** unabhängige Admin-Attestation.
2. Echtes Ende-zu-Ende mit autorisiertem KATOOS-Login → Pending-Key → Challenge → Signatur → Consume → unabhängigem Review → Active-Key → GitHub CI/Git-/MVP-Scope-Receipt → revokationsfester Recheck. Keine echte Freigabe oder bestätigte Feature-Abnahme bislang.
3. Getrenntes append-only **Accepted-Ledger** und verifizierte Prozent-/ETA-Projektion erst danach; `verifiedPercent=null` weiterhin.
4. Signierte/notarisierte Beta-Installationen und Mesh E2E auf M2/M3/Windows; M2-Speicher derzeit ~46 GiB frei, Ziel >=80 GiB.

**QA-Sicherheit:** Alle neuen Berechtigungsstufen bleiben auf einer bereits administrativ vorab vergebenen, unabhängig reviewed Identity angewiesen; kein selbstvergebener Approver möglich.

| 대표 결정 요청 | 대표 | `order_events` pending |
| 확인할 사진 | 대표 · 실장 | `ledger_documents` pending |
| 장부 알림 | 대표 · 실장 | `ledger_notices` seen_at 없음 |

현황(탭에서만, 알림 수에 들지 않음): 수주 없는 진행 중 프로젝트의 단계(`projectStage`) · 수주 상태별 수 · 제작 중 · 납품 수주(최근 8건)의 재단 · 엣지 · 조립 · 설치 필수 확인 done / total (`work/check-state.js`).

## 어떻게
- 매분 cron 안에서 08:00~08:09(KST), 업체 id 앞 8자리로 정한 분에 한 번. 알림은 볼 것 수만 센다(단계 · 작업 진행은 읽지 않음). dedupe `assistant_brief:{업체}:{사람}:dYYYYMMDD`.
- 직원 요청은 돈 · 상담 · 회계 표를 읽지 않는다. 응답에 고객 이름이 없다. 앱 알림 글은 수 하나만.
- `assistant_brief` 는 DB(0030 · 0033)가 이미 받는다 — 이 워커의 종류 목록 · 글만 연다.

author: moshez
body:
Fixes dev-skill-up/pitboss#205

## Plan

Done-when of the ticket, word for word:

1. A sweep under disk pressure (either rule: over 90% used or under 5 GiB free) cleans finished worktrees and clones of every repository the machine's worktree root holds, with the open PRs read per repository from each directory's own `origin` remote (not from the config), whatever config the sweep runs with; a directory whose open-PR state cannot be read is kept and listed with that reason.
2. The line `DISK PRESSURE` names the worktree pass it started and the bytes it freed, and when the free space is still under 5 GiB afterwards it lists each directory over 500 MB with the reason it was kept.
3. A test plays a worktree root with two repositories (one of them not in the config), each with a merged-PR directory and an open-PR directory, at 98% used and 1.0 GiB free: the merged ones are removed, the open-PR ones kept.

What I will change, and why each line is then true.

Line 1. The directories of the workspace that are not worktrees of the configured repository (full clones, and worktrees of another repository) are already judged by `deadscan` from their own `origin` remote, whatever the configuration (pitboss#194): the PRs of that slug are read, a clone whose PRs cannot be read is kept with `the PRs of OWNER/NAME could not be read`. What is missing is the trigger: the aggressive pass starts only over `pressure_percent` used, while the free-bytes rule only prints a line. So `machine.find_crowded` also takes a file system as crowded when its free bytes are under `[clean] min_free_gib` (5 by default), `Crowded` says which rule (`short`) and how many bytes are free, and the sweep's clean (`autoclean.clean_report`) runs the aggressive pass for either rule. The header says which rule: `clean: DISK OVER 90%` or `clean: DISK UNDER 5 GiB FREE`.

Line 2. `diskline.lines` no longer scans for dead paths after the clean: it takes the report of the clean (`account.Report`). For each file system that was under the minimum free space before the clean, the `DISK PRESSURE` line gives the free space, says `the aggressive clean started`, and gives the bytes freed in total and by kind (`account.kinds_text`). For each that is still under the minimum after the clean, further `DISK PRESSURE` lines list each directory over 500 MB that was kept, with why (`account.big_lines`), or say that none is over 500 MB.

Line 3. A new test module, `tests/test_clean_two_repositories.py`, plays a workspace of two repositories (worktrees of the configured one, clones of one the configuration does not name), each with a merged-PR directory and an open-PR directory, on a disk of 49 GiB used of 50 (98%) with 1.0 GiB free: the merged ones are removed, the open-PR ones kept, and the `DISK PRESSURE` lines are printed. It also plays 86% used with 1.0 GiB free (the free-bytes rule alone), a clone whose PRs cannot be read (kept, with the reason) and a disk with room (nothing starts). Unit tests cover `find_crowded` with the minimum, the header and the report lines. The docs (`doc/design.rst`, `doc/example.toml`, the sweep skill's `sweep.md`) and `skill-zips/sweep.zip` say the same.

The Evidence rows below show the head, the change, the new tests and the lines of the code that the Done-when names. I do not repeat the whole suite here: CI's `Run Nox` step (workflow `pr-main.yml`) is its proof.

## Execution

- `src/pitboss/machine.py`: `find_crowded(machine, places, limit, minimum_gib)`; `Crowded` gains `free`, `short` and `free_rule` (whether the free-bytes rule set the bytes to free); the bytes to free are the larger of the two rules'.
- `src/pitboss/cleanjob.py` (new): `Option`, `Job`, `Part`, `crowded_now`, `short_of`, moved out of `autoclean.py`, which is at the length limit. `src/pitboss/cleanheader.py` (new): the clean's header, now naming the rule, and its never-touched line.

author: magnus-gille
body:
Refs SAGA-546 (https://tickets.gille.ai/gille/browse/SAGA-546/), part of SAGA-178.

The first and cheapest step towards faster PR CI. PR CI now takes **26.5 min p50** (12 recent successful PR runs), against **10m18s** in September. This PR fixes three causes seen in the logs. Gates, tests, required checks and release workflows are unchanged.

**Merge order:** only `ci.yml` uses `.github/actions/setup`. No release, tag or dispatch path reaches it, so the 1.4.8 release build is not affected. Even so, merge it after #543.

## Changes

1. **Rust cache: pull requests only restore** (`.github/actions/setup/action.yml`)
   - **Change:** `save-if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' }}`. Pushes to `main` save as before.
   - **Why:** a cache saved from `refs/pull/N/merge` is scoped to that ref, so no other branch can use it. The repository's Actions cache was at 9.7 of 10 GB. In run 41907080860, `test-linux` logged `No cache found` and compiled 1283 crates from scratch.
2. **apt: bound a stalled mirror** (`scripts/ci/apt-install-tauri-deps.sh`)
   - **Why:** in 3 of 20 recent Linux jobs the step took 7–20 min, against about 1 min normally. One run fetched 60.5 MB in 15 min 11 s at 66 kB/s from `azure.archive.ubuntu.com`.
   - **Timeout:** `update` and `install --download-only` run under `timeout 240`, with up to 3 attempts. apt's own `Acquire::*` timeouts only catch a connection that goes silent, not one that crawls.
   - **Mirror fallback:** on a retry, the Azure line is deleted from `/etc/apt/apt-mirrors.txt`. The hosted images point their sources at `mirror+file:` (see actions/runner-images `configure-apt-sources.sh`), and the mirror method fails over only on errors, not when a mirror is slow.
   - **Install:** the real install then runs once with `--no-download` and no short time limit, so dpkg is never killed mid-unpack.
   - **Unchanged:** the package list.
3. **cargo-deny as a prebuilt binary** (`scripts/ci/install-cargo-deny.sh`)
   - **Change:** the official 0.20.2 `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` asset from EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny releases, checked against a pinned SHA-256 (`9f12ed4c…8d5f`) before it is unpacked. This replaces `cargo install` (1m32s, plus compiling on a cache miss).
   - **Version check:** a test keeps the version in step with `CARGO_DENY_VERSION` in `scripts/verify.mjs`.

The workflow tests are updated to match: `test-verify-ci-parity`, `test-dependency-policy`, `test-ci-cargo-gates` and `test-ci-parallel-gates`.

## Not in this PR

`windows-package.yml` is the biggest cache consumer: about 4.5 GB per PR, saved only from PR refs, because that workflow never runs on a push to `main`. Making it restore-only would leave the Windows package cold, so it needs an owner decision. That is recorded in a comment on SAGA-546. This PR alone will probably not stop the eviction while two or more Windows PRs are open.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run test:ci`: 277 pass, 0 fail
- [x] `shellcheck` and `bash -n` on both scripts; `actionlint` on the repo; prettier and eslint on the changed files
- [x] cargo-deny script: download, checksum and install pass. A tampered archive is rejected (checksum FAILED, exit 1, nothing installed).
- [x] apt script against stubs: a hanging first attempt is killed, and the Azure line is removed from `apt-mirrors.txt` before the retry. The download-only then no-download split and the `Acquire::*` options are asserted.
- [ ] On a real runner: the `cargo-deny 0.20.2` log line; apt behavior when a mirror stalls; `Cache Rust dependencies` shows no save on the PR run.
- [ ] After merge: once `main` has saved its caches, compare 20 PR runs with the baseline. Measure p50/p90 of the `test-*` jobs, the Linux `Set up toolchain` step and `Install cargo-deny`, plus `gh api …/actions/cache/usage`.

## Review

- **Implementation:** a Sonnet subagent wrote the change, and the conductor (Opus) reviewed it.
- **Review findings:** two grounded defects in the first version, both fixed in `cbabbd24`:
  - The mirror fallback was a no-op: it only rewrote the sources files, not `apt-mirrors.txt`.
  - The timeout could kill dpkg during the install.
- **Independent review:** no independent review with Codex has been done yet.

Part of #2

## Summary

Code review fixes for wave 3. No system prompt, tool or profile-content changes returned by tools: recordings unchanged, `pnpm agent:eval:replay --check` green, no eval re-recording.

1. **Client IP (#36, owner decision).** The Hosting hop is skipped only on `/mcp`, and only when the right-most `X-Forwarded-For` entry is in Google's user-triggered fetchers ranges (not goog.json minus cloud.json any more).

```diff
 /chat, /stats
-  clientIp: skip right-most if Google-owned (goog.json, not cloud.json)
+  clientIp: right-most entry, always
 /mcp
-  clientIp: skip right-most if Google-owned
+  mcpClientIp: skip right-most only if in user-triggered-fetchers-google.json
```

   Snapshot (`agent/src/google-ranges.json`) and `pnpm agent:ranges` now track that one list; the goog/cloud lists are gone. README, ADR 0002 ("the hop is trusted only for that range on `/mcp`; a caller that can send from that range could still choose its key") and the research note's stale `TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS=1` line are updated.
2. **`CONTACT_EMAIL`** is trimmed before it's validated, so a trailing newline in the secret doesn't stop the revision from starting.
3. **Chat Markdown:** `mailto:` links have no `target="_blank"`; http(s) links keep it.
4. **Eval results line:** "off-topic leaks" becomes "leaks" (GLOSSARY "Leak"). "incl. prompt injection" only shows when the deployed set has `injection` cases, read from its table in `agent/evals/report.md`. A test reads `agent/src/config.ts` as text and checks that `deployedSet.model` matches the agent's default model.
5. **Privacy note:** "expire after a minute and are deleted within a day" (Firestore TTL).
6. **Links:** the card `links` block and `Practices` share one `isOnPage` and one `SourceLink` component. The agent's `offPageLinks` keeps its own `https://` check, so tool output doesn't change.
7. **`Profile.contactNote` comment** now matches the contact section (the CTA sits above the ask/LinkedIn link).
8. **iOS zoom:** chat input is `text-base` (16px) below `sm`, `text-sm` above.
9. **Flaky test** (failed on spec-2-wave-3, push run 41953914842): `contact-ask.test.tsx > is disabled while an answer is streaming` checked `toBeEnabled()` right after the address appeared, but the button only re-enables once the stream ends. It now uses `await waitFor(...)`, and so does the MCP-fallback test with the same pattern. The `e2e/contact*.spec.ts` assertions already auto-wait.

## Evidence

- New tests (red on the old code, green now):
  - `/chat` and `/stats`: `X-Forwarded-For: <a>, 66.249.93.229` then `<b>, 66.249.93.229` → second is 429 (keyed on the right-most entry, the left one is ignored).
  - `/mcp`: forged `<a>, 66.249.64.1` then `<b>, 66.249.64.1` (Google-owned, not a fetcher, direct to run.app) → second is 429. Through the rewrite (`<visitor>,66.249.93.x`) it still keys on the visitor.
  - `CONTACT_EMAIL="ada@example.com\n"` → `ada@example.com`; `"\n"` → none.
  - `mailto:` link has no `target`; a card's `#...` link stays in the tab.
  - Results line without injection cases → `3 eval cases · 0 leaks · …`.
  - e2e (phone size, Chromium and WebKit): the chat input's computed font size is at least 16px.
- Local: `pnpm lint`, `agent:lint`, `test` (132), `agent:test` (250), `agent:eval:replay --check`, `build`, `agent:build`, `test:e2e` Chromium (59) all pass. The WebKit tests can't launch locally; CI runs them.
- Built page: `42 eval cases incl. prompt injection · 0 leaks · ~$0.0004 per answer on Claude Haiku 5.5 · replayed in CI`.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** rate-limit keys

Deploy-time effect: once on main, the agent's per-IP key on `/mcp` comes from the fetcher ranges. If Hosting's peer ever leaves that list, visitors through the rewrite share one key until `pnpm agent:ranges` is re-run. No infra, secret or variable changes.

author: thtbee
body:
This is the "Transfer failed after 5 attempts" over a relay.

The sender started its 30 s wait for the receiver's answer once it had finished writing, but writing only fills QUIC's buffers. At 700 kbit/s that's minutes of data. It now waits for the data to be acknowledged first.

A file filling the link also held up heartbeat answers past their 4.5 s and closed a working session after about 19 s. A heartbeat with no answer no longer counts while packets are arriving. A session whose peer is gone receives nothing, so that's still caught. Attempts that get further no longer count towards the limit of 5.

12 MB at 700 kbit/s, 80 ms round trip, real QUIC over a shaped link: failed before; now 156 s, no session drops, same bytes. Not run on a real relay yet.

Progress still shows what's been written, not what's arrived, so on a slow link the bar reaches the end early and then waits.

Explain an unquoted `kind: on` in environment graph YAML.

## Why this change?

YAML 1.1 reads an unquoted `on` as `True`, so the schema error said only `Input should be a valid string ... input_value=True`.

## What changes?

`SpatialRelationSpec` rejects a boolean `kind` with `YAML reads an unquoted 'on' as True; quote it: kind: 'on'`.

author: peppedeka
body:
Rilascio **v1.6.0**.

**La novità principale: le cose si chiamano con il nome che hanno nel codice** (#30). La regola precedente era una lista di divieti — mai «tendina», mai «lista» — che non copre il termine non ancora inventato. Diventa un permesso ristretto: se una cosa ha un nome nel codice o nel framework si usa quello, anche se la frase scorre peggio; se non ce l'ha, si chiede al dev una volta sola prima di scrivere il documento. Con due pezzi che mancavano: che un termine coniato oggi diventa una fonte autorevole domani, e un controllo meccanico prima di consegnare, perché una regola che vive solo come principio è già fallita una volta.

Nello stesso rilascio, lavoro già in develop e mai rilasciato:

- i termini tecnici usati come verbi restano in inglese, propagato in tutte le skill e negli agent
