author: foreverhighness
body:
## Summary

`providerCatalog()` asked `ctx.llm.listModels()` for each provider by its **display name**
(`腾讯云 Token Plan`, `DeepSeek`) while the DSH llm runtime resolves adapters by the registered
provider **route id** (`tencent-token-plan`, `deepseek-official`). The lookup threw `NO_ADAPTER`,
the inner `catch` turned that into an empty list, and `GET /api/metainfer-research-lab/models`
advertised `providers[].models = []` for every provider. The Lab UI model pickers (node inspector,
添加后继, merge dialog, reviewer, project role settings) therefore had no model choices at all, even
though `roles`/`default` resolved concrete provider/model pairs and runs worked.

This PR asks the runtime by `provider.id` and adds a regression test that fails on the old lookup.

Fixes #69

The branch contains two commits:

- `fix(dsh-metainfer-research-lab): query llm.listModels with the provider route id` — the one-line
  host change plus a comment stating the id/name contract.
- `test(dsh-metainfer-research-lab): cover model catalog route-id lookup` — a `node --test` unit
  test with a fake llm that only answers route ids.

Diffstat: 2 files changed, +97/−1 (all under `dsh-metainfer-research-lab/`).

## Root cause

`host/models.js:260-261` (at `master` `6c1536b`):

```js
models = typeof llm.listModels === 'function'
  ? (await llm.listModels(provider.name)).map((model) => ({ id: model.id, name: model.name ?? model.id }))
  : [];
```

- DSH `LlmRuntime.listProviders()` returns `{ id, name }`: `id` is the registered route
  (`tencent-token-plan`), `name` is the human display name (`腾讯云 Token Plan`).
- `LlmRuntime.listModels(provider)` documents the parameter as a *registered provider route* and
  internally calls `registration(provider)` → `this.adapters.get(provider)`, which is keyed by route
  id. A display name throws `NO_ADAPTER` before the adapter's `listModels()` is reached.
- The inner `catch { models = [] }` converted that error into an empty catalog for every provider,
  and `providerCatalogCache` served the empty result for the next 60 s — so the failure looked like
  "this provider has no models".

The same file already passes provider ids to `llm.resolveModelInfo()` inside `resolveCapabilities()`
(after a tolerant id-or-name check), which is why availability validation and node execution worked
while the catalog stayed empty.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `dsh-metainfer-research-lab/host/models.js` | `llm.listModels(provider.name)` → `llm.listModels(provider.id)`, with a comment explaining that `listProviders()` returns the route id in `id` and a display name in `name`. |
| `dsh-metainfer-research-lab/tests/models.test.mjs` | **New.** `node --test` regression: a fake `ctx.llm.listModels(provider)` only resolves route ids (returns `[]` for anything else), and the test asserts the catalog queries by id, returns `tencent-token-plan`'s advertised `deepseek/deepseek-flash`, and does not lose providers that legitimately have no models. Also pins project role resolution to the configured provider. |

## Verification

- `node --test dsh-metainfer-research-lab/tests/` → **2/2 pass**.
- Regression proof: restoring the old `provider.name` line makes the catalog test fail
  (`providers[].models` stays `[]`), while the role-resolution test still passes → the test covers
  exactly this bug.
- `node --check dsh-metainfer-research-lab/host/models.js` → pass.
- Manual reproduction on a live DSH `0.2.1-rc.5` instance (`dsh-metainfer-research-lab` 0.11.0,
  provider `tencent-token-plan` with `deepseek/deepseek-flash`): the `metainfer_lab` `models` action
  returned `providers[].models === []` for all three registered providers while
  `default`/`roles` resolved `tencent-token-plan/deepseek/deepseek-flash` and node runs succeeded.
  With this change the catalog advertises the model under its provider id.

## Compatibility

- No request/response shape change: only the values inside `providers[].models` become populated.
  Execution paths (`resolveModelSelection` / `validateModelSelection` / `resolveModelInfo`) are
  untouched.
- Test runner: upstream `master` has no `tests/` directory and no plugin `test` script yet
  (PR #50 adds `"test": "node --test tests/"`). This branch adds only `tests/models.test.mjs`, so it
  does not conflict with #50's test files or its `package.json` line; run it with
  `node --test dsh-metainfer-research-lab/tests/`.
- PR #65 touches `host/models.js` too (adds an `isBlankModelRef` helper near the top of the file);
  different hunk, trivial rebase if either lands first.
- CI does not currently run the plugin's JS tests, and the Python jobs are red on `master` for
  unrelated pre-existing failures — this PR does not change that.

author: ghbmrk
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"ghbmrk"} -->
_Requested by **Mark** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01R91wiieBzMSvPKFsAJVvuK?thread=cmsg_01R91wiieBzMSvPKFsAJVvuKUXCwtQzmuaEX59nJ2tSKkH)_

Closes #4900.

## Package
DECOY-match-wrap-8 (#4900, release items from #4871). Test and ASSUMPTIONS only; `match.go` unchanged. Covers KRN-12 and CLK-4 (file marker `REQ: CLK-4, KRN-12`), ASSUMPTIONS DECOY-a-5.

1. **Untimed worst case.** `TestBreakStreamCost`'s table now also holds `\/` x512 (ID 5), and the test times its near-copy (`\n/` x511 + `y`) within **16x** plain text and the double-break variant (`\n\n/`) within 12x.
   - Measured on this 4-core box, best of three, the whole test's table: `\n/` 6.4 to 10.0x over 9 runs (6 plain, 3 under `-race`); `\n\n/` 4.2 to 7.1x. #4871 measured 8.8 to 11.8x. Adding ID 5 left the other units within their gates (`<` near-copy 2.0 to 3.7x of 9; `\z` units 2.8 to 8.1x of 12).
   - The `\/` value on a table of its own runs 11 to 13.5x (plain text is faster there), so the shared table is the stabler measure.
   - **Speed-up or gate:** the gate. The cost is the designed bound (each break walks the form's rest, about 3 forms x 256 `\`s per break); profiling puts 83% in `follows`. Cutting it needs a new walk (memoising rests across breaks) in a trusted-core-linked file, beyond size S and against the core's line ceiling. 16 is twice the median (~8) and above the worst seen (11.8), so a doubling from the median fails and runner spread passes. Headroom over the worst seen is 1.36x, slightly under the `\z` gate's ~1.5x; that is the stated trade-off.
   - `-race` cost: `TestBreakStreamCost` goes from 45s to 78s here; the package under `-race` takes 495s on this box (the step's timeout is 25m).
2. **Carry pin.** New `TestJoinedFormCarry`: the value `xxxxxxxx\%0a\n\yyyy` trips sent as `xxxxxxxx\yyyy`, `…\%0d\…`, `…\%0a\…`, `…\\n\…` and with CRLF, through `wrappedTrips` (whole and split writes). Mutant `carry: len(f)` → `carry: 0` in `encodings`: the test fails (`"lead xxxxxxxx\\yyyy tail" tripped [], want [1]`); restored, it passes.
3. **Mutation gate.** Six new tests (`TestJoinedOnlyBreaks`, `TestDetectEachLabelled`, and in `stream_internal_test.go` `TestBreakReleasedAtCarry`, `TestOpenHeads`, `TestHighEntropyFloor`, `TestFormInsideBreak`), plus named equivalent sites (below).

## Mutation gate (mutgate)
Since #4908, mutgate targets the `match.go` lines the changed tests run, so this PR inherits the package's older survivors (24 on a2c6da1a). `TestJoinedOnlyBreaks` and `TestDetectEachLabelled` kill 11 of them, and 3 more on lines the new Detect cases reached (92, 171, 173). At 7876814a mutgate still failed on 13: the gate reads the PR body as of the push event, so the equivalent lines added after that push never counted.

The four tests added at db048d83 kill 7 of those 13, each checked by applying the mutant alone and running the package suite (the named test is the one that fails):
- 237 ARITHMETIC_BASE and INVERT_NEGATIVES (`len(f)+1`), 392 `>=`→`>`: `TestBreakReleasedAtCarry` pins that carry is the longest form but one and that a held break is let go exactly carry bytes after it, not one byte later.
- 424 (`break` deleted) and 427 `n > 0`→`n >= 0`: `TestOpenHeads` pins `open` on `\uu000` and `xu0` (no break head, so 0).
- 153 (length floor deleted): `TestHighEntropyFloor` calls `highEntropy` on a 23-character run of 4.5 bits per character.
- 489 `k < len(f.b)`→`<=`: `TestFormInsideBreak`. The hex form `000a` of NUL LF, lying wholly inside a CR-split JSON `\u0\r00a`, is in neither the text as written nor as joined; the mutant trips it.

The earlier equivalence claims for these 7 hold through the public API for realistic values (each delays a release, needs a form of 5 bytes or less, or is unreachable from `Detect`), but an internal test can tell each apart, so they are killed rather than waived. The 6 mutants on the 5 sites below stay named equivalent: no output or state a test can read differs (514 and 518 change only how fast `follows` finds the same break, 538 only which bucket filters a key the exact check then verifies).

Local check at db048d83: `tools/mutgate.py run` and `delete` on `decoy/match`, then `gate` without a body lists exactly these 6 mutants, and with this body passes.

Mutant-equivalent: broker/decoy/match/match.go:100 with the `last == 0` shortcut deleted the function returns b.String()+text[0:], and b is empty when no value was replaced, so the same text (the negation on this line is killed by TestDetectEachLabelled)
Mutant-equivalent: broker/decoy/match/match.go:101 with the return deleted the function falls through to b.String()+text[last:] with last 0 and b empty: the same text
Mutant-equivalent: broker/decoy/match/match.go:514 `c.at + j` makes the search return 0, and the loop below walks forward to the first break at or after j: the same break, found more slowly
Mutant-equivalent: broker/decoy/match/match.go:518 this return is reached with k == 0 only if HasPrefix(t[j:], f[:0]) is false, which cannot happen, so `k <= 0` and `k < 0` agree wherever it runs
Mutant-equivalent: broker/decoy/match/match.go:538 `- 1` shifts every key by 2, the same at build and lookup; only (NUL, 0x01) lands on 0, the either-end bucket every break already walks, and Result.add ignores a repeat

## Risk tier
A (`broker/decoy/`). `premerge.py --needs-mark`: `agent` (not a gate file). Tier A still needs the separate Security accept.

## Findings
- blocker, fixed here: mutgate was red on a2c6da1a with 24 older `match.go` survivors on lines the changed tests run. 11 are killed at 75c6c5a5, 3 more those tests reached at 7876814a, and 7 of the remaining 13 at db048d83; the other 6 are named equivalent above.
- broker-race (1) `broker/call` TestReadySentenceAlwaysGoesBeforeTheClip failed once on a2c6da1a. It is outside this diff, passed 20 times under `-race` per the reviewer, and has been re-run once.

## Before / After
Before: the `\/` near-copy was untimed, so a regression doubling it stayed green; `carry: len(f)` could be dropped with the suite green; 24 `match.go` mutants lived.

After: all three fail CI, or are named equivalent with a reason.

## Reuse
Reuses the existing `TestBreakStreamCost` harness, `wrappedTrips` and `tools/mutgate.py`; nothing new.

author: zaxshen
body:
## Summary
The sort-mail rubric left about a third of plain confirmations and rejections in the Inbox: Haiku answered `other` whenever an email carried standard boilerplate. This PR rewrites the rubric so that boilerplate no longer blocks a move, while keeping everything that asks the candidate to act in the Inbox.

- **No longer blocks a move:** these ask nothing of the candidate now:
  - "we'll contact you if selected"
  - status-page, careers, talent-community and social links
  - "do not reply" and process notes
  - general encouragement to apply to other roles
  - optional experience surveys
- **Now a rejection:** a role that was filled, closed or cancelled, and a visa the company cannot sponsor.
- **Still `other`:** an invitation to a call, interview, chat or feedback session, a link to book one, an assessment or form, a question or request to reply, a specific other role, an offer, a paused or on-hold role, and a later message doing any of these.

Only the text block in `framework/skills/sort-mail.md` changes. The steps, verification and "Never" rules are unchanged.

## Results
Haiku, scored with `integrations/gmail-apps-script/test/llm-eval.ts` logic on a private, hand-labelled corpus of 1,516 threads. The corpus has 387 rejections, 729 confirmations and 401 negatives, and 142 of the negatives are interview, scheduling or other action mail.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Rejections moved | 65.4% | 96.9% |
| Applications moved | 65.7% | 93.4% |
| Wrong moves | 0 | 0 / 1,493 |

How the rubric was checked:
- It was tuned on one half of the corpus and confirmed on the held-out half: 97.1% of rejections and 91.1% of applications, 0 wrong.
- A fresh, uncached re-sample of all 377 scored negatives also gave 0 wrong moves.
- An earlier draft did move 2 edge cases when re-sampled, a paused role and a receipt with a survey. This version keeps paused roles in the Inbox, and the survey receipt was relabelled as a confirmation.

No mail is quoted anywhere in this PR.

## Test plan
- [x] `node integrations/gmail-apps-script/test/llm-eval.ts --check`
- [x] The rubric text is byte-identical to the scored version
- [x] 0 wrong moves on the full corpus and on an uncached re-sample of the negatives

author: tomontongfamily-debug
body:
Pump photos could wait behind indefinitely hung OCR workers, unbounded fallback downloads, queued background polls, and six-station financial imports triggered during evidence saves. Own and bound the pinned primary worker, move frame analysis off the UI thread, enforce a 15s recognition budget including queue time, and let bounded background preparation finish for later photos. Evidence-only saves skip unrelated financial/POS refreshes; pump polls cannot block later writes. Cash checks, submission, immutable backups and revision/idempotency safeguards remain in place.

Add native camera fallback without createImageBitmap, retry OCR against the same saved capture, separate recognition from upload/save status, preserve stage timings, and check SIMD capability before downloading the larger runtime. Preserves interrupted-photo recovery from #57, including original request IDs and photo provenance. Browser test servers select available ports to avoid parallel-fixture collisions.

Validation: 254 unit checks and 186 pilot checks passed (5 optional browser/private-input cases skipped in the default suite). Separate Chromium and WebKit compatibility runs passed native capture→upload→real OCR→confirmation without live-camera APIs or persistent cache. All 752 audited private photo outcomes match the prior reader individually:581 automatic,171 review,zero incorrect suggestions. Reproductions cover held startup, dead workers, slow background setup, expired queued jobs, stale replies, recovery, source isolation, financial freshness and immutable retries. Build, lint, typecheck and data-preservation gates passed. Firefox remains unverified because its official browser binary cannot start on this Windows host. These are desktop-engine tests, not a guarantee for every physical phone or mobile network; a timed-out recognition returns an explicit retry/manual-review result.

body:
**What changed**
- Removed the anonymous-namespace accessors `GetCmdList`, `GetCmdListStorage`, `GetCmdListEntries`, `GetCmdStateView`, `GetCmdMode`, `GetCmdStateSelections` and `GetCmdLayoutFlag`. Every use now reads `m_cmdList` / `m_cmdState` / `m_cmdLayoutFlag` directly. JP has no layout-flag branch, so it gets a plain `#ifdef VERSION_GCCJGC` that keeps what the accessor's constant `0` did before.
- `CmdDraw` / `DrawUniteList` call the `AlphaNormal()` inline. Text locals are `char*`, so the real `CFont::Draw(char*)` / `GetWidth(char*)` are called instead of the `const char*` wrappers. To allow that, `GetSkillStr` now returns `char*` (callers in gobjwork/MenuUtil are unaffected).
- `UniteOpenAnim` now has the same shape as `UniteCloseAnim`: `entry->x += 12.8`, `__fabs`, no `step`/`targetX` locals. `CmdOpen` now has the same shape as `CmdClose`, and `CmdClose0` the same shape as `CmdOpen0`. The open/close functions use `transitionTimer++`.
- In `CmdCtrl`, a `s32 mode` local replaces the s32-returning `GetCmdMode` accessor, which was the only thing keeping `cmpwi` instead of `extsh.` there.

**Why plausible**
The EN MAP is a debug link and lists every inline that `menu_cmd.o` used: `CColor::operator GXColor`, `GetCounter`, `GetButtonDown/Repeat`, `GetFont22`, `GetFontItem`, `GetLanguage`, `GetShortItemName`, `GetTable`, `AlphaNormal`, `IsMagicArti` and the `Sprt`/`Sprt2` assignment operators. None of the removed accessors is in that list, and neither are the `const char*` CFont wrappers or `fabs`. When this source is compiled the way the debug build was (-O0, inline off, `-use_lmw_stmw off`), these functions now hit the EN MAP size exactly:

| function | EN MAP | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| CmdOpen | 404 | 432 | 404 |
| CmdClose | 460 | 500 | 460 |
| CmdOpen0 | 624 | 672 | 624 |
| CmdClose0 | 676 | 708 | 676 |
| CmdOpen2 | 428 | 476 | 428 |
| UniteOpenAnim | 656 | 704 | 656 |
| UniteCloseAnim | 636 | 656 | 636 |
| AlphaNormal | 8 | (not called) | 8 |

menu_cmd.o now has 16/34 exact sizes (8/33 before), and it no longer emits any weak or local function the MAP does not list. Other deltas moved toward the MAP size: CmdCtrl +180 -> -28, CmdCtrlCur +372 -> +120, CmdInit1 +88 -> +32, CmdInit2 +44 -> +4, CmdClose1 +220 -> +100, CmdClose2 +164 -> +64, DrawUniteList +176 -> +72.

**Validation**
- menu_cmd fuzzy is unchanged: GCCP01 99.514 -> 99.514, GCCE01 99.514 -> 99.514, GCCJGC 99.385 -> 99.385. No function moved, and data is unchanged (1272/1276/1028).
- `p_menu.h` changed, so every unit in all three regions was checked against the baseline reports: 0 units changed in fuzzy, matched code or matched data.
- `ninja all_source progress build/<v>/report.json` and `ninja build/<v>/ok` pass for GCCJGC, GCCE01 and GCCP01 (all three `main.dol: OK`). GBA images were not built in this clone (src/ changes do not affect them).

**Notes for next pass**
- What remains in CmdDraw, DrawUniteList, ChkUnite and GetCmdItem is GPR/FPR numbering and stack-slot order only. A declaration-order sweep of DrawUniteList found no gain.
- ChkUnite is 172 B short of the debug size because the EN MAP has four `.data` strings under it (`@924` `@925` `@1742` `@1743`, 13 to 19 bytes each). That is debug-only printing, so it cannot be recovered.
- `IsMagicArti` hits 80 B as `return (...) ? true : false;`, but that moves GetCmdItem at -O4, so it is not adopted.

author: chr-hertel
body:
### Submission Review Guidelines:

-   I have followed the [WooCommerce Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/woocommerce/woocommerce/blob/trunk/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [WordPress Coding Standards](https://make.wordpress.org/core/handbook/best-practices/coding-standards/).
-   I have checked to ensure there aren't other open [Pull Requests](https://github.com/woocommerce/woocommerce/pulls) for the same update/change.
-   I have reviewed my code for [security best practices](https://developer.wordpress.org/apis/security/).
-   I have assessed the impact of this change and followed the applicable [review requirements](https://github.com/woocommerce/woocommerce/blob/trunk/docs/contribution/contributing/deciding-pr-high-impact.md#review-requirements).
-   Following the above guidelines will result in quick merges and clear and detailed feedback when appropriate.

### Changes proposed in this Pull Request:

No Core ability lists the global product attributes or creates one. The product abilities can already use a global attribute by ID or name and create its missing terms (#70203), but an agent can't find out which attributes exist or set up a new one. That leaves it unable to build a variable product on new global attributes using Core abilities alone.

- **`woocommerce/product-attributes-query`** lists the global attributes (`pa_*` taxonomies) with the fields of the `wc/v3` attribute read. Each one also returns a `term_count` and its first `terms_per_attribute` terms (default 25, max 100), sorted the way the attribute sorts them. It accepts `include`, `search`, `page`, `per_page` (max 50) and `offset`, and returns `total`.
- **`woocommerce/product-attribute-create`** creates a global attribute from `name`, `slug`, `type`, `order_by` and `has_archives`. Its terms come from the product writes that use it. It's a plain `AbilityDefinition`, not an `ActionableAbility`, because a global attribute is a table row, not a `WC_Data` object. Errors follow `woocommerce_ability_product_attribute_<reason>`: `name_exists`, `name_ambiguous`, `slug_exists`, `slug_reserved`, `slug_too_long`, `name_empty`. A name that matches an existing label, ignoring case, is refused because product writes look up a global attribute by its label. It also refuses a slug that matches an existing label, or a label that matches an existing slug, because product writes resolve a name by its slug first.
- **`woocommerce/product-terms-query`** now accepts a `pa_*` taxonomy, so an agent can page through more terms than the attributes query returns. Attribute terms come back with `menu_order` and none of the category fields. A `pa_*` taxonomy that doesn't exist returns `woocommerce_ability_product_term_taxonomy_unknown` instead of a permission error.

Both new abilities check `manage_product_terms`, as the REST attribute endpoints do. Updating and deleting global attributes are left for a follow-up.

**Backward compatibility:** two abilities are added, and `product-terms-query` accepts more input than before. No PHP signature, hook or stored data changes. The Core abilities are still experimental.

**Multisite:** attributes are stored per site, in the `woocommerce_attribute_taxonomies` table, so this works the same on multisite. Not tested on multisite.

This adds a new public, agent-facing feature, so it needs an independent human review.

<!-- Begin testing instructions -->

### How to test the changes in this Pull Request:

1. Follow the [PHP test setup](../blob/trunk/plugins/woocommerce/tests/README.md), then run `pnpm --filter=@woocommerce/plugin-woocommerce test:php:env -- --filter 'ProductAttributesQueryTest|ProductAttributeCreateTest|ProductTermsQueryTest|AbilitiesLoaderTest'`.
2. In a dev environment, create an attribute, then list it:

    ```sh
    pnpm --filter=@woocommerce/plugin-woocommerce wp-env run cli wp --user=admin eval '
    echo wp_json_encode( wp_get_ability( "woocommerce/product-attribute-create" )->execute( array( "name" => "Color" ) ) );'
    ```

    Expect `slug: "pa_color"`, `type: "select"`, `order_by: "menu_order"` and an empty `terms` list. Running it again with `"name" => "color"` returns `woocommerce_ability_product_attribute_name_exists`.
3. On the next request, run `product-create` with `name: "Shirt"`, `type: "variable"`, the attribute `{"id": <Color ID>, "options": ["Red", "Blue"]}`, and one variation per option, each with a `regular_price`. Expect a variable product with two variations at those prices.
4. Run `product-attributes-query` with `{"include": [<Color ID>]}`. Expect `term_count: 2` and the terms Red and Blue. Then run `product-terms-query` with `{"taxonomy": "pa_color"}` and expect the same two terms with `menu_order`. Run it with `{"taxonomy": "pa_missing"}` and expect `woocommerce_ability_product_term_taxonomy_unknown`.
5. Run any of the three as a customer and expect a permission error.

<!-- End testing instructions -->

### Testing that has already taken place:

- phpcs and PHPStan pass on the changed files, including the `AbilityClassRule` and `AbilityRegistrationRule` rules.
- PHPUnit runs in CI; the first run caught three test-only failures, fixed in the latest commit. `ProductAttributeCreateTest` includes an end-to-end test of the flow above: two new attributes, then a variable product created with four priced variations, using only Core abilities.

**Token impact.** The ability JSON (name, description, input and output schema) as sent to a model, measured with tiktoken `o200k_base`:

| Prompt | Before | After | Δ tokens | Δ % |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| `woocommerce/product-terms-query` | 641 | 699 | +58 | +9.0% |
| `woocommerce/product-attributes-query` | 0 | 486 | +486 | |
| `woocommerce/product-attribute-create` | 0 | 407 | +407 | |
| **Total** | | | **+951** | |

This cost is paid whenever a client loads the tool list, which happens once per MCP session or agent run, not on every call.

### Milestone

<!-- milestone-target-selection -->

author: ywexcellent
body:
### Ⅰ. Describe what this PR does

**Stacked on #1121**: this branch carries the same changes as #1121 (rebased onto the latest master) plus the routes layer. Until #1121 merges, this PR shows both layers; once it merges, the diff reduces to the routes layer below. Please review and merge #1121 first.

**Layer 1 — carried over from #1121 (TemplateBuild lifecycle core):** Manager use cases (ReserveTemplate / SubmitTemplate / CreateTemplate / GetTemplate) with the reserved-draft name binding (B = CR UID), admission webhooks (build-state transitions, per-state spec immutability, pod defaults only on the reserved→submitted transition), and the status controller (Pending / TTL expiry → Failed, submitted → Ready). See #1121 for the full description.

**Layer 2 — this PR (E2B protocol routes):**

- Four routes, dual-registered on the native and `/kruise/api` prefixes: `POST /v3/templates` (reserve, 202, assigns B as the draft's UID), `POST /v2/templates/{T}/builds/{B}` (submit, completes the draft in place and folds the DSL recipe), `GET /templates/{T}/builds/{B}/status` (waiting / building / ready / error with incremental log entries), `GET /templates/aliases/{alias}` (the `exists` probe).
- Submission folds the community recipe into the workload: `from_image` becomes one business container with the reserved cpu/memory as equal requests/limits; `run_cmd` steps are persisted as build options and validated but not executed in this phase (the Ready condition states `CommandsNotExecuted`); `WORKDIR`/`USER`/`ENV` context is folded into each command.
- `from_template` builds on an existing Ready TemplateBuild: the base's accepted workload is copied, the reserved envelope applied, self-reference and backend mismatch rejected.
- Deletion is TemplateBuild-first on the existing route: a SandboxSet that still references the template through `spec.templateRef` blocks with 409 (backed by a field index that reuses the #1138 helper); expired drafts are deletable; legacy SandboxSet/Checkpoint semantics are unchanged when no TemplateBuild exists; the name `tags` is reserved so community tag methods fail explicitly.
- Details `GET /templates/{T}` projects a TemplateBuild first (only single-container workloads with whole-number cpu/mem project; others return 400) and keeps the SandboxSet fallback. Listing `GET /templates` stays SandboxSet-only.
- **Retry safety for the community SDK**: a reserve retry with the same parameters returns the original T/B; a submit retry carrying the same Build identity replays the committed submission. Requests with different parameters or a different Build identity still conflict.
- Reserve rejects names already occupied by a SandboxSet or Checkpoint (409). The auto-warm private headers are rejected with 400 in this phase; a valid-but-unconfigured backend maps to 501.
- Route registration now pairs each pattern with an exact trailing-slash twin (`/{$}`) instead of a subtree, because the aliases and build-status subtree patterns overlap ambiguously at registration time.

### Ⅱ. Does this pull request fix one issue?

NONE

### Ⅲ. Describe how to verify it

1. `go test ./pkg/servers/e2b/... ./pkg/servers/web/... ./pkg/sandbox-manager/... ./pkg/cache/...` (all green with `-race`; full CI green on this head).
2. Community SDK end-to-end: `Template().from_image(...).run_cmd(...)`, `Template.build()` polls `get_build_status` to ready; `Template.exists` works; details/delete resolve the TemplateBuild first; delete returns 409 while a SandboxSet references the template; a repeated reserve (same parameters) returns the same build ID.

### Ⅳ. Special notes for reviews

- The submit replay is keyed by **Build identity** (B = CR UID), not by an input digest: a same-B retry replays without re-comparing the input. The community SDK replays carry identical input by construction; a hand-rolled client re-submitting different input under the same B gets the stale success — an accepted, documented gap.
- `{$}` in `pkg/servers/web/framework.go` changes registration behavior globally: an exact trailing-slash twin is registered for every route. Framework tests cover the exact matching; reverting to subtree registration panics at startup, which is the intended regression net.
- The name-occupancy check lives in the handler (probing infra) rather than admission: reserve inputs are wire-level, invisible to webhooks, and the clean 409 would degrade to a 422 under `failurePolicy=ignore`.
- `docs/proposals/20260916-sandbox-template-build-and-e2b-compatibility.md` is updated in place: submit idempotency is keyed by Build identity instead of an input digest, and the request-handling layering wording matches the implemented split (Manager persists through the narrow TemplateStore).
- Regenerated artifacts: CRD descriptions, webhook manifests, RBAC.

---

### Appendix: Incidental Changes

- `config/crd/bases/...yaml` — regenerated description lines (no schema change beyond #1121's).

author: windemiatrix
body:
## What problem does this solve?

The previous PR added `Library.Collections`, `CreateFolder`, `CreateAlbum` and `RenameCollection`, but on macOS the cgo bridge answered `ErrNotSupported` for them. This PR implements the three bridge methods behind them in Objective-C. Deleting collections and changing the assets of an album are not here: they come in the next PR, together with the live test.

## How does it solve it?

- `pk_collections` walks `fetchTopLevelUserCollectionsWithOptions:` and `fetchCollectionsInCollectionList:options:`. It sends both to `PHCollection`, which declares them.
  - It keeps user folders (`PHCollectionListTypeFolder`) and albums (`PHAssetCollectionTypeAlbum`): smart folders, smart albums and the subtree of a smart folder are left out, as the `Collection` doc says.
  - A folder comes before what it holds, and the parent of a top-level collection is "".
- `pk_create_collection` makes a folder or an album in one change.
  - A parent must be a folder that can take content; otherwise it is `PK_NOT_FOUND`.
  - The parent's change request is taken before the creation request, so a failure cannot leave the new collection at the top level.
- `pk_rename_collection` sets the title of a folder or album that can be renamed; a smart one is `PK_NOT_FOUND`.
- If PhotoKit returns no change request, the block raises, so a change cannot report success and do nothing.
- Every C string becomes an Objective-C object before `performChanges:`, as in the import. A string that is not UTF-8 names no collection and is never fetched.
- An error carries only a code, the NSError domain and code, or the name of an exception, never an identifier or a title.
- `PK_NO_ASSET` maps to `ErrNoAsset`, and `pk_perform_changes` takes a NULL identifier for a change that creates nothing.

Deviations from the task:
- `internal/bridge/cgo_darwin_test.go` is edited, though the task's file table does not list it. It is not `photokit/cgo_darwin_test.go`, which the task forbids. The new test has the shape of `TestImportBeforeChange` and never reaches PhotoKit.
- `pk_identifiers` moves to the next PR: no caller here, and an unused static function fails under `-Werror`.
- The collection lookup takes a C string and converts it before `performChanges:`.

author: mvassilev
body:
`ramdump` took one region, so a list of regions meant a process each: on chr20, 100
regions of 1 kb took 65 ms a region, about 40 ms of it ROOT's libraries starting and
28 ms opening the file, against 6.3 ms a region in a process that keeps the file open.

`ramdump file region...` now reads the regions in turn from the file kept open, each
region's records in order, as `samtools view` does without `-M`, so a record in two regions
is printed twice. `-c` prints the count of all of them. The readers made at the first
record found serve every region after it.

NA12878 chr20 at 30x on a Xeon E5-2690 v4, pinned to one socket, file in the page cache,
medians of 5 runs in alternating order, the 100 regions of the paper's `access/loci.txt`:

| | wall | CPU | memory |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| develop, a process each | 6.55 s | 6.55 s | 45 MB |
| this, one process | 0.73 s | 0.75 s | 51 MB |

The output is the same, byte for byte. A new test checks the order and the counts with and
without a FLAG filter. All tests pass. No format change.

author: scottyfncodes
body:
A PLAYCRAFT pass on the current build (played in Chromium on desktop and iPhone 13). It found three things to fix, and this PR fixes all three.

## What changed
1. **Phone HUD and map text is at least 12 px.** Before, the smallest visible text was 8.5 px: the Map and Koda chips, the compass letters, "funds" and the map pins. Every label that shows during play or on the map is now 12 px or more. `scripts/verify.mjs` (no overlap, nothing off-screen, touch targets OK) passes on all five iPhone sizes, including the sled and helicopter HUDs.
2. **Hit-stop on the avalanche blast.** When the charges fire, the game clock drops to 6% speed for 90 ms, then eases back to full speed over 0.4 s. Sound and HUD keep running in real time. Measured in the browser: game time per frame goes 0.05 s → 0.003 s, then recovers.
3. **Vibration on the blast, hard sled landings and finished missions.** This uses `navigator.vibrate`, so it works on Android and does nothing on iPhone Safari. A Vibration On/Off setting is in the pause menu, shown only where the browser supports it. Old saves get it switched on.

## Verification
- typecheck, 142/142 tests (3 new in `tests/feel.test.ts`), build, `scripts/verify.mjs` PASS on 5 viewports
- `playcraft_verify`: overall 79 → 80. Game feel 74 → 79, player experience 70 → 79, mobile 93 → 95. Resolved: text legibility (verified), hit-stop, haptics.
- Verify flagged "hold centre (phone)" as a regression. I tested it directly on the baseline build and this build, 4 trials each. On both, a static hold at screen centre (the camera-look half) moves nothing; the only motion is Koda trotting, in both builds. Touch input code is unchanged. The baseline "response" was Koda moving at that moment, so this is probe noise, not a game change.

## Not done
- Time to play (about 4 s in the probe): this is measured on software rendering at 4–8 fps, so it doesn't reflect a real device.
- Assist / difficulty options: the game has no fail state, so an easy mode has nothing to soften.
- Not tested: vibration on a real phone; how the hit-stop feels at a real 60 fps.

Fresh bounded-shelf review after live failures. Root cause: prior open-cover clearance moved every spine on either side of the cover, creating giant empty gaps and making scrolling appear broken. New design leaves finite-mode CD spine coordinates **identical whether the jewel case is open or closed**. The case uses a separate overlay, may sit off-centre at a shelf endpoint, and travels offscreen naturally as users browse away. Circular modes retain original spine clearance.

Expanded regression suite exercises actual stage/cover wheel events, cover swipes, keyboard arrows, endpoint snapping, pinned-cover refresh, and an open/closed spine-position invariance matrix (five shelf positions × five cover indices). The rendered case is not yet confirmed on the user's actual browser/hardware; **do not merge until live visual verification**. JS asset version updated; Unreleased changelog updated.

author: daanvdk-mck
body:
### 📝 Description
Part of removing the closed-source `iguazio` SDK from the MLRun API server. This PR moves the Orca token, user and version calls of the Orca-leader client (`framework/utils/clients/iguazio/v4.py`) off the SDK and sends them as direct `httpx` requests, each with explicit per-call identity headers. The behavior MLRun exposes is unchanged: same `mlrun.errors.*` classes and messages, and Orca receives the same method, path and body. The HTTP-level characterization tests from ML-13184 pass unchanged against the new code.

**Depends on #10232 (ML-13184).** This branch is built on it, so until #10232 merges this diff also shows its commit. Review only the last commit, `[Auth] Send Orca token, user and version calls as direct HTTP requests`.

---

### 🛠️ Changes Made
- **Rewritten as direct requests** to `{iguazio_api_url}/api/v1/...` through one shared `_send_orca_request` helper:
  - `refresh_access_tokens`: `POST authentication/refresh-access-tokens` `{"refreshTokens": [...]}`, service-account identity
  - `revoke_offline_token`: `POST authentication/revoke-offline-token` `{"token": ...}`, caller's headers
  - `get_user_id_by_username`: `GET profile/users/{username}`, caller's headers; reads `metadata.id`
  - `get_oris_version`: `GET info/system`, service-account identity; reads only `metadata.version.orisVersion`
  - `resolve_token_from_igz_yml`: parses the YAML itself and selects the token by name, else `default`, else the first entry when there is no `default` (several `default` entries select none). It validates only the selected token, with one `POST authentication/refresh-access-token` that carries no `Authorization` header. Every failure is still `MLRunNotFoundError` with the existing two messages; any failed validation, including an unreachable Orca, gives "No valid tokens found for user".
- **Identity per call:**
  - Service-account calls send the service-account headers.
  - Forwarded calls send exactly the caller's request headers (minus `content-length`). Nothing is added when they carry no `Authorization`, e.g. a cookie-only request.
  - Every call carries the request's context id (`x-igz-ctx`) when one is set.
- **Status and errors:**
  - Any 2xx counts as success, including 202 and the 207 partial batch refresh.
  - Error statuses map through `STATUS_ERRORS` to the call's existing default class, with the `errorMessage`/`ctx` enrichment kept.
  - Transport errors and service-account token read failures raise the call's default class.
  - A missing `orisVersion` or `metadata.id` raises the call's default class. `resolve_oris_version` still returns `""` and doesn't cache it.
- **Transport:** one `httpx.Client` per `Client` (a singleton): 60 s timeout, `HTTPTransport(retries=3)` (connection attempts only, no status retries), `verify` from `iguazio_api_ssl_verify`. Its cookie jar never stores response cookies, so a cookie from one call is never sent on a later call made for a different identity.
- Deleted the unused `refresh_access_token` and its 2 tests, along with the SDK option-schema imports and `tempfile` that only these calls used.
- Docstrings in `services/api/utils/helpers.py` no longer refer to the SDK.

The SDK client stays in `Client.__init__`, used now only by `FollowerClient`'s policy calls; removing it is a separate ticket (ML-13188).

author: ii999
body:
## Summary

`credential set` gets two interactive input modes. In both, the value stays out of the calling Agent's reach.

### `--input dialog`

- Opens a local desktop window (eframe/egui, glow renderer) and blocks until the user saves or cancels.
- With `--json`, the command reports only completion metadata. Possible statuses are `stored` (exit 0), `cancelled` (exit 130 or 128+signal), and `failed` (exit 4) with a nonsecret `reason`.
- If a save is already running when cancellation is requested, the save finishes first. A confirmed write is still reported as `stored`.
- If the store cannot confirm a write, the command reports `store-unconfirmed`. It never reports an ordinary cancellation in that case.

### Dialog window

- The header shows "Save credential" and the credential name.
- The definition's description is the placeholder text of the empty input field.
- Input is masked and can span multiple lines. An eye toggle in the bottom-right corner of the field shows or hides the value. The value is hidden again whenever the window loses focus or a save starts.
- Accessibility text stays masked even while the value is shown.
- Paste through the keyboard shortcut or the field's context menu reads the raw clipboard text, so CRLF line endings, tabs, and trailing whitespace are preserved.
- Cancel and Save are centered below the field. Cmd+Enter (Ctrl+Enter elsewhere) saves, and Escape cancels.
- After a failed save the input stays editable, so the user can retry without re-entering the value.

### macOS appearance

- The window is transparent and its content extends under a hidden title bar.
- A system material is placed behind winit's content view: `NSGlassEffectView` (Liquid Glass) on macOS 26 and later, and `NSVisualEffectView` vibrancy on earlier releases.
- SF Pro and SF Mono load from `/System/Library/Fonts` when present.
- Windows uses Segoe UI and Consolas when present. Linux keeps egui's bundled fonts.
- When no backdrop is installed, which includes every non-macOS platform, the same layout paints an opaque background.

### Terminal editor

- Replaces the `rpassword` prompt for interactive terminals.
- Masks input, supports line editing, has an F2 or Ctrl+R reveal toggle, and handles bracketed paste.
- Enter inserts a newline and Ctrl+S saves.
- Nonterminal stdin keeps its existing read-to-EOF behavior. Explicit `--input terminal` refuses tool pipes.

### Packaging

- Linux desktop libraries (Wayland, X11, XKB) are dlopened only when a dialog opens, so headless executables keep the libc-only dynamic-link baseline.
- The release archive includes `licenses/` with the notices for egui's bundled fonts.
- README and the agent skill document both input modes and how an Agent must wait for the dialog's result.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --check`, plus `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` with and without `--features test-keychain`, on macOS.
- `cargo test --features test-keychain` on macOS: all suites pass. The dialog rendering tests confirm that a canary value never reaches accessibility output, platform output, or rendered shapes while masked. They also confirm that paste preserves CRLF, Unicode, and whitespace, and that the save shortcut neither inserts a newline nor saves during IME composition.
- The macOS dialog was rendered in light and dark appearance, with masked, revealed, and error states, against an isolated test credential store.
- The Windows and Linux code paths were not compiled locally. CI covers them.

body:
## Summary

- The player now tells dash.js where to start when the manifest loads. Before, the chosen quality was applied at `STREAM_INITIALIZED`, by which time dash.js could already have requested the first segment at its 1000 kbps default.
- A chosen quality starts at its exact representation and codec set, unless the last measured speed is under 2.5 times its bitrate. In that case the video starts at a low bitrate in the same codec and steps up from the next segment.
- Auto starts in the codec set it will climb in, at the highest representation within 40% of the measured speed. With no reading yet it keeps the 1000 kbps start.
- Connection speed is timed from completed video segments, because `getAverageThroughput` read 16-34 Mbps on a 5 Mbps link in testing. It is one number per device in web storage and never syncs.
- A set the browser reports as unsupported is left out of the start decision. The switch at `STREAM_INITIALIZED` stays as the fallback.

## Related issue

Closes #408

## Change type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor or maintenance
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Build, packaging, or CI

## Validation

- [x] `pnpm test`: 214 files, 1283 tests passed
- [x] `pnpm build`: passed
- [x] `cargo fmt --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --all -- --check`: passed
- [x] `cargo clippy --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --all-targets --all-features`: exit 0, warnings only
- [x] `cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --all-targets --all-features`: 63 suites, 1210 passed, 0 failed. Run before the last frontend-only constant change; no Rust file differs from main.
- [ ] I smoke-tested the affected desktop behavior. Device testing is pending with the owner.

Agent checks, with the helper bundled and run through real dash.js 5.2.1:

- Headless Chrome on macOS, synthetic ladder: fixed 1080p, VP9 across sets, a low preference, a slow link, Auto with and without a reading, and resume all started as designed. Audio stayed on the original track with a dub listed first.
- WKWebView, hidden window: H.264 and VP9 picked the right start. Two more scenarios returned no result.
- `pnpm tauri dev` on macOS, isolated profile, hidden window, real videos through the proxy, one run each:

| Case | main first frame | this PR first frame |
|---|---|---|
| Fixed 1080p, video A | 1.74 s, 1080p | 1.28 s, 1080p |
| Fixed 1080p, video B | 0.47 s, 1080p | 0.96 s, 1080p |
| Auto, H.264 preferred, 2 videos | over 40 s, 240p first | 0.42 s at 1080p and 1.16 s at 720p |
| Auto, AV1 preferred, BBB | over 40 s, 240p first | 0.28 s, 1080p |

The main Auto starts ran in a hidden window, where playback is known to stall, so that gap needs checking in a visible one. Fixed 1080p already started sharp on macOS on main, so WebView2 is the path this needs confirming on.

## Screenshots or recordings

## Risk and compatibility

- Playback: the first frame can come later when the start quality is higher than before. In Chrome on macOS, a synthetic ladder with a 3.5 Mbps top went from about 0.5 s to about 1.35 s at 20 Mbps. Not measured on Windows.
- Playback: an AV1 preference now starts on AV1 instead of hopping there from H.264. On macOS, `lGalJmyI78w` at AV1 240p failed to decode on main right after that hop, with about 30 s of black before a fallback source, and played cleanly past 100 s on this branch (one run each, hidden window).
- Network: the first segment is larger for a high start quality and smaller for a low preference.
- No migrations, database changes, permissions, Rust changes or background work.

- [x] No new secrets, private data, telemetry, or broad Tauri permissions were introduced.
- [x] User-facing documentation was updated where needed.
- [x] Dependency and lockfile changes are intentional and limited to this PR.
- [ ] Breaking changes and upgrade steps are clearly documented.

author: gesposito
body:
Task 2.1 of `alpha-release` (design D2): the release workflow's publishing path and the repository settings around it.

**Workflow.** A dispatch with `dry_run` false runs two jobs after the verify jobs:

- `gate`, in the `release` environment (the maintainer as required reviewer, `main` alone may deploy), does nothing but end the commit's deployment to `release` with success;
- `publish`, after it and outside the environment, the one job with `contents: write`, with no cache: `scripts/release-notes.sh` refuses a version other than `[workspace.package].version` (which the daemon and the server print) and a changelog section that is missing, undated or empty, and gives the notes; the job checks the tarballs against their sums, refuses an existing tag or release, creates the draft pre-release `v<version>` on the dispatched commit with the three tarballs, a `.sha256` per tarball and `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`, publishes it (which creates the tag) and reads the tag and the release back.

The first job runs the same check when a run publishes, so a refused version builds nothing. Each tarball's `.sha256` is written by the build job and checked by the verify jobs.

**Tag rule.** A tag ruleset `releases` on `v*` with `required_deployments: [release]` and no bypass (no ruleset bypass can be a deployment). Tested on a throwaway `0.0.0-dryrun2` from a branch allowed for the test alone:

- a tag pushed without a deployment: refused, "Missing successful active release deployment";
- run 42019676267, publish job inside the environment: the draft's publication, which creates the tag, refused with the same message (a deployment in progress does not count);
- run 42020858421, gate before publish: pre-release and tag published on the dispatched commit; the downloaded tarball verified with `gh attestation verify` and its sum.

The throwaway's release, tag, branch, branch policy and deployments were deleted afterwards; nothing remains.

**Settings through the API, read back:** the `release` environment, the `releases` ruleset, release immutability (enabled after the test). Left to the maintainer, optional: unticking the environment's "Allow administrators to bypass configured protection rules", which the REST API cannot set.

Checks: the workflow and hardening tests and the scripts' tests red first, then green; actionlint, zizmor offline and online; `openspec validate --all --strict`; `scripts/check-public.sh`.

author: philippe-desplats
body:
## Summary

Records the outcome of [How the desktop app reaches the Daemon](https://github.com/philippe-desplats/procly/issues/84) in ADR 0009: the desktop app is a client of the Daemon socket through a crate shared with the CLI, and `doctor` is its only path through the CLI.

```diff
 desktop app
-  (planned) thin client of the Daemon socket
+  procly-client crate          # socket types, framing, state paths, no rendering
+    connect / connect_or_start(exe)   # caller passes the procly executable
+  Response forwarded unchanged to the frontend
+  procly doctor --json         # only verb reached through the CLI
 procly (CLI)
+  depends on procly-client
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** ADR 0009 said "the Tauri app is planned as a thin client of the Daemon socket", with no crate, no exception for `doctor`, and `connect_or_start` tied to `current_exe()`.
  **After:** the ADR states the crate and its scope, the explicit executable path, and a new exception for `procly doctor --json`. Decision grilled and recorded on the ticket above, map [Procly v0.5, the desktop app](https://github.com/philippe-desplats/procly/issues/81) updated.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Documentation only, no code changes. The crate split itself is built later from the v0.5 spec.

**Blast Radius:** none

author: 4cewolf
body:
Fastboot is the path where no menu is drawn at all, so everything Visor puts on
screen is something the user did not ask for. This branch makes that path quiet,
gives it an optional splash, and fixes a documentation lie about `timeout`.

## What changed

**`splash=1` — one still frame instead of a text screen**
When autoboot is about to skip the menu, Visor paints the configured
background, logo and title once, and the handover leaves that frame on the
framebuffer instead of fading out, restoring text mode, clearing the console
and printing `Booting: <name>`. The machine goes firmware → splash → the
distro's own splash.

**`splash_image=` — a splash you can replace like a wallpaper**
A PNG/BMP/GIF drawn cover-scaled and centred, with nothing composed on top. An
unreadable or undecodable picture falls back to the composed frame, never to a
failed boot. Unset, the frame is built from `background`, `logo` and `title`.

**`splash_gui=0` — do not touch the video at all**
Skips `gui_init()` entirely: no GOP mode set, no back buffer, no painting. The
firmware's own screen (vendor logo) stays up until the kernel takes over. The
same GUI-less path is taken when `autoboot=1` with `splash=0`.

**The firmware screen is no longer cleared behind your back**
`ClearScreen` used to run unconditionally right after the startup checkpoints,
so even a boot that drew nothing blacked the screen out. It now lives in
`console_takeover()` and only runs in the branches that actually draw (GUI
menu, text menu), together with the cursor hide and the boot.log warning.

**`autoboot_key` now defaults to `V`**
A letter the user has to hold on purpose, not any stray key the firmware or a
keyboard may deliver. `autoboot_key=any` still restores the old behaviour. The
key is polled twice — once before the menu decision and once during the boot
handover — so a press that arrives late still opens the menu.

**`checkpoints=0` — nothing printed on the vendor logo**
The four startup lines exist to diagnose early hangs, but they were the only
thing a fastboot left on screen. They now print only when asked: off by
default, still written to `boot.log` either way, and still forced on when
`boot.conf` itself cannot be read. With `autoboot=1`, `splash=0` and
`checkpoints=0` the machine shows the firmware's logo and nothing else.

**An interrupted fastboot opens the menu in the configured mode**
`main_gui_ensure()` starts the GUI on demand, so `text_menu=1` gives the text
menu and everything else gives the graphical one. Previously an interrupt
after the fast path had skipped `gui_init()` would have had no framebuffer.

**Docs**
`timeout=0` was documented as "boots the default instantly with no menu". It
does not: 0 and -1 both simply never count down. The schema and example now say
so, say that `autoboot=1` ignores `timeout` entirely, and document that the
four startup checkpoints print before `boot.conf` can be read (they are what
makes a freeze visible on the machines in #38).

## Verification

- `make clean && make -j$(nproc)`: no warnings, 794,784 B `visor_x64.efi`.
- `tools/check_config_keys.py`: 136 global keys, all documented.
- `tools/check_features.py`: registry consistent.
- QEMU (OVMF, 1280x800):
  - fastboot + `splash=1`: frame painted at 0.22 s, `main: splash retained`,
    still on screen 4.5 s later after `StartImage()` of systemd-boot — no text,
    no black frame.
  - fastboot + `splash=1 splash_image=…`: the custom picture, full screen,
    nothing composed on top.
  - fastboot + `splash_gui=0`: `main: fastboot - no framebuffer needed,
    leaving the firmware screen up`, no `initialising GUI`, vendor logo still
    visible, `main: fastboot - leaving the firmware screen in place`.
  - V during autoboot: `main: autoboot interrupt key pressed - showing menu`
    → late `gui_init` → `main: entering menu loop`.
  - normal menu (`timeout=5`) and `text_menu=1`: unchanged, console still taken
    over and the menu still drawn.
  - `exclude_self=1` with an entry pointing at the running loader: the entry
    is still pruned (`config parsed, 1 entry`), #44 behaviour intact.
  - TPM probe with no `EFI_TCG2_PROTOCOL`: still logs
    `tpm: no EFI_TCG2_PROTOCOL - measured boot unavailable`, #42 intact.

One honest caveat: QEMU boots Visor end to end in about 150 ms, so a keypress
cannot be timed into the "late" poll window there. Both polls are verified
through the `boot.log` markers they emit, not by a live late keystroke; a real
machine holds the key from power-on, which is the case that matters.

Visor cannot start plymouth — it is a userspace daemon inside the initramfs. If
you want the Visor frame and the distro splash to look continuous, add
`quiet splash` to the kernel command line. Visor deliberately does not inject
it: with `luks=1` a rejected passphrase would then reprompt invisibly.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added an optional boot splash with support for custom images and controls for GUI initialization.
  * Startup checkpoints can display progress, including when the configuration file cannot be read.
  * Fast autoboot can preserve the firmware screen when no splash is shown.
* **Updates**
  * Autoboot can skip the menu and timeout. The menu can still be opened with the interruption key, now **V** by default.
  * A timeout of `0`, like `-1`, waits indefinitely; only positive values count down.
* **Documentation**
  * Updated configuration guidance for splash, checkpoints, timeout, and autoboot settings.

author: penny323mo
body:
Fixes review finding 2: `toggleRecord` in `Lesson.tsx` could leave the microphone on. This is separate from #27 and #28.

## The bug on `main`
- Tapping 「錄音」 twice while the permission prompt was open asked twice and opened two streams.
- A stream that arrived after leaving the lesson kept the microphone on.
- If `new MediaRecorder(...)` or `start()` threw, its stream was never stopped.

## What changes
Recording now goes through a small helper, `web/src/recorder.mjs`, used by `SpeakBox`:
- **Second tap while the prompt is open:** it is ignored. The button is also disabled while the prompt is open.
- **Late stream:** a stream that arrives after the screen closed, or after the learner stopped or switched mode, is stopped at once.
- **Recorder failure:** if the recorder can't be made or started, its stream is stopped and 「咪開唔到」 shows.
- **Leaving mid-recording:** this stops the stream and drops the take, without setting state on a closed screen.

## Tests
- `tests/recorder.mjs` (new), 8 unit tests with a fake microphone and a fake recorder.
- `e2e/mic.mjs` (new), added to CI for WebKit and Chromium. It fakes `getUserMedia` with a delayed real `MediaStream`, opens F1 at 跟讀 and checks:
  - a double tap while asking asks only once;
  - a stream that arrives after leaving the lesson is stopped;
  - a recorder that fails leaves no live track;
  - leaving mid-recording leaves no live track.

  Against `main`'s `Lesson.tsx`, 3 of the 4 checks fail: 2 asks, 2 live streams, 1 live stream. With this change all 4 pass in Chromium. WebKit runs in CI.
- Locally:
  - `npm test`: 178 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped (the Piper check);
  - typecheck and build pass.

## Review fix (13a4cbb0): React StrictMode
The microphone helper was created during render and disposed in an unmount-only effect cleanup. In development, StrictMode runs setup, cleanup and setup again, so the only helper was disposed and 錄音 never asked for the microphone again. Production builds weren't affected.

The helper is now created in the effect's setup, and the same instance is disposed in its cleanup. `e2e/mic.mjs` accepts `EQ_ORIGIN`, and CI also runs it against the Vite dev server. On the dev server it asked 0 times before this fix, and all checks pass after.

Not to be merged until Penny accepts.

### D1, D3, D4, D6: assessed individually against S1–S4 and the code paths
| ID | Assessment |
|---|---|

| D1 (messages counted once, id-based key) | **Indirectly covered for behaviour:** one continuation per response for three cycles, and no duplicate after regenerating. Whether live keys are id-based is not shown; count-based keys only mean a regenerated answer gets no continuation, which is the safe direction. |
| D3 (user count +1) | **Indirectly covered for behaviour:** sends were confirmed live. The user count signal itself is not shown, since confirmation may have come from the generation start; if it is wrong, the result is "uncertain" → paused, never a resend. |

None of the four diagnostics needs a live run: none would verify a safety behaviour that isn't already demonstrated.

### N1–N3
These stay unverified live. For each, the PR lists the unit and E2E tests that cover it and why it isn't practical to trigger.

### L2
English is a documented exception. The definition of done requires live validation, not validation per language.

### Found during the assessment: the es-ES notice gap
`USAGE_LIMIT_PATTERNS`, `AUTH_PATTERNS` and `ERROR_PATTERNS` are **English only**, so Spanish usage-limit and error notices on the validated es-ES interface are not recognized:
- **A notice instead of a response:** nothing more is sent, but no usage-limit reason is shown.
- **A response that ends in an error but then looks finished:** it may get the next continuation, at most one per such response, bounded by the cycle limit.

The second case doesn't meet "error states fail safely" for es-ES. Spanish texts must not be guessed, so requirement 4 stays **open** until the owner either provides the exact texts or explicitly accepts this as a limitation. `README.md` now says notices are recognized in English only.

### M1 status
Six of eight requirements are met, one with a documented exception. **Open:**
- requirement 4 (the notice gap)
- requirement 5 (S6 outcome detail)
- P1

**M1 is not marked complete.**

author: pedrochagasmaster
body:
Owner rule of 2026-11-05, a follow-up to #618: **bodyweight counts only where it's a material share of the load, a coefficient of 0.30 or more.**

## Summary

The catalog gives 1,096 of 1,345 exercises a bodyweight coefficient, from wrist curls at 0.006 up to hangs at 0.99. The engine added coefficient × bodyweight to all of them. Below the threshold, a loaded lift's effective coefficient is now 0: no contribution, no bodyweight dependency, no mismatch.

```diff
 progression-engine.js
+  BODYWEIGHT_MATERIAL_THRESHOLD = 0.3                      # one named, exported constant
+  effectiveBodyweightCoefficient(c, kind) = kind === "bodyweight" ? c : c >= 0.3 ? c : 0
   prescriptionShape: coefficient = effective(catalog)     # every bodyweight branch reads shape.coefficient
-  captured.coefficient !== shape.coefficient → mismatch
+  effective(captured.coefficient) !== shape.coefficient → mismatch   # old rows on a now-zero lift anchor

 app.js: materialBodyweightCoefficient() → engine
   slotLoadingContext, progressionCurrentSession, sessionBodyweightLifts
```

- **Where the constant lives:** in `progression-engine.js`, the engine that owns the bodyweight maths. `engine-policy.js` is the generator's policy and loads after the engine, so putting it there would have added a load-order dependency. The constant is exported for tests and the app.
- **Reps-only bodyweight movements** (`kind: "bodyweight"`) keep their coefficient, because there it's the whole load. Zeroing it would make every set unusable.
- **Stored data:**
  - Slots and rows keep the catalog's coefficient: no migration, no validator change, no stored-shape change.
  - Generated programs, the editor and swaps all store the catalog value, and everything that uses it reads through the rule.
  - #618's unknown-row rule stands for lifts at or above 0.30.
- **Found on the way:** Session details' bodyweight note (`sessionBodyweightLifts`) read `loadingModel` off `canonicalPrescriptionSlot`'s `{day, slot}` wrapper, so it never listed a lift. It now reads the slot and lists only lifts where bodyweight counts. Sessions with a material lift (a squat, say) will show that note, which may change catalog frames.

**Effect sizes**, engine at 80 kg bodyweight, main vs this branch:

| Lift | Set | Recommended load | Engine capacity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EZ ext (0.046) | 55 × 8 @ RIR 0 | 50 × 10 → **50 × 10** | 74.3 → 69.7 kg (−4.7) |
| EZ ext (0.046) | 30 × 10 @ RIR 2 | 30 × 10 → **30 × 10** | 47.2 → 42.0 kg (−5.2) |
| Machine press (0.076) | 80 × 10 @ RIR 1 | 80 × 10 → **80 × 10** | 117.6 → 109.3 kg (−8.3) |
| Wrist curl (0.006) | 20 × 15 @ RIR 2 | 22.5 × 10 → **22.5 × 10** | 32.1 → 31.3 kg (−0.8) |

- **Recommended loads don't move**, because the share was added to both the anchor and the candidates and cancelled.
- **Progress's strength figures and e1RM never included bodyweight**: `readLogRow`'s e1RM is `load × (1 + reps/30)` on the external load. So **no chart shows a step** and no history recompute is needed.
- **The Why sheet line** "It counts X kg of your bodyweight" comes from the engine's `bodyweightContributionKg`, so it disappears for these lifts.

## Evidence

- **`test/progression-engine-plan067.mjs`** (fails on main at the new block, passes here):
  - One threshold: 0.006, 0.046, 0.076 and 0.29 read as 0; 0.3, 0.626 and 0.99 are kept; reps-only 0.1 is kept.
  - The EZ ext and an incline machine press count 0 with 80 kg on file, and their anchor is the external load.
  - A row recorded with a bodyweight anchors normally, and so does one with contribution off; neither ever asks for a bodyweight.
  - A squat keeps 0.626 × 80 and still needs a bodyweight; pull-ups keep theirs.
  - #618's unknown-row cases now run on a material squat.
  - The contribution-maths cases moved from 0.25 to a material 0.5, keeping their 20 kg contributions where the per-side arithmetic depends on them.
- **`test/bodyweight-source-browser.mjs`** (13/13; on main, the engine-contribution, Why and coefficient checks fail):
  - The EZ ext counts 0 kg of the 80 kg on file, and its Why sheet has no bodyweight line.
  - Session details doesn't list it, but lists the same lift at a material 0.626.
  - Progress's e1RM equals the external-load figure (no step).
  - #618's owner path still passes.
- **`test/per-side-engine-browser.mjs`:** its 45° incline dumbbell press (0.038) no longer has a bodyweight line in its Why sheet. Passes 1/1, as does `per-side-engine-bodyweight-browser`.

## Owner question

- **Per-side Why line:** the only per-side explanation string, `why.engine.per_side_bodyweight` ("… per side × {multiplier}, plus {bw} from your bodyweight"), is bundled with bodyweight. A sub-threshold per-side dumbbell lift therefore no longer explains its × 2 multiplier either.
- **Proposed new string** (needs the owner's approval):
  - EN "It estimates total load as {load} {unit} per side × {multiplier}."
  - PT "Ele estima a carga total como {load} {unit} por lado × {multiplier}."

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way.

**Blast Radius:** bodyweight maths for sub-threshold lifts.

- The engine's internal capacity changes for 1,000+ catalog lifts, but in the samples above their recommended loads don't move.
- Session details' bodyweight note now appears where it should.
- Revisions: `app.js` and `CACHE` are at v624.

lukas-beike
body:
Closes #1665 (part of #1675).

## Change

- `ActivityRecord.external_ref` (`ExternalRef(upstream, upstream_id)`): the Intervals.icu mapper (v7, replays via backfill) sets it from `source=GARMIN_CONNECT|WAHOO` + `external_id`. It is stored in `activity_records.details` (`external_ref`), so the schema does not change. The table reader and the session linker read it back.
- `bundle_sessions`: an exact pass runs before every pass that joins a Garmin- or Wahoo-provider record. A copy joins the stored upstream record it names with `ActivityLinkKind.EXACT`, regardless of time and tolerances, one record per provider and session. A copy whose upstream is not stored stays open to the unchanged heuristics. This resolves the "exact links win" case deferred from #1666.
- `link_activity_sessions`: the exact pair is persisted on the copy's own session. Upstream records the copies name are bundled even when they fall outside the date window or sit in confirmed or hidden sessions. Merging still refuses protected sessions, so such a copy is no longer handed to a wrong heuristic partner. A pair already in one session upgrades its link kind (heuristic → exact).
- Diagnostics `canonical_session_conflicts` gains `exact_link_mismatches` (exact references whose records stay in different active, unconfirmed sessions, for example a contradicted earlier heuristic merge; never re-merged automatically) and `link_kinds` (active sessions per link kind). Only local session ids and provider names appear, no provider activity ids.
- Spec `activity-ingestion-and-storage` updated (scenario "Exact upstream reference", diagnostics contract, evidence).

## Acceptance criteria → evidence

- Copy of a Garmin/Wahoo activity with a stored upstream links as `EXACT`, independent of time and tolerances → `tests/test_canonical_sessions.py:ExactLinkTests` (elapsed 4:30 vs moving 3:40, trimmed −30 % and shifted +70 min, Wahoo), `tests/test_session_linking.py:ExactLinkTests.test_a_trimmed_copy_links_exactly_to_its_garmin_activity`.
- Heuristics decide only records without an exact link → `test_exact_links_win_over_a_closer_heuristic_pair`, `test_unknown_upstream_leaves_the_copy_to_the_heuristics`, `test_a_hidden_upstream_keeps_its_copy_from_the_heuristics`.
- Stored heuristic merge confirmed → upgraded to EXACT → `test_an_exact_reference_upgrades_a_heuristic_merge`. Contradiction → reported, not changed → `test_a_contradicted_heuristic_merge_is_reported_not_changed`, `tests/test_diagnostic_session_conflicts.py:test_lists_an_exact_reference_to_another_session`.
- Link kind visible → diagnostics `link_kinds` and `exact_link_mismatches`. The only other duplicate inspection (`latest_wahoo_garmin_duplicate`) compares two Intervals copies with each other, which can never link exactly.
- Equipment matching unchanged (its raw `external_id` join is left as is).

## Decisions and limits

- Storage in the details JSON instead of new columns (the issue's no-schema option). The lookup goes through the existing `(provider, provider_activity_id)` key, so no index or migration is needed.
- Evidence gap: no sanitized real Intervals payload with `source=GARMIN_CONNECT` or `WAHOO` was available. The Garmin format (`external_id` = Garmin activity id) is the one `equipment.py` already relies on. For Wahoo the `external_id` format is unverified; a mismatch only means no exact link, and the heuristics still apply. Strava references are out of scope.

## Validation

- `python tests/run_tests.py --changed` (selector fell back to the full suite, 8488 tests): green on the final head.
- ruff format/check, mypy on the changed files, `compileall`, `openspec validate --specs --strict`: green.
- Sonar pre-push: 0 issues; Vortex agentic analysis 403 (limit, not a pass).

## Review

One `/code-review` at high on `d775cd5ce`. Fixed in the follow-up commit: exact merge persisted on the bundle primary instead of the naming copy; upstream in a protected session left the copy to the heuristics; mismatch query ignored survivor state and athlete decisions; table reader dropped `external_ref`; stale comments. Not fixed:
- Session-level EXACT label over heuristic members: `link_kind` is a session-level strongest-link value by existing design (`_LINK_STRENGTH`).
- Wahoo `external_id` format: evidence gap above, with a safe fallback.
- Exact link bypassing the one-per-origin rule: `_assign_exact` uses the shared `taken` sets, and the persisted origin guard still refuses.
- The diagnostics query runs twice: same pattern as `_CONFLICTS`, diagnostics only.
- Equipment's own `external_id` rule: unchanged by scope ("behaves as before").

Merge danger: two-way door. There is no schema change, and the mapper bump only re-projects Intervals records. Persisted session merges are one-way, but they are guarded by the existing origin and protection rules. Blast radius: cross-provider session bundling and diagnostics.

body:
PR-2 of the action-pack quality-fixes plan (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-05-action-pack-quality-fixes.md`, Tasks 2.1–2.4; spec rev 2 §6 and the ref-date part of §7.2).

## Changes
- **Items read** (`repositories/topics._scoped_items`, both ledger shapes): adds `a.deadline_text` and `raised_on`. `raised_on` = earliest `topics.report_date` over **every** `action_items` row of the `stable_id` (no visibility, supersession or redaction filter), as a correlated subquery. `report_date` is unchanged (newest live row, `DISTINCT ON … created_at DESC`). `idx_action_items_stable` (0073) already serves the subquery (EXPLAIN: Index Scan on `idx_action_items_stable`), so there is **no migration**.
- **Items tool** (`ask_items.ITEM_FIELDS`): gains `deadline_text`, `raised_on`. `SNAPSHOT_FIELDS` is unchanged, so neither key affects apply's stale check. `lambda_rag_search._items` already passes every non-id column through `_iso`, so it needed no change.
- **Agent render** (`action_pack_stages`):
  - New `_day()` returns `YYYY-MM-DD (Wkd)` from a fixed weekday table, or `-`.
  - The agent gets its own topic/chunk renderer, `_record_line`, which prints `said_on <date> (Wkd)`. **`ask_orchestrator._item_line` is untouched**, and a test pins its output.
  - Item lines add `deadline_text "<text>"` when it is set, and `raised_on <date> (Wkd)`.
  - The plan, round and write prompts state `Today (New Zealand): <date> (Wkd) — today is not the date the records were said.`
  - Planner rule: a relative date in the instruction itself resolves against today.
  - Writer rules: a record's relative date resolves against its `said_on`; an item's `deadline_text` resolves against its `raised_on`.
- **Verifier** (`action_pack_verify.build_prompt`):
  - Evidence lines read `ref | kind | said_on <date> | text`, where the date is a topic or chunk `date`, an item's `raised_on`, or `-`.
  - The target line adds `deadline_text` and `raised_on`.
  - `VERIFY_PROMPT` gains one sentence: a relative date counts from the line's `said_on`, never from today.

## Tests
- Integration (`tests/integration/test_rag_search_items_sql.py`, local Postgres, 32 passed):
  - `test_items_rows_include_deadline_text`
  - `test_raised_on_is_earliest_row_even_if_superseded`: three rows dated D1<D2<D3, with D1's topic superseded and redacted. Asserts `report_date == D3` and `raised_on == D1`.
- Unit:
  - `test_item_fields_always_present_new_keys`
  - `test_day_renders_date_and_weekday`
  - `test_record_line_has_said_on_weekday`
  - `test_item_line_has_deadline_text_and_raised_on`
  - `test_write_prompt_states_today_with_weekday`: plan, round and write
  - `test_ask_item_line_unchanged`
  - `test_verify_prompt_carries_ref_dates`
- `test_write_render_drops_web_first_then_documents_and_truncates`: the monkeypatched `WRITE_RENDER_MAX_CHARS` moves from 380 to 430 because the dated lines are longer. The test's intent still holds in the range 410–460.
- `tests/unit` passes locally, except `test_report_bench_candidates::test_every_candidate_is_pinned`. That test is a prompt-file sha check that fails locally on CRLF (a known local-only issue) and does not touch these files.

## Not in this PR
- No `ACTION_WRITER_*` or `llm_tools_client` routing (that is PR-1).
- No `field_sources.said_on` or deadline sanity check (PR-4).
- No `reason_code` / `date_anchor` answer schema (PR-7).

## Revert
Revert the PR. There is no schema change and no config or env change.

author: pipozzz
body:
A Go program carries the standard library it was built with (net/http, crypto/tls, …): built with Go 1.24, it keeps that release's vulnerabilities for good, whatever the base image. Many exporters and operators ship like this for months.

- Goliash already reads the Go version from each Go program in an image (`pkg:golang/stdlib@1.25.7`); the oldest counts.
- Go's release cycles come from endoflife.date (`go`), cache only.
- New hygiene kind `eol-runtime` (**Go past end of life**), a warning: *has Go programs built with Go 1.25.7, past its end of life since Aug 2026: the standard library they carry gets no more security fixes; rebuild with Go 1.27, or move to a release built with a supported Go*.
- On /hygiene, the Security page's supply chain panel, and `goliash_image_hygiene_findings{kind="eol-runtime"}`.

body:
## Summary

Fourth and last of the site decisions brought into the capability vocabulary. `fullscreen` is added (default allow, prompt "This site wants to go fullscreen") on the generic engine-side gate from the pointer-lock PR.

- `requestFullscreen()` rejects with a `TypeError` and fires `fullscreenerror` when the site is blocked.
- On ask the request keeps the element and the promise's resolving functions pending (`fullscreen_request_*` in `ns_js`), reports the request through `X-Capability` and, when the shell answers, either enters fullscreen (the promise then settles with the window action exactly as before) or rejects.
- The rejection path shared with the no-activation case is one helper (`ns_fullscreen_reject`); the pending request is released with the context.
- Docs: capability table row, Direction.md status, Changelog.

With this, the site-settings popover lists six capabilities (camera, WebGL, downloads, pop-up windows, pointer lock, fullscreen), each with Ask / Allow / Block and the same prompt bar.

## Verification

- `meson compile -C builddir` clean, no warnings.
- Virtual display, site on ask: clicking "go fullscreen" shows the prompt and the promise waits; Allow puts the window in fullscreen with the usual "press Esc to exit" notice.
- Site on block: the page gets `fullscreenerror` and the promise rejects with "Fullscreen request denied by the site's settings".

author: samuelhassine
body:
Opened by the CEO Office Developer; the team reviews, the desk answers and merges on approval.

### Proposed changes

**Issue:** #8810 (follow-up of #8744 / #8777 and #8809, product decision in [this comment](https://github.com/OpenAEV-Platform/openaev/issues/8744#issuecomment-6500989433): the home dashboard must be consistent with the Results screen).

**Wrong behaviour:** the home dashboard resilience gauges (`ResilienceGaugeWidget`) compute `success / (success + failed)`, pending excluded, while their ring includes pending. With 14 success, 20 failed, 28 pending the gauge shows **41%** while the green arc covers about a quarter of the ring. `PARTIAL` results are ignored by both the ring and the number, and an all-pending gauge shows a red `0%`.

**Expected:** the same rules as the simulation Results gauges (`PostureGauges`): percentage = `success / (success + partial + failed + pending)` (14 / 62 = **23%**), partial results charted as their own arc, `0%` in grey when every expectation is pending (#8809).

**Cause:** `openaev-front/src/admin/components/workspaces/custom_dashboards/widgets/viz/ResilienceGaugeWidget.tsx`, the `counts` memo divides by `resolved = success + failed` and only reads `SUCCESS`, `FAIL` and `PENDING`; the `accent` memo has no grey rung.

**Change:**
- New `openaev-front/src/utils/resilience.ts` with `computeResilience`, the single definition used by both gauges so they cannot drift apart again (suggested in the issue).
- `PostureGauges` uses it (no behaviour change).
- `ResilienceGaugeWidget`: counts `PARTIAL` (arc in `warning.main`, legend entry shown when non-zero, included in `RING_STATUSES` so the ring click-through drills into it), percentage from `computeResilience`, accent grey (`text.disabled`) when nothing is resolved. Colour thresholds are unchanged on the home widget (they already matched `PostureGauges`, 75 / 50 / 25).

**Tests:**
- `src/__tests__/utils/resilience.test.ts`: the issue's numbers (23%), partial counted as resolved but not as success, nothing resolved.
- `src/__tests__/admin/components/workspaces/custom_dashboards/widgets/viz/ResilienceGaugeWidget.test.tsx` (new): 23% for the issue's distribution, a partial arc and legend entry, grey `0%` when all pending, red `0%` once one is failed.

### Testing Instructions

1. Have expectations with success, failed and pending results (e.g. Prevention: 14 success, 20 failed, 28 pending).
2. Open the home dashboard: the Prevention gauge shows 23%, matching the green arc and the simulation Results gauge.
3. With partial results, an orange arc and a "PARTIAL" legend entry appear; clicking it drills into the partial expectations.
4. With every expectation pending, the gauge shows `0%` in grey.

**Verified locally (sandbox):** `yarn test` on the three gauge test files (13 passed), `yarn lint` exit 0, `yarn check-ts` exit 0. **Left to CI:** the full front test suite, the build and E2E. **Not seen rendered:** the widget was not captured on a running instance.
