author: dante-sparras
body:
## Problem

Diagnostics used Session's startup backend. `Doctor` opened the packaged task with `WindowsStartupTasks.Open()`. `DoctorSignIn` took an `IStartupTask` and called `WindowsStartupRegistry.SameInstall`. `DoctorProbe` read the Run entry using `WindowsStartupRegistry`'s key constants. docs/architecture.md ("Services and feature ownership") forbids one feature using another feature's backend.

## Change

Session now owns one managed read of the sign-in entry, `SignInEntry`, in `src/Winshell.Services/Session/SignInEntry.cs`. It is a plain internal static type that needs no shell services, so `winshell doctor` can call it:

- `Name`, `RunKey`, `ApprovedKey`: the only C# copy of the Run value name (which is also the startup task id) and the two key paths.
- `RegisteredCommand()`: the command the user's Run value starts, or null.
- `TurnedOffInWindows()`: whether Startup apps turned that value off.
- `OpenTask()`: the package's startup task, or null when the package has none or Windows fails.

Who uses it:

- **Session's own backend** builds on it. `WindowsStartupRegistry` reads through it inside its existing `Try`, and still passes its own keys so tests keep using a test key. `WindowsStartupTasks.Open()` wraps `OpenTask()`. Constructors and members that `ShellServices.cs` calls are unchanged.
- **Diagnostics** calls `SignInEntry` directly: `Doctor` passes `RegisteredCommand()`, `TurnedOffInWindows()` and `OpenTask()?.State` to `DoctorSignIn.SignIn`. `IDoctorFacts`/`DoctorFacts` lose `RunEntry`/`RunEntryTurnedOff`, which would only have forwarded to `SignInEntry`. `DoctorProbe` loses its copy of the reads.
- **`DoctorSignIn.SignIn`** takes a `StartupTaskState?` instead of an `IStartupTask`.
- **`SameInstall`**, which only Doctor used, moves unchanged from `WindowsStartupRegistry` into `DoctorSignIn` as a private method.

Behavior is unchanged:

- `WindowsStartupRegistry` still swallows the same registry exceptions.
- In Doctor, a failed task lookup is still "no startup task", and a registry or `State` exception still reaches `Doctor.Guard` ("Could not check").

Separately, Diagnostics also uses the Notifications backend (`DoctorProbe.NotificationAccess` calls `WindowsNotificationBackend`). That isn't fixed here; #1382 tracks it.

## Scope and approval

Fixes #1376

## Verification

- `DoctorTests.A_packaged_sign_in_is_the_startup_task_not_a_path` passes states directly. Its fake `IStartupTask` only supplied a state. Every assertion is unchanged.
- `StartupRegistryTests` only renames `WindowsStartupRegistry.ValueName` to `SignInEntry.Name`. They still cover the Run and StartupApproved reads through `WindowsStartupRegistry` on a test key.
- The unpackaged sign-in tests are unchanged and pass.
- `pwsh scripts/check.ps1` passes on the final head: 0 warnings, formatting clean, all fast .NET tests and all 81 PowerShell tests.

**Not verified:** `SignInEntry.OpenTask()` (the packaged branch) has no test, as before: it needs an installed package. I didn't run a live shell or the slow tier, since no window or UI behavior changed.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way: a small refactor that is easy to revert.

**Blast Radius:** Sign-in. It covers Session's Run-key and startup-task reads, and the doctor's Sign-in check in `winshell doctor` and Settings' About page.

**Agent:** Claude Opus 5.5 in T3 Code through the Claude Code harness

author: jerry73204
body:
Fixes issue 2281 (found by phase-524 W4b): `nros run` relinked the image every time, even straight after `nros build`.

## Cause

`nros run` builds first, so this is a no-op `nros build` that was not a no-op. The Zephyr west road had two always-dirty edges, and each one is enough to relink `zephyr.elf` by itself:

1. **nros-c and nros-cpp shared one cargo target dir.** Their generated image crates are built as two `cargo build -p` invocations of one workspace. Cargo unifies features separately for each invocation. Measured with `--unit-graph`, the nros-cpp build turns on `nros/log`, `nros/macros`, `nros-rmw/log` and `nros-platform/alloc`, and the nros-c build does not. Both builds compiled `nros-c` into the same fingerprint dir against different dependency units, so each one rebuilt the other's work. This shows up even on a plain `ninja` run twice in a row.
2. **West re-configured on every run.** `west build` re-runs CMake whenever it is handed CMake arguments, and `nros build` always passes some. Zephyr's configure always touches `syscalls_subdirs.trigger`, which regenerates the syscall headers and everything after them.

## Fix

1. `_nros_root_cargo_dir` now takes the package. nros-c keeps `<build>/nros-rust`, which is also the header root, so nothing moves there. nros-cpp builds into `<build>/nros-rust-cpp`. With a shared cargo root, the package is part of the key. `gc-zephyr-builds.py` now sweeps `nros-rust-*` too.
2. `builder::zephyr::configure_once` records a digest of the whole west handoff (program, args, env) as `-DNROS_WEST_CONFIGURE_SHA256`. If the build dir is a finished configure with the same digest, a repeat build hands off `cmake --build <dir>`. A changed board, overlay, module or environment changes the digest. Any west option the caller passes (`-p`, `-t`, `-d`) also goes to west, as before. The configure's own inputs stay on `CMAKE_CONFIGURE_DEPENDS`.

## Verified

- `examples/zephyr/c/talker` (native_sim): three `nros build` runs. The first configures and relinks (the new digest argument); the second and third run `cmake --build`, compile nothing and keep the mtimes of `zephyr.elf` and `zephyr.exe`.
- Nucleo-F767ZI Renode twin: `nros build`, `nros build`, `nros run --expect 'Publishing:'` twice. Both runs matched in about 8 s, and `zephyr.elf` has the same mtime throughout.
- New fast-line gate `zephyr-api-cargo-target-dirs` (buildless cmake configure, with a registry row in `negative_diagnostic_registry.rs`), a unit test, and a pipeline test. Each one fails under mutation.
- Box: `just check fast` green. The first `just ci gate` run went red on my own clippy `byte_char_slices`; I fixed it. The second run passed steps 1-8 (check::build in 54m) and then went red at `test-lane-contracts`, on the registry row the new script needed. I added the row and re-ran `check::fast`, `test-lane-contracts` and `check::out-of-lane-deselected` through `run-lane-steps.sh`: all green.
- Not run: `just ci matrix build`. The change is in `zephyr/cmake/` and the CLI, not the top-level `cmake/`, `packages/core` or codegen.

author: ahmedtvmer
body:
**The cause:** the offer decision the app sends is `yes <uuid>`, and the UUID is random. Its hex groups sometimes look like Franco-Arabic words, so the clinical guard treated the decision as a Franco message and intercepted it. That's why the test failed only sometimes. It also means a real Player's decision could have been intercepted the same way, so this fixes the app as well as the test.

**What it changes**
- **Guard:** an exact `yes <uuid>` or `no <uuid>` message now skips the clinical guard. It shares one pattern with the code that reads the decision.
- **Added text still goes through:** anything beyond the bare decision is checked as before, and a new test proves it.
- **Test:** it now runs with fixed UUIDs, including one that looks like Franco-Arabic, instead of random ones. Nothing it asserts was weakened.

**Tests (on the server)**
- With the fix: 140 passed across the Franco, Arabic and assistant pipeline test files.
- Without the fix: the three fixed-UUID cases fail, so the test does catch the bug.

This is a fix to a shipped feature, so there's no Feature list entry.

Closes #569

author: detail-app[bot]
body:
**Detail bug report:** [View on Detail](https://app.detail.dev/org_c5cadc78-1d57-439b-a85b-4a6a1d3763d8/bugs/bug_a3603b4f-d024-46a6-8fa0-b105b7fdff3f)

## Bug

The v1 API's `mapError` (`hscontrol/api/v1/errors.go`) maps state/db errors to HTTP statuses, with a 409 arm for conflicts. But the `users` table's unique index `idx_name_no_provider_identifier` rejects duplicate usernames with a raw driver error that matched nothing in that arm, so it fell through to the default **500** instead of the intended **409**.

This affected two paths:
- **Rename collision** (deterministic): `POST /api/v1/user/{id}/rename/{takenName}` has no pre-check, so every rename to an already-taken name hit the constraint and returned 500.
- **Create race**: the create handler pre-checks the name, but two concurrent requests with the same name can race past the pre-check; the loser hits the constraint and got 500.

The root cause was two-fold: gorm was opened without `TranslateError: true` (`hscontrol/db/db.go`), so unique violations never became `gorm.ErrDuplicatedKey`; and `mapError`'s 409 arm had no entry for `gorm.ErrDuplicatedKey` anyway. The `CHANGELOG.md` and the parity golden both already documented/pinned 409 for duplicate create, so this was a deviation from the intended contract.

## Fix

- **`hscontrol/db/db.go`**: Enabled `TranslateError: true` in both the SQLite and PostgreSQL `gorm.Config` opens. Both drivers implement gorm's `ErrorTranslator` interface, so unique-key violations now become `gorm.ErrDuplicatedKey` and foreign-key violations become `gorm.ErrForeignKeyViolated` — making them matchable by sentinels instead of raw driver error strings.
- **`hscontrol/api/v1/errors.go`**: Added `errors.Is(err, gorm.ErrDuplicatedKey)` to the 409 Conflict arm of `mapError`. Since `gorm.ErrDuplicatedKey` previously matched nothing (it didn't exist without `TranslateError`), this cannot regress any existing mapping; the 404 (`gorm.ErrRecordNotFound`) and 400 arms are unaffected.
- **Tests**: Updated three db-layer tests that matched on raw driver error strings (`"UNIQUE constraint failed"`, `"FOREIGN KEY constraint failed"`) to use `errors.Is` with `gorm.ErrDuplicatedKey` / `gorm.ErrForeignKeyViolated`, which is more robust and works under `TranslateError`. Added a `TestAPIV1RenameUser/duplicate_name_parity` subtest + golden pinning 409 for rename collisions, closing the test gap that let the deterministic rename 500 go undetected.

## Testing

- Unit tests: `TestAPIV1CreateUser`, `TestAPIV1RenameUser` (including the new `duplicate_name_parity` subtest), `TestConstraints` (sqlite + postgres), `TestRenameUser` (sqlite + postgres), `TestCannotDeleteAssignedPreAuthKey`, and the full `hscontrol/db` and `TestAPIV1*` suites all pass.
- Build, `golangci-lint`, `golangci-lint fmt`, and `go vet` are clean.
- Integration tests via `cmd/hi` against Docker: `TestUserCommandValidation` (includes the "create duplicate" case), `TestUserCommand` (exercises rename via CLI), and `TestUserCreateCommand` all pass.
- Postgres tests required installing `postgresql-17` and running the pre-built test binary as the `postgres` user (since `initdb` refuses root); the `postgrestest` library also needed `/etc/hosts` to resolve `localhost`.

---

- [x] have read the [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) file
- [x] added unit tests
- [ ] updated documentation if needed
- [ ] updated CHANGELOG.md

---

author: zaxshen
body:
Part (d) of GH 1955: the code-reviewer's effort can follow the risk of the commit under review. It's opt-in, with an A/B to measure it, and nothing changes until a key is set.

## What changes
- `bro_atomic_close` assigns the review effort and returns it as `reviewer_effort`. It also records it in a new `reviewer_effort_assigned` audit row (`task_id`, `commit_sha`, `effort`, `reason`, plus `label`/`arm` when the task is enrolled in the A/B).
- The tier rule lives in `src/reviewer-effort.ts`:
  - `high` for a prompt-bearing task or a changed path under a `high_effort_paths` prefix.
  - `low` when every changed path is docs or tests.
  - `medium` otherwise, an empty list included.
- `require-spawn-effort` and the code-reviewer `agent_runs` row both read the task's newest assignment through `reviewerEffortFor` (`src/hooks/lib/effort.ts`). They fall back to `plugin_config.reviewer_effort` when there's no `task_id=<N>` in the prompt or no row for it. The gate is still an allowlist: it admits one effort. The deny text for the config fallback is unchanged, so the hook goldens didn't move.
- Two new config keys, both off when unset:
  - `reviewer_effort_tiers` (boolean).
  - `reviewer_effort_ab` (`{label, target}`). Even task ids get the `tiered` arm and odd ids the `fixed` arm. Enrollment stops at `target` distinct tasks, and a rework close keeps the task's arm.
- `ScopeCheck` now carries the full `changed` list. A close with no scope check gets the config effort.

## Why
An internal reviewer-effort study suggests review effort can drop on low-risk diffs without losing recall. The A/B on 20 or more tasks either proves that or refutes it before any default changes. Scaling review depth to risk follows Google's engineering practices and NIST SSDF PW.7.

No schema change and no prompt change. The per-arm report and the push-gate skill line are follow-ups.

## Verification
- Gate run on the rebased commit passed: the build, tests for reviewer-effort, require-spawn-effort, composites, config, config-key contract, audit events, swe-atomic-close agent_runs and router parity, plus `regen-generated --check`, the changelog fragment and the doc and registry greps.
- The code-reviewer passed it with no findings.

author: shahidraza-design
body:
## What this is

A voice-first assistant that runs entirely in the browser: an arc-reactor HUD, live speech
recognition and synthesis, and a local intent engine for timers, reminders, notes, live weather,
maths, unit conversion, Wikipedia lookups and system diagnostics. No build step, no dependencies,
no API keys, no accounts.

## Highlights

- **Zero-dependency static app** plus a small Node server that sets microphone permission headers.
- **Safe maths** — a hand-written recursive-descent parser, no `eval`.
- **Installable and offline** — manifest, maskable icons, and a service worker that caches the
  shell while deliberately never caching weather/Wikipedia responses.
- **Graceful degradation** — no canvas, no `ResizeObserver`, no speech APIs, no network: the
  assistant still answers in text and keeps its state.
- **Local-first** — notes, timers and transcript live in `localStorage` on the device.

## Verification

- 35/35 unit tests (`npm test`) — maths parser, intent router, speech chunking, offline shell.
- 22/22 end-to-end checks (`npm run test:ui` with jsdom) driving the real page: boot, twelve
  commands, a timer firing, the voice path, settings persistence — zero console errors.
- Icons regenerate from `tools/make-icons.py` with no image libraries.

Merging this to `main` also makes GitHub Pages deployment possible.

author: paulmaina
body:
Scheduled forecast run 42019281559 aborted while writing generation metadata because performance_tracking.read_csv hit Python's default 131,072-character field limit when rereading all_leagues_predictions.csv. Frozen research can exceed that limit, and the same issue affects the standalone closing-odds planner and report CSV readers.

Add a shared standard-library CSV reader that raises the field limit to the largest value supported by the platform, backing off on integer overflow for Windows compatibility. Use it in performance tracking (and therefore health checks, capture, replay and workflow validation), closing-odds planning, workbook export and CLV report reading. Preserve CSV/JSON content, archive hashes and prediction calculations.

Five regressions reproduce the default-limit failure with a realistic large UTF-8 JSON cell, simulate a narrow Windows C integer, exercise the exact generation-metadata path followed by snapshot capture/reload, start the closing planner in a fresh process with both current and archived CSVs, and verify standalone report readers retain large fields.

Validation: run_offline_tests.py passed 1,195 tests; pytest passed 1,202 tests and 877 subtests. The focused consumer tests also passed. This is an I/O fix; no live-provider rerun or accuracy claim is included. After merge, rerun Scheduled forecast collection to generate and publish fresh forecasts.

## Summary

Follows #43 (60 packets). That run separated the eight models on two traps only, an amendment one party never signed and a four-amendment chain filed out of order, with every one-party packet at heavy noise. This appends a third cut of 40 packets on those two traps (16 one-party, 16 chain, 8 ordinary controls, spread over clean/light/heavy noise), declares `minimum_meaningful_difference: 0.05`, and commits the 8-model run of the 100.

**The set**: `gen/generate.mjs` draws the third cut after the 60 on the same seeded rng stream, so ct-001..060 regenerate byte-identical. 100 items: 76 traps, 40 holdout. `check-task`: 0 blocking, 0 warnings.

**The run** (`runs/contract-terms-long-2026-11-05T10-10-04-083Z`, 800 trials, 480 reused from the 60-item run via `--reuse`, $56.10 in all, about $22 new): gpt-5.6-sol 100/100, opus-5.5 99/100, sonnet-5 92/100, kimi-k3 89/100, deepseek-flash 88/100, deepseek-v4-pro 83/100, glm-5.3 77/100, qwen3.8-max 71/100. Three tiers: gpt and opus are indistinguishable and ahead of everyone (sign test over discordant inputs, vs sonnet p 0.008 / 0.039, vs the rest p < 0.01); sonnet, kimi and deepseek-flash are indistinguishable (p > 0.28) and ahead of glm and qwen (p < 0.01); deepseek-v4-pro straddles the second and third tier. One trap does nearly all the work: of the 20 one-party amendments, opus and gpt declined all 20, sonnet 12, kimi 9, deepseek-v4-pro 9, deepseek-flash 8, glm 3, qwen 0, at every noise level, so it is the rule and not the scan. The 22 chains separate only the tail. Everything else is 100% for every model on the answers returned; deepseek-v4-pro's other five misses are four empty completions and one timeout. 35 of 100 inputs separate. At the 0.9 gates only gpt, opus and sonnet qualify; the lowest-cost pick is sonnet-5, directional because 92/100 spans the gate (95% 0.85–0.96), which at 92% would take roughly 700 items to clear.

`datasets/README.md` has the result row; the spec header records both runs.

author: kerti
body:
Closes #785. Spec: ADR-0056 §1–3.

## What

A shared `NumericInput` (`components/common/`), ported from Uruni's `AmountInput`, plus a strict locale parser in `lib/format.ts`.

- **Live grouping** in the app locale: `48,500,000` (en-GB) / `48.500.000` (id-ID) while you type.
- **A typed `.` or `,` is the decimal point**; ignored on a 0-decimal field. A second point, or a digit past the decimal/integer limit, is refused.
- **Caret** stays after the same digit; backspace/delete over a group separator takes the adjacent digit; focus moves a collapsed caret to the end a frame later but leaves a selected range alone (Uruni #429).
- **Paste** goes through `parseLocaleNumber`: locale separators, grouping only in correct groups of three, currency symbol/code and spaces stripped. Unreadable or over-limit pastes are refused whole with an inline message.
- **Wire** is always the canonical decimal string (`48500000.50`). No backend change.
- **Prefill** shows stored values grouped; a stored value with more decimals than the field's default keeps them.

**Adopted:** snapshot create/edit dialogs (amount-only, qty×price, accrued) and bulk-entry rows (desktop + mobile). The other dialogs follow in #786.

## Notes

- Money fields read `currencyDecimals()`, which still gives IDR 0, so IDR fields ignore a typed separator until #787 flips it. #787 should land before the next release.
- Price per unit takes 4 decimals (its `NUMERIC(20,4)` column; fund NAVs are quoted to four), not the currency's minor units.
- Number placeholders are grouped per locale.
- New invariant **INV-PRESENTATION-13**. `docs/qa/coverage/21-serving.md` regen was stale on main and comes along.
- HANDOFF: round (a) sequencing note.

## Testing

- `make check` all green.
- vitest: 21 `NumericInput` tests (caret insert/delete across a separator, select-then-type, over-limit paste, invalid paste, 0-decimal field), 12 parser/grouper tests, and an `EditSnapshotDialog` test sending a phone-comma decimal as canonical.
- e2e: `snapshot.spec` now types `12,500,000` (BUG-01 regression); grouped value assertions in `snapshot.spec` and `bulk-monthly-entry.spec`. Local run: 72 passed. `invite-copy-link.spec` failed locally because local mailpit's SMTP greeting took 8–11s to reach the host. That's a local environment problem, unrelated to this change.

> **Per Claude sul PC di casa.** Questa è una **richiesta**, non codice pronto: contiene solo la specifica.
> Implementala **su questo branch** dopo aver chiuso e pubblicato il lavoro in corso, seguendo
> [`Docs/richieste/README.md`](../blob/main/Docs/richieste/README.md). Prima fai `git rebase origin/main`:
> se il codice è cambiato dopo il 3/11, **il codice attuale vince sulla specifica**. Merge solo con l'ok dell'utente.

## Richiesta dell'utente
> MIGLIORARE LA UI NOTEVOLMENTE. Deve essere dinamica, bellissima e antica, aggiungi molti effetti alla ui,
> deve essere proprio di un gioco spettacolare, a partire da inventari, pulsanti, interagisci etc...

## Sintesi
Ogni elemento dell'interfaccia diventa un oggetto fisico della Napoli del 1946 (carta, inchiostro, ottone,
ceralacca, timbri, biglietti del treno) e reagisce con animazioni e suoni.

- **Base:** `UITheme`, mini motore di tween interno `UITween` (niente librerie esterne), `ButtonFx`, `PanelFx`,
  `Typewriter`, particelle UI a pool, suoni UI, texture procedurali da menu `Treno ▸ UI`.
- **Pulsanti:** ottone / cartellino / ceralacca, con hover, pressione a timbro, rilascio elastico e suoni.
- **Interagisci:** indicatore dorato nel mondo 3D + cartellino che cade e dondola, con il tasto E.
- **Inventario:** valigia di cartone che si apre, oggetti come cartoline col retro, animazione "nuovo oggetto".
- **HUD:** biglietto del treno punzonato come contatore enigmi; toast a telegramma; dialoghi a lettera con ceralacca.
- **Pausa** a quaderno anni '40, **titolo** con stampa tipografica e vapore, **enigmi** (lucchetto con ruote vere,
  spago rosso negli abbinamenti, drag & drop, timbro "RISOLTO"), **transizione Ricordo** a pellicola che brucia,
  **cutscene** con bande cinematografiche e ritratti in cornice.
- **Vincoli:** WebGL fluido su Chromebook/LIM, tutto generato da codice, font/suoni con licenza libera,
  opzione "Effetti ridotti", didattica non punitiva.

Specifica completa, ordine di lavoro e criteri di accettazione:
[`Docs/richieste/R001-ui-spettacolare.md`](../blob/richiesta/R001-ui-spettacolare/Docs/richieste/R001-ui-spettacolare.md)

author: andonorth
body:
## Summary

Closes #223.
Takes the state contract to version 2 and the artifact index to its second release: the use link table, the cache entry columns, the retired cache key rule and the revive, tombstone and purge functions.
The migration is `0301_artifact_use.sql`, expand only, applied by the runner with its default flags.
The package reads the layout through `wdf_events.layout()`, so it keeps no layout link of its own.
This PR replaces #241, which could not take the rebase onto main without a force push.

Consumers of the contract change: #3 and #6 (`contracts/state/`, `packages/artifactindex/`).
Blocks S.2 (#224), C.2 (#229), K.1 (#231), K.3 (#233).

## Notable decisions

- Decision: the migration is `0301`, as the issue and the spec section 3 say; alternative: the `0400` to `0499` range named in the task text, which the spec gives to `packages/stateops`; why: the issue body is the contract and the range of `packages/artifactindex` is `0300` to `0399`.
- Decision: `tombstone(conn, uri, at, grace)` takes the row lock and evaluates `unreferenced_content` again, returning `Deleted` or `Skipped`; alternative: an unconditional soft delete (which `mark_deleted` already is); why: a link that lands between the scan and the tombstone would otherwise leave a held row tombstoned.
- Decision: `purge(conn, uri, at, tombstone_interval, grace)` only records `purged_at` and returns `Purged` or `Skipped`, and the caller removes the object before it commits; alternative: purge taking a delete callback; why: the row lock is held to the end of the caller's transaction, so a link or revive that waits sees the result, and a failed object delete rolls the record back.
- Decision: `link_use` returns `Linked`, `Revived` or `RowPurged` and raises `LookupError` for a missing row; alternative: raising for a purged row too; why: a purged row is an expected outcome of the race with the reaper that a caller handles by putting the object again.
- Decision: `link_use` moves `last_linked_at` forward only (`GREATEST`) and takes `at` as an argument; alternative: the database clock; why: every time comparison of the reaper uses the passed time, so a repeated run finds nothing more to do.
- Decision: `expired_cache_entries(conn, before, at, limit=None)` retires the entries and returns their original keys, skipping rows another session holds; alternative: a read only query with a separate retire call; why: the issue says the expiry retires the key, and one statement is bounded and restartable.
- Decision: `index_reference` does not reset `created_at` on a revive; alternative: resetting it to restart the grace; why: the function has no time argument and the revive is always followed by a link in the same transaction.
- Decision: `checkpoints_of(conn, job_id, task)` returns live `ArtifactRow`s newest first by `row_id`, and `previous_checkpoint(conn, uri)` returns the newest live checkpoint of the same job and task indexed before the named one; alternative: ordering by attempt and segment; why: indexing order is commit order and needs no parsing of the key.
- Decision: `record_cache_entry` names `build_info_uri` in its insert only when the entry sets it, and returns `WasmGone` when the wasm or the build-info row is missing or soft deleted; alternative: always writing the column; why: the grants of `wdf_artifacts` (S.2's) do not cover the new column yet, and the existing grant test stays green.
- Decision: `artifact_use` has no foreign key to `accepted_job` and the table holds two extra checks (`build_info_uri` only on a cache entry, `purged_at` only on a soft deleted reference); alternative: a foreign key; why: dispatch links before it inserts the job row.
- Decision: `artifact-row/1.json` stays committed and is no longer generated; alternative: deleting it; why: it is the schema of state version 1 that earlier consumers pinned.
- Small edits outside Owns: none beyond the closure addendum line of `docs/delivery/epics/05-state-storage.md`.
- Grants for the new table, columns and functions are S.2's, so the `wdf_artifacts` and `wdf_reaper` roles cannot call `link_use`, `invalidate_cache_entry`, `tombstone`, `purge` or `expired_cache_entries` until that lands.
- Host note: other lanes hold the default T1 host ports, so this branch was tested with `WDF_SLOT=7`.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run --frozen pytest packages/artifactindex -q -rs` passes with no skip
- [x] `uv run --frozen python -m wdf_artifactindex.gen --check` exits 0 and exits 1 naming `schemas/artifact-row/2.json` for a renamed column in a scratch copy
- [x] `uv run --frozen python -m wdf_migrate check --dsn DSN` exits 0 against a database with every migration applied (`test_wdf_migrate_check_passes_against_every_applied_migration`)
- [x] `uv run --frozen pytest packages/artifactindex -q -k wheel` passes
- [x] `nix develop -c just ci` is green locally, and the GitHub run is green: https://github.com/AndoNorth/wasm-dag-forge/actions/runs/42038761650
- [x] `grep -rn layout.yaml packages/artifactindex/src` finds no package-local link, and `nix develop -c just ci` is green after the rebase onto main

- The reference rule reads `accepted_job` and `job_status`, so the artifact index functions need the job tables in the same database.

author: antech-greyhat
body:
## What this adds (v0.3.0)

- **Live-CTF step in `/log`:** after the platform, `/log` asks whether the writeup is from a live CTF. Yes shows the CTFs running now from CTFtime and `events.toml` (at most 8) plus "Not listed", which takes a typed end time up to 30 days ahead.
- **Holds elsewhere:** `/recent` and `/show` mark held writeups with 🔒 and the release time. `/release <id>` ends a hold early after confirming. A hold also ends on its own, and nothing is sent when it does.
- **`/export`:** buttons choose all writeups, since last export, last 30 days or one category. The owner gets a ZIP of Markdown files with an index. Held writeups are never included, and the reply says how many were held back and when the next hold ends.

## Bug fixed along the way

CTFtime's `start` parameter filters on when an event began, checked against the real API: event 3369 queried from its own midpoint was not returned. Fetching from `now` could therefore never find a running CTF. The client now fetches from 14 days back. `/events`, the digest and reminders still filter by time, so their results don't change.

## Upgrade

Migration 2 adds nullable `hold_until` and `hold_event`, so existing rows stay "not held". **Back up `data/ctfbot.db` before the first run.** Expect the log line `Database upgraded to schema version 2`.

## Design decisions worth reviewing

- **`/release` writes the release moment instead of NULL.** "Since last export" compares `max(created_at, hold_until)` with the marker. A writeup held through an export has an old `created_at`, so it would otherwise be skipped forever.
- **Only "All writeups" and "Since last export" move the marker,** and only after Telegram accepts the file. A one-category export moving it would skip other categories' new writeups.
- **A same-second writeup can repeat** in "since last export". Timestamps are whole seconds and the comparison is `>=`, which prefers a duplicate to a lost writeup.
- **"Not listed" records the platform as `hold_event`,** so `live_ctf` isn't `false` for a live CTF. `/release` keeps `hold_event`.
- **`/export` uses plain buttons like `/delete`, not a `ConversationHandler`.** Nothing is typed, so there is no state to track.
- **Front matter uses `ensure_ascii=True`.** No character can act as a line break, but non-Latin titles appear as `\uXXXX`.

## Security

- No new runtime dependency. The ZIP is built in memory and sent only to `OWNER_ID`.
- ZIP member names are `[a-z0-9-]` slugs plus `.md`, at most 80 characters and unique via the ID.
- All exported text is redacted, including names and event titles. This happens before file names are built, so a flag in a challenge name can't reach a file name.
- Front matter values go through `json.dumps`, so they can't break the block or add keys.
- An unreadable hold counts as held and logs the writeup ID only.
- All new commands and buttons are owner-locked, and the patterns are anchored with `\Z`. The handler-walk test covers them, with a new test checking every button pattern's anchor.

body:
## Why

Stage 91 item 3, from audit 7 (2026-11-04, finding R3; `docs/history/11-audit7-2026-11-04.md`). The NHL's and NBA's daily runs save a slate's picks and then go on to the standings, grading, page inputs, the drift check, the forward test and M2. The audit made each of those raise on a real input (a final game with no score in the standings, an unknown team code that passes the code contract, a duplicated game id in grading): the picks were on disk, the run failed, the workflow skipped its commit step, and the slate lived only in the run's artifact until someone committed it by hand. That is the 2026-10-10 incident (#423, #424) with the crash moved one step later.

## What changes

- New `src/core/after_save.py`: `guarded(step, fn, *args, **kwargs)` runs one step and, if it raises, prints `DEGRADED: <step>: <error>` and returns None. Both daily workflows already raise an issue on any `DEGRADED:` line (Stage 83 item 4), so a failed step is still reported, now beside committed picks instead of instead of them.
- `src/sports/nhl/daily.py`: the standings (inside the lock block, after the picks loop), grading, page inputs, drift check, forward test and M2 each run through `guarded`; grading, drift, forward test and M2 are wrapped as small local functions with the same bodies as before.
- `src/sports/nba/daily.py`: the same, plus the price record (`market.record`) straight after the picks loop and the schedule file.
- Since this branch was cut, main changed the same steps: the NBA's drift check holds each pick to the backtest of the model it ran (#620), the missed-picks line also covers yesterday's slate (#618), and the forward-test file is frozen once when the regular season ends (#632). The merges keep all three; the freeze runs inside the guarded forward-test step, straight after the forward test is written, as it does on main.
- Steps before the picks are saved are unchanged and still stop the run. In the NBA run, main's "priced none of the locking games" line (Stage 92 item 7) still prints before the guarded price record.
- `tests/test_forward_test.py`: adding `after_save` makes each daily run's `from src.core import ...` longer than ruff keeps on one line, so it is now a parenthesised block. The check that the daily run imports `forward_test` matched only the one-line form; it now accepts either (`^from src\.core import \(?[\w\s,]*?\bforward_test\b`, which stops at the block's closing parenthesis).
- `tests/test_tasks.py` and the README: `quick` now leaves out ten `slow` tests (main's eight plus this PR's two whole day runs: seven whole daily runs, two re-derivations of a saved pick, one NHL run on a renamed odds payload).

- `05455d66` Stage 91 item 3: the forward-test wiring check reads a combined import
- `2bae147e` Stage 91 item 3: quick leaves out the two after-save runs too
- `69c0d731` The forward-test import check accepts ruff's parenthesised import block
- `eb174f9c` merges main ((none)), so this head is what the merge will be.

author: bussard76
body:
Completes the naming rule in `docs/orca.md`, and fixes the way that rule stopped `cleanup.mjs` from removing anything.

**The defect.** `cleanup.mjs` treated any terminal whose title contains `· Worker` as busy. With the naming rule, a finished worker's setup terminal is `T22-S5 · Worker Developer · Setup`, and it stays open. So the worktree counted as busy forever and worktrees piled up.

**Changes**
- `isHelperTerminal` and `holdsWorktree` in `lib.mjs`: terminals ending in ` · Setup` or ` · Shell` no longer hold a worktree.
- `stallwatch.mjs` no longer watches helper terminals. Otherwise each one is reported as a worker, and as `GONE` when it closes.
- `cleanup.mjs` no longer closes a helper terminal in the integration worktree as a finished wave.
- `names.mjs` renames terminals that still carry Orca's own name, in entries with a known name: `Setup` to `<entry> · Setup`, and `user@host: path` to `<entry> · Shell`.
- `docs/orca.md`: wave and script terminals in the table, tabs named explicitly, the tooling and its limits updated.

**Tests.** `npm test`: 56 of 56 pass. The stallwatch test and the extended wave test failed before the fix. Not run against a real Orca: `names.mjs`, `stallwatch.mjs` and `cleanup.mjs` ran against a fake CLI here. The field names were checked against a real `terminal list`, but no terminal there carried these titles.

**Limits**
- A human who names a terminal exactly `Setup` gets it corrected.
- Renaming only runs when `names.mjs` runs, after a start and in each cleanup, so a setup terminal can show `Setup` for a short time.
- `names.mjs` now fails if `terminal list` fails. `start.mjs` and `cleanup.mjs` catch that, and entries are named first.

Explicitly hold affected checkouts until supplier-specific DDP costs/fees are verified and provide a clear customer-facing message. Add a regression test proving no Shopify cart is created for an unverified Belgian Tapstitch shipment. The required MOSE_BE_TAPSTITCH_DDP_VERIFIED flag defaults to disabled and must not be set without supplier proof. US gating and ad campaigns remain unchanged.

## Summary

CI did not check the mobile app at all, so green dependency PRs said nothing about it, and the Jest suite stayed broken on `main` until #131. This adds three checks to the `verify` job.

## Changes

- **Typecheck:** a `typecheck` script brings `@gloups/mobile` into `bun run typecheck`.
- **Tests:** runs the mobile Jest suite.
- **Bundle:** a `bundle` script exports the production iOS and Android JS, which catches broken imports that Jest mocks hide.

Native iOS and Android builds are not included: iOS needs a macOS runner.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run check`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`
- [x] Mobile tests locally: 216 passed
- [x] iOS and Android bundles locally
- [ ] The new steps pass on the self-hosted ARM64 runner


## Rename

Also renames the package to `@gloups/mobile`, matching the other `@gloups` packages.

author: kirlosyousef
body:
Makes every config change reversible, and adds the commands to upgrade and roll back. Nothing here talks to a server other than the npm registry.

- `init`, `init --update` and `uninstall` copy each config file to `~/.spookling/backups/<timestamp>/` before changing it. A JSON or TOML file that does not parse is refused and left untouched.
- `spookling restore [<timestamp>] [--yes]` lists the backup runs or puts one back (the current files are backed up first).
- `spookling update [--check] [--version x [--force]]` finds the newest published version and runs its `init --update`, a non-interactive re-wire of what is already set up. `status` shows an `update` line (checked at most once a day, never from hooks) and an `upgrade` line when hooks still point at an older version folder.
- The Claude desktop app and Codex (`config.toml`) get the MCP entry too, through the same backup path.
- Command routing moves to `cli/src/main.js`. Adds a root `.gitignore`, Node 18 in the CI matrix, and README and cli/README updates.
- Test infrastructure: `cli/test/helpers.mjs` (temp dirs that clean up, a fake API server), and `npm test` runs `cli/test/run-suite.mjs`, which fails the run if a test touches the developer's real Claude/Codex config or `~/.spookling/backups`.

Merge order: this PR has no dependency. It is the first of four.

**How to test**

```bash
npm test
uv run --project server pytest -q
node bin/spookling-memory.js demo --fast      # writes nothing
HOME=$(mktemp -d) node bin/spookling-memory.js restore    # lists nothing, exits 0
node bin/spookling-memory.js update --check   # exit 0, or 10 when a newer version is published
```

**Files touched**

- Added: `.gitignore`, `cli/src/backup.js`, `cli/src/restore.js`, `cli/src/update.js`, `cli/src/registry.js`, `cli/src/toml-check.js`, `cli/src/main.js`, `cli/src/credentials.js` (only the private-write helper in this PR), `cli/test/helpers.mjs`, `cli/test/run-suite.mjs`, `cli/test/guard-real-home.mjs`, `cli/test/guard.test.js`, `cli/test/backup.test.js`, `cli/test/restore.test.js`, `cli/test/update.test.js`, `cli/test/upgrade.test.js`, `cli/test/codex-mcp.test.js`, `cli/test/contract.test.js` (only the smoke-test cases in this PR)
- Changed: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `bin/spookling-memory.js`, `cli/src/wizard.js`, `cli/src/hooks.js`, `package.json` (test script), `README.md`, `cli/README.md`, `cli/test/codex.test.js`, `cli/test/ghost.test.js`, `cli/test/hooks.test.js`, `cli/test/ui.test.js`, `server/tests/test_subscription.py`

**Stacked PRs (1 of 4).** Merge in order, 1 to 4. These PRs come from a fork, so GitHub cannot stack them. #8, #9 and #10 target `main` and show the diff of every earlier PR until those merge. Review each PR by its own commit (the last one in the list), or retarget it onto the previous branch while reviewing. After PR N merges, GitHub shows only PR N+1's own changes.

CI passes on all 9 jobs (Windows, macOS and Linux on Node 18, 20 and 24).

author: resonant-jones
body:
## Summary

Three frontend tests fail intermittently on GitHub-hosted runners. Each has a different cause, and none is caused by the product code: in every case the test asserts on state that is delivered asynchronously, without waiting for the delivery.

This PR makes the three tests synchronize deterministically. No application code, runtime contract, Docker configuration, CI workflow, or qualification artifact is touched.

### Affected test paths

| # | Path | Failing case |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `frontend/src/features/onboarding/__tests__/Onboarding.test.tsx` | `never asks for a username or calls messaging when unavailable` |
| 2 | `frontend/src/features/commandCenter/components/__tests__/CodingWorkOrdersPanel.test.tsx` | `renders orchestrator recommendations and skipped reasons` |
| 3 | `frontend/src/features/chat/__tests__/GuardianChat.turn-lock-lifecycle.test.tsx` | `projects owned global command failure %s: %s through the actual hook` (and two sibling terminal-event cases in the same file) |

### Root causes and corrections

**1 — `Onboarding.test.tsx`: the step advance is awaited on a condition that is already true.**
`OnboardingProvider.advance` applies the next step only *after* the awaited save resolves (`await save(...)` then `setStep(next)`), so the visible step changes after the patch call has been *initiated*. The test's `next()` helper waited for `mocks.patch` **to have been called**, which is cumulative: after the first advance that condition is already satisfied, so the second `next()` returned without waiting for anything. The following synchronous `getByText(/People messaging is not enabled/)` could therefore run before the `username` step — the only step that renders that notice — had mounted.
*Fix:* `next()` now waits for **this** advance's patch call (call count must increase), and the assertion awaits the notice itself with `findByText`. Every original assertion is retained.

**2 — `CodingWorkOrdersPanel.test.tsx`: the assertion waits for the container, not for the content.**
The `coding-orchestrator-recommendations` container is mounted from the first render, while the orchestrator response that fills it is still in flight (`useOrchestratorRecommendations` starts with `recommendations: []` and `loading: true`). `findByTestId` therefore resolved immediately, and the synchronous `within(recommendations).getByText(/Recommendation one/)` could run against an empty container.
*Fix:* the recommendation text is awaited with `within(recommendations).findByText(...)` before the original assertion. The container's existence is no longer treated as proof that its content has arrived.

**3 — `GuardianChat.turn-lock-lifecycle.test.tsx`: the live-event subscription lives in a React passive effect.**
`GuardianChat` registers — and re-registers — its live-event subscription from a `useEffect`. React runs an effect's *cleanup* during the commit but its *setup* in the passive phase, which it schedules as a **macrotask**. The test emits a terminal event right after the inference state carries its task id, which is inside that window: the subscription has been torn down but not yet re-established, or it is still the previous render's handler, whose captured `inferenceRequest.state` predates the task attachment. The component's guard then treats the event as belonging to another turn and drops it, so the inference phase never leaves `queued` and the terminal-state assertion times out.

Captured under load by instrumenting the component's guard (instrumentation removed again; it is not part of this change), the handler observed `inferenceTaskId: null` and `phase: "sending"` while the rendered state already carried `task-1`.

*Fix:* `emitLiveEvent` now drains React's pending work before delivery — `await act(async () => {})`. A *synchronous* `act` does not drain the macrotask queue, which is why a first attempt with `act(() => {})` did not close the window; the helper is therefore async and every call site awaits it. The handler set is re-read after the drain because the re-subscription replaces it. Two sibling cases additionally await the inference projection with `waitFor` instead of asserting it synchronously after an unrelated observable (the turn-lock release) — a separate race on the same transition. No assertion was weakened or removed.

With the correction, fourteen consecutive loaded runs of the affected cases pass, against a baseline that failed the same case under the same load.

### Preserved behavioral coverage

All three contracts still verify exactly what they verified before: the People-messaging-unavailable state, the orchestrator recommendations and skipped reasons, and the GuardianChat `tool_command_blocked` completion behaviour. The fix is synchronization only — the expected values, the queried elements, and the assertions themselves are unchanged.

### Not used, by design

No global or per-test Vitest `retry`, no arbitrary sleeps, no increased timeouts, no skipped tests, no conditional CI exclusions, no weakened assertions, and no change to `frontend/src/vitest.config.ts`. The Guardian CI change filter that runs the frontend suite when `docker-compose.yml` changes is untouched.

### Test-isolation corrections in the same file

While diagnosing, two further leaks in the same file were found and closed:

- `vi.clearAllMocks()` clears call history but **keeps queued one-shot implementations**, so a test whose `requestCancel` is never called left its queued value behind and the next test silently consumed it. The mock is now reset in `beforeEach` and its documented default restored.
- A continuation that resumes after a test has ended can call the shared mocks and pollute the next test's counts. Pending work is now settled at the end of each test and after each live-event delivery, and the provider-switch observable is awaited instead of asserted synchronously.

### Validation

- Each affected file run individually, then all three together (117 tests, all passing).
- Repeated runs under CPU contention: the affected cases failed intermittently at baseline and pass consistently after the correction (14/14).
- Repeated runs with **shuffled ordering** (`--sequence.shuffle` across six seeds), which is how the two isolation leaks above were found. Two seeds still fail, on two *other* cases in the same file — see the remaining-uncertainty note.
- Full frontend suite (`pnpm test`).
- Repository lint and type-check commands; `git diff --check`.
- A Draft PR with a successful full **Frontend Quality** job on the final evaluated head — repeated local success alone is not treated as sufficient evidence.

**CI on the final head (`bf9f2b54`):** all six Guardian CI jobs green — Architecture Contracts, Backend Tests (Python 3.11), Campaign Control Plane Dry Run, Detect Changed Areas, Frontend Quality (4m52s), Migration Contract (Container), alembic-config-sanity.

Local-environment notes (not product failures): the shared checkout's `node_modules` predates the current lockfile, so three `generativeUi` test files cannot resolve `@openuidev/react-lang` in this worktree; CI installs from the frozen lockfile and runs them normally. One unrelated suite-level flake (`tests/thread_documents_rehydration.spec.tsx`) was observed once in a full local run and passes in isolation.

### Remaining uncertainty

The three identified failures are fixed with mechanism-grounded corrections, and they have not recurred in any CI run since. The file nevertheless retains order/timing sensitivity in two **other** cases, which this PR does not claim to fix:

- `uses the actual hook for stream cancellation and {accepted,late-failure} stop POST` — the cancel request is not issued inside the `waitFor` budget. The real hook's `requestCancel` rejects silently when the task id, the task stream, or the phase is not yet what it expects, and the test cannot observe which guard rejected. It does not reproduce locally (14/14 under load). The only remaining lever is a larger `w

author: rpgmem
body:
Part of #2344 (PR 5 of 7: sections and required fields, item 3)

## Problem

`ffc-section-collapse.js` showed and hid `[data-ffc-section]` blocks without touching their required fields, and constraint validation ignores visibility. On the Rate Limit and Geolocation tabs, a cleared required number inside a section whose switch was off therefore blocked the save. Nobody could see the field that blocked it.

## Change

- Both the initial pass and the change handler now call `FFC.setRequiredWithin()` on each of the master's sections:
  - when a section hides, its required fields lose `required` and are marked;
  - when it shows, only those marked fields get `required` back.
- The script's dependency on `ffc-core` already landed in #2399.
- CHANGELOG entry.

## Tests

- `section-collapse.test.js`:
  - a section that is off on load lets its form validate with a cleared required number;
  - turning the section on restores `required`;
  - a field that was never required is not promoted.
- The new test fails against the previous script and passes with this one.
- Vitest OK (2816), ESLint clean. No PHP changed.

## Risk

None for data. The save handlers already treat an empty number as "keep the stored value".

## Checklist

- [x] Base is `develop`; no version bump
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` bullet under `[Unreleased]`
- [x] No settings to document
- [x] No new strings
- [x] Minified JS rebuilt

author: quangphung218
body:
Follow-ups the reviewers of #72, #73 and #74 noted as non-blocking. 1. **Chat follow** (`scroll_follow.rs`, `app/follow.rs`): Page Up / Arrow Up / Home / Shift+Space, a finger dragging the content down, and a grab on the scrollbar now stop the follow before their scroll lands. Nothing scrolls under a finger on the list or a held scrollbar; letting go at the end catches up. A wheel in a box inside the list (`.run-log-text`) that can still go up leaves the list's follow alone. 2. **Turn files** (`routes/files.rs`, `turn_files.rs`): the app's save notes the file's prior stamp (`note_saved`). A file that was there before the run and that the agent left alone is no longer listed as "Wrote X"; one the agent changed stays the turn's. Saving the same file twice keeps the first prior stamp. 3. **Held queue** (`studio.rs`, `chat_ops.rs`, `workspace.rs`): deleting a conversation removes `od:chat-composer:held-queue:

:`. A queue that is already held keeps its reason (Stop vs connection lost). 4. **Covers** (`routes/raw.rs`, `od-preview/still.rs`): `still_page` reads at most 5 MiB, and a larger page gets a blank cover. `without_scripts` matches tags in any case without making a lowercased copy. 5. **Preview**: the dead `__odMotionRender` guard is gone. `announceDeck` checks again on DOM changes for 10 s after `load`. A WebM cover with no duration seeks past its end so the browser finds the length, then shows the middle frame. ## Tests - New unit tests: `scroll_follow` (keys, held list), `workspace::a_held_queue_keeps_why_it_waits`, `turn_files::a_file_the_user_saves_over_…`, `still::any_case_…`, `projects::a_film_with_no_length_…`. - New integration and browser tests: `runs.rs` (old.html), `preview.rs::a_still_page_over_the_limit_is_a_blank_cover`, `bridge_browser::late_decks_are_announced`. e2e: chat 14c (`keysAndTouch`), preview 5d (reason) and 5e (`heldQueueDeleted`). - Each one fails on the old code: run against it with the new tests, or broken at the new guard line. - `make check` rc=0 (1199 tests). Local e2e: `chat` and `preview` PASS. No version bump; CHANGELOG Unreleased › Fixed.

author: phun-ky
body:
Tests ran through `glob` and `global-jsdom` although no test uses the DOM, coverage was not enforced, and the typecheck skipped the tests. Tests now run with Node's own globs, coverage has a floor, and the typecheck includes them.

## What has changed

- `test`: `node --import tsx --test 'src/**/__tests__/**/*.spec.ts'`.
- `test:coverage`: coverage of `src` without tests, `--enable-source-maps` so lines map to the TypeScript, and thresholds at the measured floor: 89% lines, 88% branches, 95% functions. The floor is raised as tests are added, toward 99, 95 and 100.
- `typecheck`: `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`; `tsconfig.json` no longer excludes `__tests__`.
- Removes `glob`, `global-jsdom`, `jsdom`, `@testing-library/dom`, `@testing-library/jest-dom`, `cobertura` and `tsconfig.test.json`, which only the old scripts used, along with `test:unit`, `test:ci` and `pretest:ci`.

## How to test

1. `npx --yes npm@11 ci && npm test && npm run test:coverage && npm run typecheck`
   - Success: all exit 0.
   - Measured: 35 of 35 tests; coverage 89.91% lines, 88.36% branches, 95.56% functions; typecheck covers 9 test files.
2. Each check fails on broken input:
   - Coverage: the same command with `--test-coverage-lines=95`. Measured: "89.91% line coverage does not meet threshold of 95%", exit 1.
   - Tests: a planted `assert.equal(1, 2)`. Measured: exit 1.
   - Typecheck: `const planted: number = 'not a number'` in a test file. Measured: exit 2.
3. `npm test` ten times in a row.
   - Success: no failures.
   - Measured: 0 failures in 10 runs.

Note: Node reports coverage only for files the tests load, so the floor covers the tested modules; untested modules are not counted yet.

Lockfile: 60 entries removed, nothing added or changed. Deploy impact: none.

## Related issues

- Closes #26
- Stacked on #52: merge #52 first.

body:
Owner (2026-11-05): «الإعلان والإشعار يجب أن يكون محفوظًا … ثم يحذفها، الحذف يجب أن يوافق عليه مدير النظام أو مشرف النظام» · «أنشئ مشرف نظام يقوم بمهام المدير في غيابه كل شيء عدا الحذف، ويتاح له الموافقة على حذف الإعلانات» · admin and site manager delete without approval.

**Role `system_supervisor` «مشرف النظام»** (`accounts/rbac.py`, migration `accounts/0010`)
- Added to every capability the admin holds except `*.delete`; new `deletions.approve` (admin + supervisor).
- `scope_for/can(..., deleting=True)` ignore the supervisor; `core.permissions.capability` and `ScopedModelViewSet.scope` pass it for DELETE → every DELETE refused for the supervisor (users, departments, roles, media, …); department **merge** also checks `deleting=True`.
- Grants/creates every role except `system_admin`/`system_supervisor`; `_not_above()` refuses password reset, rename and profile edits of admin/supervisor accounts.
- Direct admin checks (inquiries, announcements addressing, users list, ops notifications, audiences, ops alerts) include the supervisor; portal nav/access/home treat it as the admin; «حذف الحساب» shows only with `users.delete`.
- Demo account `supervisor@demo.ecst.test`; matrix: supervisor allowed wherever the admin reads/writes (`_with_supervisor`).

**Deletion by request** (`content/models.DeletionRequest`, `content/deletions.py`, migration `content/0011`)
- `DELETE /api/v1/announcements/<id>`: admin → 204; site manager → 204 for what they may delete; author or anyone who may delete it → **202** pending request (one at a time, 409 `pending`). Same for `DELETE /api/v1/notifications/sent/<id>` (sender's own; deleting removes it from every inbox).
- `GET /api/v1/deletion-requests?state=pending`, `POST …/approve|reject {note}` (`deletions.approve`): approve deletes (audited `announcement.delete`/`notification.delete`), reject keeps it; the author is notified; approvers are notified of new requests.

author: bielxdh3
body:
## Follow-up P2: rotated code survival after session remount (commit `7754b27`)

Independent review found that `App.tsx` mounts `RouterProvider` inside `SessionQueryProvider key={sessionRevision}`. On successful code recovery, `recoverWithCode` increments that revision; the previous implementation stored the new one-time offline code only in local page state, which could unmount before the user saw or saved it. The follow-up stores the code **atomically with the recovered session** in the already-existing volatile Zustand `pendingRecoveryCode` (same as registration), renders it from that store across the hard remount and delayed `/auth/me`, and clears it **only on explicit** `Já guardei, continuar` acknowledgement. No localStorage/sessionStorage or persisted recovery secret is introduced.

**RED→GREEN full-App DOM evidence:** Isolated original `66cd4e9` checkout, same new regression test `frontend/tests/auth-recover-remount.test.ts`, **RED**: `pendingRecoveryCode` was `null` after revision remount. New HEAD `7754b27` **GREEN 1/1**: renders real `App`+RouterProvider and real recovery form in Happy DOM, models stale in-flight `/auth/me`, proves code survives the session remount and stale response, remains on recovery route, never enters localStorage, then disappears from screen and memory only after acknowledgement and dashboard navigation. Existing auth-session/cross-tab/register full-App tests **13/13 PASS**. Complete frontend test-project TypeScript `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --noEmit` PASS, edited-file ESLint PASS, `git diff --check` PASS. Isolated `happy-dom@21.0.4` installed only in review worktree from frozen lockfile. Prior PostgreSQL18 HTTP auth regressions **3/3** and service tests **4/4**, **11/11** remain applicable; no backend logic changed in this follow-up.

## Problem and behavior

**MCP cash:** After a paid manual PIX expense is voided via `archiveExpense`, its historical `ExpensePayment` remains auditable, but must no longer reduce the MCP monthly cash balance. Filter the manual expense parent query by `voidedAt: null`. Merely archived (not voided) paid expenses and independent `EntryReceipt` remain counted.

**Induced login 429:** Ten invalid passwords for a known email across different IPs exhaust the 15-minute per-identifier failure budget and temporarily block the actual password holder. The existing offline recovery code is a high-entropy one-time credential that works outside the per-email password limiter. Previously successful `/auth/recover-password` revoked old sessions and cleared the cookie, forcing another `/auth/login` that was still 429. Now a **successful** recovery-code CAS transaction rotates password and recovery code, invalidates previous sessions/OAuth grants, and issues a new HttpOnly session cookie bound to the **exact new `sessionVersion`** from that successful CAS (no later re-read for token version). An invalid/replayed code or rolled-back transaction never receives a session. The frontend displays the newly rotated recovery code until the user explicitly clicks **Já guardei, continuar**, then goes to the authenticated dashboard without retrying the blocked password route.

No extra password checks or per-email budget reset are introduced. Existing IP and identifier limiters, CSRF/Origin defense, and generic rejection messages remain unchanged.

## Reproduction and validation

- MCP PostgreSQL 18: original RED `expensesBrl=120.00`, `balanceBrl=-75.00` following void of R$85 PIX, expected `35.00` and `10.00`; GREEN after filter. Full `financial-overview.itest.ts`: **5/5 PASS**, including pagination and patrimony budget.
- Login original baseline `eebe72e`, fresh isolated checkout: new adversarial HTTP recovery integration **RED** because response after recovery 200 had no authenticated `user` or new login session; password login remained 429. Follow-up commit `66cd4e9`: `login-recovery-lockout.itest.ts` **3/3 PASS** against disposable PostgreSQL 18. Covers ten distributed 401s, valid password still 429, valid one-time recovery code -> Set-Cookie(HttpOnly) -> `/auth/me` 200, stale cookie 401, original code replay 401 without cookie, nonexistent vs existing account generic 401 and 429, unchanged exhausted login quotas for target and another identifier, single successful session under concurrent recovery, and trusted one-hop proxy ignoring forged earlier XFF headers with per-IP ceiling.
- Forced transaction-abort regression: simulated OAuth revocation failure causes complete rollback of password, recovery-code hash and session epoch; previous recovery proof stays usable. `auth.itest.ts`: **4/4 PASS**. Previously existing auth unit/HTTP suites: **11/11 PASS** including expiry and NAT ceiling.
- Frontend `tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit`: **PASS**; ESLint of edited backend/frontend sources: **PASS**, diff check: **PASS**. Full frontend test-project TypeScript and full-App Happy DOM regression are now green in follow-up `7754b27`. Full backend typecheck previously blocked by missing MCP/OIDC dependencies in reused `node_modules`; hosted CI should perform clean lockfile install and verify both. An actual full-App Happy DOM interaction test is green; no real Chromium/Edge browser session was run.

## Remaining scope and limits

Recovery-code holders can escape a malicious password lockout without extra password guesses. Users who **only know the password** still receive 429 until the 15-minute identifier window expires; that residual risk is not solved without an independent credential or a change in anti-stuffing policy. Per-IP login limiter (20/15m production), finite windows and per-process `MemoryStore` remain unchanged; 20 distinct identifiers from one verified source cannot exceed its IP limit. No hard global cardinality/memory bound for attackers with arbitrarily many distributed IPs is claimed. Proxy spoofing proof assumes the configured trusted nginx sanitizes the forwarded nearest hop; it is not a substitute for network-level verification.

**Refs #122.** Remains DRAFT; no merge, production or real database changes.

author: ali-mosavian
body:
TL;DR: lea candidacy back in MachineCSE, with two guards; vs release/next 15 x86 cells shrink (-2 to -16 B), 0 grow, 0 m32 bench rows move. m64 quicksort -O3 runs +855 instr but no slower on 3 padded layouts.

- Re-adds what #7328 removed (a `lea` is a CSE candidate), plus DEVIATE CSE7 (a `lea` counts as cheap: not shared at a distance, which spilled x_life/x_transpose) and CSE6 (no copy propagation into a `lea`, which cost quicksort +9.7% clk).
- Tests: `test_a_lea_two_blocks_away_is_not_shared` (CSE7), `test_a_lea_of_a_copy_that_has_another_reader_keeps_reading_the_copy` (CSE6), `tests/cse_lea_countdown.rs`. Each unit test fails with its rule off.
- Guard (`ab_guard.sh`): base d79e57a383 = newest release/next commit in head; llrm-cc/llrm-llc md5 differ (d26b1c76f981/4dc74632758d vs 0fbfdfc1b917/c3d93fd27878).
- m32 vsgcc bench, 452 rows (O1/O2/O3/Os, x_bubble/x_insertion/x_mergesort O2 included), all ok: 452 SAME, 0 worse. m32 bench is inert here: its loops have no adjacent identical `lea` left once CSE6/CSE7 apply.
- Object identity m16/m32/m64 x O1/O2/O3/Os (bench + tests/run/c, 2424 cells; FAILs identical on both sides): m16 768 SAME, 0 DIFF; m32 7 DIFF; m64 8 DIFF. `.text` base -> head, all smaller: m32 frameless O1 322->306, Os 266->259; switch_empty_cases O1 52->47, Os 45->40; tail_calls O2/O3 719->716, Os 538->536. m64 frameless O1 348->332, Os 307->300; switch_empty_cases O1 52->46, Os 48->42; tail_calls O2/O3 905->902, Os 518->515; bench quicksort O3 1879->1863.
- m64 countdown -Os: 45 -> 42 B (one `lea [acc*3]` instead of two); -O2 158 = 158. No clocks measured for it.
- Not claimed: anything about clocks outside the 452 m32 rows.
- Executed instructions, 15 changed cells (perf, whole process, same startup): 14 fewer (-4 to -23, e.g. m32 frameless O1 169341->169318); outputs equal. Whole-process cycles are noise at this size (m32 swings 40% at equal instructions), so no clock claim for them.
- m64 quicksort -O3: +855 instr (+0.35%), -16 B, but cycles (host min-of-101, padded layouts 0/37/101 B) base -> head: 411663 -> 407748, 355797 -> 347293, 349742 -> 348219. Not slower on any layout; the earlier +0.9% was one layout. The two arms' `lea [r15+rdi*4]` become one before the compare (not PRE: PRE of a Mem-source expression is refused).
- m32 clocks: the 452 bench rows are SAME in the emulated table; the 7 m32 DIFF cells are tests/run/c (not in that harness), instructions only.

author: clubanderson
body:
Fixes #630

## Why

The meetings page and the public Google Calendar it calls "the source calendar" agree through 2026-12-31 and then disagree on **every** 2027 date.

- **Page:** Thursdays in odd-numbered ISO weeks (`getUpcomingOddIsoWeekMeetings`, from #31). 2026 has 53 ISO weeks, so this produces back-to-back calls (2026-12-31 → 2027-01-07) and is then one week out of phase for all of 2027.
- **Calendar (fetched `basic.ics`):** one series, `DTSTART;TZID=America/New_York:20260910T100000`, `RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;WKST=SU;INTERVAL=2;BYDAY=TH`, no `EXDATE`/`UNTIL`. A strict 14-day cadence. `TZID` handles DST, so there is no drift.
- **Stated cadence:** the join page says "every other Thursday, 10:00 AM ET" / "biweekly". The calendar satisfies that; the odd-ISO-week rule does not.

The calendar is what people's clients and Google Group invites show, and it honours the stated cadence, so the page is the side that must change.

| Date | ISO week | Calendar (14-day RRULE) | Page before (odd ISO week) | Stated cadence ("every other Thursday") | Page after |

author: federicocarabelli-arch
body:
### Summary
Adds Mirico to the shared integration registry and implements a read-only client for its Analysis Engine API. The client uses `Authorization: Bearer <API key>` and defaults to the documented staging base URL, `https://api.mirico.dev/engine-api`.

The connection probe calls the authorized-sites endpoint. A successful empty list is accepted, so a valid key can be checked even before test-site data is available. The client also provides methods to list sites and deployments for the next integration phase.

An optional API base supports another environment supplied by Mirico. The client requires HTTPS and rejects URLs containing embedded credentials, query parameters, or fragments. Authentication failures and malformed responses produce safe errors without exposing the key or upstream response body.

body:
Android business saves can disappear when rows omit their bakery workspace, and customer saves target a loopback development server. Manual sync omits business uploads and ignores failures. Website invoices and quotes use different line-item, total and status fields, producing missing lines or balances on Android.

Persist each record and a durable Room upload entry in one transaction, use the established account workspace, check Firestore transaction results, and retain failed or conflicting edits for retry/manual review. Recipe ingredients wait for their parent and reconcile within the owning bakery, including identical old document IDs in different accounts. Cloud document IDs prevent phone-local ID collisions. Recover legacy unassigned or never-uploaded rows only for their explicit local account owner, including legacy recipe pricing/photo edits.

Save invoice/quote headers, JSON and normalized lines atomically. Preserve website/Android field aliases, product cloud IDs, separate packaging lines, stored totals, tax metadata and status filters. Report local-only saves separately from confirmed cloud completion. Add non-destructive Room migration 15→16 and repair the compatibility workflow's dependency-install step for the repository's missing lockfile.

author: davidatwhiletrue
body:
## Description

Adds `specs/schemes/upto/scheme_upto_casper.md`, defining the `upto` payment scheme on Casper.

This is PR 1 of the [Adding a New Chain Family](https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#adding-a-new-chain-family) workflow for `upto`: spec only, no SDK changes. Casper `exact` is already merged (#2741). The reference implementation will follow once the spec is approved.

Casper `exact` uses CEP-3009, which commits to a fixed value and cannot settle less. `upto` instead uses Permit2 for Casper, a port of Uniswap's Permit2 for any CEP-18 token, through an `x402UptoPermit2Proxy` contract, following the structure of `scheme_upto_evm.md`. The client signs a `PermitWitnessTransferFrom` with the proxy as spender and a witness of `(to, facilitator, validAfter)`. The facilitator calls `proxy.settle` with the actual amount, bounded by the signed maximum.

Casper-specific points for review:

- The client approves Permit2 on the token once and pays that gas. No sponsored approval is defined; a missing allowance returns `412` with `permit2_allowance_required`.
- Casper has no `CREATE2`, so the Permit2 and proxy package hashes are per-network constants, never taken from the payload or `extra`.
- Addresses use the 33-byte tagged `Address` encoding, and signatures use ed25519 or secp256k1, as in the `exact` Casper spec.

## AI-assisted contribution

Per the [AI-assisted contributions](https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#ai-assisted-contributions) guidelines: writing of this spec was assisted by Claude Code.

## Tests

Docs-only change. The spec was checked against the Permit2 for Casper and `x402UptoPermit2Proxy` Odra contracts and their tests; no automated tests apply.

- [ ] All new and existing tests pass

}

author: maxgronlund
body:
Uses [bifrost-core 0.5.0](https://github.com/Happy-Bananas/bifrost-core/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) and fixes the run-lock risk from the review.

## Run lock
- Every command that used to be locked by `bin/bifrost-connect` now calls `RunLock::takeOrExit()` itself, right after loading `.env`: `scenario:run` (the seed takes it in bifrost-core).
- A command started directly, for example `php bin/scenario-run`, is now protected too. If the dispatcher is killed, the lock stays with the command that does the work.
- `bin/bifrost-connect` only finds and starts the command. It no longer needs `.env` or the PHP packages.
- Exit code `75` and the "Another integration command is already running" message are unchanged.

## Composer without the GitHub API
The bifrost-core repository entry gets `"no-api": true`. Composer then reads the package's versions with a plain `git clone` over HTTPS, instead of the GitHub API, which allows 60 anonymous requests an hour per address. Today that limit ran out and `composer update` failed: Composer fell back to SSH, which the container doesn't have. With `no-api` the update worked while the limit was still at zero. `composer install` from the lock file downloads the package archive as before.

## Checks
- `composer test`: 27 tests pass, 1 new: a command started directly is skipped while another holds the lock.
- Removing the lock call makes both lock tests fail, so they really test it.
- With the real `.env`: `./check-connection` passes for both connections, `tracezilla:seed --dry-run` finds all 15 records, and `php bin/scenario-run` started directly gets past the lock.

body:
## Summary
- Add bounded native extraction for fragmented-MP4 DASH STPP/TTML subtitle tracks.
- Reuse the existing `mp4box` sample-table parser and `quick-xml` namespace-aware reader; no new dependencies.
- Normalize the supported plain-text TTML subset to private WebVTT staging and retain the existing FFmpeg sidecar/embedding path.
- Keep unsupported profiles, non-zero Period starts, non-zero presentation-time offsets, multiple Periods, styled/layout TTML, external resources, and unsupported timing on the existing yt-dlp fallback path.
- Share the existing MP4 bounds, safe file opening, fragment counting, and private-output helpers with WVTT extraction.

## Safety and limits
- Single static zero-origin Period, SegmentTemplate addressing, and zero presentation-time offset only.
- One `stpp` sample entry and one `subt` track.
- Bounded assembled track, sample count and size, XML depth and element count, cue count/text, and normalized output.
- Non-empty TTML `head` metadata is rejected rather than silently discarded.
- CPU parsing runs in `spawn_blocking`.

## Tests
- TTML time expressions, sample-interval clipping, TTML1/TTML2 namespaces, entity handling, unsupported styling/layout/timing, malformed XML, nesting and output limits, repeated-cue coalescing.
- DASH STPP representation planning and zero-origin timeline eligibility.
- Existing WVTT extraction and finalization paths remain unchanged.

## Review and validation
- Independent Rust review completed against the project's Rust 2024 / MSRV 1.98 application-code conventions. Two pre-push issues were corrected: stale timeline-guard test calls and a TTML1 test passing a `String` instead of its byte slice.
- No local Rust toolchain is available in this environment, so local `cargo fmt`, Clippy, and test results are not claimed. GitHub Actions is the validation gate for this PR.
- A complete real-world STPP fMP4 fixture is not added in this initial bounded implementation; the parser logic and DASH eligibility are covered by focused unit tests.

author: backnotprop
body:
Show me now makes a real Shape. Clicking it, on selected lines or on the Overview, asks the session that wrote the review for a Shape board through the same `plannotator shape update` path agents already use. The board opens over the review, and clicking a part lands on its line in the diff.

Behind Settings → Capabilities → Code review, off by default.

**What changes**

- **The request** is short and general; the how lives in `plannotator shape --help`. It adds one line on `data-code`, so a part that is code lands on the diff; that line lives only here, so Shape's own text is byte for byte with Code review off (pinned by hash). The agent stores with `--thread <thread> --through <review>`.
- **The selection bar** is words only, split by hairlines, with Show me in the accent's text. It sits under the last selected line at the start of its code, on the side the selection ends on in Split, and above the first line when the viewport has no room below. It covers the lines only when neither fits. It stays on the file it opened on, and hides while its lines are off screen or dropped by the diff. The diff's + mark is gone while it shows. Inbox only; the review app has no bar.
- **A turn takes only its own board.** Show me again counts its board; a Show me a new board through its review, and an updated one only once it ended with none. A turn with no end kept that is not running names nothing.
- **A board drawn on an earlier review** paints where that code is now, stored through a reply too (the review before that reply). With no `--through`, or one before any review, it uses the review its Show me names, else the newest review when the version was stored. When the code really changed, or the file is deleted or renamed, it shows the file with a note and paints nothing. Lines the diff can't show, and a board stored before any review, go to the board's own viewer.
- **A turn finds its board at read time** (`showMeShapes`): nothing new is stored, there is no new route and no new CLI flag.
- **Full board over the review.** The drag window from #2600 is gone. A click on a part goes through a new `onCode` seam on `ShapeSurface`, lands on the line, and shrinks the board to the corner card. A file the review lacks opens in the board's own viewer.
- **Works with Code review on, whatever Shape's own switch says.** The routes, stream, Pebble and CLI follow either switch. The row, grid, ⌘K group and `/shape` stay on Shape's switch.
- **The thread works with the board as Shape does on its own:** Chat, Annotate, Global comment, the Thread tab. No second comment system. With Code review on, Change it wakes the session (`wakeOnChange`).
- **Show me again** is the board's refresh button (`refreshLabel`): a new turn, a new version of the same board.
- **`review draw` / `review drawings` are removed**, with their route, store and tests; the files they wrote stay on disk, so a downgrade finds them. With Code review on, an older agent's call is refused and pointed at Shape. With it off, the review parse takes those words as it always did.

**Runtimes:** Bun only. The Inbox and its Ask are Bun-only, and the `/api/shapes` routes did not change, so Pi needs nothing.

**Seams in `packages/ui` (additive):** `ShapeSurfaceProps.onCode`, `ShapeHost.refreshLabel`.

**Tests**

- `tests/e2e/inbox-show-me.spec.ts`: the whole walk on the real binary, 14 tests, with a scripted agent storing a real board through the real CLI.
- `tests/e2e/inbox-review-selection-bar.spec.ts`: the bar on the real binary, 11 tests: Split, Unified, All files, the bottom of a card and of the viewport, a phone, two files with the same line numbers, its lines gone.
- `packages/server/inbox-show-me-shape.test.ts`, `packages/inbox/shapeWake.test.ts`, `packages/review-editor/components/selectionChooserPlace.test.ts`
- `packages/ui/components/shape/ShapeSurface.onCode.test.tsx` (DOM)

author: obkaro
body:
## Why
Cloud analytics saw that someone opened the app and that they saved work, but nothing in between: which screens people use, where they go after opening, or whether they find settings. The app has no browser analytics SDK (removed in #354), and adding one is off the table.

## Change
- **`lib/screen-views.ts`:**
  - Notes each kind of screen shown (`home`, `doc`, `records`, `record`, `settings`, …). Repeats of the same screen aren't counted.
  - Sends them as one `keepalive` POST to `/api/analytics/screens` when the tab hides, or after 20 screens. Moving around the app costs no request.
  - Uses `authenticatedFetch`, so the request carries the session's CSRF token.
- **`components/screen-views.tsx`:** mounted in the root. Active only on Cloud (`capabilities.analyticsChoice`), so local and self-hosted Worktables send nothing.
- **Route mapping:** typed against the generated `FileRoutesById`, so a new route fails the build until it names its screen (or `null`). Only route IDs are used, never paths or params.
- **Shared types:** `APP_SCREENS`, `isAppScreen`, `SCREEN_VIEWS_PATH`, `SCREEN_VIEWS_MAX` and the `product:screen_viewed` event in `@worktable/types/analytics`.

The Cloud gateway answers the request itself and sends `product:screen_viewed` only for people with analytics on. The Worktable server never sees it.

## Checks
- A new unit test covers one request per hide, kinds only, the CSRF header, keepalive and dedupe.
- `tsc -b` for apps/web passes, and so does `perf:guards`.
