author: thagale
body:
## Summary

manta's required `test (ubuntu-latest)` check spends 60–65 minutes on main because `cargo test --workspace --locked` runs every test binary one after another: the per-binary durations on run 41726268369 sum to ≈61 minutes, and the nine slowest binaries alone account for ≈34. The merge queue's 60-minute check timeout ejected green PRs as `checks_timed_out` (#483, twice on 2026-11-03), and the stopgap raised it to 90 minutes. This change replaces the serial Unix workspace-test leg with whole-binary sharding across eight hosted runners per OS, behind aggregates that keep the exact required check names. Nothing about the tests themselves changes: no Rust source, fixture, Cargo manifest or lockfile is touched.

The shape per Unix OS (ubuntu and macOS are symmetric):

- **`<os>-support` (1 job)** — every non-Cargo-test command that used to run in the OS test job, with its platform conditions intact: toolchain-pin check, `cargo fmt --all --check`, workspace clippy, Linux rustdoc with `-D warnings`, doctests as an explicit required step (`cargo test --workspace --doc --locked`), the FT8/FT4 clippy-and-test trio, both release shell suites, and all Python script suites. It also runs the new `test_ci_shards` regression suite and uploads a support/doctest evidence artifact (on failure too, without suppressing the failure).
- **`<os>-shards` (8 jobs, shard 0–7)** — `fail-fast: false`, `timeout-minutes: 35`. Each builds the workspace once and runs its assigned whole test binaries via `scripts/ci-shards.py`, then uploads a machine-readable shard evidence artifact (`if: always()`, `if-no-files-found: error`).
- **`<os>-aggregate`** — named exactly `test (ubuntu-latest)` / `test (macos-latest)` so every downstream consumer (dispatch service, `scripts/check-release-ci.py`, the merge queue) sees the same check names as before. It runs `if: always()` subject to the usual trusted-author predicate and fails unless *both* of its OS dependencies succeeded (a jq check over `needs`), so a failed, cancelled, skipped or missing worker cannot produce a green required check, and one OS's conclusion stays independent of the other's.

The `test` matrix retains only `windows-latest`, so Windows keeps its native `test (windows-latest)` name and its original serial command sequence unchanged. The trusted-dispatch service now `needs: [create-ci-check, test, ubuntu-aggregate, macos-aggregate]` and still relays each exact job's own conclusion — it cannot publish success when only some shards completed. Every executable job keeps the existing trust setup byte-identically (enforced by `test_ci_trust_boundary.py`, whose job list now covers all five): trusted-author native routing, reviewed checkout ref, inline merge-with-main (MAN-340), `persist-credentials: false`, read-only contents, and restore-only rust-cache outside pushes to main.

## The shard driver (`scripts/ci-shards.py`)

Discovery is real, not a hand-maintained list: the driver builds with `cargo test --workspace --locked --no-run --message-format=json` and keeps every compiler artifact that is a test executable (lib/bin/test/example/proc-macro unit tests plus integration tests), keyed by package ID + kind + name. Conflicting artifacts, unknown executable categories and malformed JSON fail closed; targets excluded by default features stay excluded; a newly added test target enters the schedule automatically. Deterministic longest-first assignment uses checked-in estimates in `scripts/ci-test-weights.json` — weights affect placement only and can never filter coverage — with `golden_v8_v8w` pinned alone on shard 0 and a 30-second default for unknown targets.

Each binary runs whole, one at a time, with normal libtest threading from its package directory, carrying the full set of Cargo package environment variables, `CARGO` and the dynamic-library search paths (including build-script outputs and the toolchain's Rust libraries). That preserves the process-local locks `multi_input_hpsdr` relies on and keeps compiled `CARGO_BIN_EXE_manta` paths working — which is why a nextest-style process-per-test runner was rejected. Before executing anything, each shard inventories test and ignored names with libtest listing; unsupported listing fails the audit rather than reporting an empty suite. The assignment assertion proves complete and disjoint placement before any test runs.

`--audit` mode checks a hosted evidence bundle: all shards present exactly once, every discovered target selected and executed once with exit 0, per-target ignored sets equal to the unsharded reference, support and doctest success, and elapsed time measured from workflow creation — not from the aggregate's few seconds — so queue delay cannot hide inside a short gate job.

## Coverage guarantees

No test was made faster, skipped, weakened or moved. Assertions, repetition counts, ignore annotations, fixture data, timeouts, the Cargo profile and `.catalyst/catalyst.toml`'s serial verification command are all untouched; no coverage moved to a scheduled or non-required job. Doctests remain explicitly required work per OS. Windows and the Soapy job keep their prior shape.

Against the pre-change command on the same build, platform and features, the driver's inventory matches Cargo's serial listing per executable: 152 test executables, 4,740 test names and 46 ignored names at this branch head, each target assigned exactly once across the eight shards (shard 0 = golden alone; the rest hold 14–24 binaries each).

## Timing evidence

No individual test got faster, so there is no per-test before/after speedup to claim — the change is scheduling. Baseline times are carried forward as placement estimates:

| Binary | Supplied hosted baseline (s) | Local shared-host probe (s) | Hosted after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| golden_v8_v8w | 626 | 1490.9 | pending |
| manta_engine unit tests | 425 | 942.3 | pending |
| determinism_hsmm | 239 | 1089.8 | pending |
| multi_input_hpsdr | 180 | 156.9 | pending |
| listen_inputs | 122 | 183.5 | pending |
| rtty | 120 | 176.4 | pending |
| soak_ci | 120 | 120.3 | pending |
| multi_input | 118 | 109.8 | pending |
| rtty_detector | 102 | 99.4 | pending |

The baseline column is ticket evidence from Ubuntu run 41726268369, not re-measured here. The local column comes from a six-core container running four shard drivers concurrently — a contention probe, not the CI layout — and is recorded for completeness, not as a speedup. On paper the hosted critical path is roughly a 4-minute build plus the 626-second golden pole plus checkout/setup, comfortably inside 20 minutes; the hosted numbers above stay pending until the rollout below measures them.

## Verification

author: eurikamonica
body:
## 出了什么问题

Disclosure Hub 里“价格估算”这一步（每 6 小时一次的 `prices` 收集，用于给 13F 持仓估算季度平均成本、给官员交易估算股数）从 **2026-10-29 起就再没成功过**。每次运行到 “Collect configured sources” 大约两分钟时，GitHub 报错：

> The runner has received a shutdown signal … The operation was canceled.

例子：[run 41981763869](https://github.com/eurikamonica/filing-flows/actions/runs/41981763869)、[run 41935170086](https://github.com/eurikamonica/filing-flows/actions/runs/41935170086)、[run 41848648910](https://github.com/eurikamonica/filing-flows/actions/runs/41848648910)，以及 10-30、11-01 等更早的运行，日志里都是 `MODULE: prices` → `Collecting prices` → 被关机。`disclosures/docs/data/prices-status.json` 的 `last_attempt` 一直停在 2026-10-29。

## 原因

`apply_prices` 会把**全部 10,872 家 13F 管理人的全部历史持仓一次性读进内存**再计算。10-29 时大约 330 万条持仓，现在约 2,250 万条。本地实测：仅前 169 家就已占用 4.5 GB 内存，全部读入远超 GitHub 机器的内存，机器因内存耗尽被强制关停。

## 修复

- 逐家读取：先把每家管理人依次读一遍收集 CUSIP，再依次读一遍计算价格；算完立刻写回该管理人的缓存和公开分片，内存里不再同时保存所有持仓。
- 只有估算值真的变化时才重写该管理人的文件（没变的就不动）。
- 同一股票同一季度的平均价只算一次（以前每条持仓都重算一遍）。
- 增加时间预算（默认 15 分钟，可在配置 `prices.time_budget_minutes` 调整）：超时后剩下的管理人保留原有估算，下次运行继续；状态文件里会写明数量（`managers_deferred`）。这样整个任务能在 40 分钟限制内完成并提交。
- 写分片的代码从 `publish_shards` 中提取为 `publish_manager`，两处共用，输出格式不变。

## 测试

- 新增回归测试：缓存中的管理人被逐个定价并写回、内存中保持“懒加载”、估算未变的管理人不被重写、超出时间预算时正确跳过并计数。
- `disclosures` 全部离线测试 933 项通过（`test_ui.js` 留给 CI）。
- 用真实数据（10,872 家、约 2,250 万条持仓）离线试跑：内存峰值约 1.75 GB（以前会超过机器内存），在设定的时间预算内正常结束。

## 修改的文件

- `disclosures/app/prices.py`
- `disclosures/app/shards.py`
- `disclosures/tests/test_officials.py`

author: csandanov
body:
## Problem

The `zookeeper` container asked for no CPU or memory by default. Kubernetes then treats it as needing nothing: it can place the service on a node that is already full, the cluster never adds a node for it, and Wodby's check of whether a new environment fits on its cluster counts it as zero.

## Cause

The service manifest declared no resource requests for the container.

## Solution

The `zookeeper` container now requests 20m CPU and 96 MiB of memory by default, with a memory limit of 2048 MiB: well above the Java heap the image sets, so the service has room to run but cannot take over a node. The values come from what this container uses on running Wodby clusters, kept close to its idle usage, so small clusters stay usable.

Stack services and app services that set their own resources keep them. App services without their own values get these requests with their next stack upgrade, which restarts their pods; on a cluster that is already full, a pod can then wait for room instead of squeezing in.

## Release

Kept as a draft until Wodby supports resource presets and CPU values in steps of 10 millicores in production; until then the import refuses this manifest. After merging, release a minor version.

author: seewoo5
body:
This PR remove files under `ForMathlib` that are already upstreamed (in certain form), and bump to `v4.35.0`.

---

## Summary

Removes three ForMathlib files that nothing in the development imports (only the root `SpherePacking.lean` did) and that are superseded:

- `ForMathlib/CauchyGoursat/OpenRectangular.lean` was upstreamed to mathlib as `Complex.*_unbounded_rect_*` in `Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/CauchyIntegral.lean` (mathlib #26479, merged 2026-10-27, after v4.35.0). Upstream uses a weaker decay hypothesis, `Tendsto f (comap im atTop ⊓ 𝓟 ([[x₁, x₂]] ×ℂ univ)) (𝓝 0)`, which ours implies. `Complex.tendsto_integral_atTop_nhds_zero_of_tendsto_im_atTop_nhds_zero` kept its name upstream, so it would clash on the next bump. Removing the file also removes one `sorry`.
- `ForMathlib/Vec.lean`: `Matrix.cons_val_five/six/seven` are handled by mathlib's `cons_val` dsimproc.
- `ForMathlib/Finsupp.lean`: `Finsupp.linearCombination_eq_sum` is `by simp [Finsupp.linearCombination_apply, Finsupp.sum_fintype]`.

Also pins mathlib to `v4.35.0` in `lakefile.toml`. The automated update (#503) moved `lean-toolchain` and `lake-manifest.json` to v4.35.0 but left `lakefile.toml` at `v4.35.0-rc4`, so `lake update` would resolve mathlib back to rc4.

## Effect on open PRs

The upstream replacements only arrive with the next mathlib bump. Until then, these PRs need adjusting after merging `main`:

- #467 rewrites `OpenRectangular.lean`, so it will have a modify/delete conflict.
- #435 and #437 cite `Complex.*open_rect*` in blueprint `\lean{…}\leanok`, so `checkdecls` will fail. Remove those `\lean{…}` references for now. After the bump, point them at mathlib's `Complex.integral_boundary_unbounded_rect_eq_zero_of_differentiable_on_off_countable`, `Complex.tendsto_integral_boundary_unbounded_rect_one_side_atTop_nhds_sum_other_two_sides` and `…_of_integrable_on`.
- #229 imports the file and uses `integral_boundary_open_rect_eq_zero_of_differentiable_on_off_countable_of_integrable_on`.

Other open PRs that edit the root import list merge cleanly with this change (checked with `git merge-file`).

## Checks

- The root imports match the files on disk, which is what `lake exe mk_all --check --module` checks.
- No references to the removed modules or declarations remain, including in `blueprint/`.
- Not built locally; this relies on CI.

author: alexkarpov98
body:
**Changes:**

Page and feature state lives in 26 `@ngrx/component-store` stores. That API is observable-first. In the zoneless app, a consumer either wraps every selector in `toSignal`/`| async`, or subscribes and copies values into local signals with a `markForCheck()`. 88 of the 125 consumer files subscribe, and those copy-on-subscribe handlers are where bugs hide (see the leak below). This PR picks the replacement, documents it, and converts the first five stores so the rest can follow one feature at a time.

**Target pattern:** `@ngrx/signals` 22.0.1 (new dependency, same NgRx release as our other `@ngrx/*` packages), used inside ordinary `@Injectable()` classes. DI, `providers: [...]` and `mockProvider(Store, {...})` in specs are unchanged. Each ComponentStore piece maps one-to-one:

| ComponentStore | `@ngrx/signals` |
|---|---|
| `extends ComponentStore<S>` | `private readonly state = signalState(initialState)` |
| `select(...)` / `state().x` | `this.state.x` or `computed()` |
| `setState` / `patchState` / `updater` | `patchState(this.state, …)` in a method |
| `effect(...)` | `rxMethod<T>(pipe(...))` + `tapResponse` |

The pattern and the full table are in the new `docs/devs/signal-stores.md`. `CLAUDE.md` points to it and says not to write new ComponentStores.

**Stores converted (5):**

- **`CertificatesStore`**: drop-in. Its consumer already read signals.
- **`InterfacesStore`** (Network → Interfaces card): the card no longer copies `state$` into local signals. It reads the store's signals, feeds the table from an `effect()`, and derives the zero-traffic map with `linkedSignal`. Two existing bugs are fixed along the way:
  - The card called `subscribeToUpdates()` on **every** `state$` emission: at least 3 per load, plus every reload after an add, edit, delete or reset. Each call opened another realtime traffic subscription that lived until the page closed. It now subscribes once in `ngOnInit`.
  - A failed `interface.query` left `isLoading` true forever, and the error killed the effect, so later reloads did nothing. `tapResponse` + `finalize` fixes both. The old spec asserted the spinner stayed on; it now asserts the opposite, plus a reload after a failure.
- **`PermissionsCardStore`** (Datasets → Permissions card): the card reads the store's signals. The NFSv4 `owner@`/`group@` `who` fill-in moved from the card's subscription into the store (the old code had a `TODO: Move elsewhere` on it). A new `reset()` replaces the card's local `acl.set(null)` / `stat.set(null)` for locked, unmounted or mountpoint-less datasets.
- **`ManualDiskDragToggleStore`** (pool manager manual disk selection): two templates read `dragActive()` instead of `dragActive$ | async`.
- **`DashboardStore`**: `groups`/`isLoading` are signals. The dashboard's `groups$` subscription became an `effect()` that skips while editing, same as before. Load errors are now handled inside `switchMap`, so one failed `auth.me` no longer stops later `entered()` calls. The dead `globalError` field was removed: it was always `''` and nothing read it.

**Deliberately left out:**

- The other **21** stores. The largest are `PoolManagerStore`, `EnclosureStore`, `ContainersStore`, the apps stores, `DatasetTreeStore` and `SigninStore`. Each should be its own PR per feature, so the consumer and spec churn stays reviewable: 147 spec files touch these stores in total.
- **`ConsoleMessagesStore`**: its two consumers auto-scroll a `<pre>` on new messages and rely on running before the DOM updates. A signal version needs a different scroll strategy and a manual check, so it gets its own PR.
- `@ngrx/component-store` stays in `package.json` until the last store is converted. Nothing lints against new usages yet; the docs and `CLAUDE.md` carry that rule for now. A `no-restricted-imports` rule can land once the count is low enough to list the exceptions.

**Testing:**

- Store specs read the public signals after `settleApi()` instead of `firstValueFrom(state$)`. Component specs mock signals with `signal(...)` instead of `of(...)`.
- New specs:
  - `InterfacesStore` clears loading on error, and loads again after a failure.
  - The Interfaces card subscribes to traffic updates once, however often the list reloads.
  - `PermissionsCardStore.reset()`.
- `yarn test:changed`: 15 suites, 116 tests pass. The wider areas pass too: dashboard 309, network + certificates + pool manager 619, dataset permissions 161.
- `yarn lint` on the changed files, `yarn check-test-ids`, and `yarn buildng` are clean. Spec `tsc` errors: 295 before and after, none new.
- Manual, against a real box:
  - Dashboard loads; Configure → delete a group → Cancel restores the layout.
  - Network → Interfaces shows the NIC with its live status icon.
  - Credentials → Certificates lists the certificate.
  - Datasets → `dozer` → Permissions shows owner and Unix permissions.
  - No new console errors.

`data-test` values: none removed or renamed. The only template changes are `dragToggleStore.dragActive()` bindings in the two manual-disk-selection templates.

### Downstream

|Affects         |Reasoning
|----------------|-------------------------------
|Documentation   |Developer-only: new `docs/devs/signal-stores.md`, and a pointer in `CLAUDE.md`. No user-facing change.
|Testing         |Regression check on the five pages above. The Interfaces card should hold a single realtime traffic subscription after several add/edit/reload cycles.

author: jay23606
body:
## Bug

Auto-aliasing only kept one past name for a resource. `autoResourceSettings.apply` called `RenameResourceWithAlias` once per past name, and each call replaced the previous one, so a resource renamed more than once lost every past name except the last. Users still on an older name were forced into a breaking change (#3013).

## Change

- `pkg/tfbridge/auto_aliasing.go`: all past names are now kept as aliases of the current resource, in the order they were listed. The `<tfToken>_legacy` resource still points at the last past name, which matches the behaviour before this change, so existing state under that legacy target is unaffected.
- The rename aliases are now added to the resource returned after `RenameResourceWithAlias`, which replaces the stored resource. Before, they were appended to a stale pointer.
- `pkg/tfbridge/auto_aliasing_test.go`: `TestAutoResourceSettingsApplyMultiplePastNames` checks that both past names are aliases of the current resource, and that the `_legacy` resource still points at the last one.

## Testing

- `go test ./pkg/tfbridge -run TestAutoResourceSettingsApplyMultiplePastNames -count=1 -v` passes.
- The same test fails on the base implementation with `expected: []string{"pkg:mod/r1:R1A", "pkg:mod/r1:R1B"}`, `actual: []string{"pkg:mod/r1:R1B"}`.
- `gofmt -l pkg/tfbridge/auto_aliasing.go pkg/tfbridge/auto_aliasing_test.go` and `go vet ./pkg/tfbridge/` are clean.
- `go test ./pkg/tfbridge/... -count=1` fails in `pkg/tfbridge/tests`. Its two `TestConfigureSimple*` tests need the `terraform` binary, which is not on PATH in this environment.

**Regression test:** fails on base three times (/expected: \[\]string\{"pkg:mod/r1:R1A", "pkg:mod/r1:R1B"\}/), passes on fix twice (`go test ./pkg/tfbridge -run TestAutoResourceSettingsApplyMultiplePastNames -count=1`)

Fixes #3013

body:
## What
`config.json.bak` is now rewritten only on an **effective change** instead of on every successful parse/Save.

- Equivalence = same JSON document ignoring formatting, key order and `update_last_check` (the bookkeeping the TUI reload path already ignores).
- Missing or corrupt backup → always (re)written.
- Plain starts and update-check write-backs no longer touch the `.bak` or its mtime.

## Not a full fix for #404
An effective wipe (agents dropped) still updates the backup, so this does not by itself protect against that incident. "Backup = previous content", atomic writes and refuse-to-persist-defaults stay tracked in #404 (see the forensics comment there).

## Tests
Four new tests in `internal/config`: unchanged/timestamp-only/reformatted saves leave the `.bak` alone (content and mtime), effective change writes, corrupt/missing backup is replaced, repeat `LoadFrom` leaves the backup untouched. Verified they fail with the guard disabled. `go test ./internal/config ./cmd/milk` pass against a throwaway HOME.

Refs #404

body:
## Summary

- Adds `scripts/hermit-upstream-report.sh`, a read-only tool that reads `scripts/hermit.pin`, clones the upstream and fetches the fork into a temporary directory, and prints a Markdown report: the pinned commit and its upstream base, ahead/behind counts for the pin and the fork branch, whether the replay patch still applies to the upstream head (`git apply --check` only), the Rust toolchain on each side, the newest version tag, new upstream commits grouped by subject keywords (fix, feat, perf, build, deps), a watch list for areas the Hermit backend depends on, open upstream issues by title keyword (through `gh`, when available) and last-activity dates.
- `--self-test` builds a fixture repository in a temporary directory and checks the report against it with no network access. CI runs it in the install-scripts job.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` gets a short section: check what changed upstream before deciding to bump the pin.

The script never changes the repository, the pin or the patch, and builds nothing. The pin, the patch and the support statements are unchanged in this PR.

## Test plan

- [x] `shellcheck -S style scripts/hermit-upstream-report.sh` is clean
- [x] `bash scripts/hermit-upstream-report.sh --self-test` passes (bash 5 and macOS bash 3.2)
- [x] `bash scripts/test-scripts.sh` still passes
- [x] A live run against the real fork and upstream prints the full report
- [ ] CI green

author: martin-rueegg
body:
Fixes `massimo update` in v0.1.0-alpha.10, which fails every update with `the new binary does not run here: … open /dev/null/none: not a directory`.

The smoke test (which runs `<new binary> version` before the swap) set `MASSIMO_ENV_FILE` to a path below `/dev/null`. Opening that path fails with ENOTDIR, not ENOENT, and massimo's `.env` loader ignores only ENOENT. The test now runs the binary in a fresh empty directory whose `.env` does not exist. A new test builds the real binary and smoke-tests it; the stand-in shell scripts in `internal/update` could not catch this.

Checked end to end against the published v0.1.0-alpha.10: a v0.1.0-alpha.9 build on channel `phase-0`, built from this branch, found the release, verified its signature against the compiled-in key and the binary's SHA-256, ran the smoke test, swapped binaries, wrote the status file, and rolled back.

The bug sits in the update code of the running binary, so an alpha.10 binary needs a manual update or `massimo install` from the next release. Nothing runs alpha.10 yet.

body:
Replaces the realtime WebGL camera flythrough on /3d/ with an Apple-style **image sequence scrubbed by scroll on a 2D canvas**. The MacBook couldn't keep up with live WebGL. The Agentic Engineering Team demo stays live three.js and is lazy-loaded only when it nears the viewport.

- `3d/seq.js` + `3d/seq-core.mjs`: same thesis scroll mapping as fly.js, so captions stay in sync. Progressive preload order is first/last/middle and then gap-filling. Draws only when the frame index changes. Passive scroll, canvas DPR capped at 1.5, skips drawing while #ag covers the screen. `prefers-reduced-motion` loads only one still frame per thesis.
- Frames recorded from the existing flythrough (`fly.js ?capture` + `window.__at(u)`) with `tools/seq/record.mjs`, so robots match groups.json. Desktop: 150 frames at 1600×900, ≈2.0 MB. Mobile: 80 frames at 540×1170, ≈0.27 MB.
- `?live` forces the old WebGL flythrough. If the manifest fails to load, it falls back to the live version.
- Shared loader moved to `3d/model.js`.
- Tests: `tests/seq.test.mjs` (unit) and a `/3d/` smoke check.
- Caveat: frames were rendered with software GL (SwiftShader, CPU-only rendering). Re-record on a GPU machine or at a higher width for sharper mobile frames.

author: kniazkov
body:
Closes #38

## Changes
- Extend common vector operations with element access, checked at, size/capacity queries, reserve/resize, overload-specific insertion/erasure, iteration and swap.
- Preserve result reference/value/iterator distinctions, writability, index and both swap destinations. Track temporal handle validity and storage transfer separately from creation snapshots.
- Use conservative capacity/position proofs; handle reverse iterator base invalidation, nested argument effects, unevaluated operands, assignment capacity and conditional swap ownership without false safety promises.
- Integrate query/element/reference/iterator dependencies with DFG, including delayed iterator assignment and indexed writes; preserve at exception paths and nontrivial user effects.
- Resolve genuine catalogue iterator types and member overloads without assuming pointer layout; exclude bool proxy iterators from ordinary reference rules.
- Add owned API/JSON/DOT metadata, mandatory vector-access native corpus, RU/EN documentation and checklist/matrix coverage.

- Independent focused review: all reported semantic/DFG issues fixed and independently replayed on final local candidate.
- Focused model5/5, normalization19/19, DFG28/28, resolver61/61 affected and43/43 final tests pass.
- Native acceptance3/3 passed: full API/CLI JSON/DOT, compact SVG, copied graphs, original/GREEN/FOLDED main programs and compact original/GREEN examples under strict GCC14/Clang19.

body:
## 요약

커밋되지 않았던 v18 코드를 올리고, 소스 분석에서 찾은 문제 세 가지를 수정합니다.

### `fc19287` v18 기능
- 위젯별로 코인 2개를 고르는 설정 화면
- 모든 위젯의 코인을 합친 업비트·바이낸스 일괄 조회
- Yahoo 실패 시 open.er-api.com 환율 폴백
- 실패 시 캐시 유지와 경과 시간(⚠️) 표시
- 잠금 해제 시 갱신(5분 쿨다운)

### `15545d2` 수정
- **LTC 전체 실패:** 업비트 KRW 마켓에 LTC가 없어, 위젯 하나가 LTC를 고르면 일괄 요청이 404로 거부되어 모든 위젯의 갱신이 멈췄습니다. 목록에서 LTC를 빼고, 일괄 요청이 거부되면 코인별로 다시 조회합니다. 없는 코인의 슬롯만 "데이터 없음"으로 표시됩니다. 바이낸스(400)도 같게 처리합니다.
- **저가 코인 표시:** SHIB이 `₩0`, `$0.00`으로 보이던 문제를 고쳤습니다. 1 미만 가격은 유효숫자 4자리로 표시합니다.
- **갱신 스레드 수명:** `goAsync()` 없이 스레드만 띄워 갱신 중 프로세스가 동결·종료될 수 있었습니다. `goAsync()`와 단일 스레드 실행기를 쓰고, 갱신 1회의 새 시도를 9초 안으로 제한합니다. 요청 타임아웃은 15초에서 3초로 줄였고 4xx는 재시도하지 않습니다.
- **연속 터치 제한:** 터치가 차례로 모두 실행되면 업비트 한도(HTTP 429)에 걸려, 마지막 시도 후 3초 안의 터치는 건너뜁니다. 설정 저장은 제한 없이 갱신합니다.

## 동작 변경
- 타임아웃이 짧아져 신호가 약한 곳에서는 ⚠️가 전보다 자주 보일 수 있습니다.
- LTC는 더 이상 선택할 수 없습니다. 이미 LTC를 고른 위젯은 해당 슬롯에 "데이터 없음"이 표시됩니다.

## 테스트

Android 16 에뮬레이터에서 수정 전 v18 APK와 비교했습니다.

| 상황 | 수정 전 | 수정 후 |
|---|---|---|
| LTC 설정이 남은 위젯 | BTC/USDT 위젯까지 `⚠️10m`으로 멈춤 | LTC 슬롯만 "데이터 없음", 나머지는 정상 |
| 갱신 중 프로세스 상태 | `cch-empty` | `RCVR` |
| 연속 터치 6번 | 측정 안 함 | 갱신 1번, 나머지 5번은 건너뜀 |
| 네트워크 끊김 | 측정 안 함 | 7.1초 후 종료, 새로고침 아이콘 사라짐 |
| 재부팅 | 측정 안 함 | 크래시·ANR 0건 |

Android 17 갤럭시(`SM-S947N`)에 설치해 BTC/USDT 위젯 갱신도 로그로 확인했습니다. 약 1.2초 걸렸고 크래시는 없었습니다.

**확인하지 못한 것**
- 서버가 응답하지 않아 타임아웃이 나는 경로
- 부팅 시 `BootReceiver`와 서비스 경로의 실제 실행 여부
- 실제 기기에서 절전으로 프로세스가 종료되는 상황과 잠금 해제 갱신

자동화 테스트는 이 프로젝트에 아직 없습니다.

## 병합 후 할 일
`docs/`의 배포 APK는 아직 수정 전 빌드입니다. 새로 배포하려면 버전을 올리고 APK를 교체해야 합니다.

author: maxgronlund
body:
Uses [bifrost-core 0.5.0](https://github.com/Happy-Bananas/bifrost-core/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) and fixes the run-lock risk from the review.

## Run lock
- Every command that used to be locked by `bin/bifrost-connect` now calls `RunLock::takeOrExit()` itself, right after loading `.env`: the catalog, location, inventory, order and failure-retry commands and `scenario:run`, eleven in all (the seed takes it in bifrost-core).
- A command started directly, for example `php bin/import-individual-orders --execute`, is now protected too. If the dispatcher is killed, the lock stays with the command that does the work.
- `bin/bifrost-connect` only finds and starts the command. It no longer needs `.env` or the PHP packages.
- Exit code `75` and the "Another integration command is already running" message are unchanged.

## Composer without the GitHub API
The bifrost-core repository entry gets `"no-api": true`. Composer then reads the package's versions with a plain `git clone` over HTTPS, instead of the GitHub API, which allows 60 anonymous requests an hour per address. Today that limit ran out and `composer update` failed: Composer fell back to SSH, which the container doesn't have. With `no-api` the update worked while the limit was still at zero. `composer install` from the lock file downloads the package archive as before.

## Checks
- `composer test`: 70 tests pass, 6 new. The template gets the dispatcher tests from WooCommerce (it had none), plus a test that the order import is skipped while another command holds the lock.
- Removing the lock call makes both lock tests fail, so they really test it.
- No live check: the local Shopify `.env` still uses the old `TRACEZILLA_API_KEY`.

author: jannef
body:
Part of #977. A design document for the owner's line-by-line review; **merging this PR approves the design.** Only `docs/design/no-caster-level.md` is added (CI skips the build). Implementation issues follow once it is merged.

## The rule

Caster level goes. What a scroll teaches depends on **learning**, a benefit of the Spellcraft skill: a curve in `data/skills.toml`, `[[10, 0], [60, 10], [100, 30], [150, 70]]` (0 below 10, 10 at 60, 30 at the soft cap 100, the last spell level 70 at 150), at least 1 for everyone (cantrips). A spell of a level at most the learning is certain; above it the 2d12 check is as today (Intelligence modifier, Spellcraft ÷ 10 and Decipher script ÷ 10, affinity, Quick study, against 12 + overreach + known ÷ 20), with the overreach now the spell's level less the learning. Nothing is computed from the character level.

## Starting points

| Class | Spellcraft |
|---|---|
| Wizard | 2d6+10, known for (as today) + Arcane training's +10 |
| Witch | 2d6+10, known for (as today) |
| Priest, druid | 2d6+10 (the priest's one-in-four 2d4 replaced) |
| Bard, paladin, ranger | 2d4+4 |
| Aristocrat | by chance, 35 %: 2d4+4 |
| Ascetic | by chance, 20 %: 2d4 |
| The 25 % classes | none: learning 1 for ever (cantrips, and the low spells by check) |

Races and birth signs give none (none do today). The `casting` field goes from the classes.

## What happens to the readers

- **Of the Adept**: deleted, with `Effect::CasterLevel`; of the Scholar (Spellcraft +8 to +50) is the affix of learning, `"weapon"` proposed on its bases; the Eorcanstān takes `of_the_scholar:6`. Loot: the suffix draw on weapons, helmets, rings, and amulets re-weights among the rest.
- **Arcane training**: Spellcraft +10 (`skill`, an existing kind). **Attuned**: deleted with its kind. **Overreach**, **Quick study**: unchanged.
- **Creatures**: read nothing in play today; the dev dump's `cl N` goes; their `spellcraft` values stay data nothing reads.
- **Spells classes grant**: the player's at the table's level, whatever their Spellcraft; the load-time test's caster-level clause goes.
- **Training**: a `cast` mark on Spellcraft at 25 %, as Concentration's.
- Dumps, JSON, the probe's column, spec, `docs/dev/`, the wiki, and every test are listed with what happens to each.

## Worked numbers

The chance of learning Magic missile, Fireball, Call the elements, and a level-56 spell at levels 1, 10, 30, and 60 per class, today against the design at a steady and a focused pace of level-up rolls, and where the outcome moves and why (§2.2).

## Implementation issues

N1 the rule and the starting points; N2 the talents, the affix, the unique; N3 caster level itself (code, `casting`, dumps, probe, docs, wiki); N4 the cast mark.

## Open questions

1. The curve's shape (recommended: the bent one above; the straight line is the alternative).
2. Arcane training as Spellcraft +10, or dropped into the wizard's dice (recommended: keep).
3. The cast mark now, or after #973 (recommended: now, at 25 %).

author: ormastes
body:
Repro lane for the byte-identical `0x0000001100000001` tail of the par_state record. The defect is now **minimally reproduced and bisected**; the seed fix belongs to a follow-up lane with proper codegen-test infrastructure. No production code changed (in-guest probe reverted); the record + one repro example are the deliverable.

## Repro strategy result

- **Host JIT passes**: `simple run` of the identical struct-literal repro prints `STRUCT LITERAL OK` — so the shared frontend/MIR is fine (SMF output is also target-independent).
- **In-guest AOT fails deterministically**: a struct literal with **four `[i64]` fields** faults on the first field read (scause=5, `stval = 0x0000003300000008` — an `{alloc_size<<32 | HEAP_STRING_BUILDER=8}` header word; the size half tracked the program's allocations: 0x11=17 in the earlier build, 0x33=51 now). The field receives an unrelated allocation's header.
- **Bisect boundary**: 1-field struct OK, 2-field (`[i64]`,`[text]`) OK, **4 array fields BROKEN** — points at register-pressure/spill value plumbing in the AOT emitter, not the offset table.
- Plain array-literal LOCALS (`var a: [i64] = [0]`, `[" "]`, four of them) are **correct in-guest** — the trigger is specifically struct-literal field initialization.
- Both the checked-in seed and a seed rebuilt from this branch (release tip `13a060d644e`) reproduce it — a genuine release-tip AOT cranelift defect, not seed staleness. Host AOT x86_64 builds of even a trivial entry exceeded 5 min on this host (SCV admission closure), so the in-guest loop (~80 s kernel build + ~3.5 min boot) was the practical iteration vehicle.

## Root cause (bounded, not yet fixed)

AOT cranelift-only struct-literal field-value corruption once ~4 array-typed field values are live — candidate area `src/compiler_rust/compiler/src/codegen/instr/closures_structs.rs::compile_struct_init` (stores `field_values` at MIR offsets; value/field pairing breaks under spill pressure). Recorded with the minimal repro, the bisect boundary, and the iteration loop in the dated repro section of `doc/08_tracking/bug/riscv64_in_guest_parse_recursion_par_state_uninit_2026-11-05.md`.

## Files

- Record: dated repro/bisect section (method, evidence, candidate area, next-lane loop).
- `examples/10_tooling/arr_repro_tmp.spl`: standalone JIT-passing repro (the AOT trigger is the 4-field struct in the record).

`bug_db.sdn` untouched. Cycles used: 6 of 6 (stopped per the rule with the defect bounded and reproducible).

author: kaeawc
body:
## Summary

On an iOS 26.5 simulator with Xcode 26.6, `xctrace record` never finishes saving a trace. SIGINT, the time limit and SIGTERM all fail, so `performanceTrace stop` waited 60 s and returned a bundle with no data. Following the owner decision on [#16999](https://github.com/kaeawc/auto-mobile/issues/16999), `XctraceRecorder.start` now checks the environment before it runs any xctrace command:

- `xctraceCompatibility.ts` holds `XCTRACE_BROKEN_COMBINATIONS`, a small data table with one row today (Xcode `26.6` × simulator runtime `26.5`). Versions match by dotted prefix, so 26.6.x and 26.5.x also match, but 26.60 does not. To cover another combination, add a row.
- `HostXctraceEnvironment` reads the Xcode version from `xcodebuild -version` through the existing `XcodebuildClient`, and caches it once read. It takes the simulator runtime from `device.iosVersion`, or falls back to `simctl list --json devices <udid>`. Physical devices have no simulator runtime. If either read fails, the version counts as unknown, which fails open and keeps today's behaviour.
- A matching combination throws `XctraceUnsupportedEnvironmentError` (an `ActionableError`). The error names both versions and tells the user to run with Xcode 27.x, for example `DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode-27.app/Contents/Developer`, or to use a different simulator runtime.
- The SIGINT stop path is unchanged.

Reuse: `parseXcodeVersion` moved from the doctor check into `XcodebuildClient.ts`, and both now import it. `iosVersionFromSimctlListDevices` (a dotted string) now backs the existing `iosMajorVersionFromSimctlListDevices`.

Docs: new `docs/using/performance-trace.md` (added to mkdocs nav) documents the limitation. No `docs/using` page covered performanceTrace before.

## Linked Issue

Closes #16999

## Bug / Regression Context

- **Observed symptom:** `stop` failed with `xctrace did not finish finalising the trace within 60000 ms after SIGINT`. The bundle held only `RunIssues.storedata`.
- **Repro steps / conditions:** Xcode 26.6 (17F113) with an iOS 26.5 simulator. The raw `xcrun xctrace record` hangs the same way. The same flow works on Xcode 27.1 with iOS 27.0 (device research in the issue comments).

## Validation

- [x] `bun run typecheck` and `bun run typecheck:test` report no errors
- [x] `bash scripts/prepush-node.sh --changed`: format, typecheck, lint, test typecheck, fast validation static checks, repository lint tests, changed unit tests and affected unit tests passed. Two stages need a note:
  - **Tool definitions drift:** fails on `origin/main` as well, on `portReverse` from #17102 / #17105, which this PR does not touch. I regenerated it locally only to let the gate continue, and did not commit it.
  - **Safe integration tier:** only the `PrototypeHttpExecutor` / `PrototypeChannelExecutor` local-server tests failed. They pass with the container's HTTPS proxy unset, so the failure comes from the container, not this change.
- [x] New code uses interfaces and fakes. Unit tests cover: the broken pair is refused before any xctrace command (no template list, no spawn); 26.6.x / 26.5.x point releases are refused; Xcode 27 is allowed; other iOS runtimes are allowed; an unknown Xcode or runtime is allowed and still stops with SIGINT; the environment probe falls back and caches.
- [x] Docs describe current behaviour only
- [x] Rebased onto latest `main`

## Device Verification

Not run on a device: this container has no Mac. The refusal fires before xctrace starts, so the unit tests with fakes cover the decision.

author: johnson-zs
body:
## Root Cause Analysis

ShareWatcher in the "My Shares" view only subscribed to `signal_Share_ShareAdded` and `signal_Share_ShareRemoved` DPF signals — it never subscribed to any attribute-change signal. When a share directory's permission changes (e.g., read-only → read-write), `ShareWatcherManager` detects the filesystem attribute change via `LocalFileWatcher` and emits `fileAttributeChanged`, but that signal was only connected to `UserShareHelper::onShareChanged` (triggers metadata poll-refresh) and was never forwarded through the DPF signal channel. Meanwhile `dirshare.h` had no `signal_Share_ShareChanged` registered at all, so `ShareWatcher` could never receive attribute-change notifications, leaving the lock icon stale until manual refresh.

Key evidence: `sharewatcher.cpp:43-44` (only 2 subscriptions), `usersharehelper.cpp:468-472` (`initConnect()` missing `fileAttributeChanged` connection), `dirshare.h:30-33` (no `signal_Share_ShareChanged`).

## Fix

Three-layer change to complete the signal chain:
1. Register `signal_Share_ShareChanged` DPF signal in `dirshare.h`
2. Add `emitShareChanged()` method in `UserShareHelper` — declares `shareChanged` Qt signal in `Q_SIGNALS`, emits both `Q_EMIT shareChanged(path)` and DPF `signal_Share_ShareChanged` (consistent with `emitShareAdded`/`emitShareRemoved` dual-emit pattern); connect `ShareWatcherManager::fileAttributeChanged` → `emitShareChanged` in `initConnect()`
3. Add `shareChanged()` slot in `ShareWatcher` (refresh + emit `fileAttributeChanged`), subscribe/unsubscribe `signal_Share_ShareChanged` in `start()`/`stop()`

Signal chain: `ShareWatcherManager::fileAttributeChanged` → `emitShareChanged` (`Q_EMIT shareChanged` + DPF publish) → DPF `signal_Share_ShareChanged` → `ShareWatcher::shareChanged` → `Q_EMIT fileAttributeChanged(url)` → view refreshes lock icon

### Amendment (per CI reviewer feedback)

The initial submission's `emitShareChanged()` only published the DPF signal, missing the Qt signal emission — inconsistent with sibling methods (`emitShareAdded`/`emitShareRemoved`/`emitShareRemoveFailed` all use `Q_EMIT` + `dpfSignalDispatcher->publish` dual-emit). Amended to add `void shareChanged(const QString &path)` in `Q_SIGNALS` and `Q_EMIT shareChanged(path)` in `emitShareChanged()` implementation, ensuring in-process Qt signal consumers also receive permission-change notifications.

## Change Safety Assessment

### Code Safety

- **Risk Level**: Low
- All changes are purely incremental — new signal registration, new Qt signal declaration, new emit method, new subscribe/unsubscribe pair — no existing function signatures modified, no public members removed, no existing signal flow altered
- New code mirrors existing `emitShareAdded`/`shareAdded` and `emitShareRemoved`/`shareRemoved` patterns; commit `40a4a1f6` (permission modification fix) is not reverted
- Amended `emitShareChanged` now follows the same dual-emit pattern as all sibling methods

### Business Impact Scope

- **My Shares view**: Share directory permission changes (read-only ↔ read-write) now trigger real-time lock icon refresh
- **Regression scope**: Share add/remove behavior unchanged; normal file view lock icon refresh unaffected
- Affected modules: `dfmplugin-dirshare` (signal registration + forwarding), `dfmplugin-myshares` (signal subscription + view refresh)

### Verification Suggestion

1. Change a shared directory's permission (read-only → read-write and reverse), verify lock icon updates in real-time in "My Shares" view
2. Verify share add/remove still triggers correct view refresh (regression)
3. Rapid permission changes should not cause signal storms or crashes

---

## 根因分析

"我的共享"视图的 `ShareWatcher` 仅订阅了 `signal_Share_ShareAdded` 和 `signal_Share_ShareRemoved` 两个 DPF 信号，未订阅任何属性变更信号。当共享目录权限变更时，`ShareWatcherManager` 通过 `LocalFileWatcher` 检测到属性变更并发射 `fileAttributeChanged`，但该信号仅连接到 `UserShareHelper::onShareChanged`（触发轮询刷新元数据），从未通过 DPF 信号通道转发。同时 `dirshare.h` 未注册 `signal_Share_ShareChanged`，导致 `ShareWatcher` 无法收到属性变更通知，锁图标不会实时刷新。

关键证据：`sharewatcher.cpp:43-44`（仅订阅 2 个信号）、`usersharehelper.cpp:468-472`（`initConnect()` 未连接 `fileAttributeChanged`）、`dirshare.h:30-33`（无 `signal_Share_ShareChanged`）。

## 修复方案

三层改动补全信号链路：
1. `dirshare.h` 注册 `signal_Share_ShareChanged` DPF 信号
2. `UserShareHelper` 新增 `emitShareChanged()` 方法——在 `Q_SIGNALS` 区段声明 `shareChanged` Qt 信号，实现中同时 `Q_EMIT shareChanged(path)` 与 DPF publish `signal_Share_ShareChanged`（与 `emitShareAdded`/`emitShareRemoved` 双发模式一致）；`initConnect()` 连接 `ShareWatcherManager::fileAttributeChanged` → `emitShareChanged`
3. `ShareWatcher` 新增 `shareChanged()` 槽（refresh + emit `fileAttributeChanged`），`start()`/`stop()` 订阅/取消订阅 `signal_Share_ShareChanged`

信号链路：`ShareWatcherManager::fileAttributeChanged` → `emitShareChanged`（`Q_EMIT shareChanged` + DPF publish）→ DPF `signal_Share_ShareChanged` → `ShareWatcher::shareChanged` → `Q_EMIT fileAttributeChanged(url)` → 视图刷新锁图标

### 修订说明（按 CI reviewer 建议）

首次提交的 `emitShareChanged()` 仅做了 DPF 信号发布，缺少 Qt 信号发射，与同类方法（`emitShareAdded`/`emitShareRemoved`/`emitShareRemoveFailed` 均为 `Q_EMIT` + `dpfSignalDispatcher->publish` 双发模式）不一致。amend 补全：`Q_SIGNALS` 区段新增 `void shareChanged(const QString &path)` 信号声明，`emitShareChanged()` 实现中新增 `Q_EMIT shareChanged(path);`，确保同进程 Qt 信号消费者也能收到权限变更通知。

## 改动安全评估

### 代码安全评估

- **风险等级**: 低风险
- 所有改动均为纯增量操作——新增信号注册、新增 Qt 信号声明、新增 emit 方法、新增 subscribe/unsubscribe 对——不修改已有函数签名、不删除公开成员、不改变现有信号流
- 新增代码镜像现有 `emitShareAdded`/`shareAdded` 和 `emitShareRemoved`/`shareRemoved` 模式；commit `40a4a1f6`（权限修改修复）未被撤销
- amend 后 `emitShareChanged` 与所有同类方法遵循相同的双发模式

### 业务影响范围

- **我的共享视图**：共享目录权限变更（只读↔读写）后锁图标实时刷新
- **回归范围**：共享添加/删除行为不变；普通文件视图锁图标刷新不受影响
- 受影响模块：`dfmplugin-dirshare`（信号注册+转发）、`dfmplugin-myshares`（信号订阅+视图刷新）

### 验证建议

1. 修改共享目录权限（只读→读写及反向），验证"我的共享"视图锁图标实时刷新
2. 验证共享添加/删除仍正常刷新视图（回归）
3. 频繁权限变更不应导致信号风暴或崩溃

## Summary by Sourcery

Propagate shared-directory attribute changes to the My Shares watcher to keep permission state and lock indicators up to date.

Bug Fixes:
- Refresh the My Shares view when shared-directory permissions change so lock icons stay current.

Enhancements:
- Complete share-change notification propagation across Qt and DPF signal channels, including registration, forwarding, and watcher subscription handling.

author: danielhanchen
body:
## Summary

When an image render needs the card, Studio parks SAM 3 (the Detailer / segment model) in host RAM instead of unloading it. Today the parked copy is pageable unless `UNSLOTH_SAM3_PARK_PIN=1`, because torch's pinned allocator took minutes to pin 1.7 GB on a loaded host (#14616). A pageable copy makes every park and unpark about 2.6x slower.

The park now pins by default with the registered host memory the offload pinners already use (`registered_pinned_empty`). That is an anonymous mapping, faulted in parallel and then `cudaHostRegister`ed, so it never goes through torch's single-threaded pinned allocator.

- If registered memory is not available (Windows, WSL, ROCm, capped pinning, integrated GPU, or a failed register), the copy stays pageable. It never falls back to torch's allocator.
- `UNSLOTH_SAM3_PARK_PIN=0` keeps the copy pageable. `=1` keeps torch's pinned allocator, as before.

## Evidence (Kaggle Tesla T4, torch 2.14.1)

Each arm runs the real `_HostWeights` class from its own tree (main 157305f659 vs this branch) on a SAM 3-sized model: 1.7 GB bf16 in 1500 tensors on the GPU. Each arm runs a first park, then 5 unpark/park round trips. Two full rounds, A/A included.

| arm | first park s (r0 / r1) | park median s | unpark median s | weights after round trip |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main, unset (pageable) | 1.622 / 1.550 | 0.330 / 0.333 | 0.357 / 0.361 | bit-exact |
| main, `=1` (torch pinned allocator) | 1.211 / 0.158 | 0.130 / 0.130 | 0.138 / 0.138 | bit-exact |
| this PR, unset (registered pin) | 1.030 / 0.957 | 0.130 / 0.130 | 0.138 / 0.138 | bit-exact |
| this PR, `=0` (pageable) | 1.541 / 1.547 | 0.335 / 0.331 | 0.360 / 0.359 | bit-exact |

- Unpark (the latency a Detailer pass waits on) goes from 0.36 s to 0.14 s, and park from 0.33 s to 0.13 s. The first park is also faster (1.6 s to 1.0 s), because the registered buffer is faulted in parallel.
- The kill switch `=0` reproduces main's pageable numbers.
- On round 2, torch's allocator reuses its cached block (0.158 s). That is a property of an idle process, not of a loaded host.

## Tests

- New tests in `tests/test_diffusion_segment.py`:
  - `test_park_pins_with_registered_memory_by_default` covers unset, empty, `0`, `off` and `1`.
  - `test_fast_park_pin_falls_back_to_pageable_not_the_torch_allocator`.
- Base vs head on `tests/test_diffusion_segment.py` (each arm imports its own tree):
  - head: 69 passed, 2 failed.
  - base with the new tests: 66 passed, 5 failed.
  - The 3 extra base failures are the new default tests.
  - The 2 failures common to both are environmental on this host (its transformers has no `Sam3Config`): `test_tiny_config_is_small_but_the_real_input_is_1008` and `test_a_failed_load_places_no_weights`.

## Not covered here

- No run on a heavily loaded host, which is the case that made torch's allocator slow. The registered path is the one the video and offload pinners use there for the same reason.
- No end-to-end Detailer render timing, only the park and unpark itself. Only a T4 was measured.

author: koumatsumoto
body:
## 目的

refs #1820

FREDの同値再確認でもhandoff/inputごとに全履歴SQLiteを不変objectへ追加していた経路を、共有本文packと小さいstate・固定参照へ分ける。既存schema13の正本、受入・遅着判定、L2、他14groupの保存形式は変えない。現行のschema13本番切替とは独立した後続変更で、このPRから本番データ更新やGCは行っていない。

## 変更

- Collectionの `fred_transport.py` が本文pack・月別metadata pack・固定rootを所有する。既存gzip payloadのexact bytesを維持し、同値とA→B→Aの既知本文を再コピーしない。
- 完全応答の確認時計はsource単位で保持し、原受領時計・採用参照とは区別する。固定入力からschema13 SQLiteの全論理行を再構成し、従来の統合へ渡す。
- 新pack/rootはcreate-only＋全bytes読戻し。unknown ACK、未完了PUT、CAS競合、破損・欠損は確認またはfail closedとする。
- 可変inventoryは重複保存防止hintだけ。旧固定入力の読取はinventory・最新pointer・canonical・現在のsource catalog・L2へfallbackしない。
- 旧SQLite handoff/inputを改変・削除せず読める状態を維持し、新旧の同一stage retryも元の固定内容を検証する。

## 合成測定とGETの代償

初版の独立レビューで正確性blockerは見つからなかった。以下は実R2ではなくMemoryR2Storeによる実 `publish_inputs` 経路の測定。

1,000期間×同値5回の旧SQLite方式とpack方式を比較:

| 指標 | 旧SQLite | pack |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 5回後の保持bytes | 2,398,308 | 787,149 |
| 初回PUT bytes | 479,724 | 734,237 |
| 5回目PUT bytes | 479,724 | 23,023 |
| 定常GET bytes | 492 | 745,717 |
| 定常GET回数 | 2 | 10 |
| 定常HEAD回数 | 9 | 28 |

本文packの追加PUTは `[1,0,0,0,0]`。全PUTが0になるわけではなく、小さいrun/state/root/manifestは増える。保持量はこのfixtureで67.2%減った一方、base64/metadata等で初回は増え、保存時に既存packを照合するGET帯域も増える。最新固定inputのcold読取は6 GET / 592,452 bytesだった。長期差分pack数に応じて読取回数は増え、実環境の速度・課金削減は未検証。

別の240期間×3日、stage→通常経済統合→15 input公開では、本文60,709 bytesの1 packを維持し、固定metadata/root込みの不変領域は162,265→169,313→176,585 bytes。canonicalとinventoryを除いて初日のinputをcold再現できた。

author: nithinchandranr-aws
body:
## Description

Run one SQL unit of work as a single transaction on Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 from AWS Step Functions. A Standard state machine calls the Amazon RDS Data API: BeginTransaction, three ExecuteStatement calls (insert an order, decrement stock with a guard, insert an audit row), then CommitTransaction, or RollbackTransaction when a step fails. No AWS Lambda function is in the request path. Claim issue: #3415.

## Key Innovation

**First AWS Step Functions to relational database pattern in the repo.** The transaction id travels through workflow variables, so a failure in a later state rolls back an insert made in an earlier one. The open PR #3307 (appsync-aurora-serverless-v2-rds-data-api-cdk) uses the same Data API from AWS AppSync resolvers; the caller and the edge differ.

## Architecture

AWS Step Functions (BeginTransaction, ExecuteStatement x3, CommitTransaction or RollbackTransaction) -> Amazon RDS Data API -> Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 PostgreSQL, with AWS Secrets Manager holding the cluster credentials

## Composition

- **AWS Step Functions**: holds the transaction id across states and runs the Catch to RollbackTransaction
- **Amazon Aurora Serverless v2**: PostgreSQL in private isolated subnets with no inbound rule, scales to 0 ACUs
- **AWS Secrets Manager**: generated cluster secret, read by the Data API with the caller's permissions

## Deployed and Tested

Stack deploys in us-west-2 (about 570 s), 18 CloudFormation resources, no Lambda function. README Testing run as written in zsh and bash 3.2 with identical results:
- commit path: SUCCEEDED, stock 5 -> 3, one order row, one audit row
- rollback path: order of 10 units ends FAILED with InsufficientStock after InsertOrder and DecrementStock; the counts are unchanged, so the insert was rolled back (independent read with `aws rds-data execute-statement`)
- a check constraint violation and a foreign key violation end FAILED with RdsData.DatabaseErrorException; RollbackTransaction was accepted after each failed statement and the counts are unchanged
- the first execution after the cluster auto-paused failed once with RdsData.DatabaseResumingException, the retry succeeded (17 s; later executions 1.3 to 1.6 s)
- the cluster is not publicly accessible, has storage encryption on and its security group has no inbound rule
- `cdk destroy` took about 12.5 minutes and left nothing from the stack behind
- Not tested: a second Region, a stopped or timed-out execution that leaves a transaction open, a failing CommitTransaction

## Checklist

- [x] IAM least-privilege (four `rds-data` actions on one cluster ARN, `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue` on one secret; `Resource: *` only for the Amazon CloudWatch Logs delivery actions of Step Functions logging)
- [x] CDK synth passes (18 resources)
- [x] Deployed and tested end-to-end in us-west-2
- [x] `validate.js` passes, including the admin IAM check
- [x] No duplicate patterns in repo

author: jirathip-k
body:
Closes #491

## For humans

A reviewer whose FAIL verdict is rejected for missing Proof blocks no longer leaves the issue stuck. If the reviewer's pane is still open, it is told once what to fix. If it has gone, or goes quiet again without fixing the file, drive starts a fresh review of the same head, and that does not use up a review round. Drive also stops re-submitting a rejected file that hasn't changed.

## What changed

- `gate::no_proof(body)`: the existing #418 check, pulled out so drive can call it; `verdict` uses it unchanged.
- `drive::no_proof`, run for each `verdict … FAIL` step:
  - A FAIL with its Proof blocks is recorded as before.
  - A proofless FAIL goes through `verdict` once for each (head sha, file content hash) since the review spawn, and that refusal is logged as a `proof-refused` event. The same file at the same head is not tried again (fix 2).
  - If the reviewer is still in herdr and hasn't been told yet, drive types the NO_PROOF text into its pane once and checks that it landed (fix 3). A corrected file has a new hash, so it is recorded on the next pass.
  - If the reviewer has ended, drive runs `spawn <fleet> <n> <check role> --supersede` at the same PR head and logs `lane-lost` with `why: "verdict refused NO_PROOF: re-review"` (fix 1). Ended means: gone, or idle again after being told, or the prompt could not be delivered. No verdict is recorded, so the round count stays the same.
  - Issues already stuck (synergy #3088) have no `proof-refused` event yet. On the first pass after this lands they get the one refusal, then the prompt or the fresh review (fix 4).
- Decision: "live" means the reviewer is still listed in herdr, not that it is `working`. `waiting` never offers a verdict while its reviewer is working (`crates/core/src/waiting.rs:421`), so a working reviewer can never reach this path. That makes the idle reviewer the one to prompt, and idle-again-after-being-told counts as ended. One consequence for fix 4: if #3088's reviewer pane is still open, it is prompted on the first pass and gets the fresh review on the pass after it goes idle again without fixing its file.
- Fast passes only record the refusal and prompt; the re-review spawn waits for a slow pass.

## Tests (at f0b360bc642f0a8a018f4cf1c3d4a7362e837fa0)

New in `crates/cli/tests/drive.rs`:
- `a_proofless_fail_from_an_ended_reviewer_gets_one_fresh_review_of_the_same_head`: one `herdr agent start` for the rev lane, `spawn … rev --supersede`, no verdict, state stays `review(1)`, old verdict.md removed.
- `an_idle_reviewer_is_told_once_then_the_unchanged_file_is_not_retried_but_re_reviewed`: prompted once. Two hours later (past drive's 1 h quiet period for repeated refusals) the unchanged file is not tried again and the reviewer is not told again; it gets the fresh review instead.
- `a_told_reviewers_corrected_fail_is_recorded`: after the prompt, the fixed file is recorded as FAIL and moves to `fix(1)`.
- A well-formed FAIL behaves as today: covered by the existing drive tests, e.g. `the_third_fail_stops_at_needs_human_with_the_findings`.

All three new tests fail when the drive.rs change is reverted (checked locally).

- `cargo fmt --check`: exit 0
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0
- `cargo test --workspace`: exit 0
- `herdsman cap-check --config ci/cap.toml`: exit 0 (24825 / 24995)

`src/` net +79 (budget +50): drive needs the extra lines for the prompt-once and ended-reviewer paths, plus the formatter's line breaks.

## Not verified

The live readback (synergy #3088 gets a new review lane and a recorded verdict) can only be checked after this merges and drive runs on the real host.

author: kibanamachine
body:
Fixes #257562

### Summary

- The `installMockPrebuiltRulesPackage` root hook failed with `retry.try reached timeout 20000 ms waiting for 'installFleetPackageByUpload'`, wrapping a `503 {"message":"Request timed out"}`.
- `installFleetPackageByUpload` declares 5xx as transient and retryable, but gave itself a **20s** budget — shorter than a *single* worst-case attempt, so the retry it declares could never run.
- Raises that budget to 90s, so two worst-case attempts plus the 10s upload rate-limit delay fit.

### Context

- An upload that hangs on Elasticsearch only comes back as 503 once Kibana's [30s `elasticsearch.requestTimeout`](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/blob/main/src/core/packages/elasticsearch/server-internal/src/elasticsearch_config.ts#L140) fires — `"Request timed out"` is `@elastic/transport`'s `TimeoutError` message, so the failing attempt necessarily lasted ≥30s. With a 20s budget and [`retryForSuccess`](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/blob/main/src/platform/packages/shared/kbn-ftr-common-functional-services/services/retry/retry_for_success.ts#L74-L78) checking its deadline *between* attempts, the loop aborted after attempt one with zero retries — even though [`retry_fleet_request.ts`](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/blob/main/x-pack/solutions/security/test/security_solution_api_integration/test_suites/detections_response/utils/rules/prebuilt_rules/retry_fleet_request.ts#L16-L17) is explicitly written to absorb that 503.
- The 20s value was sized for Fleet's 10s upload rate-limit window, which is unrelated to how long a *failing* attempt can take. A timeout bump is normally the wrong tool, but here it is not buying slack for a slow operation: it is what makes an already-declared retry path reachable at all. A healthy upload finishes in ~2s, so the wider budget only costs wall-clock when an attempt actually hangs.
- Follows the [latest investigator analysis](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/issues/257562#issuecomment-6658610016) (posted minutes before this PR). Its underlying trigger — an Elasticsearch stateless commit-notification authorization denial that stalls the saved-object bulk write — is an ES-side defect with no Kibana-side fix; this PR only repairs the part that is in our control.
- The earlier [429 rate-limit analysis](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/issues/257562#issuecomment-4582387866) on this issue describes a different trigger and is superseded: the attempt-count limit it pointed at no longer exists now that the helper is purely timeout-based.
- Failures are on `kibana-package-registry-verify-and-promote` (6 occurrences, Mar 2026) and most recently [`kibana-chrome-forward-testing` build 774](https://buildkite.com/elastic/kibana-chrome-forward-testing/builds/774#01a1aba2-4f8c-412b-9f43-617476d1b7a3) (`ftr_configs_29`, 2026-11-05).

<details>
<summary>Verification</summary>

#### Verified locally

- ✅ Passed: `node scripts/eslint x-pack/solutions/security/test/security_solution_api_integration/test_suites/detections_response/utils/rules/prebuilt_rules/install_fleet_package.ts`

#### Not verified locally

- The suite is an FTR API integration test and needs a live Elasticsearch + Kibana, which this environment does not provide, so it was not executed.
- The trigger (an Elasticsearch stateless commit-notification denial) cannot be reproduced on demand, so the fix is justified by the budget arithmetic rather than by a reproduced-then-green run.
- If that denial turns out to be systematic rather than transient in the serverless simulation image, the wider budget will not save the suite — the retry will simply hit the same hang twice.

</details>

> The flaky test runner may verify the PR, but the owning **team is responsible the next steps**:

> - Make changes (check out the branch locally, or ask `@copilot` if Copilot is enabled on your account)

Bootstrap the first package under `next` using the verified artifact and a maintainer's npm authentication, then configure npm trusted publishing for repository `LibreChat-AI/code-interpreter`, workflow `code-package.yml`, environment `npm`. No long-lived publishing token is required by this workflow.

Run a main-branch dispatch with the committed version and `publish: false` to prepare/test an artifact without publication. Later explicit publishes use a matching `code-v...` tag or a main dispatch with `publish: true`. Repository `v...` tags remain independent.

author: alexanderrex
body:
MIL-F-8785C p. 60 defines low altitude as "ground level to approximately 2,000 feet AGL", and the medium/high model is for phases "where proximity to the ground is not a factor". `Turbulence()` was given the height above sea level, so 30 ft above 6000 ft terrain flew the high altitude model: 23.6 ft/s rms at severity 6 in dead calm, with the wind at 20 ft ignored.

- The height above the ground now picks the model and sets the low altitude scales. Fig. 7's table stays read above sea level: the figure says only "ALTITUDE", and only the behaviour near the ground should change.
- That height jumps at roofs, cliffs and tile gaps, and PteroSim answers 164,042 ft when it knows no ground. Tustin's second-order filters ring on a jump, so the height moves at 50 ft/s at most, between the 10 ft clip and the 2000 ft where the model stops reading it.
- A step of no time takes the height outright, as RunIC and a trim run at no time and PteroSim runs RunIC at load and again at the real start.
- The high altitude branch can no longer be reached, and the blend ends on it: L is 1750 ft exactly, and sigma is the table's within 8.9e-16 ft/s.

## Measured

Held c172p at 100 ft/s, severity 4, wind at 20 ft 33 ft/s, 1/240 s, 48 seeds, Tustin. Peak ft/s median / worst, then the median ratio to the run without the jump at the end height.

| Case | No limit | 1 s low-pass, 2000 ft cap | 50 ft/s, 2000 ft cap |
|---|---|---|---|
| 30 -> 3000 ft, east | 222 / 654, 14.8 | 70 / 225, 4.5 | 12 / 20, 0.6 |
| 30 -> 3000 ft, down | 315 / 1378, 17.5 | 79 / 358, 3.7 | 9 / 13, 0.5 |
| Tile gap 5 s and back, east | 151 / 386, 8.2 | 56 / 168, 3.3 | 18 / 24, 1.0 |
| Tile gap 5 s and back, down | 179 / 802, 17.1 | 49 / 253, 4.3 | 11 / 13, 1.0 |

The final code gives the 50 ft/s column exactly. 30 -> 130 ft peaks at 72 / 206 ft/s east without the limit and 15 / 24 with it. Jumps of that size hold at 30, 100 and 200 ft/s; cliffs and gaps were measured at 100 ft/s only. Milspec does not ring on any of these. 50 ft/s is chosen from these runs, no source gives it.

## Known costs

- Terrain rising suddenly leaves the aircraft on the wrong model for up to 39 s (3000 -> 30 ft: 1.29 median, 3.16 worst).
- A real rise of the height takes the same 39 s, under-reading meanwhile. Roll rate on 30 -> 3000 ft reads 1.77 to 1.85 at the median against the end height, as lag rather than ringing.
- A gap over about 39 s still reaches the high model, without ringing.
- A real descent at 100 ft/s lags, with 8% less rms in the longitudinal gust.
- In free flight over streaming tiles the turbulence now depends on when a tile arrives, because the height does. By reading, step mode and static levels are not affected.
- Bare API only: `hold()`, `reset_to_initial_conditions(0)`, `resume()` places the aircraft but walks the height from the last flight, up to 39 s. `DONT_EXECUTE_RUN_IC` with no RunIC keeps it too. PteroSim does neither: its reset always runs an unheld RunIC.

## For the PteroSimCore PR that takes this DLL

- `FGWinds` gains a data member, so its layout changes: the headers and the library must change together, along with #22's `FGWinds.h`.
- The public turbulence text says JSBSim reads altitude above sea level: `client.py`, `WorldService.proto` and `EnvironmentManager.h`. It changes in that PR.

## Checks

- `testLowOverHighTerrain` and `testSecondRunICTakesItsHeight` fail on the unfixed build at the assertion.
- `testHeightJumpSmoothed` fails with the limit removed, 7 of 8 subtests. Over 128 seeds the bound of 3 is exceeded by 81 seeds on the ordinary jump and 111 on no ground without the limit, and by none with it.
- `testHighModelTableReadAboveSeaLevel` fails with the table read back on `h`: its ratio falls from 1.11 to 1.000005.
- Traces at seed 1 over flat terrain against the exact base: bit-identical at 5000 ft, at most 2.0e-8 ft/s of turbulence and 3.0e-7 ft of height at 1500 ft, repeatable across runs.
- The same seed after a reset repeats the episode sample by sample, Milspec and Tustin, including a terrain jump.
- ctest 98/98.

author: adamkany
body:
## Summary

**Part 1: model v2 (condition categories)**
- `src/features.py`: `condition_features(conditions)` adds keyword multi-hot flags `cond_oncology`, `cond_cardio`, `cond_neuro`, `cond_infectious`, `cond_metabolic`, `cond_psych`, `cond_respiratory`, `cond_healthy` plus `n_condition_categories`. Patterns match at word starts. `build_features` calls it, and the columns are in `FEATURE_COLUMNS`.
- `python src/build_dataset.py --backfill` adds these columns to the existing `trials.parquet` from the `conditions` text (split on `"; "`), so no raw pages are needed.
- Retrained with the identical pipeline, calibration, CV and split. **v2 does not meet the promotion bar** (test ROC-AUC +0.0037 < 0.005), so **`models/gbm.joblib` stays v1** and v2 is saved as `gbm_v2.joblib` / `gbm_uncalibrated_v2.joblib`.
- `train.py` now has `FEATURE_SETS` (`v1` for the app, `v2`). A plain `python src/train.py` still reproduces the app model (identical metrics to float noise); `--features v2` writes only `_v2` files. `predict.model_features` feeds each saved model its own inputs.

| Model | Features | CV ROC-AUC | Test ROC-AUC | Test PR-AUC | Test Brier |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gbm` v1 (app) | 29 | 0.7099 | 0.7102 | 0.2319 | 0.0974 |
| `gbm_v2` | 38 | 0.7143 | 0.7139 | 0.2396 | 0.0971 |

**Part 2: per-trial drivers**
- `src/predict.py`: `explain(features, top_n=5) -> [(friendly_name, value, direction, size)]`.
- SHAP TreeExplainer was tried first. Its values missed the model's log-odds by up to 2.2 because it does not follow `HistGradientBoostingClassifier`'s native categorical splits, so it is not used (and not added to requirements).
- Method used instead: set one input at a time to the typical training trial (`models/explain_reference.json`: train medians, or the most common value for categories) and measure the change in the uncalibrated GBM's log-odds. Max age and its flag move together.
- Friendly names now live only in `src/labels.py` (`FEATURE_NAMES`, `feature_name`, `feature_value`). The Explain page, the drivers charts and the what-if table all use them.

**Part 3: app**
- Search detail view: "What pushes this trial's risk up / down" bar chart.
- Check your own trial:
  - The form returns a design dict that goes through the new `features_from_design` helper (API-shaped record into `build_features`), so the training rules are no longer copied by hand.
  - New conditions text box that shows the recognised condition areas.
  - Same drivers chart as Search.
  - Plain message instead of a bare `assert` when the model and the form disagree.
  - "What would lower the risk" only tries design levers: blinding, allocation, arms, eligibility length, age limits and DMC. It never suggests phase, sponsor, purpose or condition, and never an impossible design such as a randomized single arm.
- `risk_gauge.py` uses `src.predict.percentile` instead of its own copy.

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest tests/`: features (new condition, backfill and design-helper tests), predict (new `explain()` tests on a model with known drivers, plus one on the saved model), app helpers
- [x] `python tests/test_pages.py`: every page in `streamlit.testing` AppTest with the API stubbed. New checks: drivers chart on Search and Check, design-only levers, condition recognition, model-mismatch message
- [x] `python src/train.py` reproduces the v1 metrics exactly

body:
## Description
Going back from the stored payment method screen to the preselected bottom sheet with predictive back showed a broken animation. The sheet was a `ModalBottomSheet` in a dialog window, rendered as a nav3 `OverlayScene`. During the gesture `NavDisplay` animated towards that overlay scene, which it draws in a separate window, so the sheet popped in on top of the outgoing screen and was recreated when the gesture completed.

This PR draws the sheet inside the Drop-in window:

- **Render the preselected payment method sheet inside the screen**: M3's `BottomSheet` with a scrim, inside the screen itself instead of a dialog window, so it takes part in `NavDisplay`'s transitions and predictive back. `BottomSheetSceneStrategy` is removed. While another screen animates over or away from the sheet, it cannot be dismissed.
- **Slide the screens opened from the preselected sheet up over it**: the stored payment method screen and the payment method list slide up over the sheet, and the sheet and scrim stay in place underneath.
- **Dismiss the preselected sheet when tapping outside it**, as `ModalBottomSheet` did.
- **Keep the preselected sheet below the status bar** when it is taller than the screen.

Closing Drop-in only after its screens have animated away, and the scrim behind the full-screen screens, are in the follow-up PR stacked on this one.

## Что было

На первой неделе Premium (диагностика) в полосе «План на 7 дней» все карточки показывали «практику», даже дни после конца диагностики, где по ротации 1-из-6 должно быть изучение метода. Под карточками стояло «Сегодня — занятие 6 из 6», а это просто побочный эффект формулы слота.

- В `session_info` добавлено поле `diag_day_num`. Дашборд пишет «Сегодня — диагностика, день N из 7» вместо «занятие 6 из 6».
- Назначение настоящих уроков не менялось: эта логика уже была верной.

- New unit tests in MyFeatureTest.Codeunit.al pass locally; full module test suite green.

## Risk & compatibility

<!-- Anything reviewers should watch for: breaking changes, upgrade/data impact, permissions,

author: yiuhong
body: ## Summary On a phone, Statistical Power’s range sliders are the 44px controls from #95. A horizontal drag still moves them after the page has scrolled. What fails is the gesture that starts on the slider and goes vertically: `touch-action: pan-x` tells the browser not to scroll, so the long parameter card cannot be panned from those controls. When a scroll does win, the native range has already jumped to the finger’s x, and that jump was left in place. This keeps the 44px target (8px track, 28px thumb) and changes the shared coarse-pointer rule to `pan-y pinch-zoom`. A vertical finger scrolls. A horizontal finger still moves the control. If the browser cancels the gesture to scroll, the value returns to where it was when the finger went down. ## Root cause `body.demo-page input[type="range"]` in both demo themes set `touch-action: pan-x` under `(max-width: 768px), (pointer: coarse)`. That declaration allows a horizontal pan and refuses a vertical one. Checked in Chrome 156 at 390×844 with touch, on the standalone page and inside the Catalog iframe (`?embed=shell`, body `overflow-x: clip`): - Before any scroll, a horizontal drag moves Significance Level (0.01 → 0.15) and the readout matches. - After `scrollTo`, and again after a touch-scroll of the Catalog iframe has settled, the same drag still moves it (0.01 → 0.15). Sample Size, which is below the fold, moves after scrolling down to it (10 → 75). The box stays 44px tall. `elementFromPoint` on the control is the input. The chart tooltip is `pointer-events: none`. No parent of the slider has a transform, filter, or sticky/fixed cover. - A vertical swipe that starts on the slider does not change `scrollY` while `touch-action` is `pan-x`. The value does change, because a range sets itself on touch-down. With `pan-y`, the same swipe scrolls (about 40 → 529) and `pointercancel` fires. Restoring the snapshotted value on that cancel puts α back to 0.05, label included. - A mostly horizontal drag with about 28px of vertical drift still moves the slider and does not scroll, before and after a settled scroll. - During an in-progress fling the next touch is taken as scrolling and can miss the slider because the content is still moving. Once the fling ends, the drag works. That is momentum, not a stuck control. - WebKit 27.2 (Playwright, iPhone-like, coarse pointer) also moves the slider after `scrollTo`, with the 44px box. Synthetic touch moves there did not scroll the document, so the after-touch-scroll case was checked in Chrome. Ruled out for this failure: the chart press-readout overlay, a fixed shell header covering the iframe, a transform on a parent, and the 44px hit box itself. The hit box is unchanged. ## Repro Phone width, or a coarse pointer. Touch, not only a mouse. 1. Open Statistical Power, on its own or from Catalog / Guided Tracks. 2. Drag Significance Level. α and the chart move. 3. Scroll the page down (in the shell, scroll inside the demo pane). 4. Drag Significance Level again, and drag a slider that was below the fold (Population Std Dev or Sample Size). 5. Put a finger on a slider and swipe vertically. The page should scroll, and the value should end where it started. ## Other demos The `pan-x` rule lived in both shared themes, so every coarse-pointer range on a `demo-page` had it. body:
🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01BCa71BbaXaC34n89fqj1Gq

Step 3 of the data exchange plan (Claude doc "ORM2 as hub for data exchange").

## What it adds
- **Exchanges.** An exchange is a chain of steps, saved in the file and part of undo. A step is a two-way mapping, which can run either way, or a view, which only runs forward. Each step starts where the previous one ended. The Mappings tab has a new Exchanges section with + Step, Run, and a report for each step.
- **Result check.** Every schema an exchange fills is checked against its own constraints, using the Validation panel's population checks. Violations on a relational schema are written in table terms ("The album row 1 has no title."). Violations of one kind about one element are grouped together. A single view run gets the same check.
- **Apply.** Apply puts the last step's population into its schema as one undo step. The populations of the schemas in between are not kept.
- **Rows as SQL.** `populationSql` writes the rows as INSERT statements or COPY blocks:
  - parents come before children;
  - views and fully derived columns are left out;
  - the sequences of generated columns are moved past the values written.
  
  It is available from the exchange report and from File › Export Sample Rows as SQL….
- **Casts.** New data operators asInteger, asDecimal, asFloat, asBoolean, asDate, asDatetime and asTime. They are verbalised in all six languages and written as `CAST` in SQL.
- **Fix:** `runView` now adds the reference values of the entities it makes to their value types. Before, the result check reported every derived Artist as missing from ArtistId.

## Tested
- On Chinook: Supplier SQL → ORM2 ⇒ Consumer ORM2 (view) ← Consumer SQL.
  - Without a rule for Album has Title, the check reports "The album row 1 has no title. (and 346 more like it)".
  - With that rule, the check passes for both the consumer's ORM2 schema and its tables.
- The INSERT and the COPY scripts both load into PostgreSQL 16 after the exported DDL: 275 artists and 347 albums.
- The `setval` lines were checked on a serial column and on an identity column.
- The verbalisation golden tests pass, `vite build` passes, and a Playwright run of the tab reports no page errors.

Six dedicated case study pages, `studio/work-<slug>.html`, one per project on the Work grid, all in the same structure:

author: cinquinandy
body:
## Pourquoi

Renovate n'a ouvert aucune PR sur ce dépôt depuis l'onboarding de 2024 (#1, fermée par le bot 37 minutes après son ouverture). `renovate.json` est sur `main` depuis le 2 novembre. Côté GitHub, rien ne bloque : l'app Renovate est installée sur For-Hives avec « All repositories », sans suspension. La config est valide.

Le blocage est chez Mend : le dépôt n'y est pas analysé. Il n'a ni Dependency Dashboard ni branche `renovate/*`, alors que ForVoyez et ForVoyez-Doc, avec la même base de config, ont reçu des PR aujourd'hui. Il faut réactiver le dépôt sur developer.mend.io. Cette PR ne peut pas le faire.

Elle prépare le dépôt pour que Renovate y fusionne seul, et sans danger, dès qu'il sera réactivé.

## Contenu

**`renovate.json`**
- Passage de `config:base` à `config:recommended`. La migration est validée par `renovate-config-validator --strict`, qui échoue sur l'ancienne config.
- Tableau de bord des dépendances (`dependencyDashboard`).
- `minimumReleaseAge` de 3 jours, comme ForVoyez et ForVoyez-Doc.
- Fusion automatique :
  - des mineures et des correctifs npm et composer ;
  - de la maintenance du fichier de verrouillage.
- Restent en PR : les majeures et GitHub Actions (aucun test n'exécute `deploy.yaml`).
- `platformAutomerge: false` est conservé : `main` n'a pas de contrôles obligatoires.

**`tests.yml`**, nouveaux jobs :
- **ESLint, Prettier (`assets/js`) et lint-staged.** Reprend le commit 9ee310a.
- **phpcs** (`phpcs.xml`) et **PHPCompatibilityWP 8.0+**. `phpcs.xml` déclare `testVersion` mais ne charge pas PHPCompatibility.
- **Contenu du zip.** `composer run zip`, la même commande que `deploy.yaml`, est comparé à la liste exacte des 40 fichiers livrés.
- **release-guard.** Lit les `paths-ignore` de `version-bump.yml`. Une PR de `renovate[bot]` qui toucherait un autre fichier échoue, donc ne se fusionne pas seule. Les autres PR reçoivent seulement une notice si leur fusion publie une version.
- Inchangés : PHPUnit sur PHP 8.0, 8.2 et 8.4 (avec multisite) et Admin CSS.

**`version-bump.yml`**
- `paths-ignore` est élargi à `.github/**` et `composer.lock`. Ce dernier n'est pas suivi aujourd'hui (`.gitignore`) : c'est une précaution.

**`deploy.yaml` et `tests.yml`**
- `npm ci --ignore-scripts` : aucun script de cycle de vie npm ne tourne dans un job qui reçoit les identifiants SVN.

## La fusion ne publie rien

Fichiers modifiés : `.github/workflows/deploy.yaml`, `.github/workflows/tests.yml`, `.github/workflows/version-bump.yml` et `renovate.json`.
- **Version Bump :** les 4 sont déjà dans les `paths-ignore` de `main` (`.github/workflows/**`, `renovate.json`).
- **Deploy :** aucun ne fait partie de ses chemins de déclenchement (`package.json`, `auto-alt-text-for-images.php`, `readme.txt`).

## Vérifié en local

- ESLint, `prettier --check assets/js` et lint-staged : OK.
- phpcs : 0 erreur. PHPCompatibilityWP 8.0+ : 0 erreur.
- Rebuild de la CSS : aucun écart.
- Contenu du zip : conforme à la liste.
- actionlint : aucune remarque sur les nouveaux jobs.
- release-guard, essayé sur 3 cas :
  - cette PR : « publishes nothing », sortie 0 ;
  - PR Renovate qui modifie `readme.txt` : échec ;
  - PR humaine qui modifie `readme.txt` : notice seulement.

body:
## Why
\`Plastic Components.zip\` holds one STEP part and seven Parasolid (\`.x_t\`) parts. The importer created one BOM item and listed the rest as \"skipped (not a STEP file)\", which reads like a drawing or a note, not like seven parts that did not come in. The platform reads STEP only (OpenCascade has no Parasolid reader), so the files are correctly left out, but the message did not say what they are or what to do.

## What
A file of a zip that is not STEP is now skipped with a reason that depends on what it is: a native CAD format (\`x_t\`, \`x_b\`, \`sldprt\`, \`sldasm\`, \`catpart\`, \`catproduct\`, \`prt\`, \`asm\`, \`ipt\`, \`iam\`, \`3dm\`, \`dwg\`; the list the direct-upload check already used) reads \"a native CAD file (.x_t), not read: export it as STEP (AP242) and upload that\"; anything else keeps \"not a STEP file\". The same function in both cores (\`skipReason\` in check-upload.ts, \`skip_reason\` in core/crates/runner/src/job.rs), and the \"no STEP file\" error no longer depends on the reason text.

## Not changed
No new format is read. Reading Parasolid directly would need a licensed converter (a product decision, not part of this change).

## Verified
Unit tests for both (backend cad-uploads 63 passed; \`cargo test -p runner\` 47 passed; clippy -D warnings, fmt, tsc clean). A new parity-harness fixture (a STEP part beside \`.x_t\`, \`.sldprt\` and a PDF) and the real \`Plastic Components.zip\` run through the real Python path and the real Rust runner container (image rebuilt from this change): 0 findings, identical \`skipped\` lists.
