author: special-place-administrator
body:
## Why

Ledger rows G13 and G14 (`docs/research/2026-11-02-gate-modes/LEDGER.md`), both seen live on 2026-11-05:

- **G14:** after an autonomous task completed, the agent could not even run `supervisor status`. Every tool outside the read-only tool list got a bare "GATE: task is completed", with no next step.
- **G13:** a Terminal Commander job stopped with `command_stop` stayed `pending` in `task_state` forever.

## What

- `adapter.rs`, terminal-task refusal: it now uses the same `inspection()` test an unclassified prompt gets (read-only tools, read-only commands, and the proposal command), so those stay open. The refusal names the next step: "a new work prompt starts the next task (intent_apply start)".
- `supervisor level` without arguments (and with `--project <dir>` or `status`) joins the read-only commands. Setting a level stays refused.
- `observation.rs`: the owner's `command_stop` for a known job appends a `stopped` row. `pending_jobs` skips stopped jobs, and the row has no exit, so it can never count as a completion. Another session cannot stop-mark the job.

No enforcement is loosened: mutations after completion are still refused, and a read-only web fetch is still refused during a discussion turn.

## Tests (regression-first)

Both new tests were observed failing first, then passing:

- `autonomous_completion.rs` `a_completed_task_still_allows_read_only_commands_and_names_the_next_step`. Red: `supervisor status --json` returned `Deny("GATE: task is completed")`.
- `observation.rs` `a_stopped_tc_job_is_no_longer_pending_and_counts_as_no_completion`. Red: the stop was not recorded.

author: tse-wei-chen
body:
## Scope
Security regression campaign for the six SQL dialects at the existing Query/DML/DDL compiler boundary. This is a **test-only** feature branch from `develop`; no runtime policy or public API changes.

## Deterministic coverage floor
- 768 Query/DML statement-stacking rejection attempts (8 second-statement shapes × 4 separators × 4 entry prefixes × 6 providers)
- 192 single-statement DDL stacking rejection attempts
- 48 malformed lexical/control-character rejection attempts
- 24 physical table policy attacks via direct queries/CTEs/joins/subqueries
- 24 comment-obfuscated unbounded UPDATE/DELETE cases requiring typed Policy diagnostics
- 144 **positive controls**: attack-shaped text must compile as SQL parameter values, not be blacklisted or interpolated
- Cross-six-dialect positive Query/DML/DDL controls

## Security assertions
Query/DML failures must be deterministic across repeats, reject with typed compile evidence and no plan fingerprint. DDL single-statement attempts must reject, never yield a compiled plan. Positive controls require literal payloads in typed parameters and absent from rendered native SQL. Physical-table whitelist must not be bypassed by CTE names.

## Verification
- [ ] SqlAgent.Test CI on **this PR head SHA**
- [ ] Existing Server tests / baseline comparison
- [ ] Review all failing variants; fix compiler bugs at their owning boundary, or correct an invalid test case without reducing the safety floor
- [ ] Confirm no regression to existing positive grammar corpus

## Boundaries / remaining work
Offline deterministic compilation tests, not live database penetration tests. This PR intentionally does not claim Host authorization, approval replay, version/session-specific dialect injection, or real-provider differential parity is solved. Those require their own runtime/integration gates. No production source, dependencies, APIs, or separate test framework are added.

## Stop rule
Merge only after required checks and tests green at the final head SHA. No automatic merge until evidence is verified.

author: ecoutu
body:
Stacked on #85.

## Bug
Every close of a grouped tab (the user's, Close group, a duplicate close) logged "user moved tab out of group" in the why-log and put the tab in leave-alone.

## Root cause
Chrome fires `tabs.onUpdated` with `groupId: -1` just before `onRemoved` for any closed grouped tab (checked in Chromium 156 with both `tabs.remove` and a user-style close). `Reconciler.onTabGroupChanged` took it for a drag out.

## Fix
By the time that event is handled the tab is already gone (checked: `tabs.get` fails). A `-1` update for a tab missing from the snapshot is ignored. The snapshot is only read for `-1` updates.

## Tests
`tests/engine/reconciler.test.ts`: closing a grouped tab logs no leave-alone and adds none. The drag-out tests still pass.

**Symptom:** In the upload wizard, step 3 "Create comparisons" shows empty selectors (no "Choose phenotype") when every row of samples.csv has at least one NA. "Auto-detect comparisons" also does nothing. No error is logged.

Verified on a 1034 × 33 samples.csv with 0 complete rows: `isTruthy(m)` is FALSE, `isTruthy(dim(m))` is TRUE.

author: anhtahaylove
body:
Fixes the four defects (D1-D4) the independent Codex verifier found in round 3 at 97ee34c5, each with a regression test that fails on the unfixed code. The round-3 report is committed unchanged as `docs/team-ui-evidence/codex-custodian-round-3.md` (VERDICT: FAIL); round 4 runs on the fixed main.


Codex round 3 (`docs/team-ui-evidence/codex-custodian-round-3.md`, unchanged, at 97ee34c5) found four defects. Each is fixed here with a regression test. Codex's tests are kept without the `round3` prefix, and their assertions are unchanged.

| Defect | Fix | Test | Before / after |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1: a setup that returned an error could leave a verified FKEK usable (the collect ran before the setup credential was deleted) | `src-tauri/src/lib.rs` `team_fleet_key_setup`: release the setup key (forget it, persist `fkek_nonce` cleared) right after `bootstrap_fleet` confirms activation and BEFORE the verified collect. After `prepare`, nothing reads the setup key, so a resumed run replays the saved bytes and collects without it. Doc comments in `fleet_custody.rs` updated. | `custodian_it::a_setup_whose_cleanup_fails_leaves_no_usable_verified_key` (Codex), plus a retry: Ok, `created && !setup_key_held`, same `fkek_key_id`, `has_fleet_key` | FAIL ("a failed setup left a verified key usable for sealing") / PASS |
| D2: the device-list IPC reply could echo the access token through a server-controlled `label_hex` | `src-tauri/src/fleet_client.rs` `list_tenant_devices`: each row's free text goes through `redact` with the access token (and the v2 prefixes): `device_id`, `account_id`, `status`, and the label after it is decoded (it is encoded again as hex). Key fields are hex that the custodian decodes and checks. | `fleet_custody::tests::a_successful_device_listing_does_not_echo_its_access_token_to_ipc` (Codex) | FAIL ("the device-list IPC reply leaked the access token") / PASS |
| D3: after Team was reopened, an active pinned device whose code expired was offered Enroll again, which the backend always refuses | `src-tauri/src/lib.rs` `team_join_code`: when the window is closed and the device holds a pin, it asks the server for the device's status with the login it already has. If the status is `active`, it refuses with the new `fleet.joinedCollectKey`. Any other answer, or a failed lookup, keeps `fleet.joinCodeExpired`. `TeamJoin.tsx` shows the expired line plus that notice in place of Enroll again. The e2e mock does the same. en/vi locale entries added. | e2e `an active pinned device is not offered reenrollment after reopening Team` (Codex); Rust `custody_tests::an_expired_code_on_an_active_pinned_device_points_at_its_key` (new: active pinned gives joinedCollectKey, pending pinned gives joinCodeExpired) | e2e FAIL (1 Enroll again button) / PASS; Rust FAIL with the branch disabled / PASS |
| D4: "Fleet key ready" and the Approve gate read the setup journal, not whether the key is usable now | `TeamCard.tsx` passes `has_fleet_key`, `fleet_key_blocked` and a status reload into `TeamDevices.tsx`. Ready shows only when the journal is done and the key is usable. When the journal is done but the key is blocked, the Q-18 notice shows. When it is done but no key is usable, a new en/vi notice points to Collect key custody. Approve needs a usable key (the backend builds a new approval with `fleet_key(generation)`). Revoke needs only the saved Create fleet key (`custodian()` = `create_request`), so a lost key does not block it. A setup reloads `team_status`. | e2e `a custodian with no usable key is not shown Fleet key ready` (Codex) | FAIL (1 ready message) / PASS |

## Deviations from the brief

- D3 does not use team status. A pending pinned device can still enroll again (`a_pinned_pending_device_can_enroll_again`, the Architect S3 amendment). So the "active" half has to come from the server, which `team_status` cannot ask without the network. The join-code reply asks only when the window is closed and the device holds a pin. It then reuses the login the UI already sends.
- D1 residual: if the server refuses the ack after the collect kept the key, setup still returns that error while the key is verified and usable. `team_collect_custody` behaves the same way. The setup journal is consistent (the setup key is released). A retry, or Collect key custody, replays the saved ack.
- D4: when the Q-18 notice shows, Approve is disabled too, as the brief asked. The backend `fleet_key` closure itself does not check Q-18. A saved approval that was never sent, on a custodian that lost its key, cannot be resent from the UI until the key is collected again.

author: nek0der
body:
## Summary

Weir no longer reads or writes `~/.codex/config.toml`. At launch it used to read the file and, when it held the hook trust tables Limpid 0.1.11 and earlier wrote, take them out and save the whole file back, so an edit the person saved in that moment, by hand or through Codex, could be lost. The tables now stay where they are, and they do nothing: each holds a hash of a hook command from the build that wrote it, and the trust Weir passes in the `-c` flags that carry its hooks takes its place.

`CodexHookInstaller.removeLegacyTrust` and its call at launch are gone, with `CodexUserConfig`, `CodexConfigSyntax`, and `CodexConfigFile`, which only it used. `docs/known-limitations.md` now names the tables and says how to remove them. `docs/data-migration.md`, the privacy page in English and Japanese, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, and the shim and fixture READMEs describe the change. `docs/data-migration.md` also no longer says that a build wrote `# BEGIN weir` markers, which none did.

## Related issue

author: jakes1345
body:
## README
Replaces the marketing-style README with one written from the code:
- How profiles, the hub, the reconciler, the dashboard, the tray and the CLI fit together.
- The five built-in profiles and what a profile controls.
- The maintenance commands that run on every switch.
- Install and run-from-source steps, and the CLI.

It also corrects claims the old README got wrong: the config path, plugin hooks that only log a line, and GPU, NVIDIA and compositor settings that are saved in a profile but not applied.

## CI (`Build & Lint`)
This check has been red on `master` since August: `ruff check switcher/` found 55 errors, so the test step never ran.
- Applied ruff's safe fixes: import order, unused imports and variables, type hints, f-strings.
- Passed `check=False` explicitly to all 19 `subprocess.run` calls. Each caller already checks `returncode` or the output itself.
- Stopped silently swallowing exceptions:
  - Telemetry and the dashboard's hub stream catch `grpc.RpcError` for the expected "hub offline" case, and log anything unexpected.
  - The pulse thread logs once per run of failures.
  - The desktop notification ignores only `GLib.Error`.
- Small cleanups: collapsed nested `if`s, iterate `dict.values()`, timezone-aware log timestamps, and dropped the unused shebang in `switcher/__main__.py`.
- `test_build_script_with_tweaks` expected `nohup`, which the v1.0.0 commit removed on purpose. Start commands can be compound, like `systemctl start x || true`, and `nohup` breaks those. The assertion now checks the current behavior: the command starts in the background with output discarded, guarded by `pgrep`.
- Added `ruff.toml` with `target-version = "py311"`, the minimum the code needs because it uses `tomllib`. Without it, ruff gave different results locally and in CI.
- Pinning the target exposed a real bug. `save_config()` put a backslash inside an f-string expression, which is a `SyntaxError` before Python 3.12, so the app couldn't start on 3.11. It's fixed, and the TOML it writes is unchanged.

Locally, `ruff check switcher/` passes, `python -m unittest discover -s tests` passes all 10 tests, and everything compiles under Python 3.11.

## Security
- **Hub reachable from other machines.** `citadel-hub` runs as root with an unauthenticated gRPC API, and it listened on `[::]:50051`, meaning every network interface. It now binds to `127.0.0.1:50051`, and the dashboard, tray and CLI connect to `127.0.0.1` explicitly.
- **Passwordless root through PolicyKit.** Any user in the active session could run `citadel-apply`, which executes any script it's given, as root with no password (`allow_active=yes`). It's now `auth_admin_keep`. The hub runs as root and executes scripts directly, so normal profile switching doesn't change.
- Fixed the policy's `vendor_url`, and the README's Security section now describes the fixed behavior.

author: kk4oda
body:
The 0.3.4 speed tweaks for DV slow data, plus a timing bug found while measuring them.

**Bug: the real ACK was ignored after a held write.** Releasing the write hold (0.3.3) shifted every sender timer by the whole write. That included the stale-ACK guard (`earliest_answer`) and the RTT anchor (`air_end`), which already allowed for the burst's air time, so it was counted twice. The peer's ACK arrived "too early", was ignored, and the sender waited ~12 s for its retry timer, every window. A simulated-link capture shows the gaps: ACK at 34.6 s, next data at 47.4 s.
- `LegacySender::burst_written(now)` caps both at the end of the write; `Transfers::release(.., Hold::Write, ..)` calls it.
- Regression test `the_answer_after_a_held_write_is_accepted`: fails without the fix.

**8-block windows** on DV slow data (was 4): 960 bytes per REQACK, half the round trips. D-RATS receivers accept any count.

**`piece_bytes`** per serial port (default 180, valid 64–2048), for experiments with the radio's piece size. At 220 the REQACK would join each window's last block, but that size is untested on the radios. Combining it by shrinking blocks costs more overs than it saves, so it isn't done.

**Simulated link, 3 kB random file, 2 runs each:**

| | 4-block windows | 8-block windows |
|---|---|---|
| before the fix | 104–112 s | 114–115 s |
| with the fix | 92–93 s | **81–82 s** |

Tests: workspace tests, fmt and clippy are clean. `docs/bench-results.md` updated (Transceive OFF made no measurable difference).

body:
Native record mutation and page SQL still lived in Core. This moves their common owner into the existing app storage package and keeps the original host transaction, admission and workflow/history hooks. Core will consume these same functions rather than keeping a duplicate CAS or query implementation.

The mutation pipeline serializes a record, handles exact import replay, rejects stale revisions and overflow, writes the existing minimized outbox event and invokes mandatory host hooks. Bounded page queries retain typed shared-index equality and public status/channel/schedule predicates; all field names and values are parameter-bound. Model/index admission and final field projection remain host responsibilities.

Validation: formatting and clippy pass. Real PostgreSQL contract tests pass for CAS races, exact/changed replay, before/after-hook and outbox rollback, foreign namespaces, translations, overflow, bounded keysets, typed filters, hostile inputs and publication. The package remains a trusted host library; standalone authenticated service/model/identity extraction is still open.

author: jackowfish
body:
## Description

Restoring a sandbox fails if a file it holds open on a gofer mount was deleted or renamed on the host after the checkpoint. `restoreFile` can't walk to it, and the whole restore aborts with `failed to walk ... no such file or directory`. This happens a lot on shared ReadWriteMany volumes, where other pods change files between checkpoint and restore.

This adds `--restore-missing-files=fail|stale`. The default `fail` keeps today's behavior. With `stale`, a regular file or directory that's missing on restore gets marked stale and invalidated from the dentry tree, along with its descendants. Open FDs on it then fail with `ESTALE`, the same error NFS returns for a stale handle, and path lookups go back to the host. Saving skips stale dentries, so the sandbox can be checkpointed again.

author: matthewcorven
body:
Closes #155.

The same pr-triage agent as the merged Band C baseline, with its state in a Durable store instead
of a JSON blob on a git branch.

**Rebased onto `dev` at `2fbd0bf`.** Head `5b3467f`.

## Verdict on the review's six findings

| # | Finding | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | A memo from a failed transaction is resurrected | **Fixed and proven** |
| 2 | The resume path is unreachable once the store holds two tasks | **Fixed and proven** |
| 3 | The mid-phase seam proves the ledger, not the memo | **Fixed** (`BAND_C_HIDE_LEDGER`) and the claim **restated** |
| 4 | The comment-effect window was called "measured" with no stage | **Fixed and proven** |
| 5 | Requirement 4's refusal is the store *file* lock, not a commit gate | **Restated** — no code change; the claim was wrong, not the code |
| 6 | No `CHANGELOG.md` entry for `Transaction.Memo` | **Fixed** |

Details for each, below, then the original description.

---

### 1. Memo resurrection — FIXED AND PROVEN

Confirmed as described. The mechanism is exactly as reported, plus one detail that decides where the
fix goes: `UndoLog.Restore` restored the record but not the provider's `_taskStates` baseline, and
`UpdateTask` had already moved that baseline forward to the post-write state. TypeScript's
`restore` already did `states.set(task.id, snapshot)`; C# and Python did not.

Fixed in `UndoLog.Restore` (both ports), which now takes the baseline map and puts the snapshot back
so the record and the baseline are restored together. No change to `Transaction.Memo` itself.

Proven by the exact sequence the finding describes, with and without the fix:

```
$ dotnet run .scratch/probe-jsonl.cs      # JSONL store, second failing tx, then a later commit, then reopen
# with the fix
after first failure: memos=0
after second failure: memos=[]
after a later commit: memos=[]
after reopen:        memos=[]

# without the fix (git stash lib/Durable.cs)
after first failure: memos=0
after second failure: memos=[comment/101/d]
after a later commit: memos=[comment/101/d]
after reopen:        memos=[comment/101/d]
```

The judge's persistence claim is confirmed: it reaches disk and survives a reopen once any later
transaction commits.

Tests, **both failing without the fix** (2 failed / 0 passed with `lib/Durable.cs` stashed, 2 passed
with it):

- `MemoDiscardedByARollback_DoesNotReappearInTheNextFailedTransaction` — stages a **second,
  unrelated** failing transaction, which is what makes the stale baseline observable. Fails on
  `the memo discarded by the first rollback must not reappear in the next one`.
- `CheckpointDiscardedByARollback_DoesNotReappearInTheNextFailedTransaction` — the same shape with
  **no memos at all**, so it is independent of `Transaction.Memo` and shows the defect was never
  memo-specific.
- `a memo discarded by a rollback does not reappear in the next failed transaction` (TypeScript) —
  guards the behaviour TS already had.
- `test_memo_discarded_by_a_rollback_does_not_reappear_in_the_next_failed_transaction` (Python) —
  fails without the Python fix.

The false "a rollback then restores the memo map" comments are corrected in all three ports: they now
say what arms the undo and point at `UndoLog.Restore` for both halves, instead of asserting an
outcome.

### 2. Dead resume path — FIXED AND PROVEN

Confirmed as described. `TriageStore.CurrentTask` was `Tasks.FirstOrDefault(name == …)`; after one
completed generation that is always the finished task, so `existing.Status == Terminal` was always
true and `Runner.cs`'s resume branch was dead.

Fixed: the selection prefers a non-terminal task and tie-breaks on creation sequence (parsed from the
`t{sequence}` id, so it does not depend on provider iteration order).

Proven by the exact sequence: complete → seam → resume, same store. Before the fix the third process
printed `task t2 is finished (generation 1); starting a new one` and created `t228`, stranding the
interrupted `t223`. After it:

```
$ dotnet <dll> --store <scratch>/generation/store.jsonl --run-dir <scratch>/generation/run-3 ...
run:        resuming durable task t223 at phase 'classify' (attempt 2, restarts so far 0)
...
run:        completed — 13 triaged, 13 commented, 2 in cooldown, 1 not ours, 1 not open
```

This is **stage 5c** of `./evidence.sh`, with four assertions: the resume adopted `t223`, exactly one
resume banner, it never printed `is finished`, and it finished the work. The first generation's
thirteen comments are adopted by the ledger rather than re-posted, which the stage also asserts.

### 3. The seam proves the ledger, not the memo — FIXED, AND RESTATED

Confirmed, and I reproduced it: erasing every memo from the store at the seam and resuming gives the
identical `7 skipped`, attributed to the ledger, so stage 4 on its own did not show which guard did
the work.

I did **both** things the finding offered, because the first was cheap:

- **Added a control that separates them.** `BAND_C_HIDE_LEDGER=1` withholds the ledger entry and
  leaves the memo. Stage 4a: the ledger is empty (`ledger entries: 0`), the task holds 7 memos, the
  resume skips 7 and posts 6, and **zero** skips are attributed to the ledger. So the memo alone
  carries the seven.
- **Restated the requirement-3 text** to say what each stage is evidence for, and to say plainly that
  the pair is atomic and the ledger is the cross-run guard. The stage-4 block no longer implies the
  memo is what stops a re-post at that seam.

The memo's other evidence remains stage 8 (the pre-fix hang) and the rollback tests from finding 1.

### 4. The comment-effect window — FIXED AND PROVEN

Confirmed: the word "measured" appeared with no stage behind it. Now there is one. **Stage 4c** sets
`BAND_C_EXIT_AFTER_COMMENT_EFFECT=1` and asserts the shape rather than the prose:

```
✓ the seam exited 42 between the effect and its record: 42
✓ comments on disk at the seam: 1
✓ the ledger has no record of the comment that exists: ledger entries: 0
✓ and no memo of it either: 0
✓ the resume posts #101 again — the duplicate this window costs, and exactly one: 1
✓ comments on disk afterwards (13, not 14): 13
```

The capture is regenerated from that run; the section that used to say "measured, not argued" now
cites the stage and its assertions.

### 5. Requirement 4 is the file lock — RESTATED, not fixed

Confirmed, and no code change is the right answer. The refusal is `StoreFileLock.Acquire`, which is
the layer's, and it fires because two processes were pointed at one path. The variant does not
implement a commit gate that knows what a repository is, and inventing one would need an owner record
inside the store — a private lock file beside it would be exactly the "no private store" line
requirement 5 draws.

The README now says this in three places instead of implying a designed gate:

- the requirement-4 bullet: *"meets the requirement as written and only as written… the guarantee is
  not 'one run per repository', it is 'one writer per store file'"*;
- §"Concurrency": what is demonstrated is *"two processes over one store cannot both proceed"*, not
  *"two triage runs of one repository cannot both proceed"*; satisfying it depends on the host
  deriving one path per repository, which `run.sh` does and the layer does not enforce;
- the comparison table's **Overlapping runs** row, rewritten to say the same.

Control 5b (two stores, both proceed) is unchanged and is what makes the limit visible rather than
asserted.

### 6. CHANGELOG — FIXED

`## [Unreleased]` now has `### Added` → `Transaction.Memo`, and `### Fixed` → the rollback defect and
the `MemoAsync` remark. Both cite #201.

---

## The five requirements of #155

1. **All eight phases remain visible.** `Phases.Order` is the baseline's eight headings; the four
   output documents are byte-identical to the baseline's (stage 1).
2. **Re-running without changes must not re-comment.** Stage 2: 0 posted, 13 adopted. Control 2b
   removes the guard and posts all 13.
3. **In

author: magicaldave
body:
Adds first-class timers and standard input to Jess, as the handoff for `feat/timers-stdin` asked.

Builds on [DreamWeave-MP/l3i#9](https://github.com/DreamWeave-MP/l3i/pull/9), now merged. `Cargo.toml` takes l3i `main`, locked at `322b70c`.

## Timers: `@jess/timer`

```luau
local timer = require '@jess/timer'

local once = timer.after(250, function() print('elapsed') end)
local repeating = timer.every(1000, function() print('tick') end)
repeating:cancel() -- idempotent; safe inside its own callback; repeating.active says if it can still fire
print(timer.now()) -- simulated milliseconds
```

- There is no second scheduler. `runtime::timers` is a bounded deadline queue, independent of Luau and of any clock, moved by `advance(delta)`. Dispatch goes through the same `DomainCore::call` as every handler, in the existing `Phase::Timer`, so budgets, attribution, diagnostics and profiling apply.
- A timer remembers its context and the source location that scheduled it. **Its authority and budget are the context's, read when it fires**, so reconfiguring a context reaches timers already queued. If the context has gone or no longer schedules the timer phase, the timer is dropped unrun.
- Code outside a handler gets a context named `@jess/timer`, which holds the domain's whole grant. Authority follows where a timer was scheduled, so a timer scheduled at load is not narrowed by a restricted context the same module binds to; to run under one, schedule from its handler. This is documented and tested. Scheduling from a context that doesn't schedule the timer phase is an error. Managed modules' contexts now always schedule it.
- Due timers run after `lateUpdate` and before the event drain, by deadline and then registration order. Timers scheduled during dispatch wait for a later frame.
- Missed ticks are skipped: a repeat fires at most once a frame, then schedules an interval on from that frame. A domain holds at most 16,384 active timers.
- A frame delivers at most 1,024 callbacks and the rest stay queued. That bounds a count, not a time, so a host can also set `DomainSpec::timer_dispatch_budget(Duration)`: once a callback ends past it, the rest of the batch waits for the next advance, in order, with at least one callback run per advance. It is **off by default, and the application host doesn't set it**, because it lets wall time decide which frame a timer lands on.
- A failed load, `stop` and `restart` drop all timers, and the clock restarts at 0.
- `on.host.timer` stays refused, with a new message pointing at `@jess/timer`. A timer is scheduled, not declared, and there is no payload for such a callback to receive.
- `jess run`, `jess test`, command targets and workers have no frames, so the module raises instead of scheduling something that would never fire. The standalone error points at `@jess/net`'s `run` and `sleep`.

## Standard input: l3i's `process.openStdin()`

`read` and `readLine` never block. `wait` is the explicit way to block. Jess adds `runtime::stdin`, an l3i input policy:

- Under a domain dispatch, opening is checked against the caller's authority, so a restricted context is denied.
- Under a dispatch, including on a worker, `wait` raises rather than stalling. `jess run` and command targets may wait.
- **Reads are not checked, by decision:** the handle is the authority to read, so passing it to a less privileged context delegates reading.
- The claim is process-wide with one consumer. It comes back on `close`, or when the runtime is dropped, which ending a generation or a worker does. `Runtime::shutdown()` also releases it (in l3i, tested there). A blocked reader thread is never joined and never calls Luau.

## Tests

- `tests/runtime/timers.rs`: ordering, cancellation including during dispatch, invalid delays, bounded dispatch of 5,000 due timers, 40,000 create/cancel cycles, the domain limit, the dispatch budget (deterministically at zero, and against real work with a positive budget), the contrast between a timer from load and one from a restricted handler, failing repeats and their attribution, restart, failed load, scheduling while stopping, and workers. Time is simulated throughout.
- `src/runtime/domain/timer.rs` unit test: a queued timer picks up a context's narrowed grant, new budget, lifted limits and removed phase mid-generation. It is a unit test because only the crate can redeclare a context.
- `tests/runtime/stdin.rs`: real runtimes in child processes with controlled pipes, covering delegation, a restricted context's denial, restart and stop releasing an unclosed handle, and a worker holding the claim.
- `tests/cli/stdin.rs`: the real binary, covering lines, empty lines, EOF, no final newline, CRLF, binary, line bounds, null stdin, target capability denial, an application keeping its frames while stdin is silent and then hearing it, stopping with a read blocked, and timers on real frames.

## Validation

On the final tree, with no-LTO development builds on Linux:

- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -W clippy::pedantic -D warnings`
- `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features` (199 library, 2 binary, 565 integration, 2 ignored)
- `cargo check --workspace --no-default-features`
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --all-features --no-deps`
- `cargo +1.95 check --workspace --all-features --all-targets` (the manifest's MSRV; AGENTS.md still says 1.92)
- `jess package test jpk/builtin` (456 passed, 0 failed) and a site build (106 pages), both with the branch's binary

The earlier head `77a569d` passed CI on Linux, Windows and macOS (ARM64 and X64). This was merged on the maintainer's go-ahead with CI on the final head still to report, so CI on `main` is the check for the review commits on those platforms.

The commits were split from one tree and were not all built individually. An interactive terminal was not tested: every stdin test uses pipes.

## Measurements

Verified release builds, seven runs alternating between `main` (`c1ab833`) and this branch, median with range:

| Idle `advance` | ns |
| --- | --- |
| `main`, no timers | 78.7 (74.4-79.8) |
| This branch, no timers | 80.0 (77.9-81.0) |
| This branch, 100 timers not due | 78.2 (76.1-79.9) |
| This branch, 16,384 timers not due | 78.9 (76.5-81.5) |

The no-timer path measures about 1.3 ns slower than `main`, and the ranges overlap, so these runs can't separate that from noise. Parked timers add nothing visible, even at the domain's limit.

| This branch | 100 timers | 16,384 timers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Schedule, each, ns | 586 (530-1144) | 683 (639-983) |
| Cancel, each, ns | 158 (137-189) | 196 (190-260) |
| Dispatch, per callback, ns | 367 (360-380) | 484 (464-494) |

Schedule and cancel are measured from Luau, including the call and the handle; dispatch includes the callback call.

Method: `cargo test --release --test integration --all-features -- --ignored --nocapture --exact runtime::timers::measure_timer_overhead`, in a shell without `tools/dev/no-lto.sh`, on Linux. The `main` side ran the same idle loop from a throwaway test in a scratch worktree. It links the l3i its own lockfile pins, not `368040d`, so the comparison also covers that l3i difference. Nothing ran on other platforms, and `timer_dispatch_budget` was not set in these runs.

## Review findings addressed

- **Timers snapshotted authority and budget:** fixed, as described above. `declare_context` already reconfigures a context in place, so this was reachable inside the crate.
- **Callback count isn't a time limit:** `timer_dispatch_budget` added. A single callback is still limited only by its context's budget.
- **Worker timer test asserted the wrong error:** the test was passing, because a worker gets a different message from a standalone script, one that does name workers. The assertion was loose, so it now pins `@jess/timer.after is for a domain`.
- **Benchmark command:** `--test integration` is correct, since `[[test]] name =

author: alexxgalea
body:
## Summary

The athlete hears each count late. This PR measures where that time goes. It changes nothing a release build does.

```text
scored frame captured ─► engine ─► apply() asks for the count ─► TTS onStart ─► sound out of the speaker
└──────────── engine trace: new `voice` rows (ASKED, STARTED, STOPPED) ────────┘
                                         └─────── SpokenCountLatencyTest, through the microphone ───────┘
```

- **Debug engine trace.** A `voice` row records when a count is asked for, when it starts and when it is cut off, on the engine's clock.
- **`replay_trace.py`.** `--voice-rows` and `--max-voice-ms N` give each scored frame's delay per stage.
- **`SpokenCountLatencyTest`.** An opt-in androidTest (`voiceLatency=true`) says counts with the phone's own engine and listens for them with the microphone. A second probe plays one rendered count trimmed and untrimmed, plus a click as the floor. `RECORD_AUDIO` is added in a debug-only manifest.

## Evidence

The phone is a P40 with Huawei HiAI TTS (`com.huawei.hiai`), English, speaking through its own speaker.

- **Trace, live Cindy session, 60 scored frames:** capture to `onStart` has a median of 135 ms and a p90 of 197 ms. Camera and analysis take ~120 ms of it, the handoff ~7 ms and TTS ~3 ms. The app's own path is fast.
- **`SpokenCountLatencyTest`, three runs:** from the ask to the count being heard, the median was **534, 479 and 540 ms** against a 250 ms limit (red). The engine's first audio chunk arrives at ~40 ms. **196–333 ms of leading silence** follow inside the synthesized audio, the same for each word on every run.
- **Probe, 8 plays each:**

| played | play → heard, median |
|---|---|
| "five" as rendered (820 ms, 304 ms of leading silence) | 450 ms |
| "five" trimmed | **142 ms** |
| click (speaker + microphone floor) | 134 ms |

The engine's leading silence accounts for most of the delay. The fix comes in a separate PR.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** debug-only

`Speaker.say` now returns the utterance id, and `VoiceDirector` reports which utterance started or stopped. Neither changes behaviour. The trace rows and `RECORD_AUDIO` exist only in debug builds. The test is skipped unless `voiceLatency=true` is passed. Run it with `adb install -r` and `am instrument` (command in the test's doc comment), not `connectedDebugAndroidTest`, which uninstalls the app and wipes its data. The JVM suite passes: 1660 tests.

author: leejianrong
body:
Undo and redo for the editor, backed by an engine history that the API, CLI and MCP share (SPL-75).

**How it works**
- Undo is a forward write: it saves the state before the latest edit as a new revision, so revisions stay monotonic and the events stream, stills and playback keys work unchanged. It takes `If-Match` / `--base-revision` / `base_revision` like any write.
- History lives behind `ProjectStore` (`history_state`, `step_history`), recorded inside the three write paths (`update_timeline`, `save_timeline`, `update_video_timeline`), so every edit type is covered, including a recording's splits, apply-ops, apply-plan and the editor's saves. One write is one entry; a batch of ops is one undo.
- Sidecar `.split-video-history/<project file>.json` next to the project (git-ignored), written under the project's lock. The project file formats do not change, so no version bump. The log keeps 100 entries within 4 MiB and drops the oldest.
- Other writers: the log is linear and the CLI, MCP and other tabs record into it, so undo reverses the latest write whoever made it. `base_revision` refuses if someone edited since. A project changed by something that does not record history has no undo until its next edit.
- A video with nothing saved shows its recording as one clip; undoing its first edit goes back to that (`initial` on `update_video_timeline`).
- Surfaces: `POST /compose/projects/{name}/undo|redo`, `POST /project/undo|redo?path=`, `compose undo|redo`, MCP `undo` / `redo`. Every project view carries `history: {can_undo, can_redo, undo_label, redo_label}`. New error code `history.empty`.
- Frontend: Ctrl/Cmd+Z, Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z and Ctrl+Y through the existing shortcut registry (text fields keep their own undo), and the toolbar buttons follow `history`. The result replaces `project.timeline`, so selection pruning, playhead clamping, preview and playback use the same path as an external change.

**Net line change: +1914 / -92 overall.** Hand-written source is +544 / -74 (src), tests +538, docs +46 / -10; the rest is regenerated `openapi.json`, the TypeScript client and `docs/errors.md`. It grew because this is a new capability with a new module (`history.py`, 111 lines) and three adapters; nothing was superseded, but the placeholder undo/redo wording in the docs was replaced.

**Verified**
- `tests/unit/test_history.py`: undo and redo of every op type, split_clip, set_canvas, properties, add/remove, moves, track flags, text, apply-plan replace, on both stores, comparing the serialised project; reopen persistence, caps, base-revision conflict, another writer, unrecorded change, a recording's first edit.
- `tests/integration/test_history_surfaces.py`: one scenario with the same results and errors on HTTP, CLI and MCP, plus the recording routes.
- Vitest for `project.step`; Playwright `e2e/undo.spec.ts` (edit, undo, redo, reload, undo again; Ctrl+Z in a text field is left alone) at 1440x900 and 1280x720 with region boxes checked.
- Full `uv run pytest`, frontend lint, check, test, build, and the whole e2e suite (28 passed).

Not in this PR: undo steps per drag are still one edit per gesture (a drag is already one edit); a history list UI.

author: squishy-squooby
body:
Closes #3192

## What changed

**Before.** Claim all sent one `POST /api/news/:newsId/claim` per unclaimed entry, one after another. Each was its own request, spend turn and transaction: about 24 Postgres round trips each (half of them the `set_config` re-stamp `run_as` sends before every store method), and every answer carried the whole board. With 54 entries live, one press was 54 requests in a row and about 1,300 round trips.

**After.** `POST /api/news/claim-all` is one spend: one request, one turn, one transaction under the account's economy lock, about 24 round trips whatever the number of entries.

- `crates/server/src/economy/news.rs`: `claim_all_news_once`. It takes no list: the server claims every entry live now and every dev post standing now that the account has not claimed, the same test one claim puts to an entry. `grant_of` builds an entry's grant for both paths.
- `crates/server/src/economy/store.rs`: three batch methods, each one statement in Postgres and one call in the fake. `economy_news_claim_all` (`insert … select from unnest(…) on conflict do nothing returning`, whose key decides what is paid), `economy_jlore_grant_all` and `economy_inventory_grant_all` (a data-modifying CTE that upserts the summed balance and writes one ledger row per grant, in order). The grant batches are payouts only: every delta above 0, one account.
- `crates/server/src/api/news.rs`, `app.rs`: the route. The single claim route is unchanged, so an older open tab still works.
- `apps/web/src/routes/NewsPanel.tsx`, `apps/web/src/net/api.ts`: Claim all sends one request; its answer replaces the list once.

## Tests run

- `cargo test -p jackioh-server`: every binary passed (1,750 in `server`, 684 in `server_store`), 0 failed.
- `server_store store::` against a local Postgres 16, migrated by `jackioh-server migrate` with `tests/db/bootstrap.sql` and `grants.sql` (as `tests/db/run.sh` does, without Docker): 684 passed.
- New: `r3191000_*` in `tests/api/news.rs` (every live entry paid once with its own ledger row; the store calls for 20 entries equal those for 2; the key replays and belongs to its route; a dev post is marked read and paid nothing; economy off and a pending account are refused) and the store contract case `r3191000_batch_news_claims_and_payouts_write_what_one_at_a_time_would`, run on both stores. `economy_turns.rs` checks the route waits its turn.
- Web: `vitest run src/routes/landing src/net src/economy/JlorePill.test.tsx src/auth/no-raw-html.test.ts src/in-app-links.test.ts`: 38 files, 887 tests passed. `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` and `eslint` on the changed files: clean.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo jackioh spec check`: ok. `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main`: App.
- After the renumber: the news, turns and contract tests, the two web files and `spec check` again, all ok.
- CI on `dafee6fe`: `rust`, `web`, `e2e smoke` and `db` passed; `bot selftest` skipped (no bot paths).

## Risks

- A Claim all now claims in one go what the server finds unclaimed, including an entry posted after the panel loaded; its answer shows it claimed.
- A store error rolls the whole press back, where a run used to keep the claims made before it.
- Security is as before: no client input decides what is paid, and the turn, lock, `Idempotency-Key`, `news_claims` key, `ECONOMY_LIVE` and active-account checks all hold.
- Not measured on a deployed site: the round-trip counts are from the code, and a test pins that the store calls do not grow with the entries.

## Player note

Claim all on the news claims every reward at once, so it no longer lags.

## Rulings and patch version

- R-rows added or changed: R3191000 (Claim all is one spend; amends R2982000), the first number of this pull request's block, taken before #3192 was opened, with its §11 paragraph in `spec/pending/3191.md`; R2982000's title and an **Amended** note; R2124000, R2378000 and §14.13 list the route.
- Fragment: none (no card plays differently).

- [ ] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (ran for `jackioh-server` locally; CI's `rust` ran it)
- [ ] `cargo test --workspace --features jackioh-engine/testkit,jackioh-engine/ts` (ran `cargo test -p jackioh-server` locally; CI's `rust` ran its groups)

- [ ] ~~bot checks~~ (no bot paths)

body:
Step 5 of 0.6.0's component consolidation, stacked on #667. Four more components that were another component with one prop set:

| Removed | Use instead |
| --- | --- |
| `<FilterToggle label="Agents" pressed onPressedChange>` | `<Button variant="selector" size="sm" pressed onPressedChange>Agents</Button>` |
| `<Gauge value label valueLabel aria-label>` | `<Meter shape="gauge" value label valueLabel aria-label>` |
| `<ParameterPopover trigger …>` | `<ParameterPanel trigger …>` (the same popover, title and Close button) |
| `<DeleteResource kind name consequence>` | `<AlertDialog tone="danger" title description confirmLabel confirmText={name}>` |

- **Button `pressed`:**
  - Any `Button` becomes a toggle with `pressed` and `onPressedChange`: `aria-pressed`, and the new state on click unless its own `onClick` prevents it.
  - The `selector` variant is FilterToggle's look: quiet like an unset select, and a check with full-weight text while on.
- **Meter `shape`:**
  - `bar` (the default) or `gauge`.
  - The gauge keeps its drawing, its near and over wording, and its 0.8 tick when no thresholds are given.
  - The gauge part is internal to the meter module, and `charts/gauge` is no longer an entry.
- **ParameterPanel `trigger`:** with one, it opens in the 320px popover and keeps the focus inside until Close or Escape. Without one, it sits in the page.
- **DeleteResource:** it only composed an `AlertDialog`. Its strings leave the library's catalogs, and the agent guide's row on irreversible actions points to `AlertDialog` with `tone="danger"` and `confirmText`.
- **Budget:** `button.js` may take 4 kB of its own, up from 3.8 kB (it is 3.9 kB now). It draws what `IconButton` and `FilterToggle` drew from their own entries, so an app loads less in total.
- **Showcase:**
  - The FilterToggle, Gauge and DeleteResource pages fold into Button, Meter and AlertDialog, which already had a typed-confirmation example.
  - The home grid shows `Status` in the gauge's cell and keeps 24 cells.
  - Texts in German and Chinese. 115 pages.
- **Tests:**
  - `button/toggle.test.tsx` covers state and reporting, disabled, a plain button without `aria-pressed`, and a cancelled click.
  - `meter/gauge.test.tsx` is the gauge test, ported.
  - The parameter tests open the panel from a trigger.

156 documented components after this step.

## Testing

- The library builds: registry and bundle budgets.
- The console, docs and showcase typecheck, and the showcase generates every page translated.
- Library tests: 1542 passed. Console tests: 2318 passed.
- Lint, format and knip pass.

author: jrunic
body:
## O que muda para quem opera

- `mensagens --remetente`, `identificar` e os demais filtros por remetente alcançam o celular brasileiro pelas duas formas (com e sem o 9). O Acervo passa a aprender o par das duas formas na gravação (recepção ao vivo, importação, metadados de coletiva, citação) e no estoque, por `malote identidade aprender-formas-do-celular` (ensaio por padrão; Operação `por-efeito` com `desfazer`).
- O ouvinte envia ao endereço que o Acervo guarda; o pedido de Envio avisa o endereço usado ou que o Acervo não conhece o número (`enderecoUsado`, `enderecoDesconhecido`). O número desconhecido sai como foi pedido.
- `identificar` diz a forma pedida e a gravada quando diferem.

## Muda a forma do Acervo (v30 para v31)

Um índice por fonte e canônico na tabela de correspondências. A migração roda sozinha na primeira abertura, é idempotente e não perde linha, e nenhum passo de migração anterior foi alterado: é precaução, não bloqueio, e a volta é a cópia consistente que se tira antes. O Acervo v31 não abre no código v0.45.0. Onde a atualização automática segue `production`, a release se aplica sozinha na primeira passada; onde a atualização é manual, ela se faz com cópia antes.

## Medido antes

Suíte de 2.420 testes sem falha; custo recorrente por Mensagem abaixo de 0,1 ms (a primeira Mensagem de um celular nunca visto custa até cerca de 0,3 ms a mais, medido de 0,02 a 0,27 ms, uma vez por número); 19 mutantes do estoque e 25 dos pontos de Envio e de `identificar` mortos.

## O que não entra

O aprendizado do estoque dos Acervos existentes não roda sozinho: é um comando do operador, depois da atualização.

author: turnisan-code
body:
Claude connector, part 1 of 4. Stacked on the last-sweep PR (#66).

## What changes
This part lays the groundwork for connecting Claude to Mado. Nothing new is visible in the app yet.

- **Database** (migration `20261105_mcp.sql`). It adds:
  - Claude connections, one-time sign-in codes and tokens. Tokens are stored only as hashes.
  - Actions that Claude prepared and that are waiting for your approval.
  - A log of Claude's requests, kept for 90 days.

  Only you can read these, and only after the second factor. The token tables are not readable from the browser at all.
- **Approval rules in the database.** SQL decides from your settings whether an action needs approval in Mado or can be confirmed in Claude:
  - A Claude session can never change those settings (MI040) and can never approve an action itself (MI041).
  - Approving in Mado needs an authenticator code entered in the last 5 minutes (MI043), unless you switch the code off in Account.
  - Revoking a connection stops anything it prepared from being approved; it can only be rejected.
- **History entries written from a Claude connection are marked as Claude's.** The database sets the mark from the connection, so it cannot be faked or changed later.
- **Shared code for the next parts:**
  - encryption helpers
  - the tool and action registries
  - one error mapper, so Claude only ever gets a plain English message and a code, never database text
- **Status changes and deletions moved into shared code** (`src/lib/services/lifecycle.ts`). The status menu, draft deletion, deleting a client and deleting a project call it from the browser. Bulk delete calls it on the server, and Claude uses it too, so the app and Claude follow exactly the same rules. The app behaves as before: checks against the old code show identical queries and results for every success and error case.
- **New dependency:** `@modelcontextprotocol/server` 2.3.1, pinned exactly.

Two reviews (security and product) found one gap: a Claude session could insert or delete the settings row and so get around the approval rules. That is fixed and verified, together with all the smaller findings.

## Before merging
- The SQL for this part (`supabase/migrations/20261105_mcp.sql`) is changed again in part 4. Run it once, from part 4's branch, as part 4 describes.
- After merging, run `npm install` once in the main checkout. The new package was copied into the shared node_modules by hand, and this lets npm install and record it properly.

body:
Cherry-pick of https://github.com/zama-ai/fhevm/pull/4783 (d5380496f) onto `feature/solana`, unchanged.

## Why

`js-sdk-dod` fails on `feature/solana` with three EVM decrypt tests that time out at 120 s (`clientDecrypt.extraDataV0` and `clientDecrypt.stalePermitMigration`, viem). The cause is on main:

- https://github.com/zama-ai/fhevm/pull/4724 (merged 2 Nov 15:21 UTC) made the kms-connector refuse `extraData` v0. A v0 permit is dropped and the relayer answers 202 until the client gives up.
- https://github.com/zama-ai/fhevm/pull/4783 (merged 4 Nov 21:35 UTC) made the SDK refuse v0 up front with `InvalidSignedPermitError` and changed those tests to expect it.

The last main sync was based on main at b817e7d88 (2 Nov 18:12 UTC). It took 4724 but not 4783, so `feature/solana` runs the old tests against a connector that drops v0. This PR brings 4783 in; the remaining main commits come with the next sync.

## Solana

No change for Solana users. The Solana permit path has its own routing check and already refuses any routing version other than the current one (`sdk/js-sdk/src/solana/permit/validate.ts:209`). 4783 only touches the EVM permit path and tests.

## Verification

- The cherry-pick applied with no conflicts. None of its 31 files changed on `feature/solana` since the sync.
- In `sdk/js-sdk`, after `npm run --prefix solana/clients/zama-host setup` (as CI does): `npm run lint` passes, `npm run build:tests` passes, and `vitest run --config src/vitest.config.ts` passes 82 files and 1,698 tests.

author: schmoelder
body:
The probe behind #473 found its defects exactly where no test looked, so this adds the missing tests rather than more fixes. Every difference metric is now checked for returning as many finite scores as it declares, `bad_metrics` of the same length, a score of zero against its own reference, and unchanged scores inside a `Comparator`. On the code before #473, this fails for L1, L2 and both breakthrough metrics. Base-class keywords are checked against applying the same operation to both traces, and every metric must return finite scores or a clear error for a simulation in which nothing elutes. Hand-computed values on two components now cover SSE, RMSE, NRMSE and the area metrics. Analytic values for shifted and rescaled Gaussian peaks check SSE, RMSE, NRMSE and the area metrics on a smooth profile. A pure translation tests the keywords of `Shape` and `ShapeFront`, where the `smooth` cases fail before #473. Resampling and normalization of `SolutionIO`, which every metric relies on, replace two empty placeholder tests.

The module docstring of `tests/comparison/test_metric_contracts.py` now states what every metric must guarantee, and which of those requirements are still untested, so the remaining gaps are visible next to the tests that will close them.

author: lpicci96
body:
## Why Run Analysis is failing

Every scheduled run since 11 May has failed in `extract_raw_data` with `InvalidDCInstanceError`, before any data is fetched. The cause is `from bblocks import places`: when it's imported, `bblocks-places` creates a Data Commons client for `datacommons.one.org` and checks it with a live request. That instance has been retired, and the package needs it to turn country names into codes, so it can't be kept. `bblocks-places` is deprecated, and [`resolvekit`](https://pypi.org/project/resolvekit/) is its replacement. (The 4 May run failed for a different reason: the World Bank download hit the 30-minute timeout. The last successful run was 27 April.)

This is the same fix as ONEcampaign/debt_overview#9, plus the same DSA fallback being added to debt_overview.

## Changes

**Replace `bblocks-places` with `resolvekit`**, which works offline from data shipped in the package:
- `names_to_iso3()` uses a countries-only resolver for IDS debtor names, DSA country names and WEO ISO3 codes, so a name like "Micronesia" can't match a same-named region. A small crosswalk covers two IMF spellings in the DSA list that `resolvekit` doesn't match ("Lao P.D.R.", "Somalia, Fed. Rep.").
- `african_iso3_codes()` (Africa as defined by the UN's M.49 regions) and `high_income_iso3_codes()` (the World Bank high income group) replace the `region`, `income_level` and `filter_african_countries` lookups. They're used for the "Africa (excluding high income)" aggregate, the list of African debtors, the Africa medians in charts 2 and 6, and the DSA key stats.
- `bblocks-places` stays installed as a dependency of `bblocks-data-importers`, which never imports it.
- The `uv.lock` diff is large because uv moved the lockfile to format revision 3, which adds `upload-time` fields. The only package changes are four additions: `resolvekit`, `rapidfuzz`, `symspellpy` and `pooch`. No existing versions changed.

**Keep a saved copy of the IMF DSA list as a fallback.** The IMF currently blocks scripted downloads of the DSA list PDF (ONEcampaign/bblocks_data_importers#102). The importer's `get_dsa()` also fails on the PDF's current layout, which dropped the "joint with World Bank" and "latest DSA discussed" columns and uses "…" where no assessment applies.
- `extract_raw_data` now reads the PDF with this repo's own `parse_dsa_pdf()` and saves it to `raw_data/imf_dsa.csv`, which is tracked in git.
- If the download fails, it logs a warning, adds a warning on the GitHub Actions run summary, and keeps the saved copy. With no saved copy, it still fails.
- `scripts/update_dsa.py` updates the saved copy from a PDF downloaded by hand: `uv run python -m scripts.update_dsa path/to/DSAlist.pdf`. The README explains this.
- The saved copy is the IMF list as of 30 September 2026, saved by hand from a browser.

**Move to 2025.** The new IDS edition has 2025 debt stocks and debt service for every African debtor, so `LATEST_YEAR` is now 2025. That changes:
- The chart 3 treemap is now a 2025 snapshot (1,669 rows, no missing values).
- Debt service in charts 5 and 6 and key stat chart 1 now runs to 2031 (`LATEST_YEAR` + 6). 2025 is an actual figure, and 2026 onwards are estimates.
- The key stats for debt service, the creditor shares and `latest_year` now use 2025. The stats for debt stocks, debt to GDP and China already used the latest year in the data, which is now 2025.
- Sources without 2025 data keep their years:
  - **Health spending:** GHED stays capped at 2023, because it has 2024 data for only 7 countries.
  - **Education spending:** UNESCO data has 2025 for 16 African countries, and the code already uses each country's latest year.
  - **The "debt service vs health/education" counts** still use 2021 onwards.

**Upgrade imf-reader to 2.3.0.** `bblocks-data-importers` 0.5.0 caps `imf-reader` below 2.0. The capped 1.4.1 labels the IMF's live WEO dataset as "October 2025", although it actually holds the October 2026 edition. 2.3.0 identifies the release correctly, so a `[tool.uv]` override in `pyproject.toml` installs it anyway.
- **No data change:** the outputs already used the October 2026 edition, so the numbers don't change.
- **WEO reads:** both the bblocks WEO importer and pydeflate now report `("October", 2026)`.
- **Same data:** `gdp.csv` and `gov_expenditure.csv` are byte-identical, and pydeflate's re-downloaded IMF data matches on all 10,101 rows.
- **No output diff:** the rebuilt outputs are identical.
- **Lock changes:**
  - `imf-reader` 1.4.1 → 2.3.0.
  - `readerkit`, `pyrate-limiter` and `requests-ratelimiter` added.
  - `filelock` 3.20.3 → 4.2.9, which `readerkit` needs.
  - `pre-commit` (a dev dependency) pulls in `virtualenv`, which capped `filelock` below 4. So `virtualenv` moves 20.36.1 → 21.15.5, bringing `packaging` 26.0 → 26.3, `distlib` 0.4.0 → 0.4.4 and a new `python-discovery`.

**Outputs regenerated locally**, so merging updates the page without another workflow run.

## Testing

I ran the full pipeline locally (`extract_raw_data`, then `analysis`) and compared the results with the outputs from the last successful run (27 April). The DSA step fell back to the saved copy with the warning, as intended.

Country names and groups:
- **IDS debtors:** all 120 countries in the new IDS data resolve to the World Bank's own code, and none of the 14 aggregates resolves to a country.
- **Old outputs:** all 50 name-to-code pairs in the 27 April outputs map to the same code. The 3 aggregate names stay unresolved.
- **Africa:** the African IDS debtors are the same 50 countries under `resolvekit` and the `bblocks-places` table. The "Africa (excluding high income)" aggregate in the new raw data equals the sum over the old membership for every row (4,599 debt stock rows and 8,552 debt service rows).
- **High income:** Guyana is the only high-income IDS debtor under both libraries, so the "excluding high income" filter removes no African country.
- **DSA list:** all 68 DSA names resolve. 39 of them are African under both libraries.
- **WEO GDP:** all 195 WEO country codes resolve to themselves, including all 54 African countries.

Outputs (I checked these before the move to 2025, so the mapping change could be seen on its own):
- **No names gained or lost:** no output loses or gains a debtor, and no category changes. The one new creditor is Benin, which appears as a creditor in chart 5's new data.
- **Rows:** row counts change only because of the data and the move to 2025:
  - 2025 is added to charts 1, 2, 4 and 6, and to key stat charts 2 and 3.
  - Charts 5 and 6 and key stat chart 1 now run to 2031.
  - Chart 3 is the 2025 snapshot.
- **Values that moved more than 1% are data updates, not mapping changes:**
  - In chart 1, 320 of the 333 moved rows are individual countries, whose figures come straight from IDS.
  - In chart 6, only debt service moved; health and education spending are unchanged.
- `ruff format --check` (CI) and `ruff check` pass.

## Key stats

| Key stat | main (2024) | 2024, revised data | This PR (2025) |
|---|---|---|---|
| African countries in debt distress or at high risk | 21 | | 20 |
| Share of all such countries | 66% | | 62% |
| Debt stocks, Africa (excl. high income) | US$707.9bn | US$708.9bn | US$791.7bn |
| Debt service, Africa (excl. high income) | US$84.4bn | US$84.7bn | US$80.8bn |
| Median debt to GDP | 26.6% | 26.8% | 28.5% |
| Bilateral / multilateral / private share of debt | 21% / 37% / 42% | 21% / 38% / 41% | 20% / 38% / 43% |
| China bilateral / private share | 9% / 3% | 9% / 3% | 8% / 2% |
| Countries where debt service > health spending | 28 | 27 | 27 |
| Countries where debt service > education spending | 10 | 11 | 12 |
| `latest_year` | 2024 | | 2025 |

- **DSA stats:** these come from the new IMF list (30 September 2026). Both libraries give the same Africa count on it, so the change isn't from the mapping.
- **Health count:** this mostly compares 2023, because health spending stops there.
- **Education count:** it rises to

author: lucienkerl
body:
## What

Makes the slot rebuild ("Umbau") part of the refill tour simpler for refillers, on iOS, web and Android.

**Packing**
- There is one line per machine and product. It holds the refill and the units for that machine's slot rebuilds under one tick ("in the box") and one amount, e.g. "3 refill + ⇄ 5 rebuild · slot 57". Packing less takes units off the refill first.
- Ticked lines claim warehouse stock in the order they were ticked. A later tick never takes units away from a line that is already in the box.
- The screen shows a box counter, how many machines are ready, and a confirmation that lists the lines not in the box before the tour starts.
- The change note is now an info-only banner ("Rebuild 3 slots · 12, 14, 23") plus the spirals to take along. The per-slot accept checkbox is gone: every planned slot is packed, and skipping happens at the machine.

**At the machine**
- iOS shows one slot at a time.
- A new price must be confirmed before a slot can be marked done, the same way the age setting already is.
- The filled amount is capped by the units taken out of the machine's other changed slots plus the units packed.
- When a source slot is skipped, the slot it would have supplied explains why it gets fewer units.
- A change note withdrawn during the tour rebuilds nothing at that machine. The packed units become leftovers, and the refiller is told if slots were already marked done.

**Review**
- An empty slot no longer holds up the review step. It starts as "stays unassigned", and it can still be assigned.

## Testing

- Web: 621 vitest tests pass. The rebuild tests were rewritten and now cover tick order, price confirmation, the fill cap, skipped source slots and a withdrawn change note.
- Android: new `SlotChangeTest` cases cover the same rules. The Android Check workflow builds the app and runs these tests; its result is not in yet.
- iOS: tested end to end on the test system and in the simulator.

author: rynaro
body:
## Summary

ACI-S34 adds two commands that link ADR text to exact source code and flag code changes that need a rationale review:

```
atlas-aci rationale-map   --mapping M --repo R --graph-root G --output OVERLAY.json
atlas-aci rationale-drift --mapping M (--repo R | --before-repo B --after-repo A) \
  --before-graph-root GB --after-graph-root GA --output DRIFT.json
```

- **Input:** an operator mapping (`atlas-rationale-mapping.v1`) links ADR byte spans to exact source symbol or file identities in a stated snapshot.
- **`rationale-map`** resolves the mapping into a standalone `atlas-rationale-overlay.v1`.
- **`rationale-drift`** compares two snapshots through S19's symbol diff into a standalone `atlas-rationale-drift.v1`.
- Both outputs are content-addressed and written only to `--output`. ADRs, source, graphs and the existing comment-based `rationale` facts are never modified.
- The MCP surface is unchanged (tools JSON sha256 `94f9567a…`, 1,631,472 bytes).
- A review signal is an observation that the linked rationale deserves a look. It is not a verdict that a decision was followed or invalidated.

**Mapping resolution**
- ADR bytes are read only from the leased snapshot, never the live checkout. The document sha256, span byte range and span sha256 must match the mapping.
- Targets resolve by exact entity id, and their path, kind and name must equal the indexed row. There is no name search, and S19 rename candidates are never rebound.
- File targets are supported through each side's recorded file digest.
- Anything missing or mismatched becomes an `unresolved_mapping` record with a closed reason, not an error.

**Drift signals**
- `rationale_review_needed`: the target's signature, body or file content changed while the ADR document is byte-identical on both sides.
- No finding when:
  - the target is unchanged, confirmed present on both sides;
  - only formatting or location changed;
  - the ADR document itself was edited (this state is recorded per mapping).
- `unknown_target_history`, when S19 cannot establish the target's history:
  - an S19 `unknown` record, or a partially extracted path;
  - a renumbered same-name sibling (`sibling_ordinal_shift`). S19 would otherwise compare the survivor under its sibling's old identity;
  - a rejected comparison. The drift document is still returned, with every mapping marked.
- A target removed in the after snapshot stays `unresolved_mapping` (`target_removed`).
- Read-only leases are held on both sides and checked against the generations S19 compared.

**Footprint**
- New source files: `rationale/{__init__,adr_mapping,drift}.py`. `__main__.py` gains the two commands, imported lazily.
- No prior test, gated path or dependency changes.
- Docs: `docs/rationale-drift.md`, plus a CHANGELOG bullet (third, after the pinned S30 and S33 bullets) and a README row.

**Limitations**
- Any edit to an ADR document suppresses the signal for its mappings.
- A definition recreated under an identical id with no sibling change reads as an edit.
- A class target is not flagged for edits to its member methods.
- Replay is byte-identical only at the same checkout path.

## Verification

- **Tests:** 46 S34 tests. I reran them with the S14, S27, S28, S30 and S33 layout and isolation tests (135 passed). The regression set passed 550, including every CHANGELOG and README pin.
- **CI lint and types:** the exact CI ruff/format/mypy chain is clean.
- **Full suite:** 2331 passed, 10 skipped, 1 failed. The failure is the same `test_s01_contract::test_call_deadline_after_initialization` that fails on the base. The known-flaky `test_s08_integration::test_nonregular_pack_does_not_block_acquisition` was deselected.
- **Python 3.14:** the S34 tests pass (46) in a throwaway `python:3.14` container.
- **Scope:** protected paths are byte-unchanged against `0a70041`, and the scope drift check is clean.
- **Production image:** `atlas-aci:s34`, with no network and read-only mounts. 47 checks passed:
  - map and drift outputs are byte-identical across runs (22 mappings);
  - the body-changed mapping raises `rationale_review_needed`; the unchanged and edited-document controls do not;
  - the removed target gives `target_removed` and the renumbered sibling gives `sibling_ordinal_shift`;
  - a configuration-mismatched pair exits 0 with every mapping `unknown_target_history`;
  - a snapshot mismatch exits 1 with empty stdout, and usage errors exit 2;
  - repository, `.git`, graph and mapping inventories are unchanged;
  - the tools JSON matches the pin.
- **Ramza receipt:** the re-entry and resume checks passed.

Closes #55

body:
## Stack

Position 12, after https://github.com/bitswell-hq/stellar-registry__perch/pull/63 (base `fm/rc7-s2`). M7 stage 3 under choice B (a fresh account Wasm; no account runs this code on storage written by earlier code). Out of scope: the controller rebuild (the next PR), the storage cuts, removing `stellar-accounts` from the manifests, and any deployment.

## Summary

The account decides a recovery completion with its own check, over its own record of the recovery rule. OZ's `do_check_auth` is no longer linked, and the account writes nothing to OZ's registry.

```text
__check_auth
  reserved names, freeze, scope generation gate        unchanged
  completion (one apply_doc on self, ids == [recovery])
    authorize_completion (auth.rs), in do_check_auth's order:
      ids.len() == contexts.len()                       else 3014
      each id is the recovery rule's, with its record   else 3000
      each context a call on self, rule unexpired       else 3002
      no payload signer                                 else 3016
      enforce(context, [], record.context_rule(), self) for each context and policy
  anything else
    rule set stored?                                    else RuleEvalRefused
    gate::authorize (rule-eval), authenticate          unchanged
```

- **The controller call is the same value.** The record's `ContextRule` (zero signers, `CallContract(self)`, name `recovery`, the controller under positional policy id 0, no last ledger) is the XDR OZ's registry gave the controller on stage 2. The controller is not changed: `perch_recovery.wasm` builds byte-identical (`daa55fac…`).
- **No OZ registry entry is written.** Stage 2 kept `ContextRuleData(recovery id)` and `PolicyData(0)` for `do_check_auth`; installing, moving or removing the recovery rule now touches only the account's records and calls the controller's `install`, as before.
- **The legacy branch is gone.** An account storing no admin rule set, which the constructor never leaves, authorizes nothing but a completion (`RuleEvalRefused`), and a completion never reads the set. `apply_scope`'s `NoRuleSet` refusal could only fire on such an account after an authorization it can no longer get, so it is removed (it was the last code of `PerchAccountError`, so no other code moves).
- **The contract spec's `SmartAccountError` is the account's own.** OZ's entry left the spec with `do_check_auth`. `auth::fail` now raises `perch_account_types::SmartAccountError` typed, which puts its entry in the spec: the five codes `__check_auth` refuses with (3000, 3002, 3003, 3014, 3016), each with OZ's name and doc.
- `check_auth` binds the payload digest only on the rule-eval path; a completion never needed it.
- `perch-smart-account` still declares `stellar-accounts`; none of its code uses it. Removing it from the manifests is a later step of the plan.

## Evidence

**Ran:**

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo test --locked --workspace` (skipping the two factory tests CI skips for a `stale` deployment), deployed testnet infra fetched by `scripts/fetch-infra-wasm.sh` | 663 passed, 0 failed, 39 ignored |
| Pinned suites: `recovery` 32, `recovery_installability` 8, `scoped_docs` 18, `gate` 6 (the completion-independence test, renamed `a_recovery_completion_is_left_to_the_controller`, still tampers every stored rule and completes) | all pass |
| `completion_differential.rs` (new; OZ is a dev-dependency only): one account holds the recovery rule both as its record and in OZ's registry (installed by OZ's `add_context_rule`, alone, under the same id); each check runs as a contract call on it against a recording controller. Grid: an accepted completion, signers present (delegated and external), a wrong id (the admin id, an unknown id), an expired rule (valid through its last ledger, refused after), a wrong context (another contract, a create-contract context), a second context (on the account, elsewhere, under the admin id), mismatched lengths both ways, a refusing controller, and mixed payloads that fix the check order | 8/8. Same verdict and error code everywhere; same `enforce` calls (context, signers, `ContextRule`, account), byte for byte, in the same order; the accepted call equals `enforce(context, [], oz::get_context_rule(id), account)` |
| Mutation: `authorize_completion` forced to refuse | `gate` −2, `recovery` −12, `recovery_installability` −2, `scoped_docs` −8, differential −7: the new path is exercised |
| Mutation: the signer check moved before the context checks (the prototype's order) | the differential's `the_checks_run_in_the_same_order` fails: a signer on an expired rule is 3016 instead of OZ's 3002 |
| `oz_differential.rs` (stage 2's, `#[ignore]`d) against stage 1's OZ-registry account (`stellar contract build` at `6d54308`, `0ec759fc…`), `PERCH_DIFF_CASES=128` | 3/3: generated document sequences (same outcomes, ids, views, events), generated authorizations through each account's real `__check_auth`, completion-shaped selections included (same verdicts and codes), and the recovery flow under enforcing authorization (same transcript) |
| `release_stack.rs --ignored --skip cap_sweep`, real proofs, on `build-stack.sh --builder contract` stacks of `fm/rc7-s2` and this branch | 26/26 on each. Of 264 metered rows, 261 cost fewer instructions and all 264 less memory; no row rises on any other limit. Completions: −0.2M to −0.7M instructions and two fewer footprint entries (OZ's rule and policy entries); one that installs the recovery rule again under a new id (a ZK rotation) has three fewer footprint entries and writes three fewer. Worst completion 41.4% of the instruction limit; worst row unchanged at 41.6% (the `Protected` reconfiguration that edits every rule). Footprint 16.0% → 15.3%, written entries 20.5% → 19.0%; memory 23.6%, write bytes 50.0%, events 20.5% unchanged. Every row within 75% |
| `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check`, `scripts/test-release-scripts.py` | clean; clean; 160 OK (1 skipped) |
| `stellar contract info interface`, base vs branch, the account | unchanged except `PerchAccountError::NoRuleSet` (63) removed, and `SmartAccountError` now the account's five-code entry instead of OZ's seventeen |

**Sizes and sha256** (`build-stack.sh --builder contract`, testnet passphrase):

| Wasm | Before (`fm/rc7-s2`) | After |

| perch-account | 109,908 `5c8de14f52623af14709c708c48903c2d6786a073e14ded0b3d9ad8024230894` | **102,319 (−7,589)** `82964aacfba03ba17de00a5abd646bba02377565b29ab9aa2fae3ffc92178080` |

| perch-doc-compiler, perch-interpreter, perch-spending-limit, both verifiers, perch-zk-adapter, perch-zk-pool | as before | identical |

The account's code is −6,426 bytes, its spec −992, its data −151, and its other sections −20. 28,753 bytes under the 131,072-byte limit. `docs/recovery/budgets.md` records the sizes and the release-stack rows.

**Read, not run:**
- The OZ fork at `42089fc`: `do_check_auth`, `get_validated_context_by_id`, `get_context_rule`, `get_persistent_entry`, for exactly what a completion checked, in what order, and what it handed `enforce`.

author: turnisan-code
body:
Claude connector, part 2 of 4. Stacked on part 1.

## What changes
After this part, Claude can connect to Mado and read your data.

### Connecting
- **You connect Claude with your Mado login plus a fresh authenticator code.**
  - The consent page shows which app is asking (Claude on the web, desktop and mobile, or Claude Code).
  - You can untick "Change drafts and records" (drafts, clients, projects, payments, time and expenses) or "Prepare irreversible actions". "Read" is always included.
- **Each connection gets its own Mado session at two-factor level, kept encrypted on the server.** Claude only holds its own token and never sees your Mado session. Every request runs under the same database rules as you do in the browser.
- **Lifetimes and limits:**
  - An access token lasts 1 hour.
  - A connection ends after 30 days unused, and after 90 days at the latest.
  - Requests are limited to 120 a minute and 3000 a day.
- **Ways a connection ends:**
  - A sign-in code used twice ends it.
  - A refresh token used twice also ends it, with a 10-second allowance for two Claude windows refreshing at the same moment.
  - Changing your password disconnects Claude on its next request.
- `/api/mcp` is the address Claude talks to. It works with both MCP protocol versions in use. The discovery documents under `/.well-known/` let Claude find the sign-in by itself.

### Reading: 12 tools
- `get_context`: your business, numbering and defaults, plus this connection's permissions and approval rules.
- `search_documents`, `get_document`
- `list_clients`, `get_client`, `get_client_statement`
- `list_catalogue`
- `list_projects`, `get_project`
- `get_dashboard`, `get_vat_report`, `list_recurring`

The lists, dashboard, reports and client statement now use these same queries, so Claude sees exactly the figures you see. A check on 3000 random documents shows the statuses are identical. Long lists are paged, and results are capped at 60,000 characters.

### Account
- **Connected apps:** each connection with its permissions, last use and recent requests, and Revoke.
- **Per kind of action, you choose "Approve in Mado" (the default) or "Confirm in Claude".**
- **You can also switch off the authenticator code for approving in Mado.** It is on by default and recommended.
- Loosening a rule, including switching the code off, asks for an authenticator code. Tightening one does not.
- **Signing out in the sidebar now ends only this device's session.** The new **Sign out everywhere** ends every session and disconnects Claude.

Two reviews (security and product) said ship. Their 14 smaller findings are all fixed. Among them:
- a refused refresh no longer ends the connection
- a temporary rate limit at Supabase no longer disconnects Claude
- the consent page can only be approved once

## Before merging
- Needs the SQL and the Supabase dashboard settings that part 4 describes.
- In Vercel (Production), add `MCP_SECRET`. Generate it with `openssl rand -base64 48`. Also check that `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` is exactly `https://mado-invoice.turnovsky.pro`, with no trailing slash.
- Quick check after deploying:
  - `curl -i https://mado-invoice.turnovsky.pro/api/mcp -X POST` should answer 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate` header.
  - `curl https://mado-invoice.turnovsky.pro/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/api/mcp` should return JSON.

## O que muda

Três testes de isolamento do Fisio passavam sem provar que a requisição chegou ao código (auditoria Fisio d14, média). Cada negativo ganha uma âncora positiva, e onde dava, um caso que isola o filtro por empresa.

|---|---|---|
| `FisioPreAnamneseTest` UC-FPP-55 | 2º assert (`business_id=99 AND patient_id=<paciente da 98>`) era tautológico depois do 1º; não havia linha da 99 | linha com `business_id=99` para o mesmo paciente (o unique é empresa+paciente) **não conta como respondida**: o Hoje segue oferecendo; a 98 grava `dor=6`, a da 99 fica `dor=1`, e só então o Hoje esconde |

body:
## O que muda

- **Reproduzir / Pausar** na linha do tempo. Avança um mês por vez e para em dezembro. Só roda quando o usuário aciona.
- **Troca suave dos pontos.** Ao mudar o filtro de data, o mapa esmaece, recebe as novas obras e reaparece. É uma transição do conjunto inteiro, não de cada ponto: os agrupamentos e o calor usam os mesmos dados, então animar ponto a ponto exigiria reescrever essas camadas.
- **Voo até a obra.** Ao escolher uma obra com um único trecho, a câmera voa até ela com subida e descida. Trecho longo continua sendo enquadrado.

author: mamoralesiob
body:
## PR description

On EVM v2, CALLDATALOAD sliced the call data through Tuweni's `Bytes`, copied the slice into a new `MutableBytes32` and decoded that onto the stack: two allocations on every load.

`MessageFrame` now keeps the input data as a byte array, materialised on the first load (`inputDataArrayV2()`), and CALLDATALOAD reads the four longs of the word through a big-endian `VarHandle` view of it. A word that runs past the end of the call data is assembled byte by byte, with the missing bytes read as zero. EVM v1 is unchanged.

Adds tests for words that cross the end of the call data, call data shorter than a word, call data that is a slice of larger bytes and repeated loads on one frame, and a JMH benchmark (`CallDataLoadOperationBenchmarkV2`):

|         | ns/op          | B/op |
|---------|----------------|------|
| main    | 15.999 ± 0.258 | 48   |
| this PR | 13.691 ± 0.333 | ≈ 0  |
