- **Workout editor** (`ui/editor`): `WM-1`, `WM-2`, `WM-4` to `WM-7`, `WM-10`, specification §4.2.
  - The workout's name and three defaults, then one card per round, with its exercises as a table.
  - An own value left empty is linked to its default, and shows it as a dimmed placeholder; a "Use default" button clears an own value. Unused rests are marked "Not used" but stay editable.
  - Rounds and exercises can be added, moved up and down, duplicated and removed. The total updates with every edit.
  - Validation messages show at their fields from the first Save attempt. Cancel, the back arrow and system Back ask before discarding changes.
  - The form model (`WorkoutForm`) and the error mapping are plain Kotlin, tested on the JVM. The ViewModel holds its state in Compose snapshot state, so text fields update synchronously.
- **Settings** (`ui/settings`): the voice cues switch, `TTS-9`. Turning it on also starts preparing the audio, as P5 suggested.
- **Shared files:**
  - `formatTotalDuration()` in `ui/common`, for P7's completed screen too;
  - `AppNavHost`: the edit callback, and double-tap guards on callbacks that take an ID;
  - `MainActivity` gets `windowSoftInputMode="adjustResize"`, chosen from measurements on the tablet (T1, SPEC §4.3.6);
  - dependencies: `material-icons-core` (1.7.8, from the Compose BOM) is new; `lifecycle-viewmodel-compose` is now declared;
  - `NavigationSmokeTest` starts a seeded workout instead of the removed "Run sample" button.
- **Readability and text:** touch targets of at least 48 dp, and 56 dp for the main actions (`NF-6`). All text is in `strings_list.xml`, `strings_editor.xml` and `strings_settings.xml` (`NF-9`).

## Checks

- `./gradlew build`: passes. 411 unit tests (166 in `:app`, 93 of them new, and 245 in `:core`), 0 failures. Lint, ktlint and the no-INTERNET check are clean.
- `connectedDebugAndroidTest` on the tablet: 51 tests, 0 failures, 3 skipped (P3's manual-only `PersistenceCheck`). New: `WorkoutListScreenTest` (8), `WorkoutEditorScreenTest` (13), `SettingsScreenTest` (4). The editor test creates the §4.4 example by typing it in.
- Manual checks on the tablet (SPEC §6): all pass. A workout created in the UI and the voice setting both survive a force-stop. The app's log shows no crash and no storage warning.
- Merged debug and release manifests: the same permissions and components as `main`. `:core` is unchanged.

## Decisions to review

- **SPEC v0.4 (Q9), the editor's fields:** own-value fields have no floating label. A label would hide the default placeholder until the field has focus. So a round's exercises are a table under column headers, and the "Not used" texts are shorter ("Not used: last exercise").
- **Keyboard (SPEC v0.3):** SwiftKey isn't full screen in landscape, but its letter keyboard is 372 dp tall, which leaves 204 dp above it. Only `adjustResize` keeps the top bar on screen.
- **The icon library:** `material-icons-core` is an AndroidX library, so no third-party asset licence is involved. Google no longer adds icons to it, but every icon P6 needs is there.
- **Smaller decisions,** all in HANDOVER.md:
  - the settings factory prepares the audio on `Dispatchers.Default`, as `MainActivity` does;
  - the editor ignores edits while a save runs;
  - the touch-target helper checks the touch bounds of nodes fully on screen, because icon buttons lay out at 40 dp and take touches over 48 dp.

## Left for the reviewer

- [x] Manual checks 1–13 in SPEC §6 on the tablet: done, all pass.

## Pending wiring

- **P7, the runner:**
  - the list's Start opens `RunnerRoute(workoutId)`;
  - the runner must validate the workout before building a timeline (P3 Q2), and decide what to show for an invalid or missing one;
  - `formatTotalDuration()` is there for the completed screen;
  - `PlaceholderScreen` is still used by the runner and completed placeholders;
  - `NavigationSmokeTest`'s two runner tests click the placeholder's Finish button. P7 updates them.
- **P8:** the end-to-end test (create, run, complete), and checking `WM-8` through the UI during acceptance.

body:
## Summary

#1224 (10f670b) made a second Log tap a no-op on the Add form. Quick add's Log and the medication log's Log a dose Save had the same double-write, and neither was guarded.

- `QuickAddViewModel`: `hasSaved` (published, private set). `save()` returns early once set; it's set only after a successful write, so a failed save doesn't lock the draft. `QuickAddView` disables the Log capsule and dims it on `hasSaved`.
- `MedicationLogView` `LogDoseSheet`: a `@State saving`, set before `logDose` and kept after success through the dismissal, reset on error, with `.disabled(saving)` on Save. The same approach as `LogOnOtherDaysSheet`. The view model's `logDose` isn't guarded, because that model lives across the whole medication log and a model-level guard would block a legitimate second dose.

Closes #1313

## Testing

- `QuickAddTests`: `testSavingTwiceOnOneDraftWritesOneEntry` and `testAFailedQuickAddDoesNotLockTheDraft`, mirroring `AddIntakeDoubleSaveTests`
- No automated test for the dose sheet: `LogDoseSheet` is a private view and the guard is view `@State`. A seam for it would mean reshaping more of `MedicationLogView.swift`, which open PR #1226 and #1308 also edit, so it's left out on purpose.

author: perusonao
body:
## 概要
Issue #764 の修正です。Owner 判断（PR #759 comment 6663668627、案1）に基づき、別 Issue・別 PR として最小限の修正を行いました。詳細は `docs/reports/TETO_WEBKIT-360-COOKING-OVERFLOW_Result.md` にあります。

**HOLD / Draft です。** すべての Gate が通っても、merge は別途 Owner の判断を待ちます。Production の更新や共有 Preview の更新はしていません。

## 原因（CI の WebKit で特定）
- WebKit 360×800 では、ソーストレイ 3 列目のチップ（「ジェノベーゼソース」「カレーケチャップ」）の幅が 117px になり、108px の `1fr` 列からはみ出していました。
  - チップ名は `nowrap` で、WebKit では 101px あります（Chromium では 86px）。
  - `1fr` は `minmax(auto, 1fr)` のため、列がチップの最小幅まで広がります。その結果、`.game-screen--cooking` の `scrollWidth` が 386px（画面幅 360px）になっていました。
- 通常のトマトソースの流れでも同じく失敗するので、Batch 18 より前からある問題です。

## 修正（`src/App.css` に 17 行追加。他の行は main と同じ）
```css
@media (max-width: 389px) {
  .prepare-dock .ingredient-chip { padding-left: 3px; padding-right: 3px; }
  .prepare-dock .ingredient-chip__name { font-size: 10px; }
}
```
- 390×844 では何も変わりません。名前はどの幅でも全文表示され、省略しません。
- 採用しなかった案:
  - 案A（列を均等幅にして長い名前を省略）: 「フロマージュブランソース」が 390 でも省略されるため。
  - 案C（列幅を中身に合わせる）: すべてのトレイで列幅が不均等になるため。

## 検査（削除・緩和なし）
- `e2e/cooking-screen-sideways.spec.ts`（新規）: 生地 → ソース → チーズ → 具材 → 焼成の各工程で、トレイの全ページについて調理画面が横にスクロールしないことを assert します。
- ソースは、トマト・カレーケチャップ・フロマージュブランの 3 通り、360×800 と 390×844 の両方で確認します。

## Gate
| HEAD | CI | Codex |
|---|---|---|
| `f938de2`（spec のみ・修正前） | WebKit 360×800 で失敗（修正前の証拠） | — |
| `7ce5937`（修正） | **11/11 success** | 指摘 0 件 |
| `1e332c1`（Result Report と画像の追加、docs のみ） | 確認中 | 依頼済み |

## Human Verification
- 画像: `docs/reports/screenshots/webkit-360-cooking-overflow/`
  - 360×800 の修正前と修正後。WebKit で測った字幅を Chromium で再現して撮影しました。
  - 390×844 の修正前と修正後（見た目は同一）。
- 動画（リポジトリには含めず、セッション内で直接提出）:
  - 390×844: 修正後の調理一巡を 2 本（トマト、カレーケチャップ）。
  - 360×800: 修正前と修正後を並べた比較を 2 本。
- iPhone Safari での実機確認は Owner が行います。

## 衝突
`src/App.css`（HOT）の変更箇所は、#761（`.ingredient-glyph--shiso-leaf`）と #468（`.pizza-cheese--mozzarella`）のどちらとも重なりません。

Refs #764 #759

body:
Offline maps for the phones, and the English translation of the web UI. Pairs with zipclaude/activitytrack#155 (the app side): **merge this one first**, the app expects `mapsRev` in `sync/head` and the `maps` endpoints.

## Offline maps (docs/OFFLINE-MAPS.md)
- New **Mappe** page for administrators: a switch that offers the maps to the phones, the areas (centre, radius 5-250 km, zoom 8-12) with a live estimate of tiles and MB, 23 ready-made areas, progress and state of each, update and delete.
- `maps/pmtiles.py`, standard library only (Debian packages suffice): reads the Protomaps basemap by **HTTP range requests** (`[maps] source`, default the newest daily build), cuts the area, drops the heavy layers (`landuse`, `pois`, `buildings`, `natural`, `landcover`: ~85 % of the bytes) and writes a small PMTiles file. 100 km around Trento to z10: 2.3 MB instead of 12.9 MB.
- Preparation runs in a process of its own (`manage.py build_maps`), one at a time; the previous good file is replaced only when the new one passes the size check. `build_maps --older-than N` is for a timer.
- Phone API: `sync/head` carries `mapsRev`; `GET maps` lists the maps; `GET maps/<id>` serves a file through the same offload as the attachments. Nothing is offered unless the organisation turns it on. The wire schema does not change (docs/SYNC.md, "Maps").

## English translation
- The UI was Italian only. `locale/en` has the complete catalog (482 messages, British English, the app's terms) and its compilation `django.mo`, committed so that the package, a tarball and a clone need no `msgfmt`; a test fails if it is not the `.po` compiled.
- A **Language** card in Preferences (Italiano / English; a cookie, without one the browser's language is followed).
- Fixes `<html lang>`, which was always `it` (the i18n context processor was missing).

## Tests
- 211 tests (45 for the maps, 13 for the translation), on Django 4.2 and 5.2; `makemigrations --check` is clean.
- Run by hand against a real phone: pairing, download of a 2.3 MB map with its SHA-256, removal when the server stops offering it, download again.

Reviewing by commit is easier: the maps first, then the translation.

author: hipareshpatel
body:
## What

`CARD_PRINTED_LEVELS` (off): fixes from release check 42087566177 and from the blind check of the 90 figures it keeps.

- **A share's base.** A share needs "of" or "share of/in/to" before its base, or "to" with only article or size words ("% to net sales"). A growth's "to" ("rose 127% to ₹500 Cr revenue") is not a share.
- **A range's first end** stands only where the card states the range itself, and the second end must carry the same unit. Five of the 87 readable kept figures were a range's end on its own (SONACOMS 23% from "23 to 25%"), and this fix covers the three that were first ends.
- **Release check `printed_levels`** saves the filing text round each kept figure. It looks for the figure with its own unit first; a bare-number match is marked "(bare)", so a date like "27 May" is not shown for 27%.
- **Blind check of the 90 kept figures:**
  - 71 true, 9 wrong meaning, 7 not printed, 3 unreadable. That is 82% of the readable ones, not good enough to switch on.
  - All 36 vote shares were true.
  - Evidence: `docs/audit/rc/printed-levels-2026-11-05/`.

Next: re-run the release check, then read the text round the 7 computed figures and the 2 range last ends.

author: sideshowbarker
body:
A maintainer adds the `benchmark` label to a PR, or dispatches this workflow with the PR’s number. Then the web-benchmarks runners measure the PR’s head against its merge-base with `bench_pr.py` (from the web-benchmarks repo), and the result goes at the end of the PR’s description, where a later run replaces it in place. A label run removes the label when it finishes, so adding it again asks for a new run. The same workflow, dispatched with no PR, runs `bench_pr.py --calibrate` to record each runner’s noise floor.

Every run builds both arms from scratch in its own workspace, and saves nothing to the Actions cache. The one thing that outlives a run is each runner’s calibration record, a few hundred bytes, which a calibration run uploads as an artifact for later runs to download.

Since the runners are self-hosted, both triggers run master’s copy of the workflow, and the jobs that build and run the PR’s code get a read-only token and no secrets. A label run measures the head the PR had when the label went on.

body:
## What and why

This is the third PR for #22 (decision `5-screens.s18`). It rebuilds Templates (A6) and the template detail (A7) to their frames. A draft is now the Sections / Review / Publish wizard, which covers section order and each section's required or optional switch. Pages stay full width (`2-layout-and-navigation.s9`).

- **A6 Templates:**
  - "Templates" and "Reusable document skeletons.".
  - The table: ID (mono code), Name, Category, Versions and Latest ("v3 · draft"), with a Retired badge where it applies.
  - "+ New template" opens the create dialog (D25): name and owning top-level category. `/templates/new` keeps the same fields as a page.
- **A7 template detail:**
  - The eyebrow "Templates", the name (600 26 px), the version line in mono 13 px ("v2 active · v3 draft"), and "Discard draft" (34 px) behind its confirm (D30).
  - The three-step stepper "1 Sections | 2 Review | 3 Publish". The step showing is plum and a passed one green.
  - **Sections:** A7's rows in one card. Each row has:
    - a grip, which drags the row; on the keyboard, up and down move it and right and left indent and outdent it (H1–H5);
    - the outline number (mono 12 px, 28 px wide), the title edited in place, and the level ("H2", mono 11 px);
    - the required switch.

    Rows are indented 24 px per level. "+ Add section", the hint line, and "Next: Review" (38 px), which saves the draft, follow.
  - **Review:** "Changes against v2" lists each change: added, removed, renamed, moved, re-levelled, made required or optional, or with changed text. Then Back and "Next: Publish".
  - **Publish:** "This becomes the active template version for new policies." with "Publish version".
  - **With no draft:** "Create version" in the header, and the wizard gives way to an empty state.
  - **Version history:** a timeline with each version's dot by status, "v2 · 4 sections" and its status.
  - **Rename, Retire and Delete:** in an actions menu, Retire and Delete each behind their D30 confirm.
- **Copy:** every string on these pages is in `packages/i18n` (`admin.templates.*`).
- **Docs:** a new admin guide page, Templates, linked from the guide's index.

Refs #22.

### Differences from the frames, and why

- **Semantic versions:** the gateway's template versions have an integer `versionNo` and no semantic version or change type. So the header says "v2 active · v3 draft", not "v2.0.0 · v2.1.0", and "Minor version, because an optional section was added." isn't shown.
- **The Updated column** (A6) and the history's dates aren't shown: templates have no timestamps. I filed [Steward-GRC/steward-gateway#66](https://github.com/Steward-GRC/steward-gateway/issues/66) for all three.
- **Tab / Shift+Tab** indenting (the frame's hint) became right and left arrows on the grip. Taking over Tab would trap keyboard users in the list. The hint line says so.
- **Each row has "Text" and a remove cross.** The frame doesn't show them, but section boilerplate and removing a section were already supported and have nowhere else to live.
- **The Review step** works out the changes in the browser by comparing the draft with the active version. The brief's "section diffs" in the history wait on #66's history data.

author: jjunker
body:
Brunata changed its backend without notice, which broke the integration in two ways. This PR fixes both, and fixes sensor values that didn't match the portal.

## What broke

- **API version.** Every path under `online-webservice/v1/rest` now returns 503. The web portal uses `online-webservice/v2/rest`, which has the same `/consumer/...` endpoints and parameters.
- **Login.** Brunata moved accounts from Azure AD B2C to Keycloak. The old B2C flow now fails with *"We can't seem to find your account"*, even though the portal login works.

## Changes

- Switch to `online-webservice/v2/rest`.
- Replace the B2C login with the portal's flow: `online-auth-webservice/v1/rest/authorize` → Keycloak login form → `oauth/token`. It uses the same client ID and redirect URI. Token refresh uses the same endpoint.
- Login failures now show Keycloak's message (e.g. "Invalid username or password.") instead of a generic error.
- Radiator sensors now show the latest meter reading from `/consumer/meters`, the same value as *Seneste værdi* in the portal. Before, they showed this month's summed consumption times the meter scale, which was close to zero. Month-to-date consumption is kept as a `month_consumption` attribute. Unique IDs are unchanged, so entity IDs and history carry over.
- The three API GET calls share one helper that re-authenticates and retries once on 401.
- README: added a disclaimer that this is an unofficial project, and updated the login, sensor and API sections. It now says only heating meters have been tested.

## Testing

Tested in Home Assistant against a real account with five radiator meters. Login succeeds, and all sensor values match the portal.

## Known follow-ups

- The refresh token is saved only once, at setup, and never updated. Every restart therefore does a full login.
- Polling every 15 minutes is more than needed, since readings update about once a day.
- The client sends a Chrome User-Agent.
- `dashboard-example.yaml` still refers to water, electricity and `brunata_consumption_*` sensors that don't exist.

author: goslingmanagment
body:
## Why
Hub now serves the posts plan of `capture_coverage` for Fansly pages (goslingmanagment/hub#1021, entry E7). Two things on our side would still keep «не вышло» by posts off:

1. **The proof could never hold.** Every Hub read starts at `HUB_WINDOW_FLOOR` (2020), so each answer carries a `before_capture_floor` gap and the `gaps_present` blocker; `loadHubFacts` refuses the proof on `gaps_present`. Seen in the VM on 05.11.2026: every page's `hub_sync_state.blockers` holds `gaps_present`.
2. **A stale proof.** If Hub's posts refresh stops, its last claim would keep counting.

## What
- `pageBlockers` (sync.ts): a page whose gaps are all `before_capture_floor` does not add `gaps_present` to the run's blockers. Any other gap still does and still cancels the proof. For posts the proven end of the timeline answers that gap.
- `postsCoverage` takes the plan only with `provider_exhausted` + a proof **and** `nextProbeAt` ahead of the run's start. Hub moves the head every 6 h and sets `nextProbeAt` to the head + 18 h. When «не вышло» is checked (≥ 24 h after the slot), the proven interval reaches at least 6 h past the slot. That covers `hub_candidate_tolerance` (30 min) and the end of the day for a row without a time.
- `nextProbeAt` joins the pinned `capture_coverage` fields. Hub already declares it (`timestamp`), so the capabilities check stays green and the fake Hub gets it from the pinned list.
- Norm: SPEC §7 / §8.1 / §13, PLAN stage 5 (order item 1, E7) and schema §9.6 now say the plan exists for Fansly since 05.11.2026, how it is kept fresh, and how floor gaps are treated. OnlyFans still has no plan (E5), so «не вышло» by posts stays off there.

Where the norm was silent I picked the simplest option. Freshness comes from Hub's own `nextProbeAt` rather than a ContentOps constant, and `hub_succeeded_at` for Fansly stays the latest post sighting.

## PLAN «Готово, когда»
Stage 5 order item 1, the Hub half (E7 on ari-1). It closes once the VM runs this and ari-1 shows the proof after Hub's backfill. Not deployed to the VM here.

## Tests
`apps/server/src/hub/coverage.test.ts`: the floor gap alone no longer blocks, any other gap does; the plan counts only with a proof and a future `nextProbeAt`.

Why: Today the guard judges an existing script only for log deletion, so a script that reads the rclone config or the Cloudflare token runs unrefused. What:
- Credential-script check: refuses running an existing text file (shell or Python runner, or by suffix or shebang) whose text names the rclone config or the GOODQA_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN secret, or dumps the config.
- It is additive by construction. It runs as its own pass after the main analysis, which is unchanged and keeps its full 3 s budget. The pass has its own 1.5 s cap and runs only when nothing else already blocks and some command runs a script. Any stop in it, including the hook alarm, keeps the main verdict.
- Two pinned routes in a fixed table, until 2026-11-09T00:00Z, each needing an exact SHA-256 at an exact path. The Dropbox route is `/bin/bash -p <path>`, which skips BASH_ENV, ENV and exported functions. The DNS route accepts the tool's `list`, `set-ttl` and `set-content` shapes with names up to 40 characters.
- ASSUMPTION: the DNS route's argument shape is the coordinator's inference, not the user's words.
- Merges main d310adb (#93), which touches no guard code.

All on dev2 with env -i and a scratch HOME, except the Mac replay.

author: anfragment
body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds a pool of 32 KB buffers for copying response bodies in `writeResp`, to reduce per-response memory allocations and garbage. Previously, `io.Copy` allocated a new buffer for most HTTP/2 and streamed HTTP/1.1 responses. Bytes allocated per response, including the test client running in the same process, for an equal mix of 0 B, 1 KB, 20 KB, 100 KB, 1 MB and 10 MB bodies:

| | master (mean / median / SD) | PR (mean / median / SD) |
|---|---|---|
| HTTP/2 | 60.4 / 39.0 / 60.0 KB | 33.4 / 7.0 / 53.3 KB |
| HTTP/1.1, streamed | 38.4 / 37.3 / 2.9 KB | 6.3 / 5.3 / 2.9 KB |

### How did you verify your code works?

New automated test, `TestWriteRespOverHTTP2`, runs concurrent responses larger than the buffer over one HTTP/2 connection, with half the clients resetting their streams mid-body, and checks that the other bodies arrive intact. It fails if responses share a buffer.

author: roryprimrose
body:
## Approved outcome

Follow up #828, #829 and #831 with the requested change-aware hourly automatic main builds, without making PR admission wait for each main build to start. Existing unit-only admission already measured 6m55s for an ordinary candidate, versus the earlier 19m34s full-policy run; this PR preserves those gates and changes main scheduling, not coverage.

## Placement and scope

Repository-owned CI/admission/release orchestration.

- Add separately activated `KORA_MAIN_BUILD_PROFILE=hourly-v1`, requiring enabled independent batch delivery. Default remains per-merge; unknown/inconsistent profiles fail closed.
- Automatic main pushes explicitly coalesce heavy work. UTC hourly cron builds only changed snapshots; unchanged sources, including failed attempts, are not automatically rebuilt.
- Track exact first-attempt run/job/source evidence and an observed cursor. Scheduled admission reconciles earlier unobserved attempts before granting work. No skipped job becomes successful qualification.
- Advance PR admission from the App's persisted exact completed-source record, not from main startup. Preserve eight candidate gates and all 27 main identities.
- Preserve explicit manual/tag validation and full source-bound beta publication for selected scheduled main snapshots, with fresh same-run payloads and installer bytes.
- Add guarded administrator hold/prepare/profile-switch/resume/abort and rollback. It requires a qualified current main tip, exact tree/checkpoint/token/administrator and physical CI/publication quiescence. The workflow never writes variables itself.

No protection, secrets, App installation, global configuration, package, analyzer or coverage changes. No manual candidate dispatch, force update, cross-run proof reuse or relaxed release gates.

## User-visible behavior

PRs remain independently admitted. When the opt-in profile is activated, automatic main compilation/tests/packaging run at most once per UTC hourly slot for changed source. Push admission reports coalescing honestly; it is not a full build pass. GitHub may delay cron launch. Unchanged failed sources require an explicit retry or a new source.

The caller separately authorized repository-only activation, but only after the guarded qualification/quiescence prerequisites pass. This PR does not activate the profile. Current main still has unrelated integration failures/in-progress qualification; activation and observed live hourly cadence are not claimed.

## Validation and compatibility

- `node .\eng\run-policy-tests.cjs` — 394 passed. Includes 30 hourly helper cases, scheduled/no-change/same-slot decisions, earlier unobserved runs, API failures, source/attempt identity, guarded activation/rollback, exact full-main qualification and historical compatibility.
- `.\eng\Test-BuildVersion.ps1` — 38 assertions, 23 resolutions, seven expected rejections and three compiled binary metadata checks passed.
- `.\eng\Test-GitHubRelease.ps1` — 1,045 publication assertions, including 662 batch safety assertions, passed. Covers scheduled beta publication, snapshot/durable profile mismatch, stale/unknown profile, wrong event and late mutation fences.
- `.\eng\Test-CiPreflight.ps1` — 667 assertions passed.
- `.\eng\Test-PortableTestScheduling.ps1` — 78 assertions passed.
- `git diff --cached --check` — passed.

One legacy operation-list assertion and one fixture environment classification were updated for the explicit new administrator operations/profile before the final passing rerun. No assertion or gate was disabled. The version fixture's missing-assets case performed its expected locked restore through the machine-only feed override; no feed configuration was committed.

No production C# changes in this PR. Full hosted candidate and main/release validation remain pending and are not represented as local passes. Existing state, release records, queue enrollment, unit selection, complete portable assembly evidence and 100% line/branch thresholds are preserved. Live activation requires the documented drained transition and fresh current-source qualification; missing/failed/unknown evidence withholds the switch.

author: brandli
body:
Closes #823.

Argo CD copies an Application's sources into an automated sync operation and retries that copy, starting no new sync while it runs. After a step moves the Application (new build, new revision), it waited out every retry of the old one. D-01 sat on an operator build that could not make the vault's snapshot store while the Application already named the build that does.

## Change

- `request_argo_sync_if_stalled` (scripts/lib/argocd.sh), which D-01, C-02, B-01, D-03, E-04 and E-05 call while waiting, stops an operation that is Running, was started by automated sync, and whose copy of the sources differs from the Application's. It uses the same merge patch as `unstick_argo_hook_job`. Automated sync then starts again on the current sources.
- Nulls and empty objects are dropped before comparing. That is how Argo CD's copy remembers a value removed by a merge, not a real difference.
- A sync a person asked for, and an operation whose copy names no sources, are left alone.

## Verification

- New `make test-argo-stale-operation`, part of `lint-shell`, with 7 cases against a stand-in kubectl. 2 fail without the change.
- The comparison was run read-only on the Aluvian cluster's 31 Applications with automated operations. 14 match. The 17 that differ all differ in a real `targetRevision` move, with no formatting noise, and all of them are finished, so none would be touched.
- `shellcheck`, `lint-resolvable`, `lint-unreachable`, `validate-steps` pass. `lint-shell` stops on `test-signing-key-lookup`, which fails the same way on an untouched develop checkout on this host.

author: aray4702
body:
<!-- sm-agent: fixer -->
<!-- sm-routine: window-subagent -->
Every algorithm document of the RTP/RTCP session layer (9.1-9.5) now lists benchmarks. The two existing SDES/BYE benchmarks are linked to 9.1 in `tools/catalog.py`, and `bench/rtp_bench.cc` gains 8 more. All of them use simulated time only and build for WebAssembly.

| Algorithm | Benchmark | Unit of work | Measured on M4 (Release) | Requirement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 9.1 RTCP engine, SDES and BYE | `rtp/SdesCname_SerializeParse` (existing) | one SDES CNAME chunk serialized + parsed | 0.16 µs | <= 3 µs |
| 9.1 | `rtp/Bye_SerializeParse` (existing) | one BYE serialized + parsed | 0.15 µs | <= 3 µs |
| 9.1 | `rtp/RtcpEngine_CompoundReportBuildAndParse` | one compound SR + 3 report blocks + SDES built by `SendReport` on one engine and parsed by `OnRtcp` on another | 1.1 µs | <= 8 µs; 3 report blocks and 1 SDES chunk parsed |
| 9.1 | `rtp/RtcpEngine_NackPliFeedbackBuildAndParse` | NACK (10 seqs) + PLI queued, sent by `Process` as one compound, parsed by the media sender's engine | 1.4 µs | <= 10 µs; NACK parsed |
| 9.2 RTP sender and send-side controller | `rtp/RtpSender_SendVideoFramePaced` | one 30 fps 6000-byte H.264 frame (5 packets): packetize, `RtpSender` (MID/transport-cc/abs-send-time, RTX history), `SendSideController` (transport seq, pacing, serialization) run at its process times; transport feedback looped back once per frame | 14.5 µs | <= 120 µs; pacer keeps up (<= 6 video packets unsent) |
| 9.3 RTP receiver | `rtp/RtpReceiver_ReceivePacket` | one RTP packet of a 30 fps H.264 stream (30 kB keyframe + 89 x 4 kB deltas, replayed): parse, statistics, NACK, packet buffer, plus `Process`/frame release once per frame | 0.9 µs | <= 8 µs; >= 0.95 frames out per frame in (measured 1.00) |
| 9.4 RTP session facade | `rtp/Session_VideoFrameEndToEnd` | one 33 ms frame interval of an H.264 call through two `rtp::Session`s over two `sim::NetworkLink`s (25 ms, 3 Mbit/s): `SendVideo`, 33 ticks of `Process` on both, bytes across the links, receive to render, RTCP back | 61 µs | <= 500 µs; >= 0.95 rendered per sent (measured 1.00) |
| 9.4 | `rtp/Q_Session_Video_5pct_loss` (quality) | 20 s of the same call with 5% random loss on the forward link (NACK + RTX) | delivered 0.997, longest freeze 302 ms | delivered >= 0.98, longest freeze <= 500 ms |
| 9.5 H.264 packetization | `rtp/H264_Keyframe1080p_PacketizeDepacketize` | one 150 kB keyframe (SPS+PPS in STAP-A, IDR in 127 FU-A, 128 packets): packetize, `Parse` each payload, `Reassemble` | 100 µs | <= 800 µs; reassembly succeeds |
| 9.5 | `rtp/H264_DeltaFrame1080p_PacketizeDepacketize` | one 20 kB delta frame (17 FU-A): same | 14 µs | <= 120 µs; reassembly succeeds |

Budgets are about 8-10x the median Release time of three runs on the M4. Under Node (wasm, `--min-time=0.05`) all 10 pass at budget scale 1. Both builds were run: `out-b/bench/sm_bench --filter=rtp/ --min-time=0.25` gives 10 passed, 0 failed, and `node out-wasm/bench/sm_bench.js --filter=rtp/ --min-time=0.05` gives 10 passed, 0 failed.

Not regenerated: `docs/results/` and `docs/algorithms/`. The window re-records them once at the end. No public API change. Nothing in `agents/` or `.github/` changed.

author: alexj11324
body:
## 2026-11-05 20:55 UTC — withdrawn from this delivery

Closing this unmerged draft. Alex's later instructions in [#1210](https://github.com/alexj11324/Mikka/issues/1210#issuecomment-6667240186) and the [resource clarification](https://github.com/alexj11324/Mikka/issues/1210#issuecomment-6667341688) already authorize a suitably sized Large for the full production build and screenshots, followed by immediate shutdown. I had overlooked that superseding authorization while continuing to investigate Medium. The Owner recheck fix will use the unchanged production build configuration on one Large; this environment workaround is unnecessary for that delivery.

This patch has **not** passed a real production build and is **not** being shipped. The earlier failed builds, measurements and source-review record below remain historical evidence; no SIGKILL is relabelled as a pass or attributed to a proved cache cause. No branch history is rewritten.

---

Refs #1210

## What and why

Owner 复核入口的本地 production UI 验证被生产编译阻塞。原有 Medium（约 8 GiB）上的两次固定树 Webpack 编译分别在 139.46 秒、140.39 秒后收到 SIGKILL，最大 child RSS 为 7,227,724 KiB、7,250,684 KiB；两次分别使用 heap 6144、4096。真实 `pnpm exec node` 探针已排除参数覆盖，Next diagnostics 停在 compile/useBuildWorker=false。系统累计存在 OOM kill，但缺乏逐次前基线，不把每个 SIGKILL 单独声称为已确诊 OOM。

Next 的默认生产 filesystem cache 已包含内存缓存，又增加依赖扫描和 pack 序列化。失败日志的最后警告来自该路径；本仓开发构建已记录同一大型模块图的持久缓存序列化会产生额外大 Buffer。这个 PR 将已有的 Webpack memory-cache 策略扩展到生产构建，避免这层持久化开销。

- 仅在现有缓存启用时替换生产缓存；显式 `cache: false` 保持关闭。
- 开发构建、alias、next-intl / Workflow wrapper 和其余选项保留。
- 不同时启用 `webpackMemoryOptimizations`，不改堆上限、机器规格、swap 或 cgroup。
- 代价是后续 Webpack 构建不能复用磁盘持久缓存；应用层缓存和默认 Turbopack 构建不受影响。

参考：[Next 官方内存指南](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/memory-usage)，固定 Next 16.4.1 的 Webpack cache/编译器关闭实现及 Webpack 5.98.0 的 cache plugin 配置。此处是有明确机制的单变量修复，不把缓存警告本身当成 SIGKILL 的证明。

风险评估：实际本地 UI 构建已重复阻塞，发生可能性 7/10、影响 4/10，乘积 28；修改范围仅两文件、一个 Webpack 编译缓存条件。无 schema、auth、权限、凭据或用户界面变更。

## How it was checked

**当前为草稿，实际生产构建及指标待完成，暂不合并。** 源码已准备并审阅；将在原有 Medium 的冻结最终组合树上完成相交 PG、生产构建和 UI 截图。与早先 205 对照树之间另有 Owner expiry 与主线功能改动，报告会列明完整版本，不把前后 RSS 差异当作严格单变量因果证明。

源码 checkpoint：`e381d2dba4f5bcfceaaff935fd275c0c66a970be` / tree `366a994c80a7416ee894f89c796e8295e65fcdd7`，base `7559deef0ac8d243b6929de1ef8091dda963f26f`；只有 `next.config.mjs` 与 `docs/dev-workflow.md`。独立只读审查已确认条件与插件边界，`git diff --check` 通过；这两项不代替真实生产构建结果。

本 PR 不关闭 #1210。正式合并仍需精确最终 head CI、可合并性、上一实际部署 READY 和生产完整版本 SHA；最终上线后核对本轮 merge SHA。生产模型验收继续保留在 #1210 的相应路径记录中。


### 首次发布版本

Git Data 首次发布 HEAD `bb6245f0e5ba1a111b4a28a417416cd872664a82` / tree `e76e3f984ada25ffbeaa9c837cdc30617f7cfbc6`，唯一 parent `78381be2ba8271a3029ace8943594b6c628c23d6`。本地 checkpoint e381 与远端 commit 的元数据不同；两项补丁 blob 完全相同，完整远端 tree/parent 已读回核对。发布时 main 已到 `484d7ac66b5eba692b53ad8759e4b558a6232dfb`，783→484 的增量未修改本 PR 两个文件；最终组合会纳入相交的主线并按最终 head 验证。没有 rebase、force push 或直接 push main。

## Scope: engineering-only CE-1C3a
Adds bounded PDF and issuer-listing source staging to the existing signed-permit fetch code. No real external fetch has been run, no signed capture receipts are minted by this worker, and no K.O. enterprise business launch is authorized.

### Implemented
- Signed source permit **V3** must include `media_type=application/pdf` and is capped at 4MiB; legacy **V2** remains text/HTML-only and max 512KB. No implicit permission expansion.
- Reuse exact-host allowlist, DNS-pinned TLS, no redirects/credential forwarding, strict Content-Type and byte/encoding checks. Genuine synthetic PDF bytes go through existing bounded subprocess extraction before disk writes.
- New `approved_pdf_capture.py` provides `stage_pdf` and `stage_issuer_listing`; rechecks company approval, emergency pause and signed permit before/after network and before disk. Writes once to Git-ignored `state/competitive_engine/capture_staging` with private permissions and symlink/path traversal checks.
- Status is always UNSIGNED_CAPTURE_REQUIRES_SEPARATE_ATTESTATION; includes no signing private key, claim verification, issuer completeness assertion, publication, outreach or scheduled source crawling.
- 29 new adversarial tests including permit downgrade prevention, paused read blocking, post-read pause and permit expiry, malicious MIME/redirect, corrupt/scanned PDF, untrusted anchors and private file write isolation.

### Limits
Tests are mocked; full live issuer acquisition, independent capture signer and revocation, authoritative portal completeness, legal access/rights, PDF visual critic, and company-wide secure release controller are **NOT** implemented. author: ahmetatar
body:
## Problem

The deployed server (`templates/deploy/server.py.j2`) took `thread_id` straight from the request body and used it as the checkpointer key, with no ownership check:

- Anyone who knew or guessed a `thread_id` could continue that conversation: read it (by asking the LLM to repeat it) or poison it.
- Requests without a `thread_id` all fell back to `"default"`, so every such client shared one conversation.
- Platform auth (IAM/ingress) answers *who may reach the service*, not *which conversation a request may load*.

## Change

- **`deploy.auth`** (default `mode: jwt`): verify a bearer JWT via `jwks_url` (identity provider) or `secret_env` (HMAC).
  - `exp` is always required; `iss`/`aud` are checked when configured; `audience` is required with `jwks_url`.
  - HMAC and asymmetric algorithm sets are disjoint and `none` is never allowed (prevents algorithm confusion).
  - The secret must be at least 32 bytes; the server fails closed at startup without it.
- **Server-derived thread**: `thread_id = f"{user_id}:{conversation_id}"`. `conversation_id` is a server-issued UUIDv4 returned in every response. A body with `thread_id`, or a non-v4 `conversation_id`, gets 400. There is no shared default thread.
- **`deploy.rate_limit.requests_per_minute`** (default 60, per user, per replica): 429 with `Retry-After`.
- `abp deploy` and `DeployPackager` refuse to package until auth is configured. `deploy.auth.mode: none` is the explicit opt-out; the server warns at startup in that mode.
- `deploy.auth.secret_env` is collected and injected like other secrets.
- Docs: `docs/deploy.md` (contract, status codes, auth section, limits), `docs/memory.md`. CHANGELOG: Security, breaking, with migration.

## Breaking

`abp deploy` now requires `deploy.auth`. Clients must send `Authorization: Bearer <JWT>` and replace `thread_id` with the returned `conversation_id`. To keep an unauthenticated endpoint behind your own gateway, set `deploy.auth.mode: none`.

## Tests

- `tests/test_deployers/test_deploy_server.py`: renders the real server and drives it with FastAPI `TestClient`, with only `main.run` stubbed (it records per-thread history). Covers 401 cases (missing/non-Bearer/wrong signature/expired/no `exp`/`alg: none`/missing claim/wrong `iss`/`aud`), JWKS against a local IdP serving an RSA key (accept, wrong key, wrong audience, unreachable → 503), the stolen-`conversation_id` case (the attacker gets an empty thread of their own, the victim's history is untouched), no shared default thread, 400 cases, and 429 including window sliding.
- `tests/test_models/test_deploy_auth.py`: schema rules.
- Existing deploy-flow tests now opt out explicitly with `deploy.auth.mode: none`, because packaging intentionally requires auth; the rules they test are unchanged.
- Mutation check: 18 planted bugs (thread prefix dropped, `thread_id` accepted, signature/`exp`/audience not verified, limiter off-by-one, shared rate key, default mode flipped, …), all caught.
- Dev extras gain `fastapi`, `httpx`, `pyjwt[crypto]` and `uvicorn` so CI exercises the real server.
- Manual: generated a real project and ran `server.py` with mock LLM fixtures. curl results: 401 without a token, 200 with a `conversation_id`, 400 for `thread_id`, 429 on the 4th request at a limit of 3; the server refused to start without the secret.

## Not covered

- Container build (podman/docker) was not run: the local podman machine was stopped.
- The rate limit is per process; the docs say so. Token revocation, TLS (terminated by the platform) and the existing 500-on-input-error behaviour are out of scope.

author: brandonrc
body:
## Summary

Closes #5200

### Root cause

`advanced_search` built its `SearchQuery` from `query`, `format`, `name` and the sort fields only. `repository_key`, `path`, `version`, `min_size`, `max_size`, `created_after` and `created_before` were parsed into `AdvancedSearchQuery` and then dropped, and `SearchQuery` had no field for any of them.

### Fix

- `SearchQuery` gets the seven filters (appended after `sort_order`, so existing literals only gain `..Default::default()`).
- `field_filter_sql(first)` / `bind_field_filters` add them to both `execute_search` and `count_results` from one fragment, so items and `pagination.total` can't disagree. That covers the `per_page=0` count-only branch too.
- The handler builds the filters once (`advanced_field_filters`) and uses them as the base of both of its `SearchQuery` literals.
- The filters are ANDed on top of the existing `accessible_repo_ids` scope. Naming a repository the caller cannot read returns nothing; it does not widen the scope.

Semantics:

- `repository_key` and `version` match exactly.
- `path` is a literal prefix of the stored path. A leading `/` is ignored, and `%`, `_` and `\` are escaped.
- `min_size` and `max_size` are inclusive.
- `created_after` and `created_before` are exclusive. They take RFC 3339 or `YYYY-MM-DD` (midnight UTC). An unparseable date returns 400 instead of being silently ignored.

Facets are unchanged. As before, they describe everything the caller can see; they already ignore `query`, `format` and `name`.

## Regression test (required for `fix/*` PRs)
- [x] This PR is a `fix/*` AND adds/updates a test that would have caught the bug
- [ ] N/A — this is not a bug fix


New `advanced_field_filter_db_tests` module in `search.rs` (shard handlers-2, DB-backed). The fixture has repos `sa` and `sb` (readable) and `sc` (no grant). The tests go through the real router as a non-admin and check both items and `pagination.total`:

- control: no filter returns a1, a2, b1, and never `sc`
- `repository_key` (the issue's reproduction)
- `repository_key` naming an unreadable repo returns nothing
- `path` prefix, leading `/`, `_` treated as a literal
- `version`
- `min_size` / `max_size` / both (inclusive)
- `created_after` / `created_before` / range, date-only and RFC 3339
- invalid date returns 400
- `per_page=0` total and combined filters

Run on sparky against Postgres 16 with `AK_TESTS_REQUIRE_DB=1`: `test(/search/)` in shard handlers-2, 124 passed.

**Negative control.** With the handler wiring reverted (`..filters` changed to `..Default::default()`), 7 of the 9 new tests fail, e.g.:

```
advanced_search_filters_by_size_bounds_db
  left: ["a1", "a2", "b1"]
 right: ["a2"]
Summary 9 tests run: 2 passed, 7 failed
```

The two that still pass are the unfiltered control and the invalid-date 400.

### Rebased onto #5367

#5367 (#5338) merged first and added `hidden_artifact_ids` as `$8` / `$6` in the same two queries. The rebase binds it before `bind_field_filters`, so the field filters now start at `$9` (items) and `$7` (count).

## Regression test (required for `fix/*` PRs)
- [x] This PR is a `fix/*` AND adds/updates a test that would have caught the bug
- [ ] N/A — this is not a bug fix


New `advanced_field_filter_db_tests` module in `search.rs` (shard handlers-2, DB-backed). The fixture has repos `sa` and `sb` (readable) and `sc` (no grant). The tests go through the real router as a non-admin and check both items and `pagination.total`:

- control: no filter returns a1, a2, b1, and never `sc`
- `repository_key` (the issue's reproduction)
- `repository_key` naming an unreadable repo returns nothing
- `path` prefix, leading `/`, `_` treated as a literal
- `version`
- `min_size` / `max_size` / both (inclusive)
- `created_after` / `created_before` / range, date-only and RFC 3339
- invalid date returns 400
- `per_page=0` total and combined filters

Run on sparky against Postgres 16 with `AK_TESTS_REQUIRE_DB=1`: `test(/search/)` in shard handlers-2, 124 passed.

**Negative control.** With the handler wiring reverted (`..filters` changed to `..Default::default()`), 7 of the 9 new tests fail, e.g.:

```

  left: ["a1", "a2", "b1"]
 right: ["a2"]
Summary 9 tests run: 2 passed, 7 failed
```

The two that still pass are the unfiltered control and the invalid-date 400.

### Note for #5367

PR #5367 (#5338) adds `$8` (`hidden_artifact_ids`) to the same two queries. Whichever PR merges second gets a textual conflict on the `.bind(&query.accessible_repo_ids)` chain. Resolve it by binding `hidden_artifact_ids` before `bind_field_filters` and bumping `field_filter_sql(8)` / `field_filter_sql(6)` to 9 / 7.

author: millzach
body:
## What changed

- **A thread's agent can ask the Council (#2216).** A new loopback MCP server, `sotto_council`, offers `ask_council` (a Council question or review), `start_climb` (a Climb's setup, with the thread as the Builder) and `read_council`. It exists only where the Council is built: the `council` Owl feature and this computer's local host. Stable offers nothing. Only ordinary local threads on providers that take Sotto's tools get it, not Watcher, a Council's seats or judges, or delegated threads.
- **The user's own message is the gate.** On every call, main reads the thread's newest user message from Sotto's record. A wake-up, a Council prompt or verdict, a delegation's brief, Watcher's send or a handover never counts. The message must name the Council, or a Climb for `start_climb`. One message starts one Council or Climb, even with two calls at once. What the agent writes never counts.
- **Seats and Climb approval.** Seats are always Settings → Council's. The agent chooses only the question. A Climb's judges are the panel's Climb-capable seats, then the strongest Claude or Codex models. A Climb still waits for the user to approve its setup in the drawer.
- **Where it shows.** The asking thread's pane opens its Council tab in Ask or Climb mode. The record says "Asked by <provider> in this thread, because you said …", quoting the user while Keep local history keeps the words. This is prototype variant A, Zach's pick ([prototype](docs/prototypes/council-from-a-thread-prototype.html)).
- **The verdict comes back.** Once the fairness check allows Send to (every panelist answered, or two minutes passed), Sotto sends the asking thread one message tagged Council. It carries the same text Send to drafts and goes as soon as the thread is free. It is recorded as Sotto's before the provider hears it and is never sent twice. A Climb an agent started sends one message when it ends. `read_council` returns the verdict in full.
- **Documents.** ADR-0177 is amended for decisions 1 and 5 in this case. `CONTEXT.md` (Council), `README.md` (privacy list), `docs/guide.md` and `docs/agent-control.md` are updated, plus a verification note.
- **After review.** Sol (gpt-6.1-sol, max) reviewed both axes. Fixed:
  - Two concurrent calls could start two Councils.
  - The verdict waited on every fairness reply instead of the two-minute release.
  - `read_council` cut long verdicts.
  - Per-update and per-call scans grew with history; they are now indexed.
  - The asking message was read by loading the whole history; it is now read by its ID.
  - Raw file-system errors reached the agent; they are now plain words.
  - The Climb's starting criterion was duplicated; it is now shared.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run notices:verify`: clean.
- `npm test -- --maxWorkers=2`: not run to the end on forge. The run was slow under load and stopped as Zach asked; CI runs it. What ran instead:
  - The touched tests: 471 passed across 30 files, including the new `tests/integration/councilFromThread.test.ts` (fake providers: start, seats, open signal, one per message, concurrency, verdict back once, the two-minute release, refusals, Climb setup), `tests/unit/main/council/councilTools.test.ts` and `tests/unit/renderer/features/council/askedByLine.test.tsx`.
  - The interface catalogs, theme tokens and copy sites.
  - `tests/unit/release` and `tests/unit/scripts`: 530 passed.
  - `streamingCopyBudget` and `ownerScaleWorkBudget`: 26 passed.
  - `dynamicThreadRecord.test.ts` failed once in the loaded full run and passed alone.
- Live, on real Claude Code and Codex threads: `SOTTO_COUNCIL_LIVE=1 npx playwright test tests/e2e/council-from-thread-live.spec.ts`. Both cases passed, in separate runs of the same build:
  - A Claude thread asked "have the council review README.md" started a Council. Its pane opened the Council tab by itself, and the verdict came back as the Council's message, which Claude answered.
  - A thread whose message named only `ask_council` was refused, and nothing started.
  - Note and screenshots: [docs/verification/council-from-a-thread.md](docs/verification/council-from-a-thread.md).
- Hand test on the next Owl:
  - [ ] Ask a Claude thread to "have the council review" something on Windows.
  - [ ] Ask a Codex thread the same.
  - [ ] Start a Climb from a thread and approve it.

## Out of scope

- A Council or Climb started from a headless host's or paired host's thread. The Council is built on the desktop only (ADR-0177's first build).
- Follow-up questions through the tool.

## Known limitation

- The agent writes the question. A question the user didn't mean still gets the one Council their message allows. The question shows at the top of the record, and Stop works as on any Council.
- A dictated or typed message that names a council for any other reason passes the gate.

Closes #2216.

author: dizys
body:
## What this changes

During a rolling deploy, the logs page could leave out the marker that says where the new container begins, `-- new container web-3 of web --`. That marker is what tells a reader which lines are the new container's. So this was the product, not the test. `web/e2e/logs.ts:558` failed on and off because a person following the deploy really could miss it.

Closes #118. Milestone: M3 · Deploys on one server.

**Why it went missing.** `LogStore` decided once, on a source's first lines, whether they start a new container of a replica that had lines before. It could only decide that if it already knew each source's replica. The page tells it the replica from an effect after it draws the new sources (`LogsPage.tsx:219`). Lines go in from `useLogStream`'s flush timer, which runs at once after a quiet spell. So on a busy page the new container's first lines could reach the store first, and the marker never came.

**The fix.** When it doesn't know yet, the store waits, and places the marker just before the first line it was about, as soon as the replicas involved are known. While the view holds still, the marker goes with what's held, so nothing moves. A clear forgets what was waiting. The deep search's store, which the same effect feeds, gets this too.

The e2e step now says which markers the log held when it finds none, so a repeat explains itself.

## How I know

A harness, not in the repository, ran that step's rolling deploy over and over on one page, with Chromium's CPU slowed through the DevTools protocol, as on a busy runner. Temporary logging in the store recorded, for each deploy, when the new container's first lines reached the store, when its replica became known, and when a waiting marker was placed.

| | Deploys | Marker came | First lines before the replica |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `main`, CPU slowed 6x | 30 | 22 | 8, all 8 without the marker, 1 to 19 ms early |

## Summary

  - `did you mean 'x'?` → replaces the misspelled name with the suggestion (Clang and GCC wording).

author: danipopes
body:
abi-cafe declares f128 values as `_Float128` for GCC but initialized them with a union of `__float128`, a type GCC does not have on aarch64. Every f128 test that involves the C compiler therefore failed to build on aarch64 Linux, and the entries for them in the rules file were marked busted at the build phase. A small patch to abi-cafe, applied by the existing patch mechanism, uses the same type name for GCC in both places, and the busted entries are removed. A comment in the rules file now also says why F32Array is busted on aarch64 Linux: Cranelift gives each float of a stack-passed aggregate its own 8-byte slot, where LLVM and GCC pack the aggregate.

This branch is stacked on the ABI conformance PR, so its diff shows those commits until that PR merges. The abi-cafe run is the check: on x86_64 Linux all f128 tests pass with GCC and the patch; the aarch64 Linux result has to come from CI.

author: xsalahx
body:
`rowstile review` said "Meaning unchanged: every one of up to 3 rows of each type" for some changes that widen
access, and `rowstile prove` said "holds" where a row breaks an invariant: the small worlds never held the values
that would tell two policies apart. Now:

- A condition that compares a relation's column with an id (`{owner_id <> 7}`, `{parent_id = 0}`) gets a row with
  that id in the worlds (a user 7, a folder 0), and the ids either side of one compared in order, as far as the key's
  type holds them (whole numbers for a bigint key, texts for a text one). The listed worlds give each such row each
  of those ids, or one no condition names.
- Beside a number compared in order, the worlds hold the numbers halfway to the next ones: `{level > 1}` and
  `{level >= 2}` differ on 1.5 in a numeric column. A whole number past 8,388,607 so compared is left to the
  database (a real column rounds the half).
- A condition that reads a relation's column beside other columns (`{owner_id = authz.uid() and not locked}`)
  gets every value of those other columns in the listed worlds and the corners.
- A type's `where` on a relation's column (`where {owner_id is not null}`) is read from the row's link in the
  listed worlds, which kept no such row before.
- A condition the worlds can't read (a subquery) is the same condition however it is spaced outside its quotes.
- The review reads a backslash in `E'...'` as the parser does: a change after it is a change, not spacing.
- `{user = 'alice'}`, `{current_date is null}` and SQL's other such words are the role, the session or the clock,
  as Postgres reads them, not columns of the row.
- The review reads a policy with sync lines and shows each one that changed, instead of stopping with an error.

Each has a check in `core/tests/unit_test.py` (Review, Confidence, HandAnswers) that failed before it. The suites
that hold the evaluator against Postgres and the review (conditions_test, rewrites, small, confidence_test,
review.sh, hand_answers.sh, cookbook.sh) pass. The review of a refactor of the docs policy takes about 5% more CPU
time (6.0 s to 6.35 s for 200 drawn and 3,000 listed worlds). The generated SQL doesn't change.

Stacked on #641.

**Submitter note**

Harness: Codex

# Omit the redundant first-CTA vote in the combined selector source

This candidate starts from official main `835f2e611530f0f5903607444acbb4bcabb40279`. The promoted record `3e139917-a36d-45ef-9a0a-0c5616142e53` passed official correctness on spark-6 and scored 2.78747116567543. That score belongs to its complete source, not this candidate. The full candidate tree is `ddbf64cba7fecb46ae21b9c3728606dd65e90c65`; patch SHA-256 is `eecf2133252c0722717d20fbc8b4db0519efffac91b921f3b0e5834ae5997336`. Only `Vendor/TensorFold/zig/kernels/cuda/qmm_head_sieve.cuh` changes within the editable source.

The immediate parent `424e480a-e74f-4c10-9f01-71784987f7cb` has tree `e103b063127bd2dc4b3e38849519fadc21e38ac0`, combining a live-row selector load guard with a warp first-tile mask, in addition to its earlier scan guards. This child retains that complete parent source and adds the exact first-CTA vote omission from our earlier `4091f4f0-aecd-42e2-9415-8903e25b197b`, donor tree `89e9b64d02bacae0ed21792630c9d2f304b5189d`. That complete donor passed official correctness on spark-6 and scored 2.76493025920656, rejected. The parent passed official correctness on spark-7 and scored 2.73971445245342; it was rejected and its slot settled with admission PASS. Its official source commit 0837b3468b64f3ee12865d02050fd0fca7f5f617 has the expected tree. Neither result measures this combined tree or isolates one contribution.

## Why the first keys CTA can omit the vote

The first exact rescore receives a key array with one entry per live row. Four warps in a CTA process successive key entries. A duplicate valid first tile can be skipped because the first exact projection computes that tile for all live rows. The current source uses a block-wide `__syncthreads_or(live)` in keys mode to detect a CTA where all four warps are redundant, and skips its staged pipeline when no warp is live. That vote keeps all participating warps synchronized before any warp decides to skip.

When the grid-stride loop is executing its first CTA at `base == 0`, warp zero owns item zero. It is in range whenever that loop runs, because the keys-mode item count is the number of live rows. It cannot be a duplicate of an earlier key because no earlier index exists. The existing `live` expression deliberately retains zero or invalid keys on the original path, so they do not make warp zero a duplicate either. Consequently at least one warp is live and the original vote cannot skip this CTA. The candidate guards that vote with the CTA-uniform `base != 0` condition. Every later CTA still takes the original vote and may skip the pipeline when all of its keys are redundant. A zero-row case executes no keys-mode loop.

The same grid wait and launch boundaries, staged copies, pipeline waits, shared-memory barriers and per-warp live guards remain. The selector's live-row loop and full-warp mask collective are unchanged from the parent. The first CTA no longer executes one block-wide synchronization on this path; that is a source-level difference, not a measured instruction or timing reduction. Correctness depends on the stated index and warp conditions, and GPU execution of this exact source has not been measured.

## Why the existing selector matters

The parent skips a float4 load only when all four rows are inactive; its partial-vector scalar row guard remains. It ballots every hit before excluding first tiles and packs the full hit count separately from the emitted count, so the original overflow decision and fallback remain. The donor mask represents first tiles in each warp's 32-tile range and reduces under a warp-uniform nonzero hit ballot. This child does not change those operations. Its first-CTA vote omission is in the later exact rescore kernel, a distinct block from the selector mask.

The 4091 donor passed official correctness in a different full source. The immediate parent's result and this combined result may use different live controls or hardware, and do not establish the isolated effect of the vote omission. Depending on actual first-CTA frequency and GPU scheduling, the additional branch can be neutral or slower. No expected-gain number or effect sum is asserted. The row distribution, amount of duplicate work, generated synchronization and end-to-end latency are unmeasured.

## Verification and release conditions

author: lightminn
body:
Fixes a TERM race in `deploy/console/isaac_live.sbatch`. v-g2 found it while reviewing #322, and Codex reproduced it in plain bash.

**Bug.** The launcher started the supervisor with `… live_supervisor.py … &`, set `SUP=$!`, started the stall watch, and only then set `trap 'kill -TERM "$SUP"' TERM INT`. A TERM in that window — Slurm's, or `reloc_session.sh` ending the launch after its probe failed — killed bash with the default action. Its EXIT trap removes only the Docker bridges, so the supervisor survived and could keep starting sessions.

**Fix.** Operating behaviour is otherwise unchanged.
1. **Trap before the start.** `SUP=""; TERMED=0; on_term() { TERMED=1; [ -n "$SUP" ] && kill -TERM "$SUP"; }; trap on_term TERM INT` is set right before the supervisor starts (after the preflight and the Docker EXIT trap). A TERM during the preflight still ends the launcher, as before.
2. **Latch.** `[ "$TERMED" = 1 ] && kill -TERM "$SUP"` runs right after `SUP=$!`. It covers a TERM between the fork and the assignment.
3. **Repeated wait.** The old "wait, then wait again if alive" is replaced by `while kill -0 "$SUP"; do wait "$SUP"; done; wait "$SUP"; rc=$?` (Codex P2). A trapped TERM cuts `wait` short. With the old form, a second TERM during the supervisor's cleanup made the launcher end before its child. A child that ended between the first wait's 143 and `kill -0` also lost its real exit code.

**Reproduction hook.** `LIVE_TEST_HOLD_FILE` is test-only and unset by default. It sits **between the `&` and `SUP=$!`**: it touches `<file>.at`, then waits up to 30 s for `<file>`.
- It has to sit there. A hook after `SUP=$!` passes even without the latch line (Codex P2).
- The hook starts no background job, so `$!` is kept.

**Tests** (`tests/unit/tools/test_isaac_live_term.py`) run a real launch (not `DRY_RUN`) with fakes:
- `docker` is faked.
- `VENV_PY` is a bash shim: `live_supervisor.py` → a fake supervisor that installs its TERM handler, writes `sup_ready` and its pid, and on the first TERM cleans up for 1–2 s then exits 7; `stall_watch.py` → `sleep`; anything else → the real Python, so the preflight is real.
- Output goes to a file, not a pipe: a surviving child holding the pipe would hang `communicate()`.
- `tmp_path` is the short /tmp root from #325. ws1's pytest basetemp makes the SLAM socket path longer than AF_UNIX's 107 bytes.

The cases:
1. **TERM before `SUP=$!`:** after `.at` and `sup_ready`. Both conditions are required: the supervisor took the TERM and finished (`sup_term0`, `sup_done`, pid gone), and the launcher returned 7. **Before the fix it failed:** the launcher died alone and the supervisor stayed alive.
2. **A second TERM during the cleanup:** the launcher does not end before the supervisor and returns 7.
3. **The hook is inert unless set.**

**Codex.**
- Design consult: agreed with the early trap and the latch; P2 for the repeated wait and the hook position, both taken.
- Code review of 55ffca1a: converged with no findings.
- Notes kept from the consult:
  - Children do not run the parent's `on_term`; they start with the dispositions bash inherited.
  - A non-interactive background job ignores INT and QUIT, so the INT trap's effect is limited when the launcher itself was started with `&`. This PR claims nothing for INT.
  - `stall_watch` ends by itself once the supervisor is gone (next poll, 30 s by default), so no process-group cleanup was added.

**Not in this PR (lead's decision).** The same late-trap pattern in `slam_survey.sbatch`, `isaac_array.sbatch`, `isaac_bundle.sbatch`, `riib_scene.sbatch` and `reloc_session.sh`, and the delayed TERM while a foreground probe runs. The sim-physics session takes them, with this PR as the reference.

**Verification.**
- Full ws1 suite: 8797 passed, 10 failed, all 10 on the known ws1-only list.
- Locally the launcher, preflight and reloc_session tests pass (26).
- The replay gate does not apply: it replays `run_transport` boundary records, and the launcher is not on that path.

author: tuodraek
body:
LSPosed/Vector module (`gcam100x/`) for Google Camera 11.1.040 on a Pixel 9 Pro XL (Tensor G4).

## What it does
- **Startup**: bypasses 11.1's "Invalid version" exit (`isl.a`) so the stock, Google-signed APK runs on the 9 Pro.
- **Pro Zoom flags**: forces `enable_centaur_*`, `boba_jelly_*` and serves the Pixel 10 `centaur_p26` download manifest, so the Pro Zoom model download completes.
- **Slider and preview**: `kkp.j()` gate and `tmp.o()` state forced to ALLOWED in Photo mode on the back camera; the slider goes to 120x and the native beyond-30x viewfinder crop renders. Camera metadata is left at its real 30x max: `kkp.f()` only takes the Pro Zoom branch when the Pro Zoom level exceeds it.
- **Capture**: inside Google Camera's save pipeline (`vnn.g()` on the pending MediaStore item), the JPEG is center-cropped to the chosen zoom (scale = 30/zoom) and, from 40x, rebuilt with a x4 super-resolution model before the item is published. The shot thumbnail (`rrg.c`) is cropped too.
- **Upscaler backend**: realesr-general-x4v3 (Real-ESRGAN, BSD-3) as int8 for the Edge TPU via NNAPI `google-edgetpu`, with a float model for the GPU/CPU fallback; the fastest backend is chosen by benchmark (`tools/convert_x4v3.py`).

## Limitations
- Google's Pro Res Zoom diffusion model (`gldm` encoder/UNet/decoder) ships only as executables precompiled for the Tensor G5 TPU (`santafe_a0`), without the source graph, so it cannot run on the G4. The upscaler here is a different model.
- Obfuscated class names are specific to Google Camera 11.1.040.

## Testing
Built and run on device by the user through several iterations, using logs written to `/sdcard/Android/data/com.google.android.GoogleCamera/files/gcam100x.log`. The TPU backend in v1.4.0 has not been verified on device yet.

author: swissspidy
body:
A compiled check set now goes through an explicit review: it starts as a proposal, a reviewer approves or rejects it, and approval produces a lock that can be signed. The design is in ADR 0013.

## Lifecycle
- A compiled set starts as a proposal.
- **Approve** adds a `locked` lock to the file.
- **Reject** adds `rejected: {by, at, note, content}` to the file. Rejections are not signed, because a rejection only withholds trust.
- An approved set that is later edited shows as changed. A rejected set that is revised becomes a proposal again. A set can't be both locked and rejected; validation reports that as an error.

## Locks
- **Format:** the new lock format is a superset of the old one.
  - New optional fields: `note`, a `content` hash of the normalized set, per-item hashes `items`, a `stress` report hash, `supersedes` and `signature`.
  - The digest covers the content and every lock field except the signature. For an old `{by, at}` lock this is exactly the old formula, so existing locks still verify (frozen legacy fixture included).
- **Tamper detection names what changed**, using the per-item hashes. For example: "changed after approval: requirement R2 changed, check C3 removed". It also catches reordering and edits to the lock itself. A legacy lock can only say that something changed.
- **Signatures:**
  - Ed25519 via `node:crypto`, over `"assay.lock/v1\n" + digest`. The key id is a fingerprint used only to select which trusted key to check against.
  - Trust comes only from the keys the caller supplies; a lock never carries a public key.
  - Signature status is none, unchecked, trusted, untrusted or invalid. An invalid signature counts as a broken lock.
- **Requiring a lock:** `verify`'s `requireLocked` accepts `true` (any valid lock) or `{ trustedKeys }` (must be signed by one of them) and throws `LockError` otherwise. Records gain `locked.signature` and `lockProblems`.
- **Re-review covers the whole set:** an approval is never carried over for unchanged requirements. Instead, the diff tells the reviewer exactly what to re-read, and re-approving is one command.

## Review sheet and diffs
- **Contents:** for each check, the sheet shows:
  - its description and what it tests;
  - the evidence it reads, and how far that evidence can be trusted;
  - its settings, including `onMissing`;
  - its stress findings and warnings;
  - the approval state.
- **Output:** Markdown, GitHub Markdown with unchanged requirements collapsed for PR comments, or HTML. Text from the check set is escaped so it can't inject headings or markup.
- **Diff:** `--diff old.json` gives a semantic diff: requirements and checks added, removed or changed, including `onMissing` and `page` assertions.

## CLI
- `assay keygen [--out alice.pem]` writes the private key with mode 600, plus `alice.pub.pem`.
- `assay review <checks> [--diff old.json] [--stress report.json] [--format markdown|github|html] [--trusted-key …]`
- `assay approve <checks> --reviewer <name> [--key pem | $ASSAY_SIGNING_KEY] [--note] [--stress] [-o]`
- `assay reject <checks> --reviewer <name> --note <text>`
- `assay unlock <checks>`
- `verify` and `validate` gain `--require-signed` and `--trusted-key <file|dir>` (repeatable, or `$ASSAY_TRUSTED_KEYS`). `validate` also gains `--require-locked`, for use as a CI gate.
- Exit codes follow ADR 0010. `validate` exits 1 when a set isn't approved as required.

ADR 0013 includes an example GitHub workflow that takes trusted keys from a repository variable, so a PR can't add its own key.

## Verification
- Merged with main after #22 and #23. Format, lint, typecheck and build pass, the Playwright suite passes (593 tests), and `test:pack` passes 9/9, including a signed approve and verify from the packed tarball.
- Keyless `eval` and `eval:real` give unchanged verdicts.
- Compile replays reproduce the committed files byte for byte.
- Includes a minor changeset.

## Limits
- The stress report identifies its check set only by id and version.
- The approval time is taken from the signer's clock.

---

  * Added a review workflow for check sets, including approval, rejection, and unlocking.
  * Approvals can be signed and verified against trusted keys; verification can require a lock or trusted signature.
  * Review sheets can show changes, validation warnings, and stress-test results in Markdown, HTML, or GitHub formats.
  * Verification identifies edits made after approval, and legacy locks remain verifiable.
* **Documentation**

* **Tests**

author: bruno-andrade-azion
body:
## Summary

- Rebuilds 39 legacy Marketplace template guides, in English and Portuguese, on the How-to skeleton the earlier-migrated template guides use (astro-boilerplate as the structural model, react-boilerplate for the "Key configurations" facts). Each page now has an imperative title, an opening scope sentence, `## Prerequisites`, imperative task sections with `DocSteps`, and `## Next steps` with two `DocCard`s. The old Requirements / Deploying / Setting up / Managing boilerplate is gone, and so are "Fill in the presented fields", "You'll be redirected…" and the "Products menu" click path.
- Terminology and links: the external pricing site is replaced by the internal [Pricing](/en/documentation/fundamentals/pricing/) page (pt-br: Preços), and absolute `https://www.azion.com/en/documentation/...` links are now relative. "Set Origin" becomes **Set Connector**, as the Rules Engine reference names it. "EdgeSQL" becomes SQL Database, the legacy API operation link is replaced, and "edge stack" / "edge latency" / "on the Edge" are gone. In pt-br, "desempenho" is replaced with "performance" and leftover untranslated lines are translated.
- No fact was dropped: versions, field descriptions, defaults and allowed values, repository links, `<Video>` embeds, code blocks, and template-specific sections (static-export support, database setup, QStash schedules, rate-limiting behavior) are all kept. The cross-link text on 8 other pages was updated to the new titles.

Scope: the ticket counted ~43 legacy guides. The current count is 49 guides without Next steps; this PR migrates **39 of them**. The other **10** are also changed by #2582 (MM-16236, Deploy slugs), so they will be migrated in a follow-up PR after #2582 merges, to avoid a conflict: astro-, eleventy-, hugo-, jekyll- and nextjs-ecommerce-collection, gatsby-ecomerce-theme, vuepress-templates-collection, butter-cms, mongodb-template and azion-starter-kit. This PR does not depend on #2582.

Commits are grouped by template family (framework boilerplates, blogs/CMS, databases and LangGraph, functions and Upstash, cache and optimization, cross-link text), so the review can go one commit at a time.

## How to test

1. `cd apps/docs && pnpm build:local`. Expected: the build completes (2092 pages) and `test:frontmatter` passes.
2. Open any migrated guide, for example `/en/documentation/guides/application-development/frameworks/angular-boilerplate/` and its pt-br twin `/pt-br/documentacao/guias/desenvolvimento-de-aplicacoes/frameworks/angular-boilerplate/`. Expected: the new section order, the Deploy link inside the first step, two Next steps cards, and the internal Pricing link.
3. Optional: `pnpm ci:ratchet linkcheck` (161 vs baseline 221), `pnpm ci:ratchet webkit-adoption` (4 vs 56), `pnpm ci:ratchet astro-check` (31 vs 32), `pnpm ci:ratchet slugcheck` (6 vs 6) and `pnpm lint:navcheck`. All pass. `ci/baselines.json` is not updated, because the lower counts cannot be attributed to this PR.

## URL changes and redirects

None. Permalinks, `namespace`s and file names are unchanged, and so are the typo'd pt-br names such as `neon-databse-with-drizzle` and the legacy `edge-*` slugs. Every Console Deploy URL is unchanged byte for byte.

## Notes

Deliberate choices a reviewer may flag:
- **Next steps have two cards**, as the docs-writer how-to skeleton requires. The 12 guides migrated earlier still have four and are not touched here.
- **edge-function-starter-kit** keeps `Products menu > Functions`, copied from the migrated edge-ai-starter-kit guide. The Console path convention belongs to MM-16248 (T36).
- **langgraph-template** keeps "EdgeSQL Shell", because that is the tool's page title and repository name.
- **wordpress-edgeaccelerator** links Cache in Next steps instead of the deprecated Origins page.
- **static-cache** has no "Add a custom domain" section, because the old page did not have one.
- Framework versions are kept as they were. Updating them needs a source this task could not use.

SME follow-ups, also listed in MM-16246:
- Several templates pin old framework versions (for example React 16.13.1, Astro 2.8.0 and 3.x, Next.js 14.x). Should they be updated in the templates and then in the docs?
- jekyll-boilerplate requires Ruby 2.5.0 or higher for a Console-only deployment. Is that only for local development?
- The Cosmic and Sanity templates (and the Docusaurus ones) say the application uses Functions but do not say a function is created. The card labels avoid claiming it.
- clean-astro-sanity: the field is "Sanity Project ID" in en and "Sanity Studio Project ID" in pt-br. Each was kept from its source; which is the Console label?
- langgraph-template: the linked EdgeSQL Shell page carries a caution that the tool fails on a clean install. Should the guide keep recommending it?
- vuepress-boilerplate: the Deploy slug `vuepress--boilerplate` has a double hyphen, matching the Templates reference. Does it resolve?
- Out of scope, Templates reference: name mismatches ("Cosmic + …" vs the guide names, "Vuepress Boilerplate"), and Qwik Minimal listed under the wrong category (review finding 29).

Related issue: MM-16246 (epic MM-16212).

author: benjamindemaille
body:
Refs #547 (item 15).

### What was wrong
`bowtie2-build --bmaxmultsqrt N` (not in the MANUAL, but accepted and listed in the source as "block size as multiplier of sqrt(len)") sets `bmax = OFF_MASK` in `bt2_build.cpp`, and the `Ebwt` constructor then ran `bmax *= bmaxSqrtMult` (`bt2_idx.h:1062`). That multiplies `OFF_MASK` instead of `sqrt(len)` and overflows: for the lambda genome, `--bmaxmultsqrt 4` logs `bmax according to bmaxSqrtMult setting: 4294967292` instead of 880 (= 4 * floor(sqrt(48502))), so the whole suffix array is sorted as a single block. The resulting index is still correct; only the block size (memory use and speed of the build) is wrong.

`git log -S bmaxSqrtMult` shows the same `bmax *= bmaxSqrtMult` in the initial import (74aa525, `ebwt.h`), so there is no earlier correct formula to restore.

### Fix
`bmax = (TIndexOffU)sqrt(s.length()) * bmaxSqrtMult;`, the same expression as the default `bmax = (TIndexOffU)sqrt(s.length())` branch just below it, multiplied by N. One line.

### Testing
- `test_build_inspect.py::test_build_reports_block_settings[--bmaxmultsqrt_4]` (new parameter) checks the log says `bmax according to bmaxSqrtMult setting: <4 * floor(sqrt(n))>`. It fails on master (log shows 4294967292) and passes here.
- `test_build_inspect.py::test_build_strategy_does_not_change_index[--bmaxmultsqrt_4]` (new parameter) checks the index is byte-identical to the default build and inspects/aligns the same. It passes on both (the index never depended on bmax); it guards that the smaller blocks do not change the output.
- Full suite: 615 passed, 14 skipped (master: 613 passed, 14 skipped).

author: el-limon
body:
## Summary

Enshrouded now reports each player's character level to Takaro, so it shows on the player profile, in level history, and fires `player-level-changed` for modules.

## What Changed

- **Manifest**: declares `players.progression` with `source: client-reported`.
- **`getPlayerProgression`**: answers one `character` track with `level`, `experience` and `progress` (`experience / experienceRequired`). `null` for an unknown player, `[]` for a known player with no level read yet or who is offline.
- **Request path**: reads the value the plugin already caches on its two-second refresh, so there is no game-thread work per request.
- **Docs**: new `Player levels and skills` row in the README, plus `capabilities.json` and `API.md`.

## Why client-reported

Characters are stored on the player's PC and travel with them between servers. The server only holds the character while the player is online, so the level is the client's word.

## Reviewer Guide

- **Start here**: `MapProgression` in `mod/src/native/mapping.cpp`, then the handler in `adapter.cpp`.
- **Level below 1**: treated as not loaded yet and left out, so a half-loaded character can never turn the real level into a level-up.
- **`progress` is omitted when `experienceRequired` is 0**, because there is nothing to divide by. The field is optional in the protocol.

## Things to know

- **Stacked on #784**: levels need the `attributes*` layout, which #784 adds for the current game build, and `main`'s pinned build 1273043 no longer downloads anonymously from Steam, so its verify job fails on every Enshrouded PR (#729 too). Merge #784 first, then retarget this to `main`.
- **Other builds**: a build without that layout answers `[]`, and the capability is still declared.
- **Character switches**: joining with a different character reads as a level change, up or down, so a hook on `^character level up` can run again after switching back. The README says so.
- **Skills are not reported**: only the character level.

## Testing Plan

- [x] Native unit tests pass, including the new `bridge-player-progression` groups: track shape, `null`, `[]`, level 0, `progress` capped at 1, the level cap, and the manifest entry.
- [x] Live against a fresh game server registration with a plain client on game build 1287369: progression filled on its own after a join and stayed after leaving; the first reading fired nothing; an experience-only gain fired nothing; a level gain fired one event; switching to a lower character fired one `down`; history and the profile card matched the game.
- [x] Identity fields on the wire are unchanged.
