author: alexrbrowne
body:
## What

A directive closes when the world says the work is done, not when the agent's bookkeeping does. A directive that points at GitHub issues/PRs stays open while any of them is open and closes once they are all closed; a directive's commitment that was "delivered" by an email back to the originator does not close it (unless the directive itself asked for a message); the commitment registered for a directive now names the linked work rather than the subject line.

## Why

Mini-2, 2026-11-05, 21:48. The founder's "Priority Number 1" (focus all attention on innovology.io#228) was restored by hand after the reconciler had withdrawn it (#121). Thirty minutes later it was gone again: the directive's commitment read `Action the directive: Priority Number 1`, the CEO verified it as `email to alexander.browne — "Re: Priority Number 1"` (her reply asking him to paste the issue), the commitment went `delivered`, and `_open_directives` pruned the directive as handled. #228 had not been touched.

The reply-alone rule already existed as prompt text ("never count it handled on a reply alone") — the commitment path bypassed it.

Stacked on #121.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Tests — `tests/test_directive_grounding.py` gains 3 tests and one is extended: a delivery whose artifact is an email to the originator (or no artifact at all) leaves the directive open, and the commitment names the issue URL; a directive that asks for a message ("Send me the W45 brief") IS delivered by one; a directive about an open issue stays open even when its commitment is delivered with a real PR, an unreadable blip on re-check never voids what was read, and it closes once the issue is closed; open references are re-checked each wake and closed ones are not. 12/12 in that file; `test_inactive_agents`, `test_wake_recovery`, `test_fabric_extended`, `test_escalation_routing` 110/110. Full suite: 1,731 passed, 1 failed — `tests/integration/test_lifecycle.py::test_single_agent_cycle`, which fails identically on #121 without this change (pre-existing).
- [x] Exercised locally or in staging — the exact 21:48 case is the first new test; hot-patched onto Mini-2 (details in the PR comment).
- [x] Adjacent paths spot-checked — directives without GitHub references and without a delivered commitment are unchanged; a directive handed off to someone else (commitment `to` ≠ originator) still closes on delivery; the TTL backstop is untouched; `_ground_directives` is still bounded at 8 references per pass, with unread references ahead of re-checks.

## How

- `_open_directives`: references that were read decide first — any `open` → directive open; all `closed`/`merged` → handled. Otherwise a `delivered` commitment closes it only when `_delivered_by_reply` is false.
- `_delivered_by_reply(commitment, directive)`: commitment owed to the originator, directive words don't ask for a message, and the artifact is empty or an email (`outbox/email`, `.eml`, `mailto:`, or verification starting "email").
- `_ground_directives`: read-and-open references are re-read on each pass after the unread ones; a re-read that comes back unreadable is ignored (the earlier read stands).
- `_record_directives`: the commitment's `what` appends "deliver <urls> (closes when the issue/PR is closed; a reply is not delivery)".

## Observability Impact

**Observability Impact:** One extra GitHub read per open reference per wake (bounded at 8 per pass). No new log lines, events or service boundaries.

## ADR / RFC Reference

**ADR/RFC:** N/A — tightens the existing directive-handled rule; no architectural change

## AI Delegation

**AI Delegation:** Claude traced the second disappearance of the founder's directive on the live node to the commitment/verification path and drafted the change and tests; human review requested on the reply-detection heuristics and on whether "all references closed" should close a directive without any delivery.

**Prompt owner:** @alexrbrowne

## Agent Review Prompt

**Change summary:** Directives referencing GitHub work stay open while that work is open; an email reply to the originator never closes a directive unless it asked for one
**Risks:** backwards-compat — a directive that was satisfied by a reply the originator accepted now lingers until the 3-day TTL unless its words asked for a message; data-integrity — none, `directives.json` gains no fields
**Human review focus:** `_DIRECTIVE_ASKS_FOR_REPLY` wording list, and whether closed-references-without-delivery should count as handled

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added / updated
- [x] `ruff check .` passes
- [x] `mypy src/` passes
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable) — N/A — internal behaviour
- [x] ADR/RFC reference filled above
- [x] AI Delegation field filled above
- [x] No secrets or credentials in this diff

author: ryanmrodriguez
body:
## Problem

When a queue is shared by many teams, the Failed list can't answer "which of these are mine?". Resque setups often solve this with a code owners view. Flightdeck has nothing like it.

## Change

An **Owners** page listing failed jobs per class, with each class's owners and counts for the last 1h, 3h, 24h, 3d and 7d. It's off by default, with one setting to turn it on:

```ruby
Flightdeck.configure do |config|
  config.codeowners_path = ".github/CODEOWNERS"
end
```

Until that's set there's no sidebar link, and `/owners` shows a short setup message.

- **Owners** come from the host's CODEOWNERS file, following GitHub's rules: the last match wins, and a rule with no owners clears ownership. Each class is matched by the file that defines it rather than a naming convention, so components and engines resolve like any other path.
- **Unowned:** a class that can't be loaded, or is defined outside the repo (`ActionMailer::MailDeliveryJob`), shows as Unowned.
- **Filtering:** owner chips and a case-insensitive class search. Both work in Ruby, since every class is already in memory, so they add no query.
- **Links:** class names and counts open the Failed list, filtered by class and time window.

### `failed_within`

The links need a new `failed_within` filter on `JobsQuery`. It's carried in `list_filters`, so pagination, tabs, polling and "Retry/Discard all matching" all see the same rows. Only failed jobs can have failed recently, so with a window on, All matches Failed and the other tabs show 0.

This changes which rows the bulk actions select, so it's the part most worth reviewing. A single-row discard still ignores list filters, as it already does for class and queue.

The Filter button also used to drop an active `class_name`. It now keeps it, and the jobs page shows the class and window as chips.

## Worth knowing

- **Still failed, not a history:** Solid Queue deletes a failed execution on retry or discard, so a window counts jobs that failed in it and are still failed. The page says so.
- **Loading classes:** finding a class's file means resolving the constant. This never touches job arguments, and a class that fails to load shows as Unowned rather than breaking the page.
- **Deploys:** CODEOWNERS has to be present where the dashboard runs, and many images leave out `.github`. If it's missing, the page says so.
- **Cost:** the page runs one grouped query over `failed_executions`, which has no `created_at` index. It's cached for `chart_cache_ttl`, and the page polls at the chart interval.
- **Overlap with #19:** both change `apply_filters` in `jobs_query.rb`, so whichever merges second needs a small conflict fix. Class search on the Failed list is currently a prefix match, so the Total row stops linking during a search, because the same search there could show something different.

## Testing

- `bin/test` passes: 339 tests in both host modes, on SQLite. Rubocop and the asset check are clean.
- Bulk retry and discard have tests proving they leave jobs outside the window alone. Those tests fail if the window is dropped from `list_filters`.
- CODEOWNERS matching is covered for anchoring, `*`, `**`, `?`, `dir/*`, escapes and last-match overrides.
- `bin/demo` seeds a sample CODEOWNERS and overlapping job classes, so the page can be tried by hand. These live in `test/dummy` and don't ship in the gem.
- **Not yet run:** PostgreSQL and MySQL, which need CI here. The new SQL is plain `SUM(CASE WHEN ...)` and has no adapter-specific code. The page was checked with HTTP requests against the demo, not in a real browser, and the system tests weren't run.

author: codeshaunted
body:
## Issue Reference

Refs #5233 ([BAMLGH-103](https://linear.app/boundaryml2/issue/BAMLGH-103)). Does not close it: `#[instrument]`, a span guard and `trace::run` still need new C ABI entries and a proc-macro crate.

## Changes

- A Rust host can now create a span, so its own work and the BAML calls inside it land in one trace tree:

  ```rust
  let span = trace::start_span_sync("load_batch".to_owned(), Some(inputs), None, metadata, None)?;
  let rows = span.run_sync(|| load_batch(batch_id))?;
  span.finish_sync(rows)?;
  ```

- `sdkgen_rust` narrows the Rust type of a parameter to what a host can supply (`host_types::narrow_argument`):
  - A `reflect.AnyFunction` union arm is dropped, so `string | AnyFunction` takes `String`. A parameter that is only `AnyFunction` still skips.
  - `unknown` is taken as `baml_bridge::Json`, including inside lists, maps and optionals. Return types and fields are unchanged and still skip.
- Arguments are still stated under the declared type. The engine rejects `map<string, json>` for `map<string, unknown>`, so narrowing the type in the pool does not work.

## For review

- **Wider than `start_span`.** The `unknown` rule is general, so user functions with `unknown` parameters are now emitted, and so are 18 other stdlib symbols, some of them internal (`baml.host.call_host_value`, `baml.ops.equals_equals`, `baml._hash_structural_default`). All 20 newly emitted symbols are listed by diffing `baml generate --show-all-skips`. If that is too broad, the rule can be limited to `trace.*`.
- **Inner call names.** In `baml query`, non-retained calls made inside `run` are correctly parented to the span, but their future rows are named after the span (`load_batch`), not the function (`hello_world`). I did not trace the cause or compare with Python. This PR does not touch the engine.
- **Noise.** Each SDK call is its own root future, so `trace.start_span`, `trace.Span.run` and `trace.Span.is_closed` appear as root rows, and the span's parent is its `trace.start_span` future.
- **Limitations.** `run` closures must be `Send + 'static`. `Span.fail_with_context` is still skipped because `baml.errors.Context` is not emitted; `fail` covers it. `metadata` values need `trace::StringOrIntOrFloatOrBool`.

## Testing

```sh
cargo nextest run -p sdkgen_rust                 # 95 passed
BOUNDARY_API_KEY=local cargo nextest run --no-fail-fast -p sdk_test_rust   # 17 passed
mise run fmt && mise run clippy
cargo insta test --test-runner nextest --dnd -p baml_cli --all-features --unreferenced=reject
```

- The `baml_cli` run had 2 failures in `skill_warning_e2e`, caused by running with `DEV_BAML_CLI_DISABLE_AGENT_DETECTION=1`. That binary passes 15/15 without the variable.
- New `host_spans` tests in `test_invocation.rs` cover sync and async `run`, an explicit parent, and a closed span.
- Checked by hand with `BOUNDARY_API_KEY=local` and `baml query` on the recordings: inputs, metadata, output and `fail` values are recorded, and `child` is parented to `parent`.
- Not tested: an LLM function inside a span. The fixtures here only make non-LLM calls.

* **Improvements**
  * Rust SDK-generated function arguments now represent unknown values as JSON, including unknown values in maps.
  * Function-valued alternatives are omitted from generated argument signatures when a union contains other supported types. Declared wire types remain unchanged.

author: bartvhelvert
body:
## What this changes

Notebook UI tests repeatedly start a backend and client with identical installations and settings. Reuse one pair for the class, reducing the original twelve pair startups to one while preserving separate JUnit cases. Each scenario closes editors, uses a fresh notebook URI, resets fixture state and execution order, and discards the pair after failure.

Keep log checks scoped to each scenario with per-file backend log offsets, including logs created later. Set Starter's working directory to the checkout root so its outputs match existing CI cache and artifact paths.

For two matching notebook scenarios, observed wall time fell from **96.64 s to 68.27 s (29.4%)**; recorded JUnit time fell from 84.303 s to 38.754 s. These are individual experimental runs, not a measured full-suite speedup. Candidate wall time includes source synchronization and recompilation; baseline called Gradle directly against an existing Linux copy. JUnit time excludes final class teardown, while wall time includes it.

Fixes #95

## How it was tested

- All UI launches ran in Ubuntu-24.04 under Xvfb at 1920x1080; none ran on the Windows host.
- All **41 UI tests passed across resumed batches**, including a new regression that executes a cell and verifies fresh notebook contents and execution state in the next scenario.
- Final notebook class: 13 tests passed, 157.497 s recorded JUnit time, 180.17 s wall time.
- Added and passed a backend-log regression covering multiple files, newly created logs, and nested frontend exclusions. Reran notebook undo after the final log change.
- Full unit/integration suite ran once: **1,475 tests, zero failures/errors, nine skips**. Eight skips are Windows-only; one socket LSP fixture lacked npm dependencies.
- `git diff --check` passed.

WSL memory contention interrupted earlier UI batches, so verification combines saved passes rather than claiming one uninterrupted full run. An initial interrupted run logged an IntelliJ Java-plugin SDK initialization exception without a finalized JUnit failure; subsequent verification of the affected cases passed.

author: karthik-ramanathan-3006
body:
## Summary

When the source session sets `yb_alter_type_reuse_expr_and_partial_indexes` to a value other than the target's, a typmod-only `ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE` reuses expression and partial indexes on one side and rebuilds them on the other. Replication does not error or pause, so the two clusters silently diverge on the index's DocDB table.

Add the GUC to `xcluster_ddl_replication_gucs.def`, so the source records its value in each `ddl_queue` entry and the target sets it before replaying the DDL.

## Upgrade/Rollback safety

Each `ddl_queue` entry now carries one more variable. A target without this change ignores it and logs a warning, as it does for any variable not in its list. A source without this change does not send it, so a target with this change replays with its own value; that case behaves as it did before this change.

- [x] `./yb_build.sh --cxx-test xcluster_ddl_replication-test --gtest_filter XClusterDDLReplicationTest.AlterColumnTypmodReuseExprAndPartialIndexes`

author: ashhart
body:
Part of #2102. #2103 made `DeviceBuffer.download` stage through a per-thread pinned buffer on integrated GPUs such as the GB10, where a synchronous copy into pageable memory can miss pages. Discrete cards keep the direct copy.

This moves every other synchronous device-to-host copy on main onto the same path. There are 54, not the 18 we first counted: 27 in family code and developer tools, and 27 in device tests. Each destination is stack or allocator memory, so on a GB10 each had the exposure `download` had. They now go through `cuda.memory.download`, a borrowed device span handed to `DeviceBuffer.download`. The shared path keeps both driver calls it already had: the direct copy on discrete cards, and the copy into the pinned bounce on integrated ones. The attribute gate, the 4 MiB pieces, per-thread reuse and host accounting are as #2103 left them.

**Bytes copied don't change.** Each replaced call is checked against its original source address, destination and byte count. Host tests cover the routing on a fake driver, integrated against discrete.

author: andreas-garcia
body:
## Summary

On staging, typing several artist searches in a row shows "It seems that you are not connected to the internet" even though the connection is fine. The staging API answers `200`, but in 0.4–1 s (up to ~4 s), while the search debounce is 250 ms. So the next query often starts while the previous one is still in flight.

When the query key changes, React Query aborts the superseded request through the `signal` that `useArtistSearch` passes to `fetch`. `fetchWrapper` mapped that `AbortError` to `NET1006`, which became a `NetworkError`. `handleError` then raised the global connectivity error, and `useConnectivityErrorPopup` showed `NetworkErrorPopup`, whose only text is the offline message.

A related problem: any fetch `TypeError` (CORS, connection reset, a gateway error without CORS headers) also showed "not connected to the internet" while the browser was online.

## Changes

- `fetchWrapper`: a request aborted by its caller's own signal (`signal.aborted`, whatever the abort reason) is rethrown as-is, with no `handleError` call and no AppError mapping. An `AbortError` without an aborted caller signal, and `AbortSignal.timeout()` (`TimeoutError`), are still reported.
- `useConnectivityErrorPopup`: `renderNetworkErrorPopup` receives the `ErrorCode`.
- `NetworkErrorPopup` (app-kit-ui): new required `errorCode` prop. It shows the offline text only for `NETWORK_OFFLINE`; other network failures read "We couldn't reach the server. Please try again in a moment."
- Playground updated. CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` has a **Breaking** entry and two **Fixed** entries.

### Breaking / migration

Consumers must pass the code through:

```tsx
renderNetworkErrorPopup: (errorCode) => <NetworkErrorPopup errorCode={errorCode} />
```

grow-the-music-tree-frontend (`src/app/AppContent.tsx` and its `NetworkErrorPopup` wrapper) and hear-the-music-tree-frontend need this when they bump. TypeScript flags the missing prop, so the change can't be missed silently. Rollback: revert this PR, or keep consumers on 32.x.

## Test plan

- [x] New tests:
  - a caller-aborted request rejects with the original `AbortError`, without calling `handleError` or the error factory;
  - a caller abort with a custom reason is rethrown, not reported;
  - an `AbortError` with a signal that is present but not aborted is still reported;
  - a `TimeoutError` from an aborted timeout signal is still reported;
  - the existing "does not retry an aborted GET" test now expects the rejection;
  - `renderNetworkErrorPopup` receives the code;
  - `NetworkErrorPopup` shows the offline text vs. the server-unreachable text depending on the code.
- [x] `pnpm lint`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm test` (app-kit 580, app-kit-ui 432 passed). Full turbo runs twice showed 15 failures in `GenrePlaylistTracks.test.tsx`, which this PR doesn't touch; they pass when app-kit-ui runs alone (432/432), so they look like load flakiness under the parallel turbo run.
- [ ] After release and the consumer bump: on staging, type several artist searches quickly and check that no network popup appears.

## Review

- Intent: fix, with a public contract change (`NetworkErrorPopup` prop, `renderNetworkErrorPopup` signature) → deep depth.
- One independent reviewer on the final diff: no confirmed bug. Risks raised and handled:
  - a custom abort reason (`controller.abort("x")`) would still have raised the popup → the check now relies on `signal.aborted` and excludes only `TimeoutError`;
  - callers passing their own `signal` outside React Query now get a rejection instead of `null` → documented in the CHANGELOG Breaking entry;
  - missing tests (signal present but not aborted, timeout signal) → added.
- Limits: React Query v5 ignoring a late rejection after cancel is known from its behavior, not exercised end to end here; the staging check waits for a release and the consumer bump.

body:
Second round of this cycle: the remaining issues from external reporters. Stacked on #978 (base `integratie/issues-2026.44.9`); it will be retargeted to `main` once #978 is merged. No version bump and no release.

Fixes #880, Fixes #919, Fixes #932, Fixes #945, Fixes #951, Fixes #952, Fixes #959, Fixes #963, Fixes #969
Refs #953

## What is in it

- **Extract (#880):** goes through the Split path. Refuses still-encrypted bytes (they produced fully blank pages), remaps or drops links and `/P` references that pulled other pages and their images into the file, and uses the bytes a save would write when the document has unsaved changes.
- **OCR (#880):** recognized words are searchable right away, before the file is saved; on pages with /Rotate 90/270 the text layer now lands on the page instead of beside it.
- **Text box Esc (#951):** Esc keeps the typed text; only a just-drawn box that is still empty is removed (one undo step).
- **Merge with page choice (#963):** a page range per file in the Merge dialog, with the thumbnail chooser. Bookmarks, named destinations, links, form fields, layers and page labels that point at dropped pages are removed or cut loose, so no orphan page is copied.
- **Same document in more tabs (#919):** "New Tab for This Document" on the tab menu. Tabs are views on one shared document (annotations, undo, modified state, save), each with its own page, zoom, scroll, rotation and view mode.
- **Interface size and workspaces (#932):** 80/90/110% added to the existing UI scale with a live preview; navigation and properties panel state is remembered across restarts; named workspaces (save, apply, delete, reset) under View > Workspace.
- **File Explorer verbs (#945):** "Combine into one PDF", "Convert to PDF" and "Convert and combine", written and removed by both installer variants in their own hive. Multi-selection reaches one instance through a Rust queue and a short collection window; Combine opens the Merge dialog in a new-document mode with natural name order.
- **Extension catalogue (#969):** Installed / Browse / Add custom tabs, `extensions.json` plus schema at the repo root (empty list; authors add themselves by PR), install by link, update detection. Downloads run in Rust: https only on every redirect hop, size limits, sha256 check when known, package inspection and expected-id check, nothing executed.
- **Measurement interchange (#959):** perimeter and area now write the full ISO 32000 `/Measure` dictionary (`/X`, `/D`, `/A`) also when the scale comes from the page; foreign perimeters and areas without `/Contents` compute their value from their own `/Measure`; `/D` unit conversions are honoured.
- **Share / send (#952, #953):** Android share sheet, Windows MAPI mail with the PDF attached (fallback: mailto draft plus reveal in Explorer), `xdg-email --attach` on Linux, Web Share in the browser. Unsaved changes: save and send, or send a copy. Mobile gets a More menu with share, insert image, take photo, scan document to a page, and copy/paste/delete markup.

- `cargo check -p open-pdf-studio -p pdfium-worker --lib --bins` (MSVC): pass

author: nishit-sharma
body:
## Why

Two pieces of work in one branch, as separate commits:

1. **Office check-in.** Let managers see who is in the office and whether each clock-in met the office's verification rule. This is not payroll or continuous tracking.
2. **Citius Journal.** Rebuild the blog as an editorial magazine for both pilgrims and corporate/MICE readers, designed to look complete with only a few stories.

## Office check-in (`8c737dea`)

- **Rule per office.** An Admin chooses office network, location, both, or either. The server evaluates every named signal on the clock-in request itself; staff cannot pick an easier method. Results are pass, fail or uncertain. Missing, denied, stale, imprecise or VPN-shared signals are uncertain, never fail.
- **Trusted IP only.** The client IP is read from Vercel's `x-forwarded-for` by `POST /api/portal/office-check-in`, only after opt-in via `OFFICE_CHECK_IN_CLIENT_IP_SOURCE=vercel-edge`. It is forwarded to Convex with a server-only `OFFICE_CHECK_IN_GATEWAY_SECRET`. Any IP in the request body is ignored.
- **Location.** Requested only when Clock in or Clock out is pressed. `Permissions-Policy` allows `geolocation=(self)` on `/portal` only; the public site keeps it blocked.
- **Report only by default.** Enforce needs explicit, audited confirmation on every save. In Enforce mode a non-passing check-in is held for review rather than refused. Clock-out is never blocked.
- **Oversight follows existing roles.**
  - Admin, Directors, Director Cement and HR see all offices.
  - Department heads see same-office staff in their department, using the leave-approval mapping, and never the all-office roles.
  - Line managers see direct reports.
  - Nobody reviews their own record.
  - Review, time correction, manual entry and retry are audited with a reason.
- **Privacy.** No raw coordinates or full IPs are stored, only outcome, reason, distance band, rounded accuracy and a /24 or /48 prefix. Managers see no prefixes. Check-ins and attendance audit rows are purged after 92 days by a new controlled daily job (`jobs.purge_office_check_ins`).
- **New view.** Admin → Office check-in, with My day, Today in the office, and Office rules sections.
- **Docs.** `docs/adr/0017-office-check-in-verification-evidence.md` (status: Proposed), `docs/office-check-in/OFFICE_CONFIGURATION.md`, `docs/office-check-in/DIRECTOR_GUIDE.md`, and new terms in `CONTEXT.md`.

## Citius Journal (`261f5b8d`)

- **Pages.** The listing and article pages are server-rendered. Newsreader is scoped to the Journal. Content is visible on first paint, with no scroll-gated fade.
- **Reading.** Readable body measure, dates like "2 August 2026", and reading time counted from words.
- **Images.** Covers are uncropped with no text overlaid. Image URLs use the editor's hotspot, and alt text falls back sensibly when empty.
- **Search.** BlogPosting and BreadcrumbList JSON-LD, `/blog` added to the sitemap, and an archive beyond 12 stories.
- **Sanity schema.** Adds optional excerpt, image alt and caption, related Spiritual Trail, and author role and office.
- **Nav label.** Stays "Blog" by decision.
- **Docs.** `docs/citius-journal/EDITOR_GUIDE.md`.

## Verification (local only)

- **Static checks.** `typecheck`, `convex:typecheck`, `lint:all`, the lint ratchet (0/0), the dead-code ratchet and `coverage:check` all pass.
- **Tests.**
  - `bun run test`: 2054 pass.
  - `bun run test:convex`: 129 pass, which covers the existing CRM suites, so no regressions there.
  - The check-in tests cover authorization and office isolation; IPv4, IPv6, VPN and proxy cases; geofence inside, outside and uncertain; denied permission, timeout and stale readings; duplicate and concurrent clock-in; retry; manager review; clock-out; and retention.
- **Committed state.** Typecheck, Convex typecheck, the contract tests and the feature tests were rerun on the committed tree alone.
- **Rendered check-in view.** Fixture data in Chromium and WebKit at 320 to 1440px, with keyboard, reduced-motion and contrast checks. Firefox did not launch locally.
- **Rendered Journal.** Local `next dev` with read-only Sanity fetches.
- **Review.** An independent backend review found no critical issues and 4 important ones, all fixed.
- **Not run.** `quality:target-neutral` pins Bun 1.4.0 and the machine has 1.4.3.

**Not yet verified:** real office networks, phones and desktops, a screen reader, and anything on a deployed environment.

## Deploy notes

1. Set the same random `OFFICE_CHECK_IN_GATEWAY_SECRET` in Vercel and in the Convex deployment.
2. Confirm nothing proxies the custom domain, then set `OFFICE_CHECK_IN_CLIENT_IP_SOURCE=vercel-edge` in Vercel. Until then the IP is recorded as unavailable (uncertain).
3. Run `migrateOperationalControlCatalog`, or set "Office check-in retention" to Available, so the purge job runs.
4. Deploy the Sanity Studio (`cd citius-blog && bun run deploy`) so editors see the new fields.
5. Keep every office in Report only until the pilot exit criteria in `OFFICE_CONFIGURATION.md` are met.

## Known follow-ups

- **Amber badge contrast.** The shared amber badge measures 4.37:1 (`portalWorkspaceListUi.tsx`), just below WCAG AA.
- **Dialog focus.** The shared `ControlledDialog` can lose focus after a full Tab cycle.
- **Proxy check.** Confirm on a deployed preview that office and home clock-ins show different network prefixes.

author: wildhemp
body:
## Executive summary

**What this does**
- When the register charges a card at the end of a checkout, the SDK now tells the terminal how to treat Bilt loyalty for that charge.
- If the register turned off points redemption, or points were already redeemed earlier in the same checkout, the terminal is told loyalty is already handled: it will not offer Bilt's hosted checkout again, but the shopper still earns points.
- If the register turned off both points redemption and points earning, the terminal is told loyalty is not allowed: no hosted checkout and no automatic earning.
- In every other case nothing changes on the wire.

**Why**
- Without this signal, a terminal could offer the shopper a second way to pay with points after the register had already redeemed them, or after the register had said not to.

**What it costs / risks**
- Only the card charge at checkout changes; gift card charges, refunds and voids are untouched.
- The integrator guides and reference docs now list the four cases.
- Ships as SDK release 0.42.0.

## Summary
`PaymentOrchestrator.cardStep` builds the only card `PaymentRequest` in the settlement sequence. It now sets `PaymentTransaction.TransactionConditions.LoyaltyHandling` from `SettlementOptions` and whether the `POINT_REDEMPTION` step ran (was not skipped) earlier in the same attempt:

```
disablePoints && disableAward      -> Forbidden
disablePoints || pointRedemptionRan -> Processed
otherwise                           -> no TransactionConditions (unchanged)
```

Nothing else set `TransactionConditions` on this request before, so there is no `forceEntryMode` to preserve. The stored value `Payment` (gift card charge) and the `ReversalManager` refund `Payment`s are not card charges and are left alone. The JS SDK settles through the session host's Java orchestrator and builds no Nexo `Payment` itself, so `js/` is unchanged.

Docs: `SettlementOptions` javadoc (getters and builder setters, regenerated `docs/javadoc` with temurin-21.0.7), a mapping table under "The settlement sequence explained" in `docs/checkout-session-integration.md`, a pointer from the settlement options list in `docs/javascript-sdk-integration.md`, and a CHANGELOG entry under `[0.42.0]` (`VERSION` bumped 0.41.0 → 0.42.0 for `check-version`).

Linear: RET-7598

## Verification
- `./gradlew spotlessCheck :java:test`: green.
- `./gradlew build` (all modules, the CI `build.yml` target): green.
- New `TerminalShopperSessionPaymentTest` cases read the `LoyaltyHandling` off the JSON the mock terminal received: guest defaults (absent), identified member after a point redemption (`Processed`), `disablePoints` (`Processed`), `disablePoints` + `disableAward` (`Forbidden`).

author: mrkbac
body:
Port of lichtblick-suite/lichtblick#1351 (fixes lichtblick-suite/lichtblick#1350).

## Problem
On a live source, latched topics (e.g. `/tf_static`) are sent once. A panel that subscribes later — e.g. a 3D panel on another tab of a Tab panel — only gets them via the pipeline's cached last message, and that hand-off failed:

1. `MessagePipeline/store.ts` deleted the cached message when a topic's last subscriber left (on a tab switch the old tab unsubscribes before the new one subscribes).
2. `PanelExtensionAdapter` got the injected frame before its local subscriptions (React state) included the topic, so the render state builder filtered it out.
3. The injected frame was dropped if the panel was not initialized yet or still rendering.

## Fix
- Store keeps the cache for players without `playbackControl`; playback (seek-backfill) is unchanged.
- New `UndeliveredMessages` in the adapter holds the latest message of each requested topic on live sources until a rendered frame delivers it; if messages are still held when a render finishes, it renders again.

Upstream code applied cleanly; only change for licht is `jest.fn` → `vi.fn`.

## Tests
Fail before / pass after:
- `MessagePipeline/index.test.tsx`: live player keeps the last message and injects it into the next subscriber (playback player does not).
- `PanelExtensionAdapter.test.tsx`: injected message delivered after the in-flight render finishes, exactly once when idle, and when the panel starts watching `currentFrame` mid-render.
- `undeliveredMessages.test.ts`: unit tests for the helper.

Typecheck, oxlint and the PanelExtensionAdapter + MessagePipeline vitest suites pass.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Live-source messages are now retained until a panel is ready to render them, so panels receive the latest message after rendering resumes—even if no new frame arrives.
  * Resubscribing delivers the retained message only once. Messages from playback-controlled sources continue to follow playback behavior without injecting stale cached messages.

author: mrkbac
body:
Port of the idea from upstream lichtblick-suite/lichtblick#1330.

`messagesToDataset` marks a gap (null value) with a `{y: NaN}` point after flushing the last datum, but `downsampleStates` pushed unlabelled points straight to the output while the current pixel interval was still open. The open interval was emitted later, out of x order, and a segment resuming with the same state after the gap was merged into the interval before it, so the gap disappeared.

Fix: an unlabelled point now finishes the open interval first (clamping a multi-state interval's synthetic end to the gap's x) and starts fresh after it.

Tests: two new `downsampleStates` cases (same state on both sides of a gap; multi-state interval ending at a gap in the same pixel), both failing before the fix. StateTransitions tests pass.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved time-based charts when data contains gaps or repeated states. Intervals with multiple states now end at a nearby gap instead of extending past it, and state segments after a gap remain separate. Repeated states within the same chart interval no longer incorrectly replace the multi-state summary, helping charts represent these transitions more accurately. For single-state intervals, the final repeated point is retained so the state band extends to the correct position.

author: samuelschlesinger
body:
Supply one total native word function whose canonical behavior is exactly the existing `moduleLWEKeyGen`, serialized by `ModuleLWE.encodeSample`. The public theorem quantifies one plain polynomial-time certificate over every unary rank/degree, binary positive modulus, structured module matrix, and signed integer secret/error lift. Its private witness reuses the existing framing and number decoders, the upstream padded list dot product, binary remainder and the existing pair/list codecs; it adds no public encryption algorithm or alternate codec.

The matrix input is the full structured `(k*n)`-square expansion from `ModuleSIS.encodeMatrix`; all raw words and discarded entries count toward runtime. Positivity is needed only for the canonical residue interpretation; rank/degree may be zero and `q=1` is included. This is deterministic key generation from supplied inputs. Native construction of the structured matrix from sampled polynomial coefficients, randomized key generation, seed compression, encryption/decryption and security remain open. Independently sampling an expanded scalar matrix would give a different law.

This is original implementation algebra, not a source-attributed security result. The semantic bridge uses `ModuleLWE.flattenPolyVec_sample` and the shared integer-cast dot-product identity. Checked clients obtain the same certified function for signed rank-two/degree-two arithmetic modulo six (output coefficients `[[1,2],[5,1]]`), modulus one, both zero-dimension cases and a 129-bit modulus. Separate checks show the reused parsers' incomplete-frame and negative-zero behavior without claiming input validation. The operator manual and ROADMAP state the remaining boundary; selected formal abstracts have no changed statement or scope, and this implementation milestone is not proposed as a headline.

The prerequisite #2730 has landed. Restacked onto main at `ef604fab7ab6a8273ec432d9a63ea108cc6fa0b1`: all changed-file payloads and owned Lean/test blobs are identical to reviewed `5f5062c52`; only surrounding aggregate/manual context changed. Fresh full `scripts/check.sh` passed all eight gates. Earlier hygiene and duplicate audits cover the identical payload. Fresh native Pandoc/XeLaTeX rendering and `--check-build` passed; affected PDF page 139 (printed 133) was inspected. Existing composition rules sufficed after fixing intermediate encodings explicitly; no new machine or tidy machinery was introduced.

Closes #2721. AI-assisted implementation and validation by Codex (`codex-crypto-20261105/ring`); independent agent review is not human approval.

author: vicgopfert
body:
## Item

**B-72** (M, E5), ajuste de design depois do PR #73: na visão geral de recomendações, "Para você" e cada prateleira viram uma fileira horizontal só com as capas de 5 jogos. A página do "ver mais" continua como está.

O PR também registra os itens B-77, B-78 e B-79 (etiquetas da comunidade Steam) e o congelamento do modelo de recomendação, por decisão do autor.

## Critério de conclusão

Subitem do B-72 no `BACKLOG.md`: "na visão geral, 'Para você' e cada prateleira viram uma fileira horizontal só com as capas de 5 jogos e 'Ver mais'; a página do 'ver mais' continua como está, com os cartões e a frase do 'Pouco conhecido'".

- Na visão geral, todas as listas são fileiras de 5 capas, com "Ver mais" ao lado do título.
- A página do "ver mais" mantém os cartões completos, com o motivo e os selos.
- Com várias prateleiras, elas passam a caber nas primeiras telas.

**Status: concluído.**

## O que muda

- **`apps/api/config/recommendation.json`:**
  - `overviewMainSize` vai de 20 para 5 e `overviewShelfSize` de 10 para 5, com a justificativa no `overviewSizesRationale`;
  - `shelfMinItems` continua 4.
- **`apps/web`:**
  - `cover-row.tsx`: a fileira de capas, com 5 colunas a partir de 640 px e rolagem horizontal com encaixe abaixo disso. O nome do jogo é o nome acessível do link e aparece no `title`.
  - `GameCover`: ganha o tamanho `fluid`, com a proporção da capa fixa e a imagem recortada. Sem capa, o quadro mostra o nome.
  - `recommendations-view.tsx`: "Para você" e as prateleiras usam a fileira.
  - A frase que explica o "Pouco conhecido" fica só no "ver mais", onde está o selo (`BasisNote` com `withBadges`).
  - A opção de nível de título do cartão, criada no B-72 só para a visão geral, foi removida: a visão geral não tem mais cartões.
- **Testes:** os da visão geral passam a conferir as fileiras. Os da API e o e2e conferem que a visão geral mostra o começo da página 1 do "ver mais", e não ela inteira.
- **Docs:**
  - `docs/proposta-tecnica.md`: tópicos "Layout" e "Títulos" do B-72; registro dos itens B-77 a B-79 na seção 13; ordem e congelamento na seção 14; capacidade recontada;
  - `docs/recomendacao.md`: tamanhos e comparação das respostas;
  - `BACKLOG.md`: subitem do ajuste, itens B-77 a B-79, congelamento e notas no B-44.

## Decisões e desvios

Por decisão do autor:
- **Fileira e celular:** fileira horizontal só com as capas, inclusive em "Para você", com 5 jogos em cada. Rolagem horizontal abaixo de 640 px e 5 colunas daí para cima.
- **Nome do jogo:** é o nome acessível do link e fica no `title`, sem texto visível.
- **"Ver mais":** ao lado do título da fileira.
- **Ordem das prateleiras:** continua a da API até o B-79.
- **`shelfMinItems`:** mantido em 4.
- **Frase do "Pouco conhecido":** só no "ver mais".
- **Efeito dos tamanhos novos:** só registrado.
- **Sem item novo:** é ajuste de design do B-72; os layouts serão refeitos com a designer.
- **B-44:** observar se os jogadores reconhecem os jogos só pela capa no celular, onde não há `title`, e se sentem falta dos selos e do motivo nas fileiras.
- **Itens B-77 (medição), B-78 (etiquetas na plataforma) e B-79 (recomendações específicas):**
  - entram no P0, antes do B-36 e do B-37;
  - o B-65 é absorvido e o B-75 é substituído;
  - depois do B-79, o modelo de recomendação fica congelado até a defesa.

Desvios do plano:
- **"Para você" em fileira:** entrou depois de o autor ver a primeira versão, em que só as prateleiras eram fileiras.
- **Proporção fixa da capa:** a conferência no navegador mostrou uma capa com outra proporção ("Layers Deep") mais alta que as demais.
- **Testes de "começo da página 1":** um teste unitário do B-72 supunha que a página 1 do "ver mais" da principal era igual à principal da visão geral, o que deixou de valer com 5 jogos na visão geral. O e2e com a mesma suposição só passava porque o catálogo de teste é pequeno. Os dois passaram a conferir o começo da página.

**Linha de base vigente das respostas:** a foto completa depois deste ajuste, com 47.541 respostas e hash total `8dc8b107…`, em `~/indie-discovery-b76/b72-capas/snap-base-full-capas.json`. Ela substitui a do B-72 (`118524c3…`).

## Correções incluídas

Nenhuma.

## Fora deste PR

- **Cabeçalho no celular:** com uma pessoa logada, a 390 px, o cabeçalho do site passa 12 px da largura da tela, por causa do nome e do botão "Sair". Já existia antes deste ajuste e aparece também no catálogo. Fica para uma correção separada, a decidir pelo autor.
- **Itens registrados:** B-77 a B-79, cada um com o seu plano.

## Verificação

- **Comparação das respostas** (`recommendations:snapshot`, 400 perfis nos três modos), contra a linha de base do B-72:
  - páginas do "ver mais": 46.341 de 46.341 iguais;
  - visões gerais: 1.200 de 1.200 diferentes, como previsto.
- **Efeito dos tamanhos,** medido na mesma execução:
  - a principal vai de 20 para 5 jogos;
  - as prateleiras por visão geral ficam iguais (3,17 nos perfis por avaliações e 3,81 nos por preferências), e nenhuma visão geral ganhou ou perdeu prateleira;
  - os jogos nas prateleiras caem pela metade, mas elas continuam cheias.
- **Testes e build:**
  - API: 462 testes unitários e 143 e2e;
  - web: 141 testes;
  - lint (também sem os tipos gerados do Next, como no CI), prettier, tipos e build sem erros.
- **Navegador local (puppeteer), 25 de 25 conferências:**
  - todas as listas da visão geral em fileiras de 5 capas, com altura igual, os mesmos jogos da API e nenhuma repetição;
  - nome no link e no `title`;
  - 5 colunas a 1280 px; rolagem horizontal a 390 px, sem o conteúdo passar da tela;
  - frase do "Pouco conhecido" só no "ver mais";
  - todas as conferências do B-72 (páginas até a 5, troca de modo, lista que deixou de existir, endereços inválidos, convite sem sessão).
  - As contas locais de teste foram apagadas.

## Passos fora do ambiente de desenvolvimento

**Antes do merge:**
1. Conferir que o CI do PR está verde.
2. Na preview da Vercel, as fileiras aparecem com 20 e 10 capas, porque a preview usa a API de produção, que só passa a mandar 5 depois do deploy do Render.

**Depois do merge:**
1. No painel do Render, esperar o deploy "Live" com o hash do merge.
2. Na Vercel, conferir que o deploy de produção do mesmo hash terminou.
3. Rodar contra https://indie-discovery.vercel.app o mesmo script da conferência local, com a conta de produção reutilizada do B-76, cuja senha fica fora do repositório.

author: cre8
body:
## 📝 Description

Issuer Settings and the trust list editor had the same stale-row bug that #1420 fixed on the credential configuration screen. Languages, authorization servers and federation trust anchors in Issuer Settings, and the entities of a trust list, were rendered with `track $index`. `formControlName` binds to its control only once, and nested `FormArray`s never trigger a rebind. So after removing a row that was not the last one, moving an authorization server or changing its type, Angular reused a row view that kept editing a control no longer in the form. The screen showed the removed row's values (for example "Issuer DE" after removing language 2), and edits made afterwards were lost on save.

**Changes**
- **Row tracking:** the four loops now track rows by their control (`track display`, `track server`, `track anchor`, `track entity`).

## Summary

Add Nourish as a community-tier portable MCP tools package owned by davidmosiah. Exact source pin: `438e079efc63a3cc4bc1b7c806592ca0115e7e8b`, subdirectory `agent-plugin`. This is a new listing, not a fork of another plugin or a native memory/provider integration.

author: aayush99000
body:
## What changed
Three model inputs used information that a real-time system would not have at t0. This PR makes all of them causal, and makes training and the live app share one rule for the station channel.

1. **Station channel (`st_now`).** Samples stored the station *label* at t0 as the input. The label needs a Dust Storm Warning within ±60 min, so a dust report counted as "dust now" only if a warning was issued up to an hour **after** t0, and the nearest report could itself be up to 5 min after t0. This also decided which stations count as genesis.
   - New `events.stations.station_now()`: visibility ≤ 1 mi + a dust code, last 3 reports in (t0 − 20 min, t0], no warning check.
   - Training (`sampler.build_sample`), `16_extend_labels.py` and live (`DustAhead.station_now_live`) all call it.
   - A report with only haze (HZ) and no other dust code now counts as **clear**. HZ only counts for the label because a warning confirms it.
   - Synoptic road-weather / PM10 stations have no weather codes, so they are "no report" (−1) in the input channel and targets only, which is what the live app sees.
2. **GOES frames.** New `goes.available_file()` picks the newest scan whose file was **created** ≥ `satellite.latency_min` (2) before the frame time. The old `nearest_file` could pick a scan starting after t0. It is still used for targets (aerosol-detection pixels at t0 + lead).
3. **HRRR analysis.** New `hrrr.analysis_run()` returns `floor_hour(t0 − hrrr.analysis_lag_min)` (60). The analysis valid at hour H is published roughly 50 min after H, so "valid ≤ t0" was not "available at t0". `03_build_samples` prefetch uses the same rule.

## Bug fixed along the way
Stored samples encode the station channel as 1 = dust, 0 = clear, −1 = no report. The old `station_now_live` returned **−1 = clear, 0 = no report**. So in live mode:
- clear stations were dropped from the painted channel
- unreported stations were painted as clear
- a failed ASOS fetch painted every station as clear

The shared function fixes this. The grey "clear" dots in the dashboard, `07_demo_figures` and `09_slide_media` were actually plotting no-report stations; that's fixed too.

## Existing samples
- `scripts/20_causal_station_now.py --dry-run` measures the leak: samples whose channel changes, "dust now" station-times lost/gained, genesis positives before/after.
- Without `--dry-run`, it rewrites `st_now` and `genesis` in place from the label tables already on disk. Nothing is downloaded. The old values are kept as `st_now_label`, and `st_sid` / `st_now_causal` are added.
- It checks the station order against `st_ij`, handles samples already extended by script 16, and is resumable. Run `06_index_samples.py` afterwards.
- The GOES and HRRR timing fixes change the inputs themselves, so existing samples only get them from a full `03_build_samples.py` rebuild.
- `DustDataset` warns when it loads samples that haven't been fixed.

## What a reviewer should know
- **Every result in `results/`, the 2026 test included, was produced with the leaky inputs.** Retrain v8 (and the current best runs) on fixed samples before quoting numbers.
- Rebased onto current `main` (v11–v14). Script renumbered 14 → 20 because `14_synoptic_inventory.py` exists.
- The ~50 min HRRR publication delay is from memory, not measured; `hrrr.analysis_lag_min` is configurable, so check it on the PC.
- **Not fixed here:** `data/radar.py` uses the N0Q composite valid **at** t0, which IEM publishes a few minutes later. It's the same issue as the old GOES rule, noted in `CLAUDE.md` Known gaps.

## Testing
- `pytest -q`: 31 passed, including `tests/test_causal_inputs.py`, which covers:
  - the causal station rule and its encoding through `paint_station_now`
  - `available_file` vs the old look-ahead
  - `analysis_run` hours
  - the station-order assumption script 20 relies on
- Script 20 smoke-tested on a small fake data folder (ASOS-only and extended samples, dry run, write, resume).
- Not yet run on the real samples on the PC.

body:
Add joint orbit/parameter estimation, launch verification and measurement calibration, and a reproducible launch capability bundle. This integration contains the complete reviewed changes from PRs #98, #99 and #100.

The orbit fitter estimates named force, finite-burn and measurement-bias parameters with the six-state orbit and returns joint covariance/correlations, rank and active bounds. The launch workflows retain failed or unavailable verification evidence, fit only designated calibration cases, and evaluate frozen holdouts with predictive uncertainty. Synthetic references do not establish measured flight accuracy or mission qualification.

The capability workflow freezes the source tree and staged patch, installed versions, data hashes, inputs and generated evidence. It checks artifact integrity and reruns the pinned numerical examples against the original reference budgets. External comparisons remain explicitly NOT RUN in this bundle; mission acceptance remains BLOCKED and measured validation remains UNAVAILABLE.

Fix a reproducibility gap by configuring Astropy and native SSAPy from the recorded packaged Earth-orientation snapshot during verification. Isolate SSAPy's process-global interpolation cache, reject queries outside the snapshot coverage, and restore the caller's previous table/cache afterward.

Validation: The shared numerical implementation passed 964 package tests (15 optional skips) and 292 tooling tests (4 skips). The joint-estimation demo recovered all five specified parameters with rank 11/11. The final capability/EOP fix passed seven focused handoff/verification tests (one optional GMAT skip), strict Sphinx, policy for all 24 changed paths, syntax and whitespace checks. Bundle creation and same-environment numerical replay passed with unchanged case outcomes and reference budgets; integrity checks covered 17 files and rejected modified/extra evidence. The pinned SSAPy interpolation matched the supplied IERS row, rejected queries outside snapshot coverage, avoided automatic-table access and restored caller state. Both corrected bundle runs completed without IERS download warnings. All 19 GitHub validation checks passed on this exact integration head.

author: ryderasking
body:
## Intent

Closes #200.

When an agent command or extension wants to show someone a page (an extension's review page, `gh … --web`, `vite --open`), the request used to open a browser on the server machine. Nobody sees that when PiChamber is used from another device. Now the request reaches the person's device as an **Open request**, and they choose whether to open it. Pages on server-local addresses open in the **PiChamber browser** and load through the server, so `localhost:<port>` works over LAN, Tailscale, a tunnel or a proxy. Other pages open in the device's own browser. Each browser tab gets a **browser route** toggle: **Server** or **This device**.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Cmd as Agent command / extension
    participant L as $BROWSER launcher
    participant S as PiChamber server
    participant D as Session daemon
    participant UI as Device
    Cmd->>L: open http://localhost:4777/
    L->>S: POST /open (private Unix socket)
    alt a device has a live event stream
        S->>D: openUrl.publish
        D-->>UI: session.openUrl
        UI->>UI: notice with Open / Dismiss
    else no device
        S-->>L: delivered: false
        L->>L: original $BROWSER, xdg-open or open
    end
```

Nothing is specific to one extension. Anything that honors `$BROWSER` uses this path, and extensions can also call `ctx.ui.openUrl` (gate with `isPiChamber(ctx)`).

## Non-goals

- **Browser automation:** Playwright, Puppeteer, Selenium and `chromium --headless` start their own browser and ignore `$BROWSER`, so they are unaffected. Agents cannot see or drive the PiChamber browser.
- **Separate origin for proxied pages:** in the web app, a page loaded through the server still shares PiChamber's origin. The notice says so (picture 5). A follow-up issue will cover a separate origin.
- **Windows:** Open requests are not intercepted there; `$BROWSER` is left alone.
- **Your own terminals:** only commands the session daemon starts get the launcher.

## Affected surfaces

| Surface | Change |
|---|---|
| `packages/web` server | New `lib/open-url/` (launcher, `$BROWSER` handler, intake socket). `session.openUrl` event on `/api/pi/events`. `openUrl.publish` daemon method. The preview proxy rewrites `Origin`/`Referer` for the page's own requests. |
| Session daemon | Sets `$BROWSER` for child processes. Attributes each request to a session (`open-request.js`). Adds `ctx.ui.openUrl` for extensions. |
| Shared UI | `OpenRequestAlerts` (mounted in `App` and `MobileApp`), Open buttons for URLs in extension notice rows, browser route toggle, server-route loading in `BrowserPane`. |
| Desktop | The webview loads the server route in its own `persist:pichamber-browser` partition, with no PiChamber token, preload or cookies. Navigations that leave the proxy are sent back through it. |
| Hosted and Capacitor mobile | Phone layouts have no PiChamber browser. For server-local pages, the notice only says a page is ready. External pages can still be opened. |
| Persisted UI state | `browserRoute` per context-panel tab and `browserRoutePreference` are additive fields, normalized on load. No store version bump. |
| Runtime files | `<runtimeDir>/open-url.sock` and a `pichamber-open-url` launcher (0700) next to the daemon socket. |

## Repository guidance

| Guidance | Why it applies | How the change complies |
|---|---|---|
| `pichamber-change-discipline` | Source, exports and module ownership change | New domain logic lives in focused modules (`lib/open-url/`, `open-request.js`, `browserProxy.ts`, `open-request.ts`), and entrypoints only wire them. `bun run dead-code` reports nothing for touched files. |
| `ui-api-decoupling` | New server route behavior and UI data access | The UI calls `/api/preview/targets` through `runtimeFetch`, and URLs come from `getRuntimeUrlResolver()`. The intake is a Unix socket, so neither the HTTP app nor the relay can reach it. |
| `desktop-shell` | Electron webview behavior | No new IPC or preload. The webview gets no token or desktop globals (checked at runtime). The webview reroutes navigation through its own `did-start-navigation` events. |
| `sync-state-invariants` | New live event type | `session.openUrl` is never stored in a transcript. Replays are told apart by age on the server's clock (`serverNow - createdAt`), not the device's. A failed delivery falls back to the opener and is never reported as delivered. |
| `relay-transport` | New event on the event stream | Same frame shape as other session events, with a size-bounded payload. |
| `theme-system`, `locale-ui-patterns` | New notice, toggle and overlay | Existing `Button` and toast components, theme tokens, no new icons, sentence-case copy. |
| `packages/ui/src/lib/pi/DOCUMENTATION.md`, `stores/DOCUMENTATION.md`, `session-daemon/DOCUMENTATION.md`, new `lib/open-url/DOCUMENTATION.md`, `GLOSSARY.md` | Contracts and terms changed | All updated. `GLOSSARY.md` defines Device, Server-local address, PiChamber browser, Browser route and Open request. |

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `bun run type-check` | Pass |
| `bun run lint` | Pass |
| `bun run test` | Pass. vitest 124 files / 1434 tests. bun 3494 pass, 0 fail. node 70 + 54 pass. |
| `bun run dead-code` | No findings in touched files |
| New unit tests | `browserProxy.test.ts`, `open-request.test.ts`, `contextPanel.test.ts`, `open-url/*.test.js` (23), `open-request.test.js`, `routes.test.js`, `proxy-runtime.test.js`, `session-daemon-engines.test.js` |
| Desktop end to end (Electron under xvfb, throwaway `HOME` and data dir) | Pass. `$BROWSER` launcher → notice → Open loads the page in the visible panel. Nothing opens by itself; the notice is still there after 20s. On the server route, root-relative, absolute, `_blank` and cross-origin links stay on the proxy. A private address shows the overlay, and "open on this device" works. The webview has no PiChamber token or desktop globals. |
| Web end to end (headless Chrome) | Pass. The notice shows the warning copy, the iframe loads through the proxy, an external URL is offered for the device's browser, and the phone layout shows the information-only notice. |
| Launcher and socket recovery | Pass. Both were deleted while the server ran and were back within the 60s check. Delivery worked afterwards. |
| Not verified | Real Tailscale or Cloudflare tunnel (the proxy path is the same one the preview pane already uses there), macOS `open` fallback, Capacitor native build, dark theme screenshots. |

## Visual evidence

Light theme, with a synthetic demo repo and a local test page on `localhost:4777`. **Before:** there was no notice or route toggle. An Open request ran the server machine's `xdg-open`, so nothing appeared on the device.

| 1. Open request notice | 2. After Open: server route, page served by PiChamber (`127.0.0.1:5191`) |
| ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RyderAsKing/PiChamber/5173ac76e98711490a0d37ed7d5ea1f16830da93/desktop-a-consent-notice.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RyderAsKing/PiChamber/5173ac76e98711490a0d37ed7d5ea1f16830da93/desktop-b-server-route.png) |
| 3. Toggled to this device: served from `localhost:4777` | 4. The server refuses a private address |
| ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RyderAsKing/PiChamber/5173ac76e98711490a0d37ed7d5ea1f16830da93/desktop-d-device-route.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RyderAsKing/PiChamber/5173ac76e98711490a0d37ed7d5ea1f16830da93/desktop-c-private-address-error.png) |

| Web (1440×900) | |
|---|---|
| 5. Notice warns that the page shares PiChamber's origin | 6. After Open: iframe through the server |
| ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RyderAsKing/PiChamber/5173ac76e98711490a0d37ed7d5ea1f16830da93/web-e-consent-warning.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RyderAsKing/PiChamber/5173ac76e98711490a0d37ed7d5ea1f16830da93/web-f-server-route-iframe.png) |
| 7. A public address opens in the device's browser | |

---

### fast-uri vulnerable to scheme injection via an unescaped first-segment colon in suffix references
[CVE-2026-110725](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110725) / [GHSA-333x-w4r6-6crp](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-333x-w4r6-6crp)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact

`fast-uri`'s `serialize()`, `normalize()`, and `resolve()`, when called with the non-default option `reference: 'suffix'` on a reference that has no authority, emit a relative reference whose first path segment contains a bare colon without escaping it. RFC 3986 section 3.3 requires the first segment of a `path-noscheme` reference not to contain a colon, precisely because a bare colon makes the string reparse as an absolute URI with a scheme. `fast-uri`'s default serialization escapes that colon, but the suffix path does not.

For example, `normalize('javascript:alert(1)', { reference: 'suffix' })` returns `javascript:alert(1)`, which reparses as a live `javascript:` scheme; `data:` and `vbscript:` behave the same.

Applications that serialize or normalize a relative reference with `reference: 'suffix'` and then treat the result as a URI can turn inert input into a live `javascript:`, `data:`, or `vbscript:` URL (a cross-site scripting vector), and `equal()` can conflate a scheme-bearing reference with a relative one. Exposure is limited to applications that use the non-default `reference: 'suffix'` option.

##### Patches

Upgrade to `fast-uri` `2.4.8`, `3.1.9`, or `4.2.3`.

##### Workarounds

Do not use the `reference: 'suffix'` option on untrusted input. If suffix output is required, percent-encode a colon in the first path segment of the result before treating it as a URI.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 3.7 / 10 (Low)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N`

#### References
- [https://github.com/fastify/fast-uri/security/advisories/GHSA-333x-w4r6-6crp](https://redirect.github.com/fastify/fast-uri/security/advisories/GHSA-333x-w4r6-6crp)

### fast-uri vulnerable to host confusion via unchecked WHATWG host canonicalization
[CVE-2026-110180](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110180) / [GHSA-wjr9-j795-jxcr](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-wjr9-j795-jxcr)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact

`fast-uri` versions `>= 2.4.2, <= 2.4.7`, `>= 3.1.3, <= 3.1.8`, and `>= 4.0.1, <= 4.2.2` can silently rewrite the host of an HTTP-family URL (`http`, `https`, `ws`, `wss`, or any scheme with `domainHost: true`). For those schemes `canonicalizeHost()` passes the parsed host to the WHATWG `URL` parser and adopts its `.hostname` without checking that the parser read the whole input as a host. RFC 3986 permits `@` inside the host group and the WHATWG parser strips TAB, LF, and CR, so the authority `fast-uri` reports is rewritten by that second parser with no `error` set: data before an `@` is dropped and whitespace is removed.

For example, `fast-uri` parses `http://a@b@evil.example/` to host `evil.example` (dropping the `b` segment), and a host containing a raw TAB, CR, or LF has those characters stripped. `equal()` then treats a whitespace-smuggled host as the same as the clean one, and `resolve()` rewrites the authority the same way.

Applications that use `fast-uri` to enforce host-based policy (denylists, loopback filtering, redirect validation, outbound proxy routing) on one representation, such as the raw input, see a policy/use desync: the canonical host `fast-uri` returns differs from what was checked, and traffic can be steered to an unintended destination.

##### Patches

Upgrade to `fast-uri` `2.4.8`, `3.1.9`, or `4.2.3`.

##### Workarounds

Reject URIs whose authority contains more than one `@`, or contains TAB, CR, or LF, before calling `fast-uri`. Alternatively, treat any non-empty `parse(x).error` as fatal, and compare hosts only from the same `parse()` result.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 4.8 / 10 (Medium)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N`

### Context
Run #42110933267 successfully persisted and consumed the original one-shot dispatch reservation, but Gate 3 did not dispatch the runtime tick. Its follow-up attempt then encountered the already-consumed reservation and the 45-minute bound scope expired. ## Implemented
- Deterministic monthly transition of fractional cohort balances through 1–30, 31–60 and 61–89 day arrears, with cures and 90+ day workout transfer.
- Overdue loan cash collection/accrual, Stage 2 exposure attribution and lifetime ECL on overdue fractions.
- Transfer unpaid balances at contractual maturity into credit-impaired workouts; reconcile gross principal, allowances and the cash ledger.
- Engine-level `modifyLoanCohort` action (requires explicit `nonDerecognition: true`): remeasure amended fixed-coupon cash flows at original EIR, recognise the modification gain/loss in monthly profit, and amortise carrying adjustments through subsequent EIR income.
- POCI helper functions for initial credit-adjusted EIR from expected recovery cashflows and cumulative subsequent lifetime ECL changes.
- New tests covering arrears transitions, write-offs, gross/net reconciliation, modification P&L and POCI calculations.

## Limits
The delinquency path remains a pooled expected flow approximation rather than borrower-by-borrower transactional payment history. The modification engine assumes a prior conclusion that contractual changes do not require derecognition; fee accounting and floating-rate benchmarks remain excluded. POCI calculations are standalone; no POCI purchases are yet booked as new gameplay assets.

CI: fast/typecheck/build, model regression, 72-month calibration and browser tests.

author: yeldhamdev
body:
## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

When `Input.parse_input_event()` is used with a shortcut when running the project embedded while windowed, the action will be done twice. This can be reproduced by changing something twice in the editor, running the project, then pressing <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Z</kbd>. Both actions will be undone at once.

This happens because `WindowWrapper` sets its window to propagate shortcuts to its parent, and the PR fixes that by adding an option to `WindowWrapper` to disable this, which then is used for the game view's wrapper. CC @kitbdev since this behavior was introduced in #115980.

author: wolfgangmeyers
body:
## Status and scope

**Proposed contract clarification — not accepted.** Related to https://github.com/Identity-Digital/known-foundry/issues/56. No merge or issue closure is requested by this proposal.

Additive, language-neutral documentation in the existing shared SDK design surfaces (01 and 12), applicable to Go, Python, and TypeScript.

### New GCP-specific guarantees

- `google-kms` opens an existing fully qualified immutable `CryptoKeyVersion` using `EC_SIGN_ED25519`; no replacement generation or signer fallback on opening failures.
- Explicit `GenerateKey()` creates a pending `EC_SIGN_ED25519` version under the configured version's parent `CryptoKey`, without changing configuration, the active signer, or live publication.
- GCP `Supersede(kid)` does not disable, destroy, or schedule destruction of the corresponding cloud version; cloud retirement is a separate operator action.

### Existing contract restated or clarified

- Local eligibility and successor preservation; current-active-only listing (empty if no active key), not retained-key inventory.
- Pending-key `JWK` access, rotation proof via `SignKey`, and explicit bounded pending-key publication remain intact.
- Recovery uses existing application-owned durable state, exact provider/key bindings, and forward reconciliation of an accepted rotation, not stale deployment settings or inferred eligibility from cloud availability. No new persistence mechanism is introduced.

The provider package is bounded to provider behavior. Pending publication and crash-resume cases exercise existing managed-rotation orchestration; they do not require the provider package to implement manager orchestration.

## Review and authority

Exact proposed head reviewed: `3e5d4d7ca662270739aa28b9e0d86fac2a704949` (including initial proposal `8da478f1af7e3e6cda947143b1c1e1597c43143a` and the separate review fix).

Independent automated reviewer identity: `5091d181`; reported no remaining findings after exact review. This is an automated independent review, **not an SDK-maintainer approval or contract acceptance**. Normal authorized maintainer review/acceptance remains separate. The proposal may inform explicitly provisional implementation/tests after independent review; it does not establish contract delivery or issue closure.

## Validation and proof boundary

- Code-blind authoring: no SDK implementation or executable-test reads.
- Signed commits; latest signature verified locally.
- `git diff --check` passed; documentation changes only.
- Acceptance cases describe required observable outcomes and dependency modes; they are not executable proof. No SDK tests were run and no implementation, coverage, or conformance claim is made.

author: marcmayol
body:
A HueForge downloaded from Creality Cloud (made for a K2 Pro) came out in one colour in Creality Print. This fixes the four causes and adds automatic change height for two-colour reliefs.

## Fixes
- **Projects from another machine**: `inherits_group` and `print_compatible_printers` still named the K2 Pro, so the CLI reloaded that profile (300 mm bed) over ours. They're cleared now, and when the bed size changes the items and the prime tower are moved onto the new bed.
- **Height changes** were per-layer tool changes in `MultiAsSingle` mode: the CLI followed them, the app didn't. They're height-range modifiers now; any tool changes the 3MF had are dropped.
- **A range without `layer_height` crashes the CLI** (0xC0000005). Missing ones get the process layer height.
- **The Prepare view** showed one colour even with the ranges. On objects that sit on a rectangle (HueForge, signs, lithophanes) a solid block below the change is added as a part with the lower filament; where parts overlap the later one wins, so Prepare shows both colours. Other shapes get a warning and keep only the range.

## New
- `analyze_heights`: each object's top surfaces (height and area) and a suggested change height.
- `height_changes=[{"z": "auto", ...}]`: the change goes right above the relief's background. On the eagle flag that's 0.48 mm; the 3MF had it at 0.8 and the white came out as a thin skin.

## Tested
- 73 tests pass (1 xfail as before), including a real slice of a relief with `z: "auto"`.
- Eagle flag: same grams as the hand-made version (7.31 g black, 6.55 g white), the gcode drawn from above matches the photo, and the Prepare view shows black and white.

author: guilhermegsousa
body:
Fixes #412

<!-- concerto-agent -->
Driven by the cloud runner of the issue pipeline. Questions come first, then the spec and the plan, each approved here with `/approve`.

## Spec

### Goal

A graph node that puts a character's feet on the ground under them, on stairs,
slopes and uneven ground. It casts rays against the physics world from each
foot. It lowers the pelvis when a foot must reach lower than the floor the
clip was captured on. It bends each leg to its foot's goal and tilts the foot
to the ground. The slice needs it on the stairs in beats 4, 6 and 7 and on
the snow outside in beats 1 and 5.

The decisions are the ones agreed in the questions on this PR:
- it is a node with one input, in a new `concerto-procedural-animation` crate
  for animation techniques that use physics, not in the motion matching plugin;
- it casts physics rays at the ankle and the toe;
- each foot's offset is applied all the time;
- the pelvis drops by the lowest foot;
- the foot tilts within a limit;
- everything eases with halflives;
- a blackboard param names the body to ignore;
- weight is a constant times a param;
- tech-demo wiring is in scope.

### Today

- **IK.** `TwoBoneIkNode` (`crates/animation/src/node/two_bone_ik.rs`) rotates
  a three-bone chain and nothing else. `concerto_animation::ik::solve_two_bone`
  is the same solve, as a public function that takes joint positions in any
  one space.
- **Model space.** The model-space helpers are private to `two_bone_ik.rs`:
  `parent`, `bone_under_first`, `model_joint` and `WorldToModel`. PR #536
  (#410, approved, not merged) moves them into a `pub(crate)` module,
  `crates/animation/src/node/model_space.rs`.
- **Context.** `AnimationGraphContext::model_to_world()`, during `evaluate`, is
  the `GlobalTransform` of bone 0's parent from the last propagation, so it is
  one frame late.
- **Node inputs.** A node reads ECS data through its associated
  `EvaluateInput`. A missing resource in a plain `Res` skips the node's
  `evaluate` with a warning (`fetched`, `crates/animation/src/node/definition.rs`).
  `Option<Res<T>>` is a `ReadOnlySystemInput`.
- **Springs.** `concerto-animation` has no frame time in `evaluate`.
  `LookAtNode` on PR #536 adds up `delta_time` in `update` and takes it in
  `evaluate`.
  `concerto_foundation::math::Spring::critically_damped_with_halflife` builds a
  spring for `f32` or `Quat`.
- **Physics.** `PhysicsState::cast_ray(origin, direction, QueryFilter { ignore })`
  (`crates/physics/src/physics_state.rs:126`) returns the closest `RayHit`, with
  its `point` and `normal`. `BodyId` wraps the backend handle and is not
  `Reflect`. Physics steps in `LateFixedUpdate`. Graphs evaluate in
  `LateUpdate`, in `update_animation_players` and `animate_targets`.
- **The capsule.** The visible character's model origin sits on the floor of
  its capsule, which has a bottom origin: the character takes the capsule's Y
  (`crates/motion-matching/src/displacement.rs`). The capsule slides up stairs
  and slopes, with no step-up logic.
- **Sanatorium stairs.** The stair colliders are ramps, for example
  `COL_INT_Service_Stairs_Flight_01`, so on the sanatorium stairs feet land on
  the ramp. #551 covers stepped colliders for queries.
- **tech-demo.**
  - The character's graph is one `MotionMatchingNode`, built in code
    (`examples/tech-demo/src/character.rs:144`).
  - Its skeleton (`content/lafan1/model_skeleton`) has the legs `Hips` →
    `LeftUpLeg` → `LeftLeg` → `LeftFoot` → `LeftToe`, and the same on the
    right.
  - `Hips` is the skin's only parentless joint.
  - The capsule carries `GroundProbe`, and `CharacterLink` names the capsule
    and the skeleton.

**Prior art.**
- **Unreal.** Locomotion setups trace from each foot and offset it by the
  ground under it relative to the capsule's floor. They drop the pelvis by the
  lower foot and interpolate every offset. UE 5's `Foot Placement` node does
  this in the anim graph.
- **Unity.** Scripts raycast in `OnAnimatorIK`, then set IK goals and lower
  `bodyPosition`. Final IK's Grounder adds pelvis damping and foot-angle
  limits.
- **Bevy.** There is no foot placement or IK in the engine.

Here, as in UE 5, it is a graph node, so the wiring orders it against the
other procedural nodes: base → layers → aim → look-at → sway →
**foot placement** → hand IK.

### Design

#### A new crate: `crates/procedural-animation` (`concerto-procedural-animation`)

The crate holds animation techniques that read physics. Foot placement is the
first; later ones join it as their own modules.

- **Dependencies:** `concerto-animation`, `concerto-physics`, `concerto-app`,
  `concerto-ecs`, `concerto-foundation`, `concerto-mesh`, `concerto-name`,
  `concerto-reflect`, `glam`, `log`, `uuid` and `serde`.
- **Dev-dependencies:** `bincode = "1.3"`, for the persistence test, as in
  `crates/motion-matching/Cargo.toml`.
- **Manifest:** `version`, `description`, `repository` and `license` come
  from the workspace. `edition = "2024"` is written out, as in
  `crates/animation/Cargo.toml`, because the workspace has no edition and the
  code uses let-chains.
  The root `Cargo.toml` adds it to `[workspace.dependencies]` and to the root
  crate's dependencies.
- **Modules:** `lib.rs` declares `pub mod foot_placement` and `pub mod plugin`,
  and re-exports `FootPlacementNode`, `FootPlacementLeg`, `IgnoredBody` and
  `ProceduralAnimationPlugin` at the crate root, as motion-matching does.
- **Plugin:** `ProceduralAnimationPlugin`, one plugin for the whole crate,
  registers the node with
  `app.register_animation_node::<FootPlacementNode>()`. That also registers
  `FootPlacementLeg`, as a field of the node. `IgnoredBody` needs no
  registration: the blackboard reads it by downcast, and nothing stores it.
- **Root crate:**
  - `src/lib.rs` re-exports the crate as `concerto::procedural_animation`.
  - `DefaultPlugins` registers `ProceduralAnimationPlugin` next to
    `MotionMatchingPlugin`.

`concerto-animation` keeps no dependency on physics.

#### Model-space helpers become public

`concerto_animation::node::model_space` becomes a public module, and its
items, `ModelJoint` with its fields, `WorldToModel` with its fields and
methods, `parent`, `bone_under_first` and `model_joint`, become `pub`. Each
public item gets a one-line `///`.

If PR #536 has merged when this is built, that is the whole change. If it has
not, this PR moves the helpers out of `two_bone_ik.rs` into
`node/model_space.rs` in the same form as #536's commit `b3b8000e`. The two
then conflict on that file when the second one merges, and the `pub` items
win.

The same applies to `Spring::set_halflife` in `concerto-foundation` (#536's
commit `59f9f23b`): this PR uses it, and adds it in the same form if #536
hasn't merged.

#### The node: `crates/procedural-animation/src/foot_placement.rs`

```rust
/// Puts each leg's foot on the ground under it and lowers the pelvis for the lowest; passes its first input through first.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Reflect, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[reflect(AnimationNode)]
pub struct FootPlacementNode {
    pub pelvis: JointName,
    pub legs: Vec<FootPlacementLeg>,
    pub max_step_up: f32,
    pub max_step_down: f32,
    pub max_pelvis_drop: f32,
    pub max_foot_angle: f32,
    pub foot_halflife: f32,
    pub pelvis_halflife: f32,
    pub rotation_halflife: f32,
    pub softness: f32,
    pub weight: f32,
    pub weight_param: Option<Name>,
    pub weight_halflife: f32,
    pub ignore_param: Option<Name>,
}

/// A leg: the foot bone names the chain (its parent the knee, its grandparent the hip), and an optional toe bone adds a second ray.
